AccessorFunc.DESCRIPTION:
Adds simple Get/Set accessor functions on the specified table.
Can also force the value to be set to a number, bool or string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to add the accessor functions to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key of the table to be get/set.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the functions (will be prefixed with Get and Set).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: force
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The type the setter should force to (uses [FORCE](/gmod/Enums/FORCE)).

Add_NPC_Class.DESCRIPTION: Defines a global entity class variable with an automatic value. In order to prevent collisions with other [CLASS](/gmod/Enums/CLASS). You should prefix your variable with CLASS_ for consistency.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the new enum/global variable.

AddBackgroundImage.DESCRIPTION: Adds the specified image path to the main menu background pool. Image can be png or jpeg.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the image.

AddConsoleCommand.DESCRIPTION: Tells the engine to register a console command. If the command was ran, the engine calls [concommand.Run](/gmod/concommand.Run).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the console command to add.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: helpText
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The help text.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Concommand flags using [FCVAR](/gmod/Enums/FCVAR).

AddCSLuaFile.DESCRIPTION: Marks a Lua file to be sent to clients when they join the server. Doesn't do anything on the client - this means you can use it in a shared file without problems.
NOTES:
This function is not needed for scripts located in these paths because they are automatically sent to clients:   
			**lua/matproxy/**  
			**lua/postprocess/**  
			**lua/vgui/**  
			**lua/skins/**  
			**lua/autorun/**  
			**lua/autorun/client/**  
			
			You can add up to **8192** files. Each file can be up to **64KB** compressed (LZMA).
WARNINGS:
If the file trying to be added is empty, an error will occur, and the file will not be sent to the client.
		
		The string cannot have whitespace.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: file
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name/path to the Lua file that should be sent, **relative to the garrysmod/lua folder**. If no parameter is specified, it sends the current file.

The file path can be relative to the script it's ran from. For example, if your script is in `lua/myfolder/stuff.lua`, calling [AddCSLuaFile](/gmod/Global.AddCSLuaFile)("otherstuff.lua") and [AddCSLuaFile](/gmod/Global.AddCSLuaFile)("myfolder/otherstuff.lua") is the same thing.
NOTES: Please make sure your file names are unique, the filesystem is shared across all addons, so a file named `lua/config.lua` in your addon may be overwritten by the same file in another addon.

AddonMaterial.DESCRIPTION: Loads the specified image from the `/cache` folder, used in combination with [steamworks.Download](/gmod/steamworks.Download). Most addons will provide a 512x512 png image.
NOTES: This works with any image file with the `.cache` file extension, even outside of the `/cache` folder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The material, returns `nil` if the cached file is not an image.

AddOriginToPVS.DESCRIPTION: Adds the specified vector to the PVS which is currently building. This allows all objects in visleafs visible from that vector to be drawn.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The origin to add.

AddPropsOfParent.DESCRIPTION: This function creates a Custom Category in the Spawnlist. Use [Global.GenerateSpawnlistFromPath](/gmod/Global.GenerateSpawnlistFromPath) if you want to create a category with the contents of a folder.
WARNINGS: Using this function before [SANDBOX:PopulateContent](/gmod/SANDBOX:PopulateContent) has been called will result in an error.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pnlContent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The SMContentPanel of the Node.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: node
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Node.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: parentid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ParentID to use.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: customProps
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Table with the Contents of the new Category.

AddWorldTip.DESCRIPTION:
This function creates a World Tip, similar to the one shown when aiming at a Thruster where it shows you its force.

This function will make a World Tip that will only last 50 milliseconds (1/20th of a second), so you must call it continuously as long as you want the World Tip to be shown. It is common to call it inside a Think hook.

Contrary to what the function's name implies, it is impossible to create more than one World Tip at the same time. A new World Tip will overwrite the old one, so only use this function when you know nothing else will also be using it.

See [SANDBOX:PaintWorldTips](/gmod/SANDBOX:PaintWorldTips) for more information.
NOTES: This function is only available in Sandbox and its derivatives.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entindex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: **This argument is no longer used**; it has no effect on anything. You can use nil in this argument.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: text
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The text for the world tip to display.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dieTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: **This argument is no longer used**; when you add a World Tip it will always last only 0.05 seconds. You can use nil in this argument.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Where in the world you want the World Tip to be drawn. If you add a valid Entity in the next argument, this argument will have no effect on the actual World Tip.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Which entity you want to associate with the World Tip. This argument is optional. If set to a valid entity, this will override the position set in `pos` with the Entity's position.

Angle.DESCRIPTION: Creates an [Angle](/gmod/Angle) object, representing a [Euler Angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles) made up of pitch, yaw, and roll components.
WARNINGS:
This function is relatively expensive, in terms of performance, in situations where it is being called multiple times every frame (Like a loop, for example.) This is due to the overhead associated with object creation and garbage collection.
			Where possible, it is generally better to store an [Angle](/gmod/Angle) in a variable and re-use that variable rather than re-creating it repeatedly.
			In cases where an empty [Angle](/gmod/Angle) is needed, the global variable `angle_zero` is the preferred solution instead of `Angle( 0, 0, 0 )`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pitch
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pitch value of the angle, in degrees.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: yaw
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The yaw value of the angle, in degrees.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: roll
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The roll value of the angle, in degrees.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) that is a copy of the [Angle](/gmod/Angle) passed in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angleString
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Attempts to parse the input [string](/gmod/string) from the [print](/gmod/Global.print) format of an [Angle](/gmod/Angle).

			Returns an [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with its pitch, yaw, and roll set to `0` if the [string](/gmod/string) cannot be parsed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created [Angle](/gmod/Angle).

AngleRand.DESCRIPTION: Returns an angle with a randomized pitch, yaw, and roll between min(inclusive), max(exclusive).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DEFAULT: -90 for pitch, -180 for yaw and roll
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Min bound inclusive.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DEFAULT: 90 for pitch, 180 for yaw and roll
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Max bound exclusive.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The randomly generated angle.

assert.DESCRIPTION: If the result of the first argument is false or nil, an error is thrown with the second argument as the message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: expression
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The expression to assert.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: errorMessage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The error message to throw when assertion fails. This is only type-checked if the assertion fails.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: returns
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any arguments past the error message will be returned by a successful assert.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If successful, returns the first argument.

If successful, returns the error message. This will be nil if the second argument wasn't specified.

Since the second argument is only type-checked if the assertion fails, this doesn't have to be a string.
Returns any arguments past the error message.

BroadcastLua.DESCRIPTION: Sends the specified Lua code to all connected clients and executes it.
NOTES:
If you need to use this function more than once, consider using [net](/gmod/net) library.
			Send net message and make the entire code you want to execute in [net.Receive](/gmod/net.Receive) on client.  

			If executed **clientside**, this function won't do anything.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: code
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The code to be executed. Capped at length of 6000 bytes.

BuildNetworkedVarsTable.DESCRIPTION: Dumps the networked variables of all entities into one table and returns it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Format:
* key = [Entity](/gmod/Entity) for NWVars or [number](/gmod/number) (always 0) for global vars.
* value = [table](/gmod/table) formatted as:
  * key = [string](/gmod/string) var name.
  * value = any type var value.

CanAddServerToFavorites.DESCRIPTION: Used internally to check if the current server the player is on can be added to favorites or not. Does not check if the server is ALREADY in the favorites.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Can add to favorites?

CancelLoading.DESCRIPTION: Aborts joining of the server you are currently joining.

ChangeBackground.DESCRIPTION: Sets the active main menu background image to a random entry from the background images pool. Images are added with [AddBackgroundImage](/gmod/Global.AddBackgroundImage).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: currentgm
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Apparently does nothing.

ChangeTooltip.DESCRIPTION: Automatically called by the engine when a panel is hovered over with the mouse

ARGUMENTS.NAME: panel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Panel that has been hovered over

ClearBackgroundImages.DESCRIPTION: Empties the pool of main menu background images.

ClearLuaErrorGroup.DESCRIPTION: Clears all Lua Errors with the given group id.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: group_id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: group_id to remove. Will be "[addon-name]-0" or "Other-"

ClearProblem.DESCRIPTION: Removes the given Problem from the Problems table and refreshes the Problems panel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Problem ID to remove

ClientsideModel.DESCRIPTION: Creates a non physical entity that only exists on the client. See also [ents.CreateClientProp](/gmod/ents.CreateClientProp) if physics is wanted.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Parented clientside models will become detached if the parent entity leaves the PVS. A workaround is available on the issue tracker page linked below.
Clientside entities are not garbage-collected, thus you must store a reference to the object (in a variable) and call [CSEnt:Remove](/gmod/CSEnt:Remove) manually when necessary.
Clientside models will occasionally delete themselves during high server lag.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: model
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file path to the model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: renderGroup
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The render group of the entity for the clientside leaf system, see [RENDERGROUP](/gmod/Enums/RENDERGROUP).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created client-side model (`C_BaseFlex`) or `nil` if creation of the entity failed for any reason.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Clientside entities are not garbage-collected, thus you must store a reference to the object and call [CSEnt:Remove](/gmod/CSEnt:Remove) manually.

NOTES:
The ragdoll initially starts as hidden and with shadows disabled, see the example for how to enable it.

There's no need to call [Entity:Spawn](/gmod/Entity:Spawn) on this entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: model
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file path to the model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: renderGroup
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [RENDERGROUP](/gmod/Enums/RENDERGROUP) to assign.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created client-side only ragdoll. (`C_ClientRagdoll`)

ClientsideScene.DESCRIPTION: Creates a scene entity based on the scene name and the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the scene.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: targetEnt
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to play the scene on.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: C_SceneEntity

CloseDermaMenus.DESCRIPTION: Closes all Derma menus that have been passed to [RegisterDermaMenuForClose](/gmod/Global.RegisterDermaMenuForClose) and calls [GM:CloseDermaMenus](/gmod/GM:CloseDermaMenus)

collectgarbage.DESCRIPTION: Executes the specified action on the garbage collector.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: action
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The action to run.

Valid actions are `collect`, `stop`, `restart`, `count`, `step`, `setpause`, `setstepmul` and `isrunning`.
NOTES: `isrunning` is only available on the x86-64 versions, because of the difference in the LuaJIT version. [See here](jit.version)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: arg
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The argument of the specified action, only applicable for `step`, `setpause` and `setstepmul`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
If the action is count this is the number of kilobytes of memory used by Lua.
If the action is step this is true if a garbage collection cycle was finished.

If the action is setpause this is the previous value for the GC's pause.
If the action is setstepmul this is the previous value for the GC's step.

Color.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a [Color](/gmod/Color).
	

Here is a list of colors already cached by the game 

Variable | Color (RGBA) |
-----|------------|
| color_white | Color(255, 255, 255, 255) |
| color_black | Color(0, 0, 0, 255) |
| color_transparent | Color(255, 255, 255, 0) |
WARNINGS: Under no circumstances should these variables be modified (by a Lerp or value modification). Some addons that use these values (e.g. color_white) will be affected by this change.

This function is relatively expensive when used in rendering hooks or in operations requiring very frequent calls (like loops for example) due to object creation and garbage collection. It is better to store the color in a variable or to use the [default colors](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global_Variables#misc) available.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An integer from `0-255` describing the red value of the color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An integer from `0-255` describing the green value of the color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An integer from `0-255` describing the blue value of the color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: a
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An integer from `0-255` describing the alpha (transparency) of the color.(default 255)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created [Color](/gmod/Color).

ColorAlpha.DESCRIPTION: Returns a new [Color](/gmod/Color) with the RGB components of the given [Color](/gmod/Color) and the alpha value specified.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color) from which to take RGB values. This color will not be modified.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: alpha
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new alpha value, a number between 0 and 255. Values above 255 will be clamped.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new [Color](/gmod/Color) with the modified alpha value

ColorRand.DESCRIPTION: Creates a [Color](/gmod/Color) with randomized red, green, and blue components. If the alpha argument is true, alpha will also be randomized.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: a
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should alpha be randomized.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created [Color](/gmod/Color).

ColorToHSL.DESCRIPTION: Converts a [Color](/gmod/Color) into HSL color space.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The hue in degrees `[0, 360]`.
The saturation in the range `[0, 1]`.
The lightness in the range `[0, 1]`.

ColorToHSV.DESCRIPTION: Converts a [Color](/gmod/Color) into HSV color space.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The hue in degrees `[0, 360]`.
The saturation in the range `[0, 1]`.
The value in the range `[0, 1]`.

CompileFile.DESCRIPTION: Attempts to compile the given file. If successful, returns a function that can be called to perform the actual execution of the script.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the file, relative to the `garrysmod/lua/` directory.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: showError
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Decides whether or not a non-halting error should be thrown on compile failure.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The function which executes the script.

CompileString.DESCRIPTION:
This function will compile the code argument as lua code and return a function that will execute that code. 

Please note that this function will not automatically execute the given code after compiling it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: code
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The code to compile.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An identifier in case an error is thrown. (The same identifier can be used multiple times)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: handleError
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If false this function will return an error string instead of throwing an error.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A function that, when called, will execute the given code.

Returns the error string if there was a Lua error and third argument is false.

ConVarExists.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether a [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) with the given name exists or not

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: True if the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) exists, false otherwise.

CreateClientConVar.DESCRIPTION:
Makes a clientside-only console variable



Although this function is shared, it should only be used clientside.
NOTES: This function is a wrapper of [CreateConVar](/gmod/Global.CreateConVar), with the difference being that FCVAR_ARCHIVE and FCVAR_USERINFO are added automatically when **shouldsave** and **userinfo** are true, respectively.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Name of the ConVar to be created and able to be accessed.

This cannot be a name of existing console command or console variable. It will silently fail if it is.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: default
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Default value of the ConVar.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldsave
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should the ConVar be saved across sessions in the cfg/client.vdf file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: userinfo
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should the ConVar and its containing data be sent to the server when it has changed. This makes the convar accessible from server using [Player:GetInfoNum](/gmod/Player:GetInfoNum) and similar functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: helptext
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Help text to display in the console.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, the convar cannot be changed to a number lower than this value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, the convar cannot be changed to a number higher than this value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created convar.

CreateConVar.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a console variable ([ConVar](/gmod/ConVar)).

Generally these are used for settings, which can be stored automatically across sessions if desired. They are usually set via an accompanying user interface clientside, or listed somewhere for dedicated server usage, in which case they might be set via `server.cfg` on server start up.
WARNINGS: Do not use the FCVAR_NEVER_AS_STRING and FCVAR_REPLICATED flags together, as this can cause the console variable to have strange values on the client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Name of the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar).

This cannot be a name of an engine console command or console variable. It will throw an error if it is. If it is the same name as another lua ConVar, it will return that ConVar object.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Default value of the convar. Can also be a number.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Flags of the convar, see [FCVAR](/gmod/Enums/FCVAR), either as bitflag or as table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: helptext
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The help text to show in the console.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, the ConVar cannot be changed to a number lower than this value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, the ConVar cannot be changed to a number higher than this value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The convar created, or `nil` if convar could not be created. (such as when there's a console command with the same name)

If a ConVar already exists (including engine ones), it will simply return the already existing ConVar without modifying it in any way.

CreateMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a new material with the specified name and shader.

Materials created with this function can be used in [Entity:SetMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetMaterial) and [Entity:SetSubMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetSubMaterial) by prepending a `!` to their material name argument.

This will not create a new material if another material object with the same name already exists. All Materials created by this functions are cleaned up on map shutdown.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: .pngs must be loaded with [Material](/gmod/Global.Material) before being used with this function.

NOTES: This does not work with [patch materials](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Patch).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material name. Must be unique.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shaderName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The shader name. See [Shaders](/gmod/Shaders).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: materialData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Key-value table that contains shader parameters and proxies.

* See: [List of Shader Parameters on Valve Developers Wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Category:List_of_Shader_Parameters) and each shader's page from .
NOTES: Unlike [IMaterial:SetTexture](/gmod/IMaterial:SetTexture), this table will not accept [ITexture](/gmod/ITexture) values. Instead, use the texture's name (see [ITexture:GetName](/gmod/ITexture:GetName)).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created material

CreateNewAddonPreset.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new Preset from the given JSON string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A JSON string containing all necessary information.
			JSON structue should be [Structures/Preset](/gmod/Structures/Preset)

CreateParticleSystem.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new particle system. See also [Entity:CreateParticleEffect](/gmod/Entity:CreateParticleEffect), [ParticleEffectAttach](/gmod/Global.ParticleEffectAttach) and [CreateParticleSystemNoEntity](/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystemNoEntity).
NOTES: The particle effect must be precached with [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem) and the file its from must be added via [game.AddParticles](/gmod/game.AddParticles) before it can be used!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to attach the control point to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: effect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the effect to create. It must be precached via [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem) beforehand.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: partAtt
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: See [PATTACH](/gmod/Enums/PATTACH).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entAtt
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment ID on the entity to attach the particle system to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: offset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The offset from the [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos) of the entity we are attaching this CP to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created particle system.

CreateParticleSystemNoEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a new particle system, and sets control points 0 and 1 to given position, as well as optionally orientation of CP0 to the given angles.

See also [CreateParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystem)
NOTES: The particle effect must be precached with [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem) and the file its from must be added via [game.AddParticles](/gmod/game.AddParticles) before it can be used!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: effect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the effect to create. It must be precached via [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem) beforehand.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position for the particle system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The orientation of the particle system.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created particle system.

CreatePhysCollideBox.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new [PhysCollide](/gmod/PhysCollide) from the given bounds.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This fails to create planes or points - no components of the mins or maxs can be the same.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Min corner of the box. This is not automatically ordered with the maxs and must contain the smallest vector components. See [OrderVectors](/gmod/Global.OrderVectors).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Max corner of the box. This is not automatically ordered with the mins and must contain the largest vector components.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new PhysCollide. This will be a NULL PhysCollide ([PhysCollide:IsValid](/gmod/PhysCollide:IsValid) returns false) if given bad vectors or no more PhysCollides can be created in the physics engine.

CreatePhysCollidesFromModel.DESCRIPTION: Creates [PhysCollide](/gmod/PhysCollide) objects for every physics object the model has. The model must be precached with [util.PrecacheModel](/gmod/util.PrecacheModel) before being used with this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Model path to get the collision objects of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of [PhysCollide](/gmod/PhysCollide) objects. The number of entries will match the model's physics object count. See also [Entity:GetPhysicsObjectCount](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObjectCount). Returns no value if the model doesn't exist, or has not been precached.

CreateSound.DESCRIPTION: Returns a sound parented to the specified entity.
NOTES: You can only create one CSoundPatch per audio file, per entity at the same time.

Valid sample rates: **11025 Hz, 22050 Hz and 44100 Hz**, otherwise you may see this kind of message:

`Unsupported 32-bit wave file your_sound.wav` and 
`Invalid sample rate (48000) for sound 'your_sound.wav'`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: targetEnt
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The target entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound to play. (Sound path or a [soundscript](/gmod/sound.Add)) [Soundscript Characters](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Soundscripts/en#Sound_Characters) are supported.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A [CRecipientFilter](/gmod/CRecipientFilter) of the players that will have this sound networked to them.

If not set, the default is a [CPASAttenuationFilter](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/CRecipientFilter#Derived_classes).
NOTES: This argument only works serverside.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The sound object. You should keep a reference to this object for as long as you wish the sound to play!

CreateSprite.DESCRIPTION: Creates and returns a new [DSprite](/gmod/DSprite) element with the supplied material.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Material the sprite should draw.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new [DSprite](/gmod/DSprite) element.

CurTime.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the uptime of the server in seconds (to at least 4 decimal places)

This is a synchronised value and affected by various factors such as host_timescale (or [game.GetTimeScale](/gmod/game.GetTimeScale)) and the server being paused - either by `sv_pausable` or all players disconnecting.

You should use this function for timing in-game events but not for real-world events.

See also: [RealTime](/gmod/Global.RealTime), [SysTime](/gmod/Global.SysTime)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Time synced with the game server.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not create a unique object, but instead returns a shared reference. That means you cannot use two or more of these objects at once.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [CTakeDamageInfo](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo) object.

DebugInfo.DESCRIPTION: Writes text to the right hand side of the screen, like the old error system. Messages disappear after a couple of seconds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: slot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The location on the right hand screen to write the debug info to. Starts at 0, no upper limit

ARGUMENTS.NAME: info

DEFINE_BASECLASS.DESCRIPTION:
Generates and provides a local variable `BaseClass` that can be used to call the original version of a class functions after modifying it.

		This is a preprocessor keyword that is directly replaced with the following text:
```lua
local BaseClass = baseclass.Get
```

Because this is a simple preprocessor keyword and not a function, it will cause problems if not used properly

See [baseclass.Get](/gmod/baseclass.Get) for more information.
	

For more information, including usage examples, see the [BaseClasses](/gmod/BaseClasses) reference page.
WARNINGS:
The preprocessor is not smart enough to know when substitution doesn't make sense, such as: table keys and strings.  

Running `print("DEFINE_BASECLASS")` is the same as `print("local BaseClass = baseclass.Get")`

Either.DESCRIPTION:
An [eagerly evaluated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eager_evaluation) [ternary operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%3F:), or, in layman's terms, a compact "if then else" statement.

In most cases, you should just use Lua's ["pseudo" ternary operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%3F:#Lua), like this:

```
local myCondition = true
local consequent = "myCondition is true"
local alternative = "myCondition is false"

print(myCondition and consequent or alternative)
```

In the above example, due to [short-circuit evaluation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-circuit_evaluation), `consequent` would be "skipped" and ignored (not evaluated) by Lua due to `myCondition` being `true`, and only `alternative` would be evaluated. However, when using `Either`, both `consequent` and `alternative` would be evaluated. A practical example of this can be found at the bottom of the page.

# Falsey values

If `consequent` is "falsey" (Lua considers both `false` and `nil` as false), this will not work. For example:

```
local X = true
local Y = false
local Z = "myCondition is false"

print(X and Y or Z)
```

This will actually print the value of `Z`.

In the above case, and other very rare cases, you may find `Either` useful.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: condition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The condition to check if true or false.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: truevar
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the condition isn't nil/false, returns this value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: falsevar
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the condition is nil/false, returns this value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The result.

GetRenderTarget.DESCRIPTION:
Creates or gets the rendertarget with the given name.

See [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) for an advanced version of this function with more options.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This crashes when used on a cubemap texture.

NOTES:
Calling this function is equivalent to
```lua
GetRenderTargetEx(name,
	width, height,
	RT_SIZE_NO_CHANGE,
	MATERIAL_RT_DEPTH_SEPARATE,
	bit.bor(2, 256),
	0,
	IMAGE_FORMAT_BGRA8888
)
```
WARNINGS: Drawing rendertargets on themself can produce odd and unexpected results.

Rendertargets are not garbage-collected, which means they will remain in memory until you disconnect. So make sure to avoid creating new ones unecessarily and re-use as many of your existing rendertargets as possible to avoid filling up all your memory.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal name of the render target.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: width
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The width of the render target, must be power of 2. If not set to PO2, the size will be automatically converted to the nearest PO2 size.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: height
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The height of the render target, must be power of 2. If not set to PO2, the size will be automatically converted to the nearest PO2 size.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The render target

GetRenderTargetEx.DESCRIPTION:
Gets (or creates if it does not exist) the rendertarget with the given name, this function allows to adjust the creation of a rendertarget more than [GetRenderTarget](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTarget).

See also [render.PushRenderTarget](/gmod/render.PushRenderTarget) and [render.SetRenderTarget](/gmod/render.SetRenderTarget).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal name of the render target.
WARNINGS: The name is treated like a path and gets its extension discarded."name.1" and "name.2" are considered the same name and will result in the same render target being reused.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: width
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The width of the render target, must be power of 2.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: height
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The height of the render target, must be power of 2.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sizeMode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bitflag that influences the sizing of the render target, see [RT_SIZE](/gmod/Enums/RT_SIZE).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: depthMode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bitflag that determines the depth buffer usage of the render target [MATERIAL_RT_DEPTH](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL_RT_DEPTH).
WARNINGS: PNG's may not render to non MATERIAL_RT_DEPTH_NONE RenderTargets

ARGUMENTS.NAME: textureFlags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Bitflag that configures the texture, see [TEXTUREFLAGS](/gmod/Enums/TEXTUREFLAGS).

List of flags can also be found on the Valve's Developer Wiki:
https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Valve_Texture_Format

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rtFlags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Flags that control the HDR behaviour of the render target, see [CREATERENDERTARGETFLAGS](/gmod/Enums/CREATERENDERTARGETFLAGS).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: imageFormat
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Image format, see [IMAGE_FORMAT](/gmod/Enums/IMAGE_FORMAT).
NOTES: Some additional image formats are accepted, but don't have enums. See [VTF Enumerations.](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Valve_Texture_Format#VTF_enumerations)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new render target.

include.DESCRIPTION:

WARNINGS:

If the file you are including is clientside or shared, it **must** be [AddCSLuaFile](/gmod/Global.AddCSLuaFile)'d or this function will error saying the file doesn't exist.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the script to be executed. The path must be either relative to the current file, or be an absolute path (relative to and excluding the **lua/** folder).

Addon files (.gma files) and dedicated servers clientside do not support relative parent folders (`..` notation).

Absolute paths for gamemode files must include `

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Anything that the executed Lua script returns.

DEPRECATED: To send the target file to the client simply call AddCSLuaFile() in the target file itself.

* "_gesture"
* "_anim"

* "_shd"

NOTES: If you are sure that the object you are about to check is not `nil` and has the `IsValid` method, it would be faster to call it directly rather than using `IsValid`.
Due to vehicles being technically valid the moment they're spawned, also use [Vehicle:IsValidVehicle](/gmod/Vehicle:IsValidVehicle) to make sure they're fully initialized.

Lerp.DESCRIPTION:
Performs a linear interpolation from the start number to the end number.

This function provides a very efficient and easy way to smooth out movements.

See also [math.ease](/gmod/math.ease) for functions that allow to have non linear animations using linear interpolation.
NOTES: This function is not meant to be used with constant value in the first argument if you're dealing with animation! Use a value that changes over time. See example for **proper** usage of Lerp for animations.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: t
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The fraction for finding the result. This number is clamped between 0 and 1. Shouldn't be a constant.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: from
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The starting number. The result will be equal to this if delta is 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ending number. The result will be equal to this if delta is 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The result of the linear interpolation, `from + (to - from) * t`.

LerpAngle.DESCRIPTION: Returns point between first and second angle using given fraction and linear interpolation
NOTES: This function is not meant to be used with constant value in the first argument, if you're dealing with animation! Use a value that changes over time

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ratio
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ratio of progress through values

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angleStart
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angle to begin from

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angleEnd
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angle to end at

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: angle

LerpVector.DESCRIPTION: Linear interpolation between two vectors. It is commonly used to smooth movement between two vectors
NOTES: This function is not meant to be used with constant value in the first argument, if you're dealing with animation! Use a value that changes over time

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fraction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Fraction ranging from 0 to 1

ARGUMENTS.NAME: from
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The initial Vector

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The desired Vector

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The lerped vector.

LocalToWorld.DESCRIPTION:
Translates a vector and angle from a local coordinate system into a global coordinate system.

For the reverse of this function see [WorldToLocal](/gmod/Global.WorldToLocal).

For working with an entity's local space vectors/angles you might consider using [Entity:LocalToWorld](/gmod/Entity:LocalToWorld)/[Entity:LocalToWorldAngles](/gmod/Entity:LocalToWorldAngles) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: localPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A vector from a local coordinate system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: localAng
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
An angle from a local coordinate system.

Pass a zero angle if you don't need to translate an angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: originPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The origin of a global coordinate system, in worldspace coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: originAngle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angles of a global coordinate system, as a worldspace angle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding worldspace vector to `localPos`.
The corresponding worldspace angle to `localAng`.

MainEyeAngles.DESCRIPTION:

Material.DESCRIPTION:
Either returns the material with the given name, or loads the material interpreting the first argument as the path.

## .png, .jpg and other image formats

This function is capable to loading `.png` or `.jpg` images, generating a texture and material for them on the fly.

PNG, JPEG, GIF, and TGA files will work, but only if they have the `.png` or `.jpg` file extensions (even if the actual image format doesn't match the file extension)

Use [AddonMaterial](/gmod/Global.AddonMaterial) for image files with the `.cache` file extension. (from [steamworks.Download](/gmod/steamworks.Download))

While images are no longer scaled to Power of 2 (sizes of 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, etc.) sizes since February 2019, it is still a good practice for things like icons, etc.
WARNINGS: Server-side, this function can consistently return an invalid material (with '__error') depending on the file type loaded.
This function is very expensive when used in rendering hooks or in operations requiring very frequent calls. It is a good idea to cache the material in a variable (like in the examples).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: materialName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The material name or path relative to the `materials/` folder.  
Paths outside the `materials/` folder like `data/MyImage.jpg` or `maps/thumb/gm_construct.png` will also work for when generating materials.

To retrieve a Lua material created with [CreateMaterial](/gmod/Global.CreateMaterial), just prepend a `!` to the material name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pngParameters
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A string containing space separated keywords which will be used to add material parameters.

See [Material Parameters](/gmod/Material%20Parameters) for more information.
NOTES: This feature only works when importing `.png` or `.jpg` image files.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Generated material.
How long it took for the function to run.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Initial data to initialize the matrix with. Leave empty to initialize an identity matrix. See examples for usage.

Can be a [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) to copy its data.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: New matrix.

Msg.DESCRIPTION:
Writes every given argument to the console. Limitations of [print](/gmod/Global.print) apply.

Automatically attempts to convert each argument to a string. (See [tostring](/gmod/Global.tostring))

Unlike [print](/gmod/Global.print), arguments are not separated by anything. They are simply concatenated.

Additionally, a newline isn't added automatically to the end, so subsequent Msg or print operations will continue the same line of text in the console. See [MsgN](/gmod/Global.MsgN) for a version that does add a newline.

The text is blue on the server, orange on the client, and green on the menu:

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: List of values to print.

MsgAll.DESCRIPTION: Works exactly like [Msg](/gmod/Global.Msg) except that, if called on the server, will print to all players consoles plus the server console. Limitations of [print](/gmod/Global.print) apply.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: List of values to print.

MsgC.DESCRIPTION: Just like [Msg](/gmod/Global.Msg), except it can also print colored text, just like [chat.AddText](/gmod/chat.AddText).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Values to print. If you put in a color, all text after that color will be printed in that color.

MsgN.DESCRIPTION:
Same as [print](/gmod/Global.print), except it concatinates the arguments without inserting any whitespace in between them.

See also [Msg](/gmod/Global.Msg), which doesn't add a newline (`"\n"`) at the end.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: List of values to print. They can be of any type and will be converted to strings with [tostring](/gmod/Global.tostring).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of color

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A [Color](/gmod/Color) or nil

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Fails under certain conditions when called in coroutines

ARGUMENTS.NAME: addMetatable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If true, the created [userdata](/gmod/userdata) will be given its own metatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: userData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new [userdata](/gmod/userdata) with the same metatable the [userdata](/gmod/userdata) passed in had. The [userdata](/gmod/userdata) passed in **must be** a [userdata](/gmod/userdata) that has a metatable that was created from this function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created [userdata](/gmod/userdata).

next.DESCRIPTION: Returns the next key and value pair in a table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The next key for the table. If the previous key was nil, this will be the first key in the table. If the previous key was the last key in the table, this will be nil.
The value associated with that key. If the previous key was the last key in the table, this will be nil.

Clientside, you can use [CreateParticleSystemNoEntity](/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystemNoEntity) (and similar) instead.

This is due to the function using networked IDs for particle names, not directly networking particle system name.

Clientside, you can use [CreateParticleSystemNoEntity](/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystemNoEntity) (and similar) instead.

NOTES: Do not forget to delete the emitter with [CLuaEmitter:Finish](/gmod/CLuaEmitter:Finish) once you are done with it

Path.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a path for the bot to follow using one of two types (`Follow` or `Chase`)

`Follow` is a general purpose path. Best used for static or infrequently updated locations. The path will only be updated once [PathFollower:Update](/gmod/PathFollower:Update) is called. This needs to be done manually (typically inside the bots `BehaveThread` coroutine.

`Chase` is a specifically optimized for chasing a moving entity. Paths of this type will use [PathFollower:Chase](/gmod/PathFollower:Chase)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The type of the path to create, must be `"Follow"` or `"Chase"`

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The path

pcall.DESCRIPTION: Calls a function and catches an error that can be thrown while the execution of the call.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This cannot stop errors from hooks called from the engine.

This does not stop [Global.Error](/gmod/Global.Error) and [ErrorNoHalt](/gmod/Global.ErrorNoHalt) from sending error messages to the server (if called clientside) or calling the [GM:OnLuaError](/gmod/GM:OnLuaError) hook. The success boolean returned will always return true and thus you will not get the error message returned. [Global.error](/gmod/Global.error) does not exhibit these behaviours.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be executed and of which the errors should be caught of

ARGUMENTS.NAME: arguments
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Arguments to call the function with.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the function had no errors occur within it.
If an error occurred, this will be a string containing the error message. Otherwise, this will be the return values of the function passed in.

WARNINGS:

There is no limit clientside.

print.DESCRIPTION:
Writes every given argument to the console.
Automatically attempts to convert each argument to a string. (See [tostring](/gmod/Global.tostring))

Separates lines with a line break (`"\n"`)

Separates arguments with a tab character (`"\t"`).

Can only print up to `4096` characters at a time, and will stop at NULL character. (`"\0"`)

See [Msg](/gmod/Global.Msg) for alternative that doesn't force add a new line, and [MsgC](/gmod/Global.MsgC) for adding colored text to the console.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: List of values to print.

PrintMessage.DESCRIPTION:
Displays a message in the chat, console, or center of screen of every player.

This uses the archaic user message system ([umsg](/gmod/umsg)) and hence is limited to 255 characters.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type

RealTime.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the uptime of the game/server in seconds (to at least **4** decimal places). This value updates itself once every time the realm thinks. For servers, this is the server tickrate. For clients, this is once per frame.



You should use this function (or [SysTime](/gmod/Global.SysTime)) for timing real-world events such as user interaction, but not for timing game events such as animations.

See also: [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime), [SysTime](/gmod/Global.SysTime)
NOTES:
This is **not** synchronised or affected by the game.

This will be affected by precision loss if the uptime is more than 30+(?) days, and effectively cease to be functional after 50+(?) days.

Changing the map will **not** fix it like it does with [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime). A server restart is necessary.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Uptime of the game/server.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: unreliable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
If set to true, makes the filter unreliable. 

This means, when sending over the network in cases like [CreateSound](/gmod/Global.CreateSound) (and its subsequent updates), the message is not guaranteed to reach all clients.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new created recipient filter.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Running this function with [pcall](/gmod/Global.pcall) or [xpcall](/gmod/Global.xpcall) will still print an error that counts towards sv_kickerrornum.

NOTES: This function will try to load local client file if `sv_allowcslua` is set to `1`

Binary modules can't be installed as part of an addon and have to be put directly into ``garrysmod/lua/bin/`` to be detected.
	This is a safety measure, because modules can be malicious and harm the system.

RunConsoleCommand.DESCRIPTION: Executes the given console command with the parameters.
NOTES: Some commands/convars are blocked from being ran/changed using this function, usually to prevent harm/annoyance to clients. For a list of blocked commands, see [Blocked ConCommands](/gmod/Blocked%20ConCommands).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: command
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The command to be executed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: arguments
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The arguments. Note, that unlike [Player:ConCommand](/gmod/Player:ConCommand), you must pass each argument as a new string, not separating them with a space.

RunGameUICommand.DESCRIPTION: Runs a menu command. Equivalent to [RunConsoleCommand](/gmod/Global.RunConsoleCommand)`( "gamemenucommand", command )` unless the command starts with the `"engine"` keyword in which case it is equivalent to [RunConsoleCommand](/gmod/Global.RunConsoleCommand)`( command )`.
WARNINGS: Invoking engine commands no longer works, prints out `Not running engine cmd 'concommand'`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: command
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The menu command to run

Should be one of the following:
* `Disconnect` - Disconnects from the current server.
* `OpenBenchmarkDialog` - Opens the "Video Hardware Stress Test" dialog.
* `OpenChangeGameDialog` - Does not work in GMod.
* `OpenCreateMultiplayerGameDialog` - Opens the Source dialog for creating a listen server.
* `OpenCustomMapsDialog` - Does nothing.
* `OpenFriendsDialog` - Does nothing.
* `OpenGameMenu` - Does not work in GMod.
* `OpenLoadCommentaryDialog` - Opens the "Developer Commentary" selection dialog. Useless in GMod.
* `OpenLoadDemoDialog` - Does nothing.
* `OpenLoadGameDialog` - Opens the Source "Load Game" dialog.
* `OpenNewGameDialog` - Opens the "New Game" dialog. Useless in GMod.
* `OpenOptionsDialog` - Opens the options dialog.
* `OpenPlayerListDialog` - Opens the "Mute Players" dialog that shows all players connected to the server and allows to mute them.
* `OpenSaveGameDialog` - Opens the Source "Save Game" dialog.
* `OpenServerBrowser` - Opens the legacy server browser.
* `Quit` - Quits the game **without** confirmation (unlike other Source games).
* `QuitNoConfirm` - Quits the game without confirmation (like other Source games).
* `ResumeGame` - Closes the menu and returns to the game.
* `engine 'concommand'` - Runs a console command. Unlike [RunConsoleCommand](/gmod/Global.RunConsoleCommand) It will ignore [Blocked ConCommands](/gmod/Blocked%20ConCommands)

This function can also be used for scaling font sizes.

See [ScreenScaleH](/gmod/Global.ScreenScaleH) for a function that scales from height.

SortedPairs.DESCRIPTION:
This function can be used in a for loop instead of [pairs](/gmod/Global.pairs). It sorts all **keys** alphabetically.

For sorting by specific **value member**, use [SortedPairsByMemberValue](/gmod/Global.SortedPairsByMemberValue).


For sorting by **value**, use [SortedPairsByValue](/gmod/Global.SortedPairsByValue).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Reverse the sorting order

SortedPairsByMemberValue.DESCRIPTION:
Returns an iterator function that can be used to loop through a table in order of member values, when the values of the table are also tables and contain that member.

To sort by **value**, use [SortedPairsByValue](/gmod/Global.SortedPairsByValue).


To sort by **keys**, use [SortedPairs](/gmod/Global.SortedPairs).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to create iterator for.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: memberKey
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Key of the value member to sort by.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: descending
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the iterator should iterate in descending order or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Iterator function
Internal iterator state, not the source table. It must be passed straight through to the generic for loop; capturing only the first return value and iterating over that will error.

xpcall.DESCRIPTION:
Attempts to call the first function. If the execution succeeds, this returns `true` followed by the returns of the function. If execution fails, this returns `false` and the second function is called with the error message. 

Unlike in [pcall](/gmod/Global.pcall), the stack is not unwound and can therefore be used for stack analyses with the [debug](/gmod/debug).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This cannot stop errors from hooks called from the engine.

This does not stop [Global.Error](/gmod/Global.Error) and [ErrorNoHalt](/gmod/Global.ErrorNoHalt) (As well as [include](/gmod/Global.include)) from sending error messages to the server (if called clientside) or calling the [GM:OnLuaError](/gmod/GM:OnLuaError) hook. The success boolean returned will always return true and thus you will not get the error message returned. [Global.error](/gmod/Global.error) does not exhibit these behaviours.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to call initially.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: errorCallback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The function to be called if execution of the first fails; the error message is passed as a string.

You cannot throw an [Global.error](/gmod/Global.error)() from this callback: it will have no effect (not even stopping the callback).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: arguments
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Arguments to pass to the initial function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Status of the execution; `true` for success, `false` for failure.
The returns of the first function if execution succeeded, otherwise the **first** return value of the error callback.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: How our scripted NPC "feels" towards the entity in question. See [D](/gmod/Enums/D). Not returning any value will make [NPC:Disposition](/gmod/NPC:Disposition) return the default disposition for this SNPC's given `m_iClass` by the engine.

GetRenderMesh.DESCRIPTION: Specify a mesh that should be rendered instead of this SENT's model.
NOTES: You should not be creating or modifying an [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) in this hook. [Reference](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/6411#issuecomment-3070608549)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing the following keys:
* [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) Mesh - (Required) The mesh to render instead of the default model
* [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial) Material - (Required) The material to render the mesh with.
* [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) Matrix - (Optional) - Render matrix override (mesh position, angles, etc)

GetShadowCastDirection.DESCRIPTION: Called when the shadow needs to be recomputed. Allows shadow angles to be customized. This only works for `anim` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Type of the shadow this entity uses. Possible values:
* 0 - No shadow
* 1 - Simple 'blob' shadow
* 2 - Render To Texture shadow (updates only when necessary)
* 3 - Dynamic RTT - updates always
* 4 - Render to Depth Texture

RETURNS.NAME: dir
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new shadow direction to use.

GetSoundInterests.DESCRIPTION: Called every second to poll the sound hint interests of this SNPC. This is used in conjunction with other sound hint functions, such as [sound.EmitHint](/gmod/sound.EmitHint) and [NPC:GetBestSoundHint](/gmod/NPC:GetBestSoundHint).
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type SENTs

RETURNS.NAME: types
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A bitflag representing which sound types this NPC wants to react to.  See [SOUND_ enums](/gmod/Enums/SOUND).

GravGunPickupAllowed.DESCRIPTION: Called by [GM:GravGunPickupAllowed](/gmod/GM:GravGunPickupAllowed) on ALL entites in Sandbox-derived  gamemodes and acts as an override.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player aiming at us

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return true to allow the entity to be picked up

GravGunPunt.DESCRIPTION:
Called when this entity is about to be punted with the gravity gun (primary fire).

Only works in Sandbox derived gamemodes and only if [GM:GravGunPunt](/gmod/GM:GravGunPunt) is not overridden.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player pressing left-click with the gravity gun at an entity

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return true or false to enable or disable punting respectively.

HandleAnimEvent.DESCRIPTION:
Called before firing serverside animation events, such as weapon reload, drawing and holstering for NPCs, scripted sequences, etc.

See [ENTITY:FireAnimationEvent](/gmod/ENTITY:FireAnimationEvent) for the clientside version.
NOTES: This hook only works on "anim", "ai" and "nextbot" type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: event
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the event. See [this page](http://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Animation_Events) for a list of default events, and see [util.GetAnimEventNameByID](/gmod/util.GetAnimEventNameByID) for a helper function in handing custom events.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: eventTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The absolute time this event occurred using [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cycle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The frame this event occurred as a number between 0 and 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Event type. See [the Source SDK](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/shared/eventlist.h#L14-L23).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: options
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name or options of this event.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return true to mark the event as handled.

ImpactTrace.DESCRIPTION: Called when a bullet trace hits this entity and allows you to override the default behavior by returning true.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: traceResult
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The trace that hit this entity as a [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage bits associated with the trace, see [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: customImpactName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The effect name to override the impact effect with.
Possible arguments are ImpactJeep, AirboatGunImpact, HelicopterImpact, ImpactGunship.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return true to override the default impact effects.

Initialize.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity is created. This is called when you [Entity:Spawn](/gmod/Entity:Spawn) the custom entity.

This is called **after** [ENTITY:SetupDataTables](/gmod/ENTITY:SetupDataTables) and [GM:OnEntityCreated](/gmod/GM:OnEntityCreated).

IsJumpLegal.DESCRIPTION: Called when deciding if the Scripted NPC should be able to perform a certain jump or not.
NOTES: This is only called for "ai" type entities

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start of the jump

ARGUMENTS.NAME: apex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Apex point of the jump

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The landing position

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Return true if this jump should be allowed to be performed, false otherwise.

Not returning anything, or returning a non boolean will perform the [default action](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/ai_basenpc_movement.cpp#L319).

KeyValue.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the engine sets a value for this scripted entity.

This hook is called **before** [ENTITY:Initialize](/gmod/ENTITY:Initialize) when the key-values are set by the map.
Otherwise this hook will be called whenever [Entity:SetKeyValue](/gmod/Entity:SetKeyValue) is called on the entity.

See [GM:EntityKeyValue](/gmod/GM:EntityKeyValue) for a hook that works for all entities.

See [WEAPON:KeyValue](/gmod/WEAPON:KeyValue) for a hook that works for scripted weapons.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key that was affected.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return true to suppress this KeyValue or return false or nothing to apply this key value.

NextTask.DESCRIPTION: Start the next task in specific Lua schedule.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sched
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The schedule to start next task in.

OnChangeActiveWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Called when the currently active weapon of the SNPC changes.
NOTES: This hook only works on `ai` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: old
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The previous active weapon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: new
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new active weapon.

OnChangeActivity.DESCRIPTION: Called when the NPC has changed its activity.
NOTES: This hook only works for `ai` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new activity. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

OnCondition.DESCRIPTION: Called each time the NPC updates its condition.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: conditionID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of condition. See [NPC:ConditionName](/gmod/NPC:ConditionName).

OnDuplicated.DESCRIPTION:
Called on any entity after it has been created by the [duplicator](/gmod/duplicator) and before any bone/entity modifiers have been applied.

This hook is called after [ENTITY:Initialize](/gmod/ENTITY:Initialize) and before [ENTITY:PostEntityPaste](/gmod/ENTITY:PostEntityPaste).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The stored data about the original entity that was duplicated. This would typically contain the [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) fields that are serializalble. See [Structures/EntityCopyData](/gmod/Structures/EntityCopyData).

OnEntityCopyTableFinish.DESCRIPTION:
Called after duplicator finishes saving the entity, allowing you to modify the save data.

This is called after [ENTITY:PostEntityCopy](/gmod/ENTITY:PostEntityCopy).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The save [Structures/EntityCopyData](/gmod/Structures/EntityCopyData) that you can modify.

OnMovementComplete.DESCRIPTION: Called when the SNPC completes its movement to its destination.
NOTES: This hook only works on `ai` type entities.

OnMovementFailed.DESCRIPTION: Called when the SNPC failed to move to its destination.
NOTES: This hook only works on `ai` type entities.

OnReloaded.DESCRIPTION: Called when the entity is reloaded by the lua auto-refresh system, i.e. when the developer edits the lua file for the entity while the game is running.

OnRemove.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity is about to be removed.

See also [Entity:CallOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:CallOnRemove), which can even be used on engine (non-Lua) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fullUpdate
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Whether the removal is happening due to a full update clientside.

The entity may or **may not** be recreated immediately after, depending on whether it is in the local player's [PVS](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community"). (See [Entity:IsDormant](/gmod/Entity:IsDormant))

OnRestore.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity is reloaded from a Source Engine save (not the Sandbox saves or dupes) or on a changelevel (for example Half-Life 2 campaign level transitions).

For the [duplicator](/gmod/duplicator) callbacks, see [ENTITY:OnDuplicated](/gmod/ENTITY:OnDuplicated).

OnStateChange.DESCRIPTION: Called by the engine when NPC's state changes.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type SENTs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: oldState
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The old state. See [NPC_STATE](/gmod/Enums/NPC_STATE).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: newState
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new state. See [NPC_STATE](/gmod/Enums/NPC_STATE).

OnTakeDamage.DESCRIPTION: Called when the entity is taking damage.
NOTES: This hook is only called for `ai`, `nextbot` and `anim` type entities.
WARNINGS: Calling [Entity:TakeDamage](/gmod/Entity:TakeDamage), [Entity:TakeDamageInfo](/gmod/Entity:TakeDamageInfo), [Entity:DispatchTraceAttack](/gmod/Entity:DispatchTraceAttack), or [Player:TraceHullAttack](/gmod/Player:TraceHullAttack) (if the entity is hit) in this hook on the victim entity can cause infinite loops since the hook will be called again. Make sure to setup recursion safeguards like the example below.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage to be applied to the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: How much damage the entity took. Basically `> 0` means took damage, `0` means did not take damage.

OnTaskComplete.DESCRIPTION:
Called from the engine when TaskComplete is called.
This allows us to move onto the next task - even when TaskComplete was called from an engine side task.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

OnTaskFailed.DESCRIPTION: Called when a task this NPC was running has failed for whatever reason.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: failCode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The fail code for the task. It will be a [FAIL_ enum](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/0d8dceea4310fde5706b3ce1c70609d72a38efdf/sp/src/game/server/ai_task.h#L26) or a generated code for a custom string. (second argument)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: failReason
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, a custom reason for the failure.

OnTraceAttack.DESCRIPTION:
Called when a trace attack is done against the entity, allowing override of the damage being dealt by altering the [CTakeDamageInfo](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo).

This is called before [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage).
NOTES: This hook is only called for `ai`, `anim` (as of version `2026.07.03`) and `nextbot` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: info
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage info

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dir
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The direction the damage goes in

ARGUMENTS.NAME: trace
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult) of the attack, containing the hitgroup.

OverrideMove.DESCRIPTION: Called to completely override NPC movement. This can be used for example for flying NPCs.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type SENTs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: interval
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Time interval for the movement, in seconds. Usually time since last movement.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return `true` to disable the default movement code.

OverrideMoveFacing.DESCRIPTION: Called to completely override the direction NPC will be facing during navigation.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type SENTs.
This hook is called by the default movement hook. Returning `true` inside [ENTITY:OverrideMove](/gmod/ENTITY:OverrideMove) will prevent engine from calling this hook.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: interval
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Time interval for the movement, in seconds. Usually time since last movement.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: AILMG
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Extra data for the movement. A table containing the following data:
* [boolean](/gmod/boolean) hasTraced - The result if a forward probing trace has been done
* [number](/gmod/number) expectedDist = `speed*interval` - The distance expected to move this think
* [number](/gmod/number) flags - [AILMG flags](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/ai_movetypes.h#L113)
* [number](/gmod/number) maxDist = [NPC:GetPathDistanceToGoal](/gmod/NPC:GetPathDistanceToGoal) - The distance maximum distance intended to travel in path length
* [number](/gmod/number) navType - [NAV](/gmod/Enums/NAV)
* [number](/gmod/number) speed - [Entity:GetSequenceGroundSpeed](/gmod/Entity:GetSequenceGroundSpeed) Note these need not always agree with `target`
* [Entity](/gmod/Entity) moveTarget = `m_hGoalEnt` - Target entity as goal. 
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) dir - The step direction, towards `target` 
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) facing - The direction NPC's body will turn during movement. 
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) target = [NPC:GetCurWaypointPos](/gmod/NPC:GetCurWaypointPos) - Current waypoint in world coordinates.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return `true` to disable the default movement facing code.

PassesTriggerFilters.DESCRIPTION: Polls whenever the entity should trigger the brush.
WARNINGS: This hook is broken and will not work without code below

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that is about to trigger.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Should trigger or not.

PhysicsCollide.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity collides with anything via [physics objects](PhysObj). The [move type](Enums/MOVETYPE) and [solid mode](Enums/SOLID) must be `VPHYSICS` for the hook to be called.  
This hook only works for `anim` type entities.

This is different from [ENTITY:Touch](/gmod/ENTITY:Touch).
NOTES: If you want to use this hook on default/engine/non-Lua entities (like `prop_physics`), use [Entity:AddCallback](/gmod/Entity:AddCallback) instead! This page describes a hook for Lua scripted entities

ARGUMENTS.NAME: colData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Information regarding the collision. See [Structures/CollisionData](/gmod/Structures/CollisionData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: collider
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The physics object that collided.

PhysicsSimulate.DESCRIPTION:
Called from the Entity's motion controller to simulate physics.

This will only be called after using [Entity:StartMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StartMotionController) on a [scripted entity](/gmod/Scripted_Entities) of `anim` type.
NOTES: This hook can work on the CLIENT if you call [Entity:StartMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StartMotionController) and use [Entity:AddToMotionController](/gmod/Entity:AddToMotionController) on the physics objects you want to control
WARNINGS: Do not use functions such as [PhysObj:EnableCollisions](/gmod/PhysObj:EnableCollisions) or [PhysObj:EnableGravity](/gmod/PhysObj:EnableGravity) in this hook as they're very likely to crash your game. You may want to use [ENTITY:PhysicsUpdate](/gmod/ENTITY:PhysicsUpdate) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: phys
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The physics object of the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: deltaTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Time since the last call.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Angular force. The 3rd argument must be above SIM_NOTHING.
Linear force. The 3rd argument must be above SIM_NOTHING.
One of the [SIM](/gmod/Enums/SIM).

PhysicsUpdate.DESCRIPTION:
Called whenever a physics object of this entity is updated.

This hook won't be called if the Entity's [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) goes asleep, or doesn't exist.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: phys
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The physics object of the entity.

PostEntityCopy.DESCRIPTION:
Called after the duplicator finished copying the entity, after [ENTITY:PreEntityCopy](/gmod/ENTITY:PreEntityCopy).

Use [ENTITY:OnEntityCopyTableFinish](/gmod/ENTITY:OnEntityCopyTableFinish) to modify the dupe table for this entity.

See also [ENTITY:PostEntityPaste](/gmod/ENTITY:PostEntityPaste) for the restore hook.

PostEntityPaste.DESCRIPTION:
Called after the [duplicator](/gmod/duplicator) pastes the entity, after the bone/entity modifiers have been applied to the entity.

This hook is called after [ENTITY:OnDuplicated](/gmod/ENTITY:OnDuplicated). See also [ENTITY:PreEntityCopy](/gmod/ENTITY:PreEntityCopy).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player who pasted the entity.
WARNINGS: This may not be a valid player in some circumstances. For example, when a save is loaded from the main menu, this hook will be called before the player is spawned. This argument will be a NULL entity in that case.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity itself. Same as `self` within the function context.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: createdEntities
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: All entities that are within the placed dupe.
NOTES: The keys of each value in this table are the original entity indexes when the duplication was created. This can be utilized to restore entity references that don't get saved in duplications.

PreEntityCopy.DESCRIPTION:
Called before the duplicator copies the entity.

If you are looking for a way to make the duplicator spawn another entity when duplicated. (For example, you duplicate a `prop_physics`, but you want the duplicator to spawn `prop_physics_my`), you should add `prop_physics.ClassOverride = "prop_physics_my"`. The duplication table should be also stored on that `prop_physics`, not on `prop_physics_my`.

See also [ENTITY:PostEntityCopy](/gmod/ENTITY:PostEntityCopy).

RenderOverride.DESCRIPTION:
Called instead of the engine drawing function of the entity. This hook works on any entity (scripted or not) it is applied on.

This does not work on "physgun_beam", use [GM:DrawPhysgunBeam](/gmod/GM:DrawPhysgunBeam) instead.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Drawing a viewmodel in this function will cause [GM:PreDrawViewModel](/gmod/GM:PreDrawViewModel), [WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel](/gmod/WEAPON:PreDrawViewModel), [WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn](/gmod/WEAPON:ViewModelDrawn), [GM:PostDrawViewModel](/gmod/GM:PostDrawViewModel), and [WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel](/gmod/WEAPON:PostDrawViewModel) to be called twice.
This is called before PrePlayerDraw for players. If this function exists at all on a player, their worldmodel will always be rendered regardless of PrePlayerDraw's return.

WARNINGS: Defining or clearing this function in the entity table will not do anything, you must define this method in the entity itself

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [STUDIO_](/gmod/Enums/STUDIO) flags for this render operation.

ResolveCustomFlyCollision.DESCRIPTION:
Called during a non-VPhysics collision event for flying entities. 

This is best used to make projectiles bounce off from surfaces in their own way. For this to be triggered, this entity must be the one that's colliding, have some velocity, [Entity:GetMoveType](/gmod/Entity:GetMoveType) must be either [MOVETYPE_FLY](/gmod/Enums/MOVETYPE#MOVETYPE_FLY) or [MOVETYPE_FLYGRAVITY](/gmod/Enums/MOVETYPE#MOVETYPE_FLYGRAVITY), and [Entity:GetMoveCollide](/gmod/Entity:GetMoveCollide) must be [MOVECOLLIDE_FLY_CUSTOM](/gmod/Enums/MOVECOLLIDE#MOVECOLLIDE_FLY_CUSTOM).
NOTES: This works only on `anim` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: traceResult
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult) where the collision occured.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The calculated velocity after calculations such as bounciness, elasticity, ground sliding etc...

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return `true` to prevent default action.

RunAI.DESCRIPTION: Called from the engine every [m_flNextDecisionTime](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/ai_basenpc.cpp#L3943C10-L3943C30) in seconds. This interval changes depending on NPC's [Efficiency](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/ai_basenpc.cpp#L3093). Returning `true` inside this hook will allow [CAI_BaseNPC::MaintainSchedule](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/server/ai_basenpc_schedule.cpp#L562) to also be called.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` to run engine schedules

RunEngineTask.DESCRIPTION: Called when an engine task is ran on the entity.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: taskID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The task ID, see [ai_task.h](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/server/ai_task.h#L89-L502)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: taskData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The task data.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true to prevent default action

RunTask.DESCRIPTION:
Called every think on running task.
The actual task function should tell us when the task is finished.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: task
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The task to run

ScheduleFinished.DESCRIPTION: Called whenever a Lua schedule is finished or [ENTITY:StartEngineSchedule](/gmod/ENTITY:StartEngineSchedule) is called. Clears out schedule and task data stored within NPC's table.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

SelectSchedule.DESCRIPTION: Set the schedule we should be playing right now. Allows the NPC to start either a Lua schedule or an engine schedule. Despite sharing the same name as `CAI_BaseNPC::SelectSchedule()`, this isn't hooked to that function; this is called by Lua's [ENTITY:RunAI](/gmod/ENTITY:RunAI), doesn't return an engine function, returning an engine function doesn't help and doesn't make the NPC start an engine schedule. To alter initial engine schedule, it is recommended to use [ENTITY:TranslateSchedule](/gmod/ENTITY:TranslateSchedule).
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

SetAutomaticFrameAdvance.DESCRIPTION:
Toggles automatic frame advancing for animated sequences on an entity.

This has the same effect as setting the ``ENT.AutomaticFrameAdvance`` property. (See [Structures/ENT](/gmod/Structures/ENT))

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to set automatic frame advancing.

SetTask.DESCRIPTION: Sets the current task, to be used in a Lua schedule.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: task
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The task to set.

SetupDataTables.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity should set up its [Data Tables](/gmod/Networking_Entities).

This is a much better option than using Set/Get Networked Values.

This hook is called after [GM:OnEntityCreated](/gmod/GM:OnEntityCreated) and [GM:NetworkEntityCreated](/gmod/GM:NetworkEntityCreated).

SpawnFunction.DESCRIPTION:
This is the spawn function. It's called when a player spawns the entity from the spawnmenu.

If you want to make your SENT spawnable you need this function to properly create the entity.
WARNINGS: Unlike other ENTITY functions, the "self" parameter of this function is not an entity but rather the table used to generate the SENT. This table is equivalent to [scripted_ents.GetStored](/gmod/scripted_ents.GetStored)("ent_name").

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player that is spawning this SENT

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tr
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult) from player eyes to their aim position

ARGUMENTS.NAME: className
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of your entity

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created scripted entity.

StartEngineSchedule.DESCRIPTION: Called by the engine only whenever [NPC:SetSchedule](/gmod/NPC:SetSchedule) is called.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scheduleID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Schedule ID to start. See [SCHED](/gmod/Enums/SCHED)

StartEngineTask.DESCRIPTION: Called when an engine task has been started on the entity.
NOTES: This hook only exists for `ai` type [SENTs](Scripted_Entities).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: taskID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Task ID to start, see [ai_task.h](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/server/ai_task.h#L89-L502)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: TaskData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Task data

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true to stop default action

StartSchedule.DESCRIPTION:
Starts a schedule previously created by [ai_schedule.New](/gmod/ai_schedule.New).

Not to be confused with [ENTITY:StartEngineSchedule](/gmod/ENTITY:StartEngineSchedule) or [NPC:SetSchedule](/gmod/NPC:SetSchedule) which start an Engine-based schedule.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sched
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Schedule to start.

StartTask.DESCRIPTION: Called once when a LUA schedule has started a task.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: task
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The task to start, created by [ai_task.New](/gmod/ai_task.New).

StartTouch.DESCRIPTION:
Called when the entity starts touching another entity.

See [ENTITY:Touch](/gmod/ENTITY:Touch) and [ENTITY:EndTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:EndTouch) for related hooks.
WARNINGS: This only works for **brush** entities and for entities that have [Entity:SetTrigger](/gmod/Entity:SetTrigger) set to true.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that we started touching for the first time.

StoreOutput.DESCRIPTION:
Used to store an output so it can be triggered with [ENTITY:TriggerOutput](/gmod/ENTITY:TriggerOutput).
Outputs compiled into a map are passed to entities as key/value pairs through [ENTITY:KeyValue](/gmod/ENTITY:KeyValue).

TriggerOutput will do nothing if this function has not been called first.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of output to store

ARGUMENTS.NAME: info
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Output info

TaskFinished.DESCRIPTION:
