BLEND_ZERO.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ZERO.DESCRIPTION:
The Multiplier will be `r=0`, `g=0`, `b=0`, `a=0`

			This is useful for removing the Source or Destination from the final pixel color.

BLEND_ONE.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ONE.DESCRIPTION:
The Multiplier will be `r=1`, `g=1`, `b=1`, `a=1`

			This is useful for keeping the Source or Destination as their starting values.

BLEND_DST_COLOR.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_DST_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: The Multiplier will be the same as the Destination color and alpha.

BLEND_ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR.DESCRIPTION:
Each color and alpha channel value of the Destination is subtracted from `1`.

			**Example:**  
			If your Destination channels are: `r=1`, `g=0.25`, `b=0.1`, `a=1`  
			They will be modified by: `r=1-1`, `g=1-0.25`, `b=1-0.1`, `a=1-1`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0`, `g=0.75`, `b=0.9`, `a=0`

BLEND_SRC_ALPHA.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_SRC_ALPHA.DESCRIPTION:
All color and alpha channels will be the same as the Source alpha value.  

			**Example:**  
			If your Source channels are: `r=0.1`, `g=0`, `b=1`, `a=0.5`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0.5`, `g=0.5`, `b=0.5`, `a=0.5`

BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA.DESCRIPTION:
All color and alpha channels will be set to the Source alpha value subtracted from `1`.

			**Example:**  
			If your Source channels are: `r=0`, `g=0.23`, `b=1`, `a=0.6`  
			The alpha channel will be modified by `a=1-0.6`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0.4`, `g=0.4`, `b=0.4`, `a=0.4`

BLEND_DST_ALPHA.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_DST_ALPHA.DESCRIPTION:
All color and alpha channels will be set to the the Destination alpha value.

			**Example:**  
			If your Destination channels are: `r=0.1`, `g=0`, `b=1`, `a=0.5`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0.5`, `g=0.5`, `b=0.5`, `a=0.5`

BLEND_ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA.DESCRIPTION:
All color and alpha channels will be set to the Destination alpha value subtracted from `1`.

			**Example:**  
			If your Destination channels are: `r=0`, `g=0.23`, `b=1`, `a=0.6`  
			The alpha channel will be modified by `a=1-0.6`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0.4`, `g=0.4`, `b=0.4`, `a=0.4`

BLEND_SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE.DESCRIPTION:
First, the Source alpha is compared against the Destination alpha value subtracted from `1` and the smaller of the two is kept.

			Then, the Source color channels are multiplied by the value from the first step.

			The Source alpha channel is multiplied by `1`.

			**Example:**  
			If your Source channels are: `r=1`, `g=0.25`, `b=0.1`, `a=0.6`  
			and your Destination channels are: `r=0`, `g=1`, `b=0.5`, `a=0.75`

			The Destination alpha value subtracted from `1` is calculated: `1-0.75` = `0.25`  
			The Source alpha `0.6` is compared to the subtracted Destination alpha `0.25` and the smaller of the two is kept (`0.25`)

			The color channels of the Source are multiplied by the smaller value: `r=1*0.25`, `g=0.25*0.25`, `b=0.1*0.25`

			The final Multiplier value will be `r=0.25`, `g=0.0625`, `b=0.025`, `a=0.6`

BLEND_SRC_COLOR.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_SRC_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: The Multiplier will be the same as the Source color and alpha.

BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to determine what the Source and Destination color and alpha channel values for a given pixel will be multiplied by before they are sent to the [Blend Function](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) to calculate the pixel's final color during draw operations.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR.DESCRIPTION:
Each color and alpha channel value of the Source is subtracted from `1`.

			**Example:**  
			If your Source channels are: `r=1`, `g=0.25`, `b=0.1`, `a=1`  
			They will be modified by: `r=1-1`, `g=1-0.25`, `b=1-0.1`, `a=1-1`  
			The final Multiplier value will be: `r=0`, `g=0.75`, `b=0.9`, `a=0`

BLENDFUNC_ADD.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to combine the Source and Destination color and alpha into a final pixel color after they have been multiplied by their corresponding [Blend Multiplier](/gmod/Enums/BLEND).

All results will be clamped in the range `(0-1)` and will produce final pixel channel values in the range `(0-255)`.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLENDFUNC_ADD.DESCRIPTION:
**Source + Destination**  
			Adds each channel of the Source with the same channel of the Destination.

			**Example:**  
			Using the Source channels: `r=0.0`, `g=0.25`, `b=0.1`, `a=0.9`  
			With Destination channels: `r=0.25`, `g=0.25`, `b=1.0`, `a=0.0`  
			The final pixel channels are: `r=0.25`, `g=0.5`, `b=1.0`, `a=0.9`

BLENDFUNC_SUBTRACT.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to combine the Source and Destination color and alpha into a final pixel color after they have been multiplied by their corresponding [Blend Multiplier](/gmod/Enums/BLEND).

All results will be clamped in the range `(0-1)` and will produce final pixel channel values in the range `(0-255)`.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLENDFUNC_SUBTRACT.DESCRIPTION:
**Source - Destination**  
			Subtracts each channel of the Destination from the same channel of the Source.

			**Example:**  
			Using the Source channels: `r=0.0`, `g=0.25`, `b=1.0`, `a=0.9`  
			With Destination channels: `r=0.25`, `g=0.1`, `b=0.4`, `a=0.0`  
			The final pixel channels are: `r=0.0`, `g=0.0`, `b=0.6`, `a=0.9`

BLENDFUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to combine the Source and Destination color and alpha into a final pixel color after they have been multiplied by their corresponding [Blend Multiplier](/gmod/Enums/BLEND).

All results will be clamped in the range `(0-1)` and will produce final pixel channel values in the range `(0-255)`.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLENDFUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT.DESCRIPTION:
**Destination - Source**  
			Subtracts each channel of the Source from the same channel of the Destination.

			**Example:**  
			Using the Source channels: `r=0.0`, `g=0.25`, `b=1.0`, `a=0.9`  
			With Destination channels: `r=0.25`, `g=0.1`, `b=0.4`, `a=0.0`  
			The final pixel channels are: `r=0.0`, `g=0.75`, `b=0.0`, `a=0.0`

BLENDFUNC_MIN.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to combine the Source and Destination color and alpha into a final pixel color after they have been multiplied by their corresponding [Blend Multiplier](/gmod/Enums/BLEND).

All results will be clamped in the range `(0-1)` and will produce final pixel channel values in the range `(0-255)`.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLENDFUNC_MIN.DESCRIPTION:
**Min(Source, Destination**  
			All of the Source channels are added together and compared to all of the Destination channels added together and the smaller of the two is used as the final pixel color.

BLENDFUNC_MAX.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
These enums are used by [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend) to combine the Source and Destination color and alpha into a final pixel color after they have been multiplied by their corresponding [Blend Multiplier](/gmod/Enums/BLEND).

All results will be clamped in the range `(0-1)` and will produce final pixel channel values in the range `(0-255)`.

For an interactive demonstration of how these enums behave, see [Anders Riggelsen's Visual glBlendFunc Tool here](https://www.andersriggelsen.dk/glblendfunc.php)
BLENDFUNC_MAX.DESCRIPTION:
**Max(Source, Destination**  
			All of the Source channels are added together and compared to all of the Destination channels added together and the larger of the two is used as the final pixel color.

CHAN_REPLACE.DESCRIPTION: Used when playing sounds through console commands.

CHAN_ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Channel for items ( Health kits, etc )

CHAN_BODY.DESCRIPTION: Clothing, ragdoll impacts, footsteps, knocking/pounding/punching etc.

CHAN_STREAM.DESCRIPTION: Stream channel from the static or dynamic area

CHAN_STATIC.DESCRIPTION:
A constant/background sound that doesn't require any reaction.
**This channel allows same sounds files to play multiple times without cutting out.**

CHAN_VOICE_BASE.DESCRIPTION:
Channels 8-135 (128 channels) are allocated for player voice chat
**This channel allows same sounds files to play multiple times without cutting out.**

CHAN_USER_BASE.DESCRIPTION: Channels from this and onwards are allocated to game code

CLASS_PLAYER_ALLY_VITAL.DESCRIPTION:
HL2 - **Vital Allies**  
			- `npc_magnusson`  
			- `npc_gman`  
			- `npc_fisherman`  
			- `npc_eli`  
			- `npc_barney`  
			- `npc_kleiner`  
			- `npc_mossman`  
			- `npc_alyx`  
			- `npc_monk`  
			- `npc_dog`  
			- `npc_vortigaunt` at the end of EP2 (controlled by `MakeGameEndAlly` input)

CLASS_CITIZEN_PASSIVE.DESCRIPTION:
HL2 - **Passive / Non-Rebel Citizens**  
			- `npc_citizen` in the beginning of HL2.

CLASS_COMBINE.DESCRIPTION:
HL2 - **Combine Troops**  
			- `npc_combine`  
			- `npc_advisor`  
			- `apc_missile`  
			- `npc_apcdriver`  
			- `npc_turret_floor` ( Hostile )  
			- `npc_rollermine` ( Hostile )  
			- `npc_turret_ground` ( Active )  
			- `npc_turret_ceiling` ( Active )  
			- `npc_strider` ( Active - Not being carried by the gunship )

CLASS_MANHACK.DESCRIPTION:
HL2 - **Manhacks**  
			- `npc_manhack` ( Hostile - Not held by the gravity gun )

CLASS_VORTIGAUNT.DESCRIPTION:
HL2 - **Vortigaunts**  
			- `npc_vortigaunt` before the end of EP2 ( Controlled by `MakeGameEndAlly` input )

CLASS_ALIEN_MILITARY.DESCRIPTION:
HL:S - **Alien Military**  
			- `monster_alien_controller`  
			- `monster_vortigaunt`  
			- `monster_alien_grunt`  
			- `monster_nihilanth`  
			- `monster_snark` if it has an enemy of class  `CLASS_PLAYER` , `CLASS_HUMAN_PASSIVE` or `CLASS_HUMAN_MILITARY`

CLASS_PLAYER_BIOWEAPON.DESCRIPTION:
HL:S - **Player Bioweapons**  
			- `hornet` fired by a player

CLASS_ALIEN_BIOWEAPON.DESCRIPTION:
HL:S - **Enemy Bioweapons**  
			- `hornet` fired by anyone but a player  
			- `monster_snark` with no enemy or an enemy without the class  `CLASS_PLAYER` , `CLASS_HUMAN_PASSIVE` or `CLASS_HUMAN_MILITARY`

CLASS_PORTAL_TURRET.DESCRIPTION:
Portal - **Portal rocket and normal turrets, and the camera**
* `npc_portal_turret_floor`
* `npc_rocket_turret`
* `npc_security_camera`

COLLISION_GROUP_DEBRIS.DESCRIPTION: Collides with nothing but world and static stuff

COLLISION_GROUP_DEBRIS_TRIGGER.DESCRIPTION: Same as debris, but hits triggers. Useful for an item that can be shot, but doesn't collide.

COLLISION_GROUP_INTERACTIVE_DEBRIS.DESCRIPTION: Collides with everything except other interactive debris or debris

COLLISION_GROUP_INTERACTIVE.DESCRIPTION: Collides with everything except interactive debris or debris

COLLISION_GROUP_PLAYER.DESCRIPTION: Used by players, but NOT for movement collision. Does not collide with COLLISION_GROUP_PASSABLE_DOOR and COLLISION_GROUP_PUSHAWAY

COLLISION_GROUP_BREAKABLE_GLASS.DESCRIPTION: NPCs can see straight through an Entity with this applied.

COLLISION_GROUP_VEHICLE.DESCRIPTION: Used by driveable vehicles. Always collides against COLLISION_GROUP_VEHICLE_CLIP

COLLISION_GROUP_PLAYER_MOVEMENT.DESCRIPTION: For HL2, same as Collision_Group_Player, for TF2, this filters out other players and CBaseObjects

COLLISION_GROUP_IN_VEHICLE.DESCRIPTION: Doesn't collide with anything, no traces

COLLISION_GROUP_WEAPON.DESCRIPTION: Doesn't collide with players and vehicles

COLLISION_GROUP_PROJECTILE.DESCRIPTION: Set on projectiles. Does not collide with other projectiles.

COLLISION_GROUP_DOOR_BLOCKER.DESCRIPTION: Blocks entities not permitted to get near moving doors

COLLISION_GROUP_PASSABLE_DOOR.DESCRIPTION: Lets the Player through, nothing else.

COLLISION_GROUP_DISSOLVING.DESCRIPTION: Things that are dissolving are in this group

COLLISION_GROUP_PUSHAWAY.DESCRIPTION: Nonsolid on client and server, pushaway in player code

COLLISION_GROUP_NPC_ACTOR.DESCRIPTION: Used so NPCs in scripts ignore the player

COLLISION_GROUP_NPC_SCRIPTED.DESCRIPTION: Used for NPCs in scripts that should not collide with each other

COLLISION_GROUP_HL2_SPIT.DESCRIPTION: Half-Life 2 exclusive collision group, acts similarly to `COLLISION_GROUP_PROJECTILE` but is also ignored by player movement.

EF_BONEMERGE.DESCRIPTION: Performs bone merge on client side, merging bone positions of child entities ([Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent)) with those of the parent, by bone names. The skeletons should have identical proportions, however it is not a requirement.

EF_BONEMERGE_FASTCULL.DESCRIPTION: For use with EF_BONEMERGE. If this is set, then it places this ents origin at its parent and uses the parent's bbox + the max extents of the aiment. Otherwise, it sets up the parent's bones every frame to figure out where to place the aiment, which is inefficient because it'll setup the parent's bones even if the parent is not in the PVS.

EF_NODRAW.DESCRIPTION: Prevents the entity from drawing and networking.

EF_PARENT_ANIMATES.DESCRIPTION: Always assume that the parent entity is animating.

EF_FOLLOWBONE.DESCRIPTION: Internal flag that is set by [Entity:FollowBone](/gmod/Entity:FollowBone).

EF_NOFLASHLIGHT.DESCRIPTION: GMod-specific. Makes the entity not accept being lit by projected textures, including the player's flashlight.

EFL_KILLME.DESCRIPTION: This entity is marked for death -- This allows the game to actually delete ents at a safe time.
WARNINGS: You should never set this flag manually.

EFL_DORMANT.DESCRIPTION: Entity is dormant, no updates to client

EFL_NOCLIP_ACTIVE.DESCRIPTION: Lets us know when the noclip command is active

EFL_SETTING_UP_BONES.DESCRIPTION: Set while a model is setting up its bones

EFL_KEEP_ON_RECREATE_ENTITIES.DESCRIPTION: This is a special entity that should not be deleted when we respawn entities via [game.CleanUpMap](/gmod/game.CleanUpMap).

EFL_HAS_PLAYER_CHILD.DESCRIPTION: One of the child entities is a player

EFL_DIRTY_SHADOWUPDATE.DESCRIPTION: (Client only) need shadow manager to update the shadow

EFL_NOTIFY.DESCRIPTION: Another entity is watching events on this entity (used by teleport)

EFL_FORCE_CHECK_TRANSMIT.DESCRIPTION: The default behavior in ShouldTransmit is to not send an entity if it doesn't have a model. Certain entities want to be sent anyway because all the drawing logic is in the client DLL. They can set this flag and the engine will transmit them even if they don't have model

EFL_BOT_FROZEN.DESCRIPTION: This is set on bots that are frozen

EFL_DIRTY_ABSTRANSFORM.DESCRIPTION: Some 'dirty' bits with respect to absolute computations. Used internally by the engine when an entity's absolute position needs to be recalculated.

EFL_DIRTY_ABSVELOCITY.DESCRIPTION: Some 'dirty' bits with respect to absolute computations. Used internally by the engine when an entity's absolute velocity needs to be recalculated.

EFL_DIRTY_ABSANGVELOCITY.DESCRIPTION: Some 'dirty' bits with respect to absolute computations. Used internally by the engine when an entity's absolute angular velocity needs to be recalculated.

EFL_DIRTY_SURROUNDING_COLLISION_BOUNDS.DESCRIPTION: Marks the entity as having a 'dirty' surrounding box. Used internally by the engine to recompute the entity's collision bounds.

EFL_DIRTY_SPATIAL_PARTITION.DESCRIPTION: Used internally by the engine when an entity's "spatial partition" needs to be recalculated.

EFL_IN_SKYBOX.DESCRIPTION: This is set if the entity detects that it's in the skybox. This forces it to pass the "in PVS" for transmission

EFL_USE_PARTITION_WHEN_NOT_SOLID.DESCRIPTION: Entities with this flag set show up in the partition even when not solid

EFL_TOUCHING_FLUID.DESCRIPTION: Used to determine if an entity is floating

EFL_IS_BEING_LIFTED_BY_BARNACLE.DESCRIPTION: The entity is currently being lifted by a Barnacle.

EFL_NO_ROTORWASH_PUSH.DESCRIPTION: The entity is not affected by 'rotorwash push'--the wind-push effect caused by helicopters close to the ground in Half-Life 2.

EFL_NO_GAME_PHYSICS_SIMULATION.DESCRIPTION: The entity is currently not simulating any physics.

EFL_CHECK_UNTOUCH.DESCRIPTION: The entity is about to have its untouch callback checked, e.g. when this entity stops touching another entity.

EFL_DONTWALKON.DESCRIPTION: NPCs should not walk on this entity

EFL_NO_MEGAPHYSCANNON_RAGDOLL.DESCRIPTION: Mega physcannon can't ragdoll these guys

EFL_NO_WATER_VELOCITY_CHANGE.DESCRIPTION: Don't adjust this entity's velocity when transitioning into water

EFL_NO_PHYSCANNON_INTERACTION.DESCRIPTION: Physcannon can't pick these up or punt them

EFL_NO_DAMAGE_FORCES.DESCRIPTION: Doesn't accept forces from physics damage

FCVAR_ARCHIVE.DESCRIPTION:
Save the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) value into either client.vdf or server.vdf

Reported as "a" by `cvarlist`, except Lua [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar)s

FCVAR_ARCHIVE_XBOX.DESCRIPTION: Save the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) value into config.vdf on XBox

FCVAR_CHEAT.DESCRIPTION:
Requires `sv_cheats` to be enabled to change the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) or run the command

Reported as "cheat" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_CLIENTCMD_CAN_EXECUTE.DESCRIPTION:
`IVEngineClient::ClientCmd` is allowed to execute this command

Reported as "clientcmd_can_execute" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_CLIENTDLL.DESCRIPTION:
[ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) is defined by the client DLL.

This flag is set automatically

Reported as "cl" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_DEMO.DESCRIPTION:
Force the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) to be recorded by demo recordings.

Reported as "demo" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_DONTRECORD.DESCRIPTION:
Opposite of [FCVAR_DEMO](#FCVAR_DEMO), ensures the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) is not recorded in demos

Reported as "norecord" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_GAMEDLL.DESCRIPTION:
[ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) is defined by the game DLL.

This flag is set automatically

Reported as "sv" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_LUA_CLIENT.DESCRIPTION:
Set automatically on all ConVars and console commands created by the client Lua state.

Reported as "lua_client" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_LUA_SERVER.DESCRIPTION:
Set automatically on all ConVars and console commands created by the server Lua state.

Reported as "lua_server" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_NEVER_AS_STRING.DESCRIPTION:
Tells the engine to never print this variable as a string. This is used for variables which may contain control characters.

Reported as "numeric" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_NOTIFY.DESCRIPTION:
For serverside [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar)s, notifies all players with blue chat text when the value gets changed, also makes the convar appear in [A2S_RULES](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Server_queries#A2S_RULES)

Reported as "nf" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_NOT_CONNECTED.DESCRIPTION: Makes the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) not changeable while connected to a server or in singleplayer

FCVAR_PRINTABLEONLY.DESCRIPTION:
Forces the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) to only have printable characters (No control characters)

Reported as "print" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_PROTECTED.DESCRIPTION:
Makes the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) value hidden from all clients (For example `sv_password`)

Reported as "prot" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_REPLICATED.DESCRIPTION:
For serverside [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar)s, it will enforce its value on all clients. The [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) with the same name must also exist on the client!

Reported as "rep" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_SERVER_CANNOT_QUERY.DESCRIPTION: Prevents the server from querying value of this [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar)

FCVAR_SERVER_CAN_EXECUTE.DESCRIPTION:
The server is allowed to execute this command on clients.

Reported as "server_can_execute" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_SPONLY.DESCRIPTION:
Executing the command or changing the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) is only allowed in singleplayer

Reported as "sp" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_UNLOGGED.DESCRIPTION:
Don't log the [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar) changes to console/log files/users

Reported as "log" by `cvarlist`

FCVAR_UNREGISTERED.DESCRIPTION: If this is set, the convar will become anonymous and won't show up in the `find` results.

FCVAR_USERINFO.DESCRIPTION:
For clientside commands, sends the value to the server

Reported as "user" by `cvarlist`

FSOLID_CUSTOMBOXTEST.DESCRIPTION: Ignore solid type + always call into the entity for swept box tests

FSOLID_NOT_SOLID.DESCRIPTION: The object is currently not solid

FSOLID_TRIGGER.DESCRIPTION: This is something may be collideable but fires touch functions even when it's not collideable (when the FSOLID_NOT_SOLID flag is set)

FSOLID_NOT_STANDABLE.DESCRIPTION: The player can't stand on this

FSOLID_FORCE_WORLD_ALIGNED.DESCRIPTION: Forces the collision representation to be world-aligned even if it's SOLID_BSP or SOLID_VPHYSICS

FSOLID_USE_TRIGGER_BOUNDS.DESCRIPTION: Uses a special trigger bounds separate from the normal OBB

FSOLID_ROOT_PARENT_ALIGNED.DESCRIPTION: Collisions are defined in root parent's local coordinate space

FSOLID_TRIGGER_TOUCH_DEBRIS.DESCRIPTION: This trigger will touch debris objects

FSOLID_MAX_BITS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of bits needed to store the all the flags in a variable/sent over network.

FVPHYSICS_CONSTRAINT_STATIC.DESCRIPTION: Won't receive physics forces from collisions and won't collide with other [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) with the same flag set.

FVPHYSICS_DMG_DISSOLVE.DESCRIPTION: Colliding with entities will cause 1000 damage with DMG_DISSOLVE as the damage type, but only if EFL_NO_DISSOLVE is not set.

FVPHYSICS_DMG_SLICE.DESCRIPTION: Does slice damage, not just blunt damage.

FVPHYSICS_HEAVY_OBJECT.DESCRIPTION: Will deal high physics damage even with a small mass.

FVPHYSICS_MULTIOBJECT_ENTITY.DESCRIPTION: This [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) is part of an entity with multiple [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) , such as a ragdoll or a vehicle , and will be considered during collision damage events.

FVPHYSICS_NO_IMPACT_DMG.DESCRIPTION: Colliding with entities won't cause physics damage.

FVPHYSICS_NO_NPC_IMPACT_DMG.DESCRIPTION: Like FVPHYSICS_NO_IMPACT_DMG, but only checks for NPCs. Usually set on Combine Balls fired by Combine Soldiers.

FVPHYSICS_NO_PLAYER_PICKUP.DESCRIPTION: Doesn't allow the player to pick this [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) with the Gravity Gun or +use pickup.

FVPHYSICS_NO_SELF_COLLISIONS.DESCRIPTION: We won't collide with other [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) associated to the same entity, only used for vehicles and ragdolls held by the Super Gravity Gun.

FVPHYSICS_PART_OF_RAGDOLL.DESCRIPTION: This [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) is part of a ragdoll.

FVPHYSICS_PENETRATING.DESCRIPTION: Set by the physics engine when two [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) are penetrating each other. This is only automatically updated for non-static physics objects.

FVPHYSICS_PLAYER_HELD.DESCRIPTION: Set when the player is holding this [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) with the Physics Gun, Gravity Gun or +use pickup.

FVPHYSICS_WAS_THROWN.DESCRIPTION: This object was thrown by the Gravity Gun , stuns Antlion guards, Hunters, and squashes Antlion grubs.

IMAGE_FORMAT_DEFAULT.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).

IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA8888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA8888.DESCRIPTION: Red, Green, Blue, Alpha, 8 bit per pixel.

IMAGE_FORMAT_ABGR8888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_ABGR8888.DESCRIPTION: Probably legacy format. Alpha, Red, Green, Blue, 8 bit per pixel.

IMAGE_FORMAT_RGB888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_RGB888.DESCRIPTION: Legacy format. Red, Green, Blue, 8 bit per pixel. `D3DFMT_R8G8B8` is invalid for most modern video cards. Thats why `IMAGE_FORMAT_RGB888` and `IMAGE_FORMAT_BGR888` is legacy formats. It have fallback to `IMAGE_FORMAT_BGRX8888`. `X` means «any».

IMAGE_FORMAT_BGR888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_BGR888.DESCRIPTION: Legacy format. Blue, Green, Red order, 8 bit per pixel.

IMAGE_FORMAT_RGB565.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_RGB565.DESCRIPTION: Red, Green, Blue, 5 bit per pixel for Red and Blue channels, 6 bits for Green. Effectively uses less video memory.

IMAGE_FORMAT_ARGB8888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_ARGB8888.DESCRIPTION: `IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA8888` with different byte order. Legacy format.

IMAGE_FORMAT_BGRA8888.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_BGRA8888.DESCRIPTION: `IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA8888` with different byte order. Legacy format.

IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA16161616.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA16161616.DESCRIPTION: RGBA, but 16 bits per pixel. Was meant to be used for "Integer mode" for HDR.

IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA16161616F.BASE_DESCRIPTION: Enumerations used by [GetRenderTargetEx](/gmod/Global.GetRenderTargetEx) to determine the byte format of each pixel in the [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
IMAGE_FORMAT_RGBA16161616F.DESCRIPTION: RGBA, but floating point 16 bits per pixel. Is used for "Float mode" HDR.

NOTES:
These aren't [VMT materials](/gmod/IMaterial)!

[Material types](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Material_Types) are a [holdover from GoldSrc](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Material_surface_properties) and Quake before it. They were previously used to classify textures and entities into categories, defining their physical properties. In practice, this really only changed impact sounds and effects, and player footstep sounds. For example, `func_breakable` (in GoldSrc) used it to select which gibs to spawn when broken. Raw texture files were given these properties by assigning them to a material. These were tracked in the single file `materials.txt`, which contained mappings of material types to texture names. Materials are indexed using a letter—for example `MAT_METAL` was indexed in `materials.txt` with the letter "M". The value of `MAT_METAL` is 77, because the ASCII value for M is 77. Some entities could also be assigned materials directly in their [keyvalues](/gmod/Entity:GetSaveTable) using the same system.

In Source, materials were moved out of the single `materials.txt` file; now every texture has its own associated [material](/gmod/Materials_and_Textures) file, called [VMT](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/VMT) (**V**alve **M**aterial **T**ype). VMTs contain all the information legacy materials used to provide and more, including including shader, transparency, physical properties, animations...

Rather than place the properties directly inside the VMT (which would prevent them from being assigned directly to entities like legacy materials could), [surface properties](/gmod/Structures/SurfacePropertyData) were added, which can be selected in the VMT using the `$surfaceprop` key. Surface properties are what determine impact sounds, buoyancy, friction, and other such properties. These do not use letters as identifiers and instead use [string names](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceIndex). You can view the surface properties Garry's Mod loads by looking in the [`GarrysMod/sourceengine/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt`](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) file.

However, legacy materials still exist in Source. They are called game materials or [material types](/gmod/Entity:GetMaterialType) to separate them from the new material system where confusion between the two is a concern. For example, surface property definitions contain a `gamematerial` parameter; this field assigns a legacy game material to a surface property, which is then assigned to VMTs and entities.

The main thing legacy game materials are used for nowadays are picking impact effects and decals, like in GoldSrc. Otherwise, surface properties and VMTs replace most other functionality.

Some entities could also be assigned materials directly in their [keyvalues](/gmod/Entity:GetSaveTable) using the same system.

In Source, materials were moved out of the single `materials.txt` file; now every texture has its own associated [material](/gmod/Materials_and_Textures) file, called [VMT](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/VMT) (**V**alve **M**aterial **T**ype). VMTs contain all the information legacy materials used to provide and more, including including shader, transparency, physical properties, animations...

Rather than place the properties directly inside the VMT (which would prevent them from being assigned directly to entities like legacy materials could), [surface properties](/gmod/Structures/SurfacePropertyData) were added, which can be selected in the VMT using the `$surfaceprop` key. Surface properties are what determine impact sounds, buoyancy, friction, and other such properties. These do not use letters as identifiers and instead use [string names](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceIndex). You can view the surface properties Garry's Mod loads by looking in the [`GarrysMod/sourceengine/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt`](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) file.

However, legacy materials still exist in Source. They are called game materials or [material types](/gmod/Entity:GetMaterialType) to separate them from the new material system where confusion between the two is a concern. For example, surface property definitions contain a `gamematerial` parameter; this field assigns a legacy game material to a surface property, which is then assigned to VMTs and entities.

The main thing legacy game materials are used for nowadays are picking impact effects and decals, like in GoldSrc. Otherwise, surface properties and VMTs replace most other functionality.

MOUSE_FIRST.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
Enumerations used by:
* [input.IsMouseDown](/gmod/input.IsMouseDown)
* [input.WasMousePressed](/gmod/input.WasMousePressed)
* [input.WasMouseDoublePressed](/gmod/input.WasMouseDoublePressed)

It's also part of the [BUTTON_CODE](/gmod/Enums/BUTTON_CODE).
# Catch mouse wheel
You can catch the mouse wheel's value by:
```
local testVal = 0
hook.Add("InputMouseApply", "testMouseWheel", function(cmd, x, y, ang)
    testVal = testVal + cmd:GetMouseWheel() * 2 --any scale number you want to use
    print(testVal)
end)
```

MOVECOLLIDE_FLY_BOUNCE.DESCRIPTION: Entity bounces, reflects, based on elasticity of surface and object - applies friction (adjust velocity)

MOVECOLLIDE_FLY_CUSTOM.DESCRIPTION: [ENTITY:ResolveCustomFlyCollision](/gmod/ENTITY:ResolveCustomFlyCollision) will modify the velocity however it likes

MOVECOLLIDE_FLY_SLIDE.DESCRIPTION: Entity slides along surfaces (no bounce) - applies friciton (adjusts velocity)

MOVETYPE_ISOMETRIC.DESCRIPTION: For players, in TF2 commander view, etc

MOVETYPE_WALK.DESCRIPTION: Player only, moving on the ground

MOVETYPE_PUSH.DESCRIPTION:
Doesn't collide with the world, but does push and crush entities.  
	This is what is used by the engine for elevators, trains, doors, moving water, etc.

	In order to work properly, the entity needs to have specific Save Values/Internal Variables set which tell it how long it should be moving for.
	
	**Note:** This same process can be done for both position and angle.

	1. You'll need to [Get an existing Save Value](/gmod/Entity:GetInternalVariable) called `ltime`  
	2. Calculate how long (in seconds) the entity will be moving before it reaches its destination.  
	As a simple example, this can be done via `duration = distance / speed`  
	3. [Set the Save Value](/gmod/Entity:SetSaveValue) for `m_flMoveDoneTime` to the value you retrieved for `ltime` plus the duration calculated in step 2.  
	Put more simply: `m_flMoveDoneTime = ltime + duration`  
	4. Set the entity's velocity to move it to the destination at the speed used in step 2.

	Once the duration of the move has elapsed, the entity will stop moving.  If you have done your calculations correctly, it should stop exactly at the desired destination.
NOTES: MOVETYPE_PUSH entities only move during [Entity:Think](/gmod/Entity:Think) so if you want smooth movement, you need to set [Entity:NextThink](/gmod/Entity:NextThink) to [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime), which instructs the entity to execute [Entity:Think](/gmod/Entity:Think) as quickly as possible.

MOVETYPE_LADDER.DESCRIPTION: For players, when moving on a ladder

MOVETYPE_OBSERVER.DESCRIPTION: Spectator movetype. DO **NOT** use this to make player spectate

MOVETYPE_CUSTOM.DESCRIPTION: Custom movetype, can be applied to the player to prevent the default movement code from running, while still calling the related hooks

RENDERGROUP_STATIC_HUGE.DESCRIPTION: Huge static prop, possibly leftover from goldsrc

RENDERGROUP_OPAQUE_HUGE.DESCRIPTION: Huge opaque entity, possibly leftover from goldsrc

RENDERGROUP_OPAQUE.DESCRIPTION:
For non transparent/solid entities.


For scripted entities, this will have [ENTITY:Draw](/gmod/ENTITY:Draw) called

RENDERGROUP_TRANSLUCENT.DESCRIPTION:
For translucent/transparent entities


For scripted entities, this will have [ENTITY:DrawTranslucent](/gmod/ENTITY:DrawTranslucent) called

RENDERGROUP_BOTH.DESCRIPTION:
For both translucent/transparent and opaque/solid anim entities


For scripted entities, this will have both, [ENTITY:Draw](/gmod/ENTITY:Draw) and [ENTITY:DrawTranslucent](/gmod/ENTITY:DrawTranslucent) called

RENDERMODE_NORMAL.DESCRIPTION: Default render mode. Transparently has no effect.

RENDERMODE_TRANSCOLOR.DESCRIPTION:
Supports transparency.

Use this to make alpha of [Color](/gmod/Global.Color) work for your entity. For players, it must be set for their active weapon aswell.

RENDERMODE_GLOW.DESCRIPTION:
Intended for glowing sprites. Allows transparency, and forces the sprite or model to be rendered unlit.

The size of a sprite rendered with Glow is consistent with the screen size (unlike the alternative World Space Glow), making it appear larger at a distance, in comparison to the world.

The GlowProxySize keyvalue affects this Render Mode on sprites.

RENDERMODE_TRANSALPHA.DESCRIPTION: Enables Alphatesting. Legacy port from Goldsource. Obsolete in Source due to Alphatesting being handled in materials. Does not allow transparency.

RENDERMODE_TRANSADD.DESCRIPTION: Add the material's color values to the existing image, instead of performing a multiplication. Sprites will appear through world geometry and the sprite/model will always brighten the world. Allows transparency.

RENDERMODE_ENVIROMENTAL.DESCRIPTION: Causes the material to be not be drawn at all, similarly to Don't Render.

RENDERMODE_TRANSADDFRAMEBLEND.DESCRIPTION: Functions like Additive, but also blends between animation frames. Requires the material to have a functioning animating texture. Allows transparency.

RENDERMODE_TRANSALPHADD.DESCRIPTION: Functions similarly to Additive, except that the alpha channel controls the opacity of the sprite. An example of use is for dark sprites, with an example material being sprites/strider_blackball.vmt.

RENDERMODE_WORLDGLOW.DESCRIPTION:
Functions similarly to Glow, with the exception that the size of the sprite is relative to the world rather than the screen.

The GlowProxySize keyvalue affects this Render Mode on sprites.

RENDERMODE_NONE.DESCRIPTION:
The entity is still being drawn and networked albeit invisible, therefore not making this Render Mode ideal for performance reasons.

To completely avoid drawing and networking an entity, see EF_NODRAW.

RT_SIZE_NO_CHANGE.DESCRIPTION: Only allowed for render targets that don't want a depth buffer (because if they have a depth buffer, the render target must be less than or equal to the size of the framebuffer).

RT_SIZE_DEFAULT.DESCRIPTION: Don't play with the specified width and height other than making sure it fits in the framebuffer.

RT_SIZE_PICMIP.DESCRIPTION: Apply picmip to the render target's width and height.

RT_SIZE_FULL_FRAME_BUFFER.DESCRIPTION: Same size as frame buffer, or next lower power of 2 if we can't do that.

RT_SIZE_OFFSCREEN.DESCRIPTION: Target of specified size, don't mess with dimensions

RT_SIZE_FULL_FRAME_BUFFER_ROUNDED_UP.DESCRIPTION: Same size as the frame buffer, rounded up if necessary for systems that can't do non-power of two textures.

RT_SIZE_REPLAY_SCREENSHOT.DESCRIPTION: Rounded down to power of 2, essentially

RT_SIZE_LITERAL.DESCRIPTION: Use the size passed in. Don't clamp it to the frame buffer size. Really.

RT_SIZE_LITERAL_PICMIP.DESCRIPTION: Use the size passed in, don't clamp to the frame buffer size, but do apply picmip restrictions.

SCREENFADE.IN.DESCRIPTION: Instant fade in, slowly fade out (based on fade time given) after the hold time has passed

SCREENFADE.OUT.DESCRIPTION: Slowly fade in (based on fade time given), hold time passes, instantly disappear

SCREENFADE.MODULATE.DESCRIPTION: Instead of blending multiple active screen fades, modulate them. (TODO: What does this mean?) Internally this flag switches what material will be used to render the screen fade. Practically it forces the color to black.

SCREENFADE.STAYOUT.DESCRIPTION: Never disappear. Does nothing by itself, as if no flags were given.

SCREENFADE.PURGE.DESCRIPTION:
Used to purge all currently active screen fade effects, meant to be used in conjunction with flags above as a "priority effect".

Does nothing by itself, acts as if no flags were given

* SF_CITIZEN_* spawnflags represent spawnflags only usable on [npc_citizen](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Npc_citizen).
* SF_NPC_* - Usable on all NPCs
* SF_PHYSBOX_* - Usable on [func_physbox](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Func_physbox)
* SF_PHYSPROP_* - Usable on [prop_physics](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Prop_physics) entities
* SF_WEAPON_* - Usable on [Weapons](/gmod/Weapon)

NOTES: This is not a full list of available spawnflags, there are **a lot** more, each unique to each entity, you can find out more on the [Valve Developer Community](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Main_Page) website for the entities in question.

SND_CHANGE_VOL.DESCRIPTION: Change sound volume. If the sound is already being emitted by the entity, its volume will be changed, instead of playing another sound.

SND_CHANGE_PITCH.DESCRIPTION: Change sound pitch. If the sound is already being emitted by the entity, its pitch will be changed, instead of playing another sound.

SND_STOP.DESCRIPTION: Stop the sound. Used internally for [Entity:StopSound](/gmod/Entity:StopSound).

SND_SPAWNING.DESCRIPTION: We're spawning, used in some cases for ambients. Not sent over net, only a param between dll and server.

SND_STOP_LOOPING.DESCRIPTION: Stop all looping sounds on the entity.

SND_SHOULDPAUSE.DESCRIPTION: This sound should be paused if the game is paused.

SND_IGNORE_PHONEMES.DESCRIPTION: If the sound has any associated phoneme (character lip-sync) data, ignore it.

SND_IGNORE_NAME.DESCRIPTION: Used to change all sounds (e.g. with SND_CHANGE_VOL) emitted by an entity, regardless of scriptname.

SOLID_OBB.DESCRIPTION: Uses the entity's object-aligned bounding box for collisions.

SOLID_OBB_YAW.DESCRIPTION: Same as SOLID_OBB but restricts orientation to the Z-axis.
NOTES: Seems to be broken.

SOLID_CUSTOM.DESCRIPTION: Always call the entity's `ICollideable::TestCollision` method for traces regardless of the presence of `FSOLID_CUSTOMRAYTEST` or `FSOLID_CUSTOMBOXTEST`. This will only be called back to Lua as [ENTITY:TestCollision](/gmod/ENTITY:TestCollision) for `"anim"` type SENTs.

SOUND_CONTEXT_ALLIES_ONLY.DESCRIPTION: Only player allies can hear this sound.

STENCIL_NEVER.BASE_DESCRIPTION:
Enumerations for use with [render.SetStencilCompareFunction](/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction).

The comparison is between the reference value set by [render.SetStencilReferenceValue](/gmod/render.SetStencilReferenceValue), and the value of each pixel in the stencil buffer.

These enumerations are mirrors of [STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION](/gmod/Enums/STENCILCOMPARISONFUNCTION).

Also see this corresponding MSDN entry: https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ff476101%28v=vs.85%29.aspx.

Add.DESCRIPTION:
Adds the values of the argument angle to the orignal angle. 

This functions the same as angle1 + angle2 without creating a new angle object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to add.

Div.DESCRIPTION: Divides all values of the original angle by a scalar. This functions the same as angle1 / num without creating a new angle object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scalar
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The number to divide by.

Forward.DESCRIPTION: Returns a normal vector facing in the direction that the angle points.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The forward direction of the angle

IsEqualTol.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the angle is equal to another angle with the given tolerance.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: compare
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to compare to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tolerance
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The tolerance range for each component.

RETURNS.NAME: eq
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Are each of the the angle components equal or not within given tolerance.

IsZero.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the pitch, yaw and roll are 0 or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the pitch, yaw and roll are 0 or not.

Mul.DESCRIPTION: Multiplies a scalar to all the values of the orignal angle. This functions the same as num * angle without creating a new angle object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scalar
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The number to multiply.

Normalize.DESCRIPTION: Normalizes the angles by applying a modulo with 360 to pitch, yaw and roll.

Random.DESCRIPTION: Randomizes each element of this Angle object.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum value for each component.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum value for each component.

Right.DESCRIPTION: Returns a normal vector facing in the direction that points right relative to the angle's direction.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The right direction of the angle

RotateAroundAxis.DESCRIPTION: Rotates the angle around the specified axis by the specified degrees.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: axis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The axis to rotate around as a normalized unit vector. When argument is not a unit vector, you will experience numerical offset errors in the rotated angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rotation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The degrees to rotate around the specified axis.

Set.DESCRIPTION: Copies pitch, yaw and roll from the second angle to the first.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: originalAngle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to copy the values from.

SetUnpacked.DESCRIPTION: Sets the p, y, and r of the angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: p
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pitch component of the Angle

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The yaw component of the Angle

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The roll component of the Angle

SnapTo.DESCRIPTION: Snaps the angle to nearest interval of degrees.
NOTES: This will modify the original angle too!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: axis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The component/axis to snap. Can be either `p`/`pitch`, `y`/`yaw` or `r`/`roll`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The target angle snap interval

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The snapped angle.

Sub.DESCRIPTION: Subtracts the values of the argument angle to the orignal angle. This functions the same as angle1 - angle2 without creating a new angle object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to subtract.

ToTable.DESCRIPTION: Returns the angle as a table with three elements.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The table with elements 1 = p, 2 = y, 3 = r.

Unpack.DESCRIPTION: Returns the pitch, yaw, and roll components of the angle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: p, pitch, x, or Angle[1].
y, yaw, or Angle[2].
r, roll, r, or Angle[3].

Up.DESCRIPTION: Returns a normal vector facing in the direction that points up relative to the angle's direction.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The up direction of the angle.

Zero.DESCRIPTION:
Sets pitch, yaw and roll to 0.
This function is faster than doing it manually.

Angle.DESCRIPTION:
List of all possible functions to manipulate angles.

		Created by [Angle](/gmod/Global.Angle).

		| Type                | Name                                 | Description                      |
		| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
		| [number](/gmod/number) | `p` or `pitch` or `x` or `1` | The pitch component of the angle. |
		| [number](/gmod/number) | `y` or `yaw` or `2` | The yaw component of the angle. |
		| [number](/gmod/number) | `r` or `roll`  or `z` or `3` | The roll  component of the angle. |

		Metamethod | Second Operand | Description
		---------- | -------------- | -----------
		`__add` | [Angle](/gmod/Angle) | Returns new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with the result of addition.
		`__div` | [number](/gmod/number) | Returns new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with the result of division.
		`__eq` | [any](/gmod/any) | Compares 2 operands, if they both are [Angle](/gmod/Angle), compares each individual component. Doesn't normalize the angles (360 is not equal to 0).
		`__index` | [number](/gmod/number) or [string](/gmod/string) | Gets the component of the [Angle](/gmod/Angle). Returns a [number](/gmod/number).
		`__mul` | [number](/gmod/number) | Returns new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with the result of multiplication.
		`__newindex` | [number](/gmod/number) or [string](/gmod/string) | Sets the component of the [Angle](/gmod/Angle). Accepts [number](/gmod/number) and [string](/gmod/string).
		`__sub` | [Angle](/gmod/Angle) | Returns new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with the result of subtraction.
		`__tostring` | | Returns `p y r`.
		`__unm` | | Returns new [Angle](/gmod/Angle) with the result of negation.

ReadAngle.DESCRIPTION: Reads and returns an angle object from the bitstream.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read angle

ReadBool.DESCRIPTION: Reads 1 bit and returns a bool representing the bit.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: bit

ReadChar.DESCRIPTION: Reads a signed char and returns a number from -127 to 127 representing the ascii value of that char.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: asciiVal

ReadEntity.DESCRIPTION: Reads a short representing an entity index and returns the matching entity handle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: ent

ReadFloat.DESCRIPTION: Reads a 4 byte float from the bitstream and returns it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: float

ReadLong.DESCRIPTION: Reads a 4 byte long from the bitstream and returns it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: int

ReadShort.DESCRIPTION: Reads a 2 byte short from the bitstream and returns it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: short

ReadString.DESCRIPTION: Reads a null terminated string from the bitstream.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: str

ReadVector.DESCRIPTION: Reads a special encoded vector from the bitstream and returns it, this function is not suitable to send normals.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: vec

ReadVectorNormal.DESCRIPTION: Reads a special encoded vector normal from the bitstream and returns it, this function is not suitable to send vectors that represent a position.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: normal

Reset.DESCRIPTION: Rewinds the bitstream so it can be read again.

bf_read.DESCRIPTION: This is the object passed to [usermessage.Hook](/gmod/usermessage.Hook) when a message is received. It contains each value stored in the message in sequential order. You should read values from it in the order you wrote them.
DEPRECATED: You should be using net instead

GetSurfaceProp.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the surface property index of the effect. See [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData) for more details about what they are.

See [CEffectData:SetSurfaceProp](/gmod/CEffectData:SetSurfaceProp) for details about limitations of this function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The surface property index of the effect.

SetAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets the angles of the effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new angles to be set.

SetAttachment.DESCRIPTION: Sets the attachment id of the effect to be created with this effect data.
NOTES: This is internally stored as an integer, but only the first 5 bits will be networked, effectively limiting this function to 0-31 range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachment
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New attachment ID of the effect.

SetColor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the "color" of the effect.

All this does is provide an addition 8 bits of data for the effect to use. What this will actually do will vary from effect to effect, depending on how a specific effect uses this given data, if at all.
NOTES: Internally stored as an integer, but only first 8 bits are networked, effectively limiting this function to 0-255 range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Color represented by a byte.

SetDamageType.DESCRIPTION: Sets the damage type of the effect to be created with this effect data.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Damage type, see [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG).

SetEntIndex.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity of the effect via its index.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity index to be set.

SetEntity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity of the effect to be created with this effect data.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity of the effect, mostly used for parenting.

SetFlags.DESCRIPTION: Sets the flags for the effect. What flags do depends entirely on the effect. See [Default Effects](/gmod/Default%20Effects).
NOTES: Internally stored as an integer, but only first 8 bits are networked, effectively limiting this function to `0-255` range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flags of the effect. Each effect has their own flags.

SetHitBox.DESCRIPTION: Sets the hit box index of the effect. Used by various effects for various purposes.
NOTES: Internally stored as an integer, but only first 11 bits are networked, effectively limiting this function to 0-2047 range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hitBoxIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hit box index of the effect, for example from [Structures/TraceResult#HitBox](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult#HitBox)

SetMagnitude.DESCRIPTION: Sets the magnitude of the effect.
NOTES: Internally stored as a float with 12 bit precision for networking purposes, limited to range of 0-1023.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: magnitude
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The magnitude of the effect.

SetMaterialIndex.DESCRIPTION: Sets the material index of the effect.
NOTES: Internally stored as an integer, but only first 12 bits are networked, effectively limiting this function to 0-4095 range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: materialIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material index of the effect.

SetNormal.DESCRIPTION: Sets the normalized (length=1) direction vector of the effect to be created with this effect data. This **must** be a normalized vector for networking purposes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normalized direction vector of the effect.

SetOrigin.DESCRIPTION: Sets the origin of the effect to be created with this effect data.
NOTES: Limited to world bounds (+-16386 on every axis) and has horrible networking precision. (17 bit float per component)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin of the effect.

SetRadius.DESCRIPTION: Sets the radius of the effect to be created with this effect data.
NOTES: Internally stored as a float, but networked as a 10bit float, and is clamped to 0-1023 range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Radius of the effect.

SetScale.DESCRIPTION: Sets the scale of the effect to be created with this effect data.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Scale of the effect.

SetStart.DESCRIPTION: Sets the start of the effect to be created with this effect data.
NOTES: Limited to world bounds (+-16386 on every axis) and has horrible networking precision. (17 bit float per component)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: start
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start of the effect.

SetSurfaceProp.DESCRIPTION: Sets the surface property index of the effect. See [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData) for more details about what they are.
NOTES: Internally stored as an integer, but only first 8 bits are networked, effectively limiting this function to `-1`-`254` range. (Yes, that's not a mistake, `-1` signifying an invalid value.)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceProperties
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The surface property index of the effect.

Approach.DESCRIPTION:
Moves the [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot) incrementally closer to the provided goal location.

Each time this function is called, the NextBot moves towards the goal position passed as an argument by the amount previously set by [CLuaLocomotion:SetDesiredSpeed](/gmod/CLuaLocomotion:SetDesiredSpeed).

To achieve smooth movement, this function must be called frequently.  
This is commonly accomplished by calling it in the [ENTITY:Think](/gmod/ENTITY:Think) hook.

If unsure then set this to `1`.

There's a limit of 255 hiding spots per area.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position on the nav area
