ConVar.DESCRIPTION:
An object returned by [CreateConVar](/gmod/Global.CreateConVar), [CreateClientConVar](/gmod/Global.CreateClientConVar) (which uses [CreateConVar](/gmod/Global.CreateConVar) internally), and [GetConVar](/gmod/Global.GetConVar).

It represents a console variable. See [this](/gmod/ConVars) page for more information.

AddAllPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Adds all players to the recipient filter.

AddPAS.DESCRIPTION: Adds all players that are in the same [PAS (Potentially Audible Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PAS "PAS - Valve Developer Community") as this position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A position that players may be able to hear, usually the position of an entity the sound is playing played from.

AddPlayer.DESCRIPTION: Adds a player to the recipient filter

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Player
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Player to add to the recipient filter.

AddPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Adds players to the recipient filter from a given table or another recipient filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The filter to add players from. This can also be a sequential table of players. Non player entities or duplicate players will be ignored.

AddPVS.DESCRIPTION: Adds all players that are in the same [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community") as this position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: PVS position that players may be able to see.

AddRecipientsByTeam.DESCRIPTION: Adds all players that are on the given team to the filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: teamid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Team index to add players from.

GetCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the number of valid players in the recipient filter.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of valid players in the recipient filter.

GetPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of all valid players currently in the recipient filter.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all valid players currently in the recipient filter.

RemoveAllPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Removes all players from the recipient filter.

RemoveMismatchedPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Remove players from this recipient filter that are **NOT** present in a given table or recipient filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The filter that contains a list of players to test against. Players **NOT** in the given filter will be removed from this filter.

This can also be a sequential table of players. Non player entities will be ignored.

RemovePAS.DESCRIPTION: Removes all players from the filter that are in [PAS (Potentially Audible Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PAS "PAS - Valve Developer Community") for given position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to test

RemovePlayer.DESCRIPTION: Removes the player from the recipient filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Player
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player that should be in the recipient filter if you call this function.

RemovePlayers.DESCRIPTION: Remove players from this recipient filter that are present in a given table or recipient filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The filter that contains a list of players to remove. This can also be a sequential table of players. Non player entities will be ignored. If a player in the given table/filter is not present in this filter, it is ignored.

RemovePVS.DESCRIPTION: Removes all players that can see this [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community") from the recipient filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position that players may be able to see.

RemoveRecipientsByTeam.DESCRIPTION: Removes all players that are on the given team from the filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: teamid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Team index to remove players from.

RemoveRecipientsNotOnTeam.DESCRIPTION: Removes all players that are not on the given team from the filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: teamid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Team index.

CRecipientFilter.DESCRIPTION: List of all possible functions to manipulate Recipient Filters. Can be created with [RecipientFilter](/gmod/Global.RecipientFilter).

CSEnt.DESCRIPTION:
CSEnt is a client-side only entity which can be created with [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel), [ClientsideRagdoll](/gmod/Global.ClientsideRagdoll) and [ClientsideScene](/gmod/Global.ClientsideScene).

Its base class is [Entity](/gmod/Entity) so it inherits all of the client and shared functions used by [Entity](/gmod/Entity).

ChangePitch.DESCRIPTION:
Adjust the pitch, also known as the speed at which the sound is being played.

Appears to only work while the sound is being played. See also [CSoundPatch:PlayEx](/gmod/CSoundPatch:PlayEx).

This invokes [GM:EntityEmitSound](/gmod/GM:EntityEmitSound).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pitch
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pitch can range from 0-255. Where 100 is the original pitch.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: deltaTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The time to fade from previous to the new pitch.

ChangeVolume.DESCRIPTION:
Adjusts the volume of the sound played.

Appears to only work while the sound is being played. See also [CSoundPatch:PlayEx](/gmod/CSoundPatch:PlayEx).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The volume ranges from 0 to 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: deltaTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Time to fade the volume from previous to new value from.

FadeOut.DESCRIPTION: Fades out the volume of the sound from the current volume to 0 in the given amount of seconds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seconds
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Fade time.

GetDSP.DESCRIPTION: Returns the DSP (Digital Signal Processor) effect ID for the sound.

RETURNS.NAME: dspEffectId
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The numerical ID for the DSP effect currently enabled on the sound.

			For a list of the available IDs and their meaning, see [DSP Presets](/gmod/DSP_Presets).
The current pitch, can range from 0-255.
The current sound level, see [SNDLVL](/gmod/Enums/SNDLVL).

GetSoundName.DESCRIPTION: Returns the sound name of this sound patch. This may be name of a sound script ([sound.Add](/gmod/sound.Add)) or a file path.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The sound name.
The current volume, ranging from 0 to 1.

IsPlaying.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the sound is being played.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is playing or not

Play.DESCRIPTION: Starts to play the sound. This will reset the sound's volume and pitch to their default values. See [CSoundPatch:PlayEx](/gmod/CSoundPatch:PlayEx)

PlayEx.DESCRIPTION: Same as [CSoundPatch:Play](/gmod/CSoundPatch:Play) but with 2 extra arguments allowing to set volume and pitch directly.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The volume ranges from 0 to 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pitch
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pitch can range from 0-255.

SetDSP.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the DSP (Digital Signal Processor) effect for the sound.

Similar to [Player:SetDSP](/gmod/Player:SetDSP) but for individual sounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dspEffectId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The numerical ID for the DSP effect to be enabled on the sound.  
			
			For a list of the available IDs and their meaning, see [DSP Presets](/gmod/DSP_Presets).

SetSoundLevel.DESCRIPTION: Sets the sound level in decibel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: level
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound level in decibel. See [SNDLVL](/gmod/Enums/SNDLVL)

Stop.DESCRIPTION: Stops the sound from being played.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageIncrease
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage to add.

GetAmmoType.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ammo type used by the weapon that inflicted the damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo type ID

GetAttacker.DESCRIPTION: Returns the attacker ( character who originated the attack ), for example a player or an NPC that shot the weapon.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The attacker

GetBaseDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns the initial unmodified by skill level ( [game.GetSkillLevel](/gmod/game.GetSkillLevel) ) damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: baseDamage
damage
Bonus damage

GetDamageCustom.DESCRIPTION: Gets the custom damage type. This is used by Day of Defeat: Source and Team Fortress 2 for extended damage info, but isn't used in Garry's Mod by default.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The custom damage type

GetDamageForce.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a vector representing the damage force.

Can be set with [CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamageForce](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamageForce).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The damage force

GetDamagePosition.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the position where the damage was or is going to be applied to.

Can be set using [CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamagePosition](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamagePosition).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The damage position

GetDamageType.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a bitflag which indicates the damage type(s) of the damage.

Consider using [CTakeDamageInfo:IsDamageType](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:IsDamageType) instead. Value returned by this function can contain multiple damage types.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Damage type(s), a combination of [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG)

GetInflictor.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the inflictor of the damage. This is not necessarily a weapon.

For hitscan weapons this is the weapon.

For projectile weapons this is the projectile.

For a more reliable method of getting the weapon that damaged an entity, use [CTakeDamageInfo:GetWeapon](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetWeapon) or [GetAttacker](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetAttacker) with [GetActiveWeapon](/gmod/Player:GetActiveWeapon).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The inflictor entity.

GetMaxDamage.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the maximum damage. See [CTakeDamageInfo:SetMaxDamage](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetMaxDamage).

This is only set by "multi damage" instances in the engine, and is only checked by the strider NPC when receiving explosive damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum amount of damage in the "multi damage" instance.

GetReportedPosition.DESCRIPTION: Returns the initial, unmodified position where the damage occured.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: position

GetWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the inflicting weapon of the damage event, if there is any.

This is not necessarily a [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon) entity, but it is very likely to be one.

See [CTakeDamageInfo:GetInflictor](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetInflictor) for the actual entity that did the damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The damage-inflicting weapon or [NULL](/gmod/NULL).

IsBulletDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the damage was caused by a bullet.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: isBulletDmg

IsDamageType.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the damageinfo contains the damage type specified.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dmgType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Damage type to test. See [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether this damage contains specified damage type or not

IsExplosionDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the damageinfo contains explosion damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: isExplDamage

IsFallDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the damageinfo contains fall damage.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: isFallDmg

ScaleDamage.DESCRIPTION: Scales the damage by the given value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to scale the damage with.

SetAmmoType.DESCRIPTION: Changes the ammo type used by the weapon that inflicted the damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo type ID

SetAttacker.DESCRIPTION: Sets the attacker ( character who originated the attack ) of the damage, for example a player or an NPC.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be set as the attacker.

SetBaseDamage.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the initial damage, unmodified by the current skill level ([game.GetSkillLevel](/gmod/game.GetSkillLevel)). This is usually set automatically by the game when dealing damage.

This function will not modify the real damage that will be dealt ([CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamage](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamage)).

Use this only if you know what you are doing. Otherwise use [CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamage](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetDamage).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The base damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set the absolute damage to.

SetDamageBonus.DESCRIPTION: Sets the bonus damage. Bonus damage isn't automatically applied, so this will have no outer effect by default.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The extra damage to be added.

SetDamageCustom.DESCRIPTION: Sets the custom damage type. This is used by Day of Defeat: Source and Team Fortress 2 for extended damage info, but isn't used in Garry's Mod by default.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: DamageType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any integer - can be based on your own custom enums.

SetDamageForce.DESCRIPTION: Sets the directional force of the damage.
NOTES:
This function only affects entities using the VPHYSICS movetype. This means players and most NPCs won't receive the force vector you provide as knockback. 

If the entity taking damage is using the WALK or STEP movetypes, the damage force is instead automatically calculated. It will push the entity away from the inflictor's [Entity:WorldSpaceCenter](/gmod/Entity:WorldSpaceCenter), scaling the push by a calculated value involving the total amount of damage and the size of the entity. [Source](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/0565403b153dfcde602f6f58d8f4d13483696a13/src/game/server/baseentity.cpp#L1525)

To disable knockback entirely, see [EFL_NO_DAMAGE_FORCES](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/EFL#EFL_NO_DAMAGE_FORCES) or use the workaround example below.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: force
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to set the force to.

SetDamagePosition.DESCRIPTION: Sets the position of where the damage gets applied to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position where the damage will be applied.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage type, see [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG).

SetInflictor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the inflictor of the damage for example a weapon.

For hitscan/bullet weapons this should the weapon.

For projectile (rocket launchers, grenades, etc) weapons this should be the projectile and [CTakeDamageInfo:SetWeapon](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetWeapon) should be the weapon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: inflictor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new inflictor.

SetMaxDamage.DESCRIPTION: Sets the "maximum damage" for this damage event. See [CTakeDamageInfo:GetMaxDamage](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetMaxDamage) for details.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxDamage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Maximum damage value.

SetReportedPosition.DESCRIPTION: Sets the origin of the damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The location of where the damage is originating

SetWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the damage-inflicting weapon of the damage event.

This should be a [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon) entity, not a projectile. See also [CTakeDamageInfo:SetInflictor](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:SetInflictor).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage-inflicting weapon or [NULL](/gmod/NULL).

SubtractDamage.DESCRIPTION: Subtracts the specified amount from the damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damage
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to subtract.

CTakeDamageInfo.DESCRIPTION:
A class used to store and modify all the data concerning a damage event.
An empty CTakeDamageInfo object can be created with [DamageInfo](/gmod/Global.DamageInfo)

List of hooks that this object is passed to:
* [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage)
* [GM:DoPlayerDeath](/gmod/GM:DoPlayerDeath)
* [GM:EntityTakeDamage](/gmod/GM:EntityTakeDamage)
* [GM:PostEntityTakeDamage](/gmod/GM:PostEntityTakeDamage)
* [GM:OnDamagedByExplosion](/gmod/GM:OnDamagedByExplosion)
* [GM:ScaleNPCDamage](/gmod/GM:ScaleNPCDamage)
* [GM:ScalePlayerDamage](/gmod/GM:ScalePlayerDamage)
* [NEXTBOT:OnInjured](/gmod/NEXTBOT:OnInjured)
* [NEXTBOT:OnKilled](/gmod/NEXTBOT:OnKilled)
* [NEXTBOT:OnOtherKilled](/gmod/NEXTBOT:OnOtherKilled)

List of functions that use this object:
* [util.BlastDamageInfo](/gmod/util.BlastDamageInfo)
* [Entity:TakeDamageInfo](/gmod/Entity:TakeDamageInfo)
* [Entity:TakePhysicsDamage](/gmod/Entity:TakePhysicsDamage)
* [Entity:DispatchTraceAttack](/gmod/Entity:DispatchTraceAttack)

AddKey.DESCRIPTION: Adds a single key to the active buttons bitflag. See also [CUserCmd:SetButtons](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetButtons).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Key to add, see [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN).

ClearButtons.DESCRIPTION: Removes all keys from the command.
NOTES: If you are looking to affect player movement, you may need to use [CUserCmd:ClearMovement](/gmod/CUserCmd:ClearMovement) instead of clearing the buttons.

ClearMovement.DESCRIPTION:
Clears the movement from the command.

See also [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove), [CUserCmd:SetSideMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetSideMove) and  [CUserCmd:SetUpMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetUpMove).

CommandNumber.DESCRIPTION: Returns an increasing number representing the index of the user cmd.
WARNINGS: The value returned is occasionally 0 inside [GM:CreateMove](/gmod/GM:CreateMove) and [GM:StartCommand](/gmod/GM:StartCommand). It is advised to check for a non-zero value if you wish to get the correct number.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The command number

GetButtons.DESCRIPTION: Returns a bitflag indicating which buttons are pressed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Pressed buttons, see [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN)

GetForwardMove.DESCRIPTION: The speed the client wishes to move forward with, negative if the clients wants to move backwards.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The desired speed

GetImpulse.DESCRIPTION: Gets the current impulse from the client, usually 0. [See impulses list](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Impulse) and some [GMod specific impulses](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetImpulse).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The impulse

GetMouseWheel.DESCRIPTION: Returns the scroll delta as whole number.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Scroll delta

GetMouseX.DESCRIPTION: Returns the delta of the angular horizontal mouse movement of the player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: xDelta

GetMouseY.DESCRIPTION: Returns the delta of the angular vertical mouse movement of the player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: yDelta

GetSideMove.DESCRIPTION: The speed the client wishes to move sideways with, positive if it wants to move right, negative if it wants to move left.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: requestSpeed

GetUpMove.DESCRIPTION: The speed the client wishes to move up with, negative if the clients wants to move down.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: requestSpeed

GetViewAngles.DESCRIPTION: Gets the direction the player is looking in.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The direction the player is looking in.

IsForced.DESCRIPTION:
When players are not sending usercommands to the server (often due to lag), their last usercommand will be executed multiple times as a backup. This function returns true if that is happening.

This will never return true clientside.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: isForced

KeyDown.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the specified button(s) is pressed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bitflag representing which button to check, see [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is key down or not

RemoveKey.DESCRIPTION:
Removes a key bit from the current key bitflag.

For movement you will want to use [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove), [CUserCmd:SetUpMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetUpMove) and [CUserCmd:SetSideMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetSideMove).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: button
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bitflag to be removed from the key bitflag, see [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN).

SelectWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Forces the associated player to select a weapon. This is used internally in the default HL2 weapon selection HUD.

This may not work immediately if the current command is in prediction. Use [input.SelectWeapon](/gmod/input.SelectWeapon) to switch the weapon from the client when the next available command can do so.
NOTES: This is the ideal function to use to create a custom weapon selection HUD, as it allows prediction to run properly for [WEAPON:Deploy](/gmod/WEAPON:Deploy) and [GM:PlayerSwitchWeapon](/gmod/GM:PlayerSwitchWeapon)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weapon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The weapon entity to select.

SetButtons.DESCRIPTION: Sets the buttons as a bitflag. See also [CUserCmd:GetButtons](/gmod/CUserCmd:GetButtons).
NOTES: If you are looking to affect player movement, you may need to use [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove) instead of setting the keys.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: buttons
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bitflag representing which buttons are "down", see [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN).

SetForwardMove.DESCRIPTION:
Sets speed the client wishes to move forward with, negative if the clients wants to move backwards.

See also [CUserCmd:ClearMovement](/gmod/CUserCmd:ClearMovement), [CUserCmd:SetSideMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetSideMove) and [CUserCmd:SetUpMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetUpMove).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new speed to request. The client will not be able to move faster than their set walk/sprint speed.

SetImpulse.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the impulse command to be sent to the server.

Here are a few examples of impulse numbers:
- `100` toggles their flashlight
- `101` gives the player all Half-Life 2 weapons with `sv_cheats` set to `1`
- `200` toggles holstering / restoring the current weapon  
  When holstered, the `EF_NODRAW` flag is set on the active weapon.
- `154` toggles noclip

[See full list](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Impulse)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: impulse
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The impulse to send.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The scroll delta.

SetMouseX.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the delta of the angular horizontal mouse movement of the player.

See also [CUserCmd:SetMouseY](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetMouseY).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angular horizontal move delta.

SetMouseY.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the delta of the angular vertical mouse movement of the player.

See also [CUserCmd:SetMouseX](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetMouseX).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angular vertical move delta.

SetSideMove.DESCRIPTION:
Sets speed the client wishes to move sidewards with, positive to move right, negative to move left.

See also [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove) and  [CUserCmd:SetUpMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetUpMove).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new speed to request.

SetUpMove.DESCRIPTION:
Sets speed the client wishes to move upwards with, negative to move down.

See also [CUserCmd:SetSideMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetSideMove) and  [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove).
NOTES: This function does **not** move the client up/down ladders. To force ladder movement, consider [CUserCMD:SetButtons](/gmod/CUserCMD:SetButtons) and use IN_FORWARD from [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new speed to request.

SetViewAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets the direction the client wants to move in.
NOTES: For human players, the pitch (vertical) angle should be clamped to +/- 89° to prevent the player's view from glitching.

For fake clients (those created with [player.CreateNextBot](/gmod/player.CreateNextBot)), this functionally dictates the 'move angles' of the bot. This typically functions separately from the colloquial view angles. This can be utilized by [CUserCmd:SetForwardMove](/gmod/CUserCmd:SetForwardMove) and its related functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewAngle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New view angles.

TickCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns tick count since joining the server.
NOTES: This will always return 0 for bots.

Returns 0 clientside during prediction calls. If you are trying to use CUserCmd:Set*() on the client in a movement or command hook, keep doing so till TickCount returns a non-zero number to maintain prediction.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of ticks passed since joining the server.

CUserCmd.DESCRIPTION:
A class used to store the player inputs, such as mouse movement, view angles, [IN](/gmod/Enums/IN) buttons pressed and analog movement, the data from this class is then transfered to a [CMoveData](/gmod/CMoveData) during actual movement simulation.

Can be modified during [GM:CreateMove](/gmod/GM:CreateMove), [GM:StartCommand](/gmod/GM:StartCommand) and used in read only with [GM:SetupMove](/gmod/GM:SetupMove) and [Player:GetCurrentCommand](/gmod/Player:GetCurrentCommand).

Activate.DESCRIPTION: Activates the entity. This needs to be used on some entities (like constraints) after being spawned.
NOTES:
For some entity types when this function is used after [Entity:SetModelScale](/gmod/Entity:SetModelScale), the physics object will be recreated with the new scale. [Source-sdk-2013](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/server/baseanimating.cpp#L321-L327).

Calling this method after [Entity:SetModelScale](/gmod/Entity:SetModelScale) will recreate a new scaled `SOLID_VPHYSICS` [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) on scripted entities. This can be a problem if you made a properly scaled [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) of another kind (using [Entity:PhysicsInitSphere](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitSphere) for instance) or if you edited the [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)'s properties. This is especially the behavior of the Sandbox spawn menu.

AddCallback.DESCRIPTION:
Add a callback function to a specific event. This is used instead of hooks to avoid calling empty functions unnecessarily.

This also allows you to use certain hooks in engine entities (non-scripted entities).
WARNINGS: This method does not check if the function has already been added to this object before, so if you add the same callback twice, it will be run twice! Make sure to add your callback only once.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hook
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hook name to hook onto. See [Entity Callbacks](/gmod/Entity%20Callbacks)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to call. It's arguments and return values will depend on the hook specified in the first argument.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The callback ID that was just added, which can later be used in [Entity:RemoveCallback](/gmod/Entity:RemoveCallback).

Returns nothing if the passed callback function was invalid or when asking for a non-existent hook.

AddEffects.DESCRIPTION:
Applies an engine effect to an entity.

See also [Entity:IsEffectActive](/gmod/Entity:IsEffectActive) and  [Entity:RemoveEffects](/gmod/Entity:RemoveEffects).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: effect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The effect to apply, see [EF](/gmod/Enums/EF).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Engine flag to add, see [EFL](/gmod/Enums/EFL)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Flag to add, see [FL](/gmod/Enums/FL)

AddGesture.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a gesture animation to the entity and plays it.


See [Entity:AddGestureSequence](/gmod/Entity:AddGestureSequence) and [Entity:AddLayeredSequence](/gmod/Entity:AddLayeredSequence) for functions that takes sequences instead of [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity to play as the gesture. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: autokill
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Automatically remove the gesture when it fully plays ([Entity:GetLayerCycle](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerCycle) reaches 1).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Layer ID of the started gesture, used to manipulate the played gesture by other functions.
NOTES: If a layer has already been allocated for supplied [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT), it will return existing layer ID instead of allocating a new layer.

AddGestureSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a gesture animation to the entity and plays it.


See [Entity:AddGesture](/gmod/Entity:AddGesture) for a function that takes [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).


See also [Entity:AddLayeredSequence](/gmod/Entity:AddLayeredSequence).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID to play as the gesture. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: autokill
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Automatically remove the gesture when it fully plays ([Entity:GetLayerCycle](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerCycle) reaches 1).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Layer ID of the started gesture, used to manipulate the played gesture by other functions.

AddLayeredSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a gesture animation to the entity and plays it.

See [Entity:AddGestureSequence](/gmod/Entity:AddGestureSequence) for a function that doesn't take priority.

See [Entity:AddGesture](/gmod/Entity:AddGesture) for a function that takes [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID to play as the gesture. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Layer ID of created layer

AddSolidFlags.DESCRIPTION: Adds solid flag(s) to the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag(s) to apply, see [FSOLID](/gmod/Enums/FSOLID).

AddSpawnFlags.DESCRIPTION:
Adds onto the current SpawnFlags of an Entity.

SpawnFlags can easily be found on https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/.
NOTES:
See also [Entity:RemoveSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:RemoveSpawnFlags), [Entity:SetSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:SetSpawnFlags)

	Using [SF Enumerations](/gmod/Enums/SF) won't work, if this function is ran clientside due to the enumerations being defined only Serverside. Use the actual SpawnFlag number.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The SpawnFlag to add to the Entity

AddToMotionController.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ect to the entity's motion controller so that [ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate](/gmod/ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate) will be called for given [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ect as well.

You must first create a motion controller with [Entity:StartMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StartMotionController).

You can remove added [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ects by using [Entity:RemoveFromMotionController](/gmod/Entity:RemoveFromMotionController).
NOTES: Only works on a scripted [Entity](/gmod/Entity) of anim type

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physObj
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) to add to the motion controller.

AlignAngles.DESCRIPTION: Returns an angle based on the ones inputted that you can use to align an object.
NOTES: This function doesn't change the angle of the entity on its own (see example).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: from
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle you want to align from

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle you want to align to

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The resulting aligned angle

Alive.DESCRIPTION:
Checks if the entity is considered alive.

Checks entity's internal life state variable. Does not check health, but it is generally expected the health to be 0 or below at the point of an entity being considered dead. This internally looks up the save value `m_lifeState`

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is considered alive.

BecomeRagdollOnClient.DESCRIPTION:
Spawns a clientside ragdoll for the entity, positioning it in place of the original entity, and makes the entity invisible. It doesn't preserve flex values (face posing) as CSRagdolls don't support flex.

It does not work on players. Use [Player:CreateRagdoll](/gmod/Player:CreateRagdoll) instead.

The original entity is not removed, and neither are any ragdolls previously generated with this function.

To make the entity re-appear, run [Entity:SetNoDraw](/gmod/Entity:SetNoDraw)( false )

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created ragdoll. (`class C_ClientRagdoll`)

BeingLookedAtByLocalPlayer.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the entity is being looked at by the local player and is within 256 units of distance.
NOTES: This function is only available in entities that are based off of sandbox's `base_gmodentity` as well as `prop_effect`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the entity being looked at by the local player and within 256 units.

Blocked.DESCRIPTION: Dispatches blocked events to this entity's blocked handler. This function is only useful when interacting with entities like func_movelinear.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that is blocking us

BodyTarget.DESCRIPTION: Returns a centered vector of this entity, NPCs use this internally to aim at their targets.
NOTES: This only works on players and NPCs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector of where the the attack comes from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: noisy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Decides if it should return the centered vector with a random offset to it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The centered vector.

BoneHasFlag.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity's bone has the flag or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bone ID to test flag of.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag to test, see [BONE](/gmod/Enums/BONE)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the bone has that flag or not

BoneLength.DESCRIPTION: Returns the length between given bone's position and the position of given bone's parent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the bone you want the length of. You may want to get the length of the next bone ( boneID + 1 ) for decent results

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The length of the bone

BoundingRadius.DESCRIPTION: Returns the distance between the center of the bounding box and the furthest bounding box corner.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the bounding box.

CallDTVarProxies.DESCRIPTION: Calls all [Entity:NetworkVarNotify](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVarNotify) functions with the given new value, but doesn't change the real value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The NetworkVar Type. Supported choices:

* `String` (up to 511 characters)
* `Bool`
* `Float`
* `Int` (32-bit signed integer)
* `Vector`
* `Angle`
* `Entity`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: slot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The NetworkVar slot. See [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) for more detailed explanation.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: newValue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new value.

CallOnRemove.DESCRIPTION: Causes a specified function to be run if the entity is removed by any means. This can later be undone by [Entity:RemoveCallOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:RemoveCallOnRemove) if you need it to not run.
WARNINGS: An error being thrown inside `removeFunc` will stop other `EntityRemoved` hooks from executing.
This hook is called clientside during full updates. See [GM:EntityRemoved](/gmod/GM:EntityRemoved) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Identifier that can be optionally used with [Entity:RemoveCallOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:RemoveCallOnRemove) to undo this call on remove.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: removeFunc
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be called on remove.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Optional arguments to pass to removeFunc. Do note that the first argument passed to the function will always be the entity being removed, and the arguments passed on here start after that.

ClearAllOutputs.DESCRIPTION: Clears all registered events for map I/O outputs on this entity. If a string is given, will use the string as a wildcard to limit removed outputs by name matches.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: outputName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An optional string that will be used to limit removed outputs by name matches, supports wildcards.

ClearPoseParameters.DESCRIPTION: Resets all pose parameters such as aim_yaw, aim_pitch and rotation.

CollisionRulesChanged.DESCRIPTION: Declares that the collision rules of the entity have changed, and subsequent calls for [GM:ShouldCollide](/gmod/GM:ShouldCollide) with this entity may return a different value than they did previously.
WARNINGS: Failure to use this function correctly will result in a crash of the physics engine.
This function must **not** be called inside of [GM:ShouldCollide](/gmod/GM:ShouldCollide). Instead, it must be called in advance when the condition is known to change.

CopyBoneMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Same as [Entity:GetBoneMatrix](/gmod/Entity:GetBoneMatrix), but instead of returning a new matrix object, it copies the data to a given matrix.

This is measurably faster when accessing bone matrices a lot.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone ID to retrieve matrix of, starting at index 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to copy the bone matrix to.

CreateBoneFollowers.DESCRIPTION:
Creates bone followers based on the current entity model.

Bone followers are [Entities](/gmod/Entity) whose [Physics Objects](/gmod/PhysObj) follow a specific bone on another Entity's model.  
This is what is used by `prop_dynamic` for things like big combine doors with multiple physics objects which follow the visual mesh of the door when it animates.

Be mindful that bone followers create a separate entity (`phys_bone_follower`) for each physics object.

You must call [Entity:UpdateBoneFollowers](/gmod/Entity:UpdateBoneFollowers) every tick for bone followers to update their positions.
NOTES: This function only works on `anim`, `nextbot` and `ai` type entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone_whitelist
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, a whitelist of bone names to create bone followers for. If a models' bone name is not in this list, a bone follower entity will not be created for it.

CreatedByMap.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity was created by map or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is created by map?

CreateParticleEffect.DESCRIPTION: Creates a clientside particle system attached to the entity. See also [CreateParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.CreateParticleSystem)
NOTES: The particle effect must be precached with [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem) and the file its from must be added via [game.AddParticles](/gmod/game.AddParticles) before it can be used!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: particle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The particle name to create

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachment
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Attachment ID to attach the particle to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: options
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of tables ( IDs 1 to 64 ) having the following structure:
* [number](/gmod/number) attachtype - The particle attach type. See [PATTACH](/gmod/Enums/PATTACH). **Default:** PATTACH_ABSORIGIN
* [Entity](/gmod/Entity) entity - The parent entity? **Default:** NULL
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) position - The offset position for given control point. **Default:**  nil

This only affects the control points of the particle effects and will do nothing if the effect doesn't use control points.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created particle system.

CreateShadow.DESCRIPTION: Draws the shadow of an entity.

DeleteOnRemove.DESCRIPTION: Whenever the entity is removed, entityToRemove will be removed also.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entityToRemove
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be removed

NOTES: This function only works on `anim` type entities.

DestroyShadow.DESCRIPTION:
Removes the shadow for the entity.

The shadow will be recreated as soon as the entity wakes.
NOTES: Doesn't affect shadows from flashlight/lamps/env_projectedtexture.

DisableMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Disables an active matrix. See [Entity:EnableMatrix](/gmod/Entity:EnableMatrix) for more info about active matrixes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrixType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the matrix type to disable.

Currently the only matrix type is `"RenderMultiply"`.

DispatchTraceAttack.DESCRIPTION: Performs a trace attack towards the entity this function is called on, as if an invisible bullet is shot towards it. Visually identical to [Entity:TakeDamageInfo](/gmod/Entity:TakeDamageInfo).
NOTES: This function correctly applies damage to [func_breakable_surf](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Func_breakable_surf) entities, unlike [Entity:TakeDamageInfo](/gmod/Entity:TakeDamageInfo).
WARNINGS: Calling this function on the victim entity in [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage) can cause infinite loops.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageInfo
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage to apply.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: traceRes
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Trace result to use to deal damage. See [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dir
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Direction of the attack.

Dissolve.DESCRIPTION:
Dissolves the entity.

This function creates an `env_entity_dissolver` entity internally, which is parented to the target entity and remains until the entity is fully dissolved. Calling this function on an entity that is already dissolving will not create another `env_entity_dissolver` entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Dissolve type. Should be one of the following values:

| ID | Description |
|||
| 0 | ENTITY_DISSOLVE_NORMAL |
| 1 | ELECTRICAL|
| 2 | ELECTRICAL_LIGHT |
| 3 | ENTITY_DISSOLVE_CORE |

ARGUMENTS.NAME: magnitude
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Magnitude of the dissolve effect, its effect depends on the dissolve type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The origin for the dissolve effect, its effect depends on the dissolve type. Defaults to entity's origin.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay until starting the dissolve, in seconds. There will be some particles produced during this time.

DontDeleteOnRemove.DESCRIPTION: This removes the argument entity from an ent's list of entities to 'delete on remove'
NOTES: Also see [Entity:DeleteOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:DeleteOnRemove)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entityToUnremove
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be removed from the list of entities to delete

DrawModel.DESCRIPTION:
Draws the entity or model.

If called inside [ENTITY:Draw](/gmod/ENTITY:Draw) or [ENTITY:DrawTranslucent](/gmod/ENTITY:DrawTranslucent), it only draws the entity's model itself.

If called outside of those hooks, it will call both of said hooks depending on [Entity:GetRenderGroup](/gmod/Entity:GetRenderGroup), drawing the entire entity again.

When drawing an entity more than once per frame in different positions, you should call [Entity:SetupBones](/gmod/Entity:SetupBones) before each draw; Otherwise, the entity will retain its first drawn position.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Using this with a map model ([game.GetWorld](/gmod/game.GetWorld)():[GetModel](/gmod/Entity:GetModel)()) crashes the game.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The optional [STUDIO_](/gmod/Enums/STUDIO) flags, usually taken from [ENTITY:Draw](/gmod/ENTITY:Draw) and similar hooks.

DrawShadow.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether an entity's shadow should be drawn.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldDraw
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: True to enable, false to disable shadow drawing.

DropToFloor.DESCRIPTION: Move an entity down until it collides with something.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Trace mask.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ignoreEnt
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Trace ignore entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxDist
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Max trace dist.

DTVar.DESCRIPTION: Sets up a self.dt.NAME alias for a Data Table variable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The type of the DTVar being set up. Supported choices:

* `String` (up to 511 characters)
* `Bool`
* `Float`
* `Int` (32-bit signed integer)
* `Vector`
* `Angle`
* `Entity`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: slot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The ID of the DTVar. Can be between `0` and `3` for strings, `0` and `31` for everything else.

This can be omitted entirely (arguments will shift) and it will use the next available slot.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name by which you will refer to DTVar. It must be a valid variable name. (No spaces!)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The type of the DTVar being set up. Supported choices:

* `String` (up to 511 characters)
* `Bool`
* `Float`
* `Int` (32-bit signed integer)
* `Vector`
* `Angle`
* `Entity`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name by which you will refer to DTVar. It must be a valid variable name. (No spaces!)

EmitSound.DESCRIPTION:
Plays a sound on an entity. See also [EmitSound](/gmod/Global.EmitSound) if you wish to play sounds without an entity.

If run clientside, the sound will only be heard locally.  
If used on a player or NPC character with the mouth rigged, the character will "lip-sync" if the sound file contains lipsync data. See [this page](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Choreography_creation/Lip_syncing) for more information.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not respond to [SuppressHostEvents](/gmod/Global.SuppressHostEvents).

NOTES: When using this function with weapons, use the [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon) itself as the entity, not its owner!
WARNINGS:
Due to engine quirks, [sound scripts](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Soundscripts) can't have their soundlevel, pitch, volume, or channel changed when played from an entity—the sound script parameters will override whatever you pass to this function.

You can do one of these instead:
* Use [sound.GetProperties](/gmod/sound.GetProperties) to select a sound from the script, and play the sound file directly.
* For single-use sounds, you can pass the [SND_CHANGE_VOL](/gmod/Enums/SND) or [SND_CHANGE_PITCH](/gmod/Enums/SND) sound flags. However, this will change the volume or pitch of the sound if it's already playing, instead of starting the sound over or playing another instance.
* Use [EmitSound](/gmod/Global.EmitSound) with the entity parameter set to the [Entity:EntIndex](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex) of the entity you want to play the sound on.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the sound to be played.

This should either be a sound script name ([sound.Add](/gmod/sound.Add)) or a file path relative to the `sound/` folder. (so don't include `sound/`, and make note that it's not sound**s** when moving the sound file itself)
WARNINGS: The string cannot have whitespace at the start or end. You can remove this with [string.Trim](/gmod/string.Trim).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundLevel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A modifier for the distance this sound will reach, acceptable range is 0 to 511. 100 means no adjustment to the level. See [SNDLVL](/gmod/Enums/SNDLVL)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pitchPercent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pitch applied to the sound. The acceptable range is from 0 to 255. 100 means the pitch is not changed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The volume, from 0 to 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: channel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound channel, see [CHAN](/gmod/Enums/CHAN).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundFlags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flags of the sound, see [SND](/gmod/Enums/SND)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dsp
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The DSP preset for this sound. [DSP Presets](/gmod/DSP_Presets)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set serverside, the sound will only be networked to the clients in the filter.

EmitStepSound.DESCRIPTION:
Plays a sound of a step depending on the surface below the entity's foot.

It will use attachments `"RightFoot"` or `"LeftFoot"` to decide where to check the surface at. If the attachments do not exist, it will use regular Valve Biped skeleton bones. If they don't exist, it will fallback to the entity's origin.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: isLeftFoot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Determines whether the step is a right foot or a left foot.

This is used for certain NPCs such as Eli to determine what sound should be played. This also determines the position of the sound.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The volume, from 0 to 1.

EnableConstraints.DESCRIPTION: Toggles the constraints of this ragdoll entity on and off.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: toggleConstraints
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Set to true to enable the constraints and false to disable them.

Disabling constraints will delete the constraints.

EnableCustomCollisions.DESCRIPTION:
Flags an entity as using custom lua defined collisions. Fixes entities having spongy player collisions or not hitting traces, such as after [Entity:PhysicsFromMesh](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsFromMesh)

Internally identical to `Entity:AddSolidFlags( bit.bor( FSOLID_CUSTOMRAYTEST, FSOLID_CUSTOMBOXTEST ) )`

Do not confuse this function with [Entity:SetCustomCollisionCheck](/gmod/Entity:SetCustomCollisionCheck), they are not the same.

EnableMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Can be used to apply a custom [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) to the entity, mostly used for scaling the model by a [Vector](/gmod/Vector).

To disable it, use [Entity:DisableMatrix](/gmod/Entity:DisableMatrix).

If your old scales are wrong due to a recent update, use [Entity:SetLegacyTransform](/gmod/Entity:SetLegacyTransform) as a quick fix.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not scale procedural bones, and disables inverse kinematics of the entity.

NOTES: The matrix can also be modified to apply a custom rotation and offset via the [VMatrix:SetAngles](/gmod/VMatrix:SetAngles) and [VMatrix:SetTranslation](/gmod/VMatrix:SetTranslation) functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrixType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the matrix type.  
Currently the only matrix type is `"RenderMultiply"`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrix
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to apply before drawing the entity.

EntIndex.DESCRIPTION: Gets the unique entity index of an entity.
NOTES: Entity indices are marked as unused after deletion, and can be reused by newly-created entities

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The index of the entity.

`-1` for clientside-only or `0` for serverside-only and [NULL](/gmod/NULL) entities.

Extinguish.DESCRIPTION:
Extinguishes the entity if it is on fire.

Has no effect if called inside [GM:EntityTakeDamage](/gmod/GM:EntityTakeDamage) (and the attacker is the flame that's hurting the entity)

See also [Entity:Ignite](/gmod/Entity:Ignite).

EyeAngles.DESCRIPTION: Returns the direction a player, npc or ragdoll is looking as a world-oriented angle.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This can return an incorrect value in vehicles (like pods, buggy, ...). **This bug has been fixed in the past but was causing many addons being broken, so the fix has been removed but applied to [Player:GetAimVector](/gmod/Player:GetAimVector) only**.
This may return local angles in jeeps when used with [Player:EnterVehicle](/gmod/Player:EnterVehicle). **A workaround is available in the second example.**

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Player's eye angle.

EyePos.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position of an Player/NPC's view.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: View position of the entity.

FindBodygroupByName.DESCRIPTION: Searches the [Entity's](/gmod/Entity) model for a Body Group with a given name.
NOTES: Weapons will return results from their viewmodels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name to search for.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [Body Group's ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#id) or `-1` if no Body Group has the provided name.

FindGestureLayer.DESCRIPTION: Searches the currently active layers for a layer playing animation with given activity.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity to search for.

RETURNS.NAME: layerID
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A layer ID for given activity, or `-1` if not found.

FindGestureSequenceLayer.DESCRIPTION: Searches the currently active layers for a layer playing animation with given sequence.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID to search for. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

RETURNS.NAME: layerID
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A layer ID for given sequence, or `-1` if not found.

FindTransitionSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a transition from the given start and end sequence.

This function was only used by HL1 entities and NPCs, before the advent of sequence blending and gestures.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: currentSequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The currently playing sequence

ARGUMENTS.NAME: goalSequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The goal sequence.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The transition sequence, -1 if not available.

Fire.DESCRIPTION:
Fires an entity's input, conforming to the map IO event queue system. You can find inputs for most entities on the [Valve Developer Wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Output)

See also [Entity:Input](/gmod/Entity:Input) for a function that bypasses the event queue and [GM:AcceptInput](/gmod/GM:AcceptInput).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the input to fire

ARGUMENTS.NAME: param
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to give to the input, can also be a [number](/gmod/number) or a [boolean](/gmod/boolean).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay in seconds before firing

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that caused this input (i.e. the player who pushed a button)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: caller
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that is triggering this input (i.e. the button that was pushed)

FireBullets.DESCRIPTION:
Fires a bullet.

When used in a  hook such as [WEAPON:Think](/gmod/WEAPON:Think) or [WEAPON:PrimaryAttack](/gmod/WEAPON:PrimaryAttack), it will use [Player:LagCompensation](/gmod/Player:LagCompensation) internally.

Lag compensation will not work if this function is called in a timer, regardless if the timer was made in a predicted hook.

Due to how `Entity:FireBullets` is set up internally, bullet tracers will always originate from the first attachment/index 1. This can be avoided by supplying your own tracer effect.

When firing bullets from a [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon), it is recommended to fire bullets from the weapon owner entity ([Player](/gmod/Player) or [NPC](/gmod/NPC)), not the [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon) itself.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bulletInfo
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bullet data to be used. See the [Structures/Bullet](/gmod/Structures/Bullet).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: suppressHostEvents
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Has the effect of encasing the FireBullets call in [SuppressHostEvents](/gmod/Global.SuppressHostEvents), only works in multiplayer.

NOTES: If the entity vibrates or stops following the parent, you probably need to run [Entity:SetPredictable](/gmod/Entity:SetPredictable)( true ) clientside.

ForcePlayerDrop.DESCRIPTION:
Forces the entity to be dropped, if it is being held by a player's Gravity Gun, Physics Gun or `+use` pickup.

See also [Player:DropObject](/gmod/Player:DropObject).

FrameAdvance.DESCRIPTION:
Advances the cycle of an animated entity.

Animations that loop will automatically reset the cycle so you don't have to - ones that do not will stop animating once you reach the end of their sequence.
WARNINGS:
Do not call this function multiple times a frame, as it can cause unexpected results, such as animations playing at increased rate, etc.

[NextBot:BodyMoveXY](/gmod/NextBot:BodyMoveXY) calls this internally, so do not call this function before or after [NextBot:BodyMoveXY](/gmod/NextBot:BodyMoveXY).

NOTES: Actually binds to CBaseEntity::GetLocalVelocity() which retrieves the velocity of the entity due to its movement in the world from forces such as gravity. Does not include velocity from entity-on-entity collision.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The velocity of the entity.

GetAngles.DESCRIPTION: Gets the angles of given entity.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This returns incorrect results for the local player clientside.
This will return the local player's [EyeAngles](/gmod/Global.EyeAngles) in [rendering hooks](/gmod/3D_Rendering_Hooks).
This will return [Angle](/gmod/Global.Angle)(0,0,0) in [rendering hooks](/gmod/3D_Rendering_Hooks) while paused in single-player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The angles of the entity.

GetAnimCount.DESCRIPTION:

See also [Entity:GetAnimInfo](/gmod/Entity:GetAnimInfo)

GetAnimInfo.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table containing the number of frames, flags, name, and FPS of an entity's animation ID.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: animIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The animation ID to look up, starting at 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Information about the animation, or `nil` if the index is out of bounds.

A table with the following keys:
* [string](/gmod/string) label - Animation name
* [number](/gmod/number) fps - How many frames per second the animation should be played at
* [number](/gmod/number) flags - [STUDIO_](https://github.com/ZeqMacaw/Crowbar/blob/0d46f3b6a694b74453db407c72c12a9685d8eb1d/Crowbar/Core/GameModel/SourceCommon/SourceMdlFileData/SourceMdlAnimationDesc.vb#L181) flags, such as looping
* [number](/gmod/number) numframes - Number of frames the animation has

GetAnimTime.DESCRIPTION: Returns the last time the entity had an animation update. Returns 0 if the entity doesn't animate.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The last time the entity had an animation update.

GetAnimTimeInterval.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the amount of time since last animation.

Works only on `CBaseAnimating` entities.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of time since last animation.

GetAttachment.DESCRIPTION: Gets the orientation and position of the attachment by its ID, returns nothing if the attachment does not exist.

NOTES: The update rate of this function is limited by the setting of ENT.AutomaticFrameAdvance for [Scripted Entities](/gmod/Scripted%20Entities)!

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The table with angle and position of the attachment or `nil` if does not exist. See the [Structures/AngPos](/gmod/Structures/AngPos). Most notably, the table contains the keys `Ang` and `Pos` as well as `Bone`.

GetAttachments.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table containing all attachments of the given entity's model.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This can have inconsistent results in single-player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Attachment data. See [Structures/AttachmentData](/gmod/Structures/AttachmentData).

Returns an empty table in case its model has no attachments or there's a some kind of other issue.

GetBaseVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity's base velocity which is their velocity due to forces applied by other entities. This includes entity-on-entity collision or riding a treadmill.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The base velocity of the entity.

GetBloodColor.DESCRIPTION: Returns the blood color of this entity. This can be set with [Entity:SetBloodColor](/gmod/Entity:SetBloodColor).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Color from [BLOOD_COLOR](/gmod/Enums/BLOOD_COLOR) or [nil](/gmod/nil)

NOTES: Weapons will return results from their viewmodels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bodyGroupId

The Body Group ID to retrieve the active Sub Model ID for.  
			Body Group IDs start at `0`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The currently active Sub Model ID.

GetBodygroupCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the number of [Sub Models](/gmod/Entity:GetSubModels) in the Body Group corresponding to a given [Body Group ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#id) of the [Entity's](/gmod/Entity) model.
NOTES: Weapons will return results from their viewmodels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bodyGroupId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Body Group ID to retrieve the Sub Model count of.  
			Body Group IDs start at `0`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The number of Sub Models in the Body Group.

GetBodygroupName.DESCRIPTION: Retrieves the name of the Body Group corresponding to a given [Body Group ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#id) on the [Entity's](/gmod/Entity) model.
NOTES: Weapons will return results from their viewmodels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bodyGroupId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Body Group ID to get the name of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the Body Group.

NOTES: Weapons will return results from their viewmodels.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of Body Group information where each value is a [Structures/BodyGroupData](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData).

GetBoneContents.DESCRIPTION: Returns the contents of the specified bone.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone id, starting at index 0. See [Entity:LookupBone](/gmod/Entity:LookupBone).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The contents as a [CONTENTS](/gmod/Enums/CONTENTS) or 0 on failure.

GetBoneController.DESCRIPTION: Returns the value of the bone controller with the specified ID.
NOTES: This is the precursor of pose parameters, and only works for Half Life 1: Source models supporting it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID of the bone controller. Goes from 0 to 3.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The value set on the bone controller.

GetBoneCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of bones in the entity.
NOTES: Will return `0` for [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) or undrawn entities until [Entity:SetupBones](/gmod/Entity:SetupBones) is called on the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of bones in given entity, starting at index 0.

GetBoneMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the transformation matrix of a given bone on the entity's model. The matrix contains the transformation used to position the bone in the world. It is not relative to the parent bone.

This is equivalent to constructing a [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) using [Entity:GetBonePosition](/gmod/Entity:GetBonePosition).

See [Entity:CopyBoneMatrix](/gmod/Entity:CopyBoneMatrix) for a more performant version.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This can return the server's matrix during server lag.
This can return garbage serverside or a 0,0,0 fourth column (represents position) for v49 models.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The bone ID to retrieve matrix of, starting at index 0.
* Bones clientside and serverside will differ

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The matrix

* Some entities don't update animation every frame such as prop_physics and won't have accurate bone matrix.

GetBoneName.DESCRIPTION:
Returns name of given bone id.

	See [Entity:LookupBone](/gmod/Entity:LookupBone) for the inverse of this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID of bone to lookup name of, starting at index 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of given bone.

* `"__INVALIDBONE__"` in case the name cannot be read or the index is out of range, or we failed or entity doesn't have a model.

GetBoneParent.DESCRIPTION: Returns parent bone of given bone.
NOTES: Will return -1 for [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) until [Entity:SetupBones](/gmod/Entity:SetupBones) is called on the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone ID of the bone to get parent of, starting at index 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Parent bone ID or -1 if we failed for some reason.

GetBonePosition.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position and angle of the given attachment, relative to the world.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This can return the server's position during server lag.
This can return garbage serverside or [Vector](/gmod/Global.Vector)(0,0,0) for v49 models.
This can return garbage if a trace passed through the target bone during bone matrix access.

NOTES:
This function returns the bone position from the last tick, so if your framerate is higher than the server's tickrate it may appear to lag behind if used on a fast moving entity. You can fix this by using the bone's matrix instead:
```lua
local matrix = entity:GetBoneMatrix(0)
local pos = matrix:GetTranslation()
local ang = matrix:GetAngles()
```
WARNINGS:
This function can return entity's `GetPos()` instead if the entity doesn't have it's bone cache set up.

To ensure the bone position is correct use this:
```lua
local pos = ent:GetBonePosition(0)
if pos == ent:GetPos() then
	pos = ent:GetBoneMatrix(0):GetTranslation()
end
```

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone index of the bone to get the position of, starting at index 0. See [Entity:LookupBone](/gmod/Entity:LookupBone).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The bone's position relative to the world. It can return nothing if the requested bone is out of bounds, or the entity has no model.
The bone's angle relative to the world.

GetBoneSurfaceProp.DESCRIPTION: Returns the surface property of the specified bone. See [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData) for more details about what they are.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone id, starting at index 0. See [Entity:LookupBone](/gmod/Entity:LookupBone).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The surface property of the bone to be used with [util.GetSurfaceIndex](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceIndex) or an empty string on failure.

GetBrushPlane.DESCRIPTION: Returns info about given plane of non-nodraw brush model surfaces of the entity's model. Works on worldspawn as well.
WARNINGS: This only works on entities with brush models.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the plane to get info of. Starts from 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The origin of the plane.

This will be either the first vertex's position (if available) or the plane's normal multiplied by the plane's distance.
The normal of the plane.

The "distance" of the plane.

The distance is the dot product of the plane's normal and the point it was initialized with.

GetBrushPlaneCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of planes of non-nodraw brush model surfaces of the entity's model.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of brush model planes of the entity's model. This will be 0 for any non-brush model.

GetBrushSurfaces.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of brushes surfaces for brush model entities.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A list of [SurfaceInfo](/gmod/SurfaceInfo) elements if the entity has a brush model, or `nil` otherwise.

GetCallbacks.DESCRIPTION:

The callbacks can then be removed with [Entity:RemoveCallback](/gmod/Entity:RemoveCallback).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hook
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hook to retrieve the callbacks from, see [Entity Callbacks](/gmod/Entity%20Callbacks) for the possible hooks.

GetChildBones.DESCRIPTION: Returns ids of child bones of given bone.

GetChildren.DESCRIPTION: Gets the children of the entity - that is, every entity whose move parent is this entity.
NOTES:
This function returns [Entity:SetMoveParent](/gmod/Entity:SetMoveParent) children, **NOT** [Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent)!

[Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent) however also calls [Entity:SetMoveParent](/gmod/Entity:SetMoveParent).



This means that some entities in the returned list might have a NULL [Entity:GetParent](/gmod/Entity:GetParent).

This also means that using this function on players will return their weapons on the client but not the server.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A list of movement children entities

GetClass.DESCRIPTION: Returns the classname of a entity. This is often the name of the Lua file or folder containing the files for the entity

GetCollisionBounds.DESCRIPTION:

In most cases, this will return the same bounding box as [Entity:GetModelBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetModelBounds) unless the entity does not have a physics mesh or it has a [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) different from the default.

Collision bounds can be previewed in singleplayer via `ent_bbox` console command, while looking at a desired entity and with `developer 1`. (Will appear as an orange wireframe box)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector of the collision bounds, basically [Entity:OBBMins](/gmod/Entity:OBBMins).

The collision group. See [COLLISION_GROUP](/gmod/Enums/COLLISION_GROUP)

GetConstrainedEntities.DESCRIPTION: Returns the two entities involved in a constraint ent, or nil if the entity is not a constraint.

ent2

GetInternalVariable.DESCRIPTION:
An interface for accessing internal key values on entities.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of variable corresponding to an entity save value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The internal variable value.

GetKeyValues.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table containing Hammer key values the entity has stored. **Not all key values will be accessible this way.** Use [GM:EntityKeyValue](/gmod/GM:EntityKeyValue) or [ENTITY:KeyValue](/gmod/ENTITY:KeyValue) to capture and store every key value.

Single key values can usually be retrieved with [Entity:GetInternalVariable](/gmod/Entity:GetInternalVariable).

Here's a list of keyvalues that will not appear in this list, as they are not stored/defined as actual keyvalues internally:
* rendercolor - [Entity:GetColor](/gmod/Entity:GetColor) (Only RGB)
* rendercolor32 - [Entity:GetColor](/gmod/Entity:GetColor) (RGBA)
* renderamt - [Entity:GetColor](/gmod/Entity:GetColor) (Alpha)
* disableshadows - [EF_NOSHADOW](/gmod/Enums/EF#EF_NOSHADOW)
* mins - [Entity:GetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetCollisionBounds)
* maxs - [Entity:GetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetCollisionBounds)
* disablereceiveshadows - [EF_NORECEIVESHADOW](/gmod/Enums/EF#EF_NORECEIVESHADOW)
* nodamageforces - [EFL_NO_DAMAGE_FORCES](/gmod/Enums/EFL#EFL_NO_DAMAGE_FORCES)
* angle - [Entity:GetAngles](/gmod/Entity:GetAngles)
* angles - [Entity:GetAngles](/gmod/Entity:GetAngles)
* origin - [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos)
* targetname - [Entity:GetName](/gmod/Entity:GetName)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of key values.

GetLayerCycle.DESCRIPTION: Returns the animation cycle/frame for given layer.

GetMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the material override for this entity. 

Returns an empty string if no material override exists. Use [Entity:GetMaterials](/gmod/Entity:GetMaterials) to list its default materials.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The server's value takes priority on the client.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: material

GetMaterials.DESCRIPTION:
Returns all materials of the entity's model.

This function is unaffected by [Entity:SetSubMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetSubMaterial) as it returns the original materials.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The table returned by this function will not contain materials if they are missing from the disk/repository. This means that if you are attempting to find the ID of a material to replace with [Entity:SetSubMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetSubMaterial) and there are missing materials on the model, all subsequent materials will be offset in the table, meaning that the ID you are trying to get will be incorrect.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing full paths to the materials of the model.

For models, it's limited to `128` materials.

GetMaterialType.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the [surface material type](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Material_Types) of this entity.

This can be approximated clientside via [util.GetModelInfo](/gmod/util.GetModelInfo).

Internally, all this does is return `gamematerial` of the surface property on the first physics object of the entity. You can do this yourself using [PhysObj:GetMaterial](/gmod/PhysObj:GetMaterial) and [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Surface material type.

GetMaxHealth.DESCRIPTION: Returns the max health that the entity was given. It can be set via [Entity:SetMaxHealth](/gmod/Entity:SetMaxHealth).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Max health.

GetModel.DESCRIPTION: Gets the model of given entity.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
This does not necessarily return the model's path, as is the case for brush and virtual models. This is intentional behaviour, however, there is currently no way to retrieve the actual file path.

This also affects certain models that are edited by 3rd party programs after being compiled.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The entity's model. Will be a filesystem path for most models.

This is guaranteed to be lower case.

This will be [nil](/gmod/nil) for entities which cannot have models, such as point entities.

GetModelBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the entity's model bounds, not scaled by [Entity:SetModelScale](/gmod/Entity:SetModelScale).

These bounds are affected by all the animations the model has at compile time, if they go outside of the models' render bounds at any point.  
See [Entity:GetModelRenderBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetModelRenderBounds) for just the render bounds of the model.

This is different than the collision bounds/hull, which are set via [Entity:SetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetCollisionBounds).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector of the bounds
The maximum vector of the bounds

GetModelContents.DESCRIPTION: Returns the contents of the entity's current model.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: How many physics bones exist on the model.
The radius of the model.
WARNINGS: This can return [nil](/gmod/nil) instead of a [number](/gmod/number) in some cases.

GetModelRenderBounds.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity's model render bounds. Unlike [Entity:GetModelBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetModelBounds), bounds returning by this function will not be affected by animations (at compile time).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector of the bounds
The maximum vector of the bounds

GetModelScale.DESCRIPTION: Gets the selected entity's model scale.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Scale of that entity's model.

GetParentPhysNum.DESCRIPTION: If the entity is parented to an entity that has a model with multiple physics objects (like a ragdoll), this is used to retrieve what physics object number the entity is parented to on it's parent.

GetParentWorldTransformMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position and angle of the entity's move parent as a 3x4 matrix ([VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) is 4x4 so the fourth row goes unused). The first three columns store the angle as a [rotation matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix), and the fourth column stores the position vector.

If the entity is [parented to attachment](/gmod/Entity:GetParentAttachment) 0 or the parent isn't a BaseAnimating entity, the equivalent of [Entity](/gmod/Entity):[GetMoveParent()](/gmod/Entity:GetMoveParent):[GetWorldTransformMatrix()](/gmod/Entity:GetWorldTransformMatrix) will be returned.

NOTES: Some entities such as the Combine Ball disregard the time limit and always return the physics attacker.

NOTES: Entities don't have clientside physics objects by default, so this will return `[NULL PHYSOBJ]` on the client in most cases.

GetPhysicsObjectCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the number of physics objects an entity has (usually 1 for non-ragdolls)

GetPhysicsObjectNum.DESCRIPTION:

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physNum
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The number corresponding to the [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) to grab. Starts at 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The physics object or nil if not found

GetPlaybackRate.DESCRIPTION: Returns the playback rate of the main sequence on this entity, with 1.0 being the default speed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The playback rate.

Gets the position of given entity in the world.

See [Entity:GetLocalPos](/gmod/Entity:GetLocalPos) for the position relative to the entity's [Entity:GetParent](/gmod/Entity:GetParent).

You'll have to [remap](/gmod/math.Remap) this value clientside to [Entity:GetPoseParameterRange](/gmod/Entity:GetPoseParameterRange)'s returns if you want get the actual pose parameter value. See [Entity:SetPoseParameter](/gmod/Entity:SetPoseParameter)'s example.

GetPoseParameterName.DESCRIPTION: Returns name of given pose parameter

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Id of the pose paremeter

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum value
The maximum value

GetPredictable.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether this entity is predictable or not.

See [Entity:SetPredictable](/gmod/Entity:SetPredictable) for more information

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether this entity is predictable or not.

GetPreferredCarryAngles.DESCRIPTION: Called to override the preferred carry angles of this object.
NOTES: This callback is only called for `anim` and `ai` type entities. For rest use [GM:GetPreferredCarryAngles](/gmod/GM:GetPreferredCarryAngles).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player who is holding the object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return an angle to override the carry angles.

GetRagdollOwner.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity which the ragdoll came from. The opposite of [Player:GetRagdollEntity](/gmod/Player:GetRagdollEntity).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entity who owns the ragdoll.

GetRenderAngles.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity's render angles, set by [Entity:SetRenderAngles](/gmod/Entity:SetRenderAngles) in a drawing hook.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entitys render angles

GetRenderBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Returns render bounds of the entity as local vectors. Can be overridden by [Entity:SetRenderBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetRenderBounds).

If the render bounds are not inside players view, the entity will not be drawn!

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector of the bounds
The maximum vector of the bounds.

GetRenderFX.DESCRIPTION: Returns current render FX of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current render FX of the entity. See [kRenderFx](/gmod/Enums/kRenderFx)

GetRenderGroup.DESCRIPTION: Returns the render group of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The render group. See [RENDERGROUP](/gmod/Enums/RENDERGROUP)

GetRenderMode.DESCRIPTION: Returns the render mode of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The render Mode. See [RENDERMODE](/gmod/Enums/RENDERMODE)

GetRenderOrigin.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity's render origin, set by [Entity:SetRenderOrigin](/gmod/Entity:SetRenderOrigin) in a drawing hook.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entitys render origin

GetRight.DESCRIPTION: Returns the rightward vector of the entity, as a normalized direction vector

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: rightDir

GetRotatedAABB.DESCRIPTION: Returns axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) of a orientated bounding box (OBB) based on entity's rotation.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Minimum extent of an OBB in local coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Maximum extent of an OBB in local coordinates.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Minimum extent of the AABB relative to entity's position.
Maximum extent of the AABB relative to entity's position.

GetSaveTable.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table of save values for an entity.

These tables are not the same between the client and the server, and different entities may have different fields.



You can get the list different fields an entity has by looking at it's source code (the 2013 SDK can be found [online](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013)). Accessible fields are defined by each `DEFINE_FIELD` and `DEFINE_KEYFIELD` inside the `DATADESC` block.

Take the headcrab, for example:

```
BEGIN_DATADESC( CBaseHeadcrab )
	// m_nGibCount - don't save
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bHidden, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flTimeDrown, FIELD_TIME ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bCommittedToJump, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_vecCommittedJumpPos, FIELD_POSITION_VECTOR ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flNextNPCThink, FIELD_TIME ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flIgnoreWorldCollisionTime, FIELD_TIME ),
	
	DEFINE_KEYFIELD( m_bStartBurrowed, FIELD_BOOLEAN, "startburrowed" ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bBurrowed, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flBurrowTime, FIELD_TIME ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_nContext, FIELD_INTEGER ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bCrawlFromCanister, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bMidJump, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_nJumpFromCanisterDir, FIELD_INTEGER ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_bHangingFromCeiling, FIELD_BOOLEAN ),
	DEFINE_FIELD( m_flIlluminatedTime, FIELD_TIME ),
		
	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "Burrow", InputBurrow ),
	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "BurrowImmediate", InputBurrowImmediate ),
	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "Unburrow", InputUnburrow ),
	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "StartHangingFromCeiling", InputStartHangingFromCeiling ),
	DEFINE_INPUTFUNC( FIELD_VOID, "DropFromCeiling", InputDropFromCeiling ),
	
	// Function Pointers
	DEFINE_THINKFUNC( EliminateRollAndPitch ),
	DEFINE_THINKFUNC( ThrowThink ),
	DEFINE_ENTITYFUNC( LeapTouch ),
END_DATADESC()
```

* For each **DEFINE_FIELD**, the save table will have a key with name of **first** argument.
* For each **DEFINE_KEYFIELD**, the save table will have a key with name of the **third** argument.
NOTES: It is highly recommended to use [Entity:GetInternalVariable](/gmod/Entity:GetInternalVariable) for retrieving a single key of the save table for performance reasons.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: showAll
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, shows all variables, not just the ones marked for save/load system.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing all save values in key/value format.

The value may be a sequential table (starting with **1**) if the field in question is an array in engine.

GetSequence.DESCRIPTION: Return the index of the model sequence that is currently active for the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the model sequence.

GetSequenceActivity.DESCRIPTION: Return activity id out of sequence id. Opposite of [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seq
