ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The activity ID, ie [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT)

GetSequenceActivityName.DESCRIPTION: Returns the activity name for the given sequence id.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence id.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT) as a string, returns "Not Found!" with an invalid sequence and "No model!" when no model is set.

GetSequenceCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of sequences ( animations ) the entity's model has.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of sequences ( animations ) the entity's model has.

GetSequenceGroundSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ground speed of the entity's sequence.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ground speed of this sequence.

GetSequenceInfo.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of information about an entity's sequence.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence id of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of information about the entity's sequence, or `nil` is ID is out of range. See [Structures/SequenceInfo](/gmod/Structures/SequenceInfo).

GetSequenceList.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of all sequences ( animations ) the model has.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The list of all sequences ( animations ) the model has. The indices start with 0!

GetSequenceMoveDist.DESCRIPTION:
Returns an entity's sequence move distance (the change in position over the course of the entire sequence).

See [Entity:GetSequenceMovement](/gmod/Entity:GetSequenceMovement) for a similar function with more options.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence index.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The move distance of the sequence.

GetSequenceMovement.DESCRIPTION: Returns the delta movement and angles of a sequence of the entity's model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence index. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startCycle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence start cycle. 0 is the start of the animation, 1 is the end.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endCyclnde
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence end cycle. 0 is the start of the animation, 1 is the end. Values like 2, etc are allowed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the operation was successful
The delta vector of the animation, how much the model's origin point moved.
The delta angle of the animation.

GetSequenceMoveYaw.DESCRIPTION: Returns the change in heading direction in between the start and the end of the sequence.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seq
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence index. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The yaw delta. Returns 99999 for no movement.

GetSequenceName.DESCRIPTION:
Return the name of the sequence for the index provided.
Refer to [Entity:GetSequence](/gmod/Entity:GetSequence) to find the current active sequence on this entity.

See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence) for a function that does the opposite.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the sequence to look up.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the sequence, `"Unknown"` if it was out of bounds or `"Not Found!"` if -1 is provided.

GetSequenceVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Returns an entity's sequence velocity at given animation frame.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequenceId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence index.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cycle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The point in animation, from `0` to `1`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Velocity of the sequence at given point in the animation.

GetShouldPlayPickupSound.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity plays a sound when picked up by a player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if it plays the pickup sound, `false` otherwise.

GetShouldServerRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Returns if entity should create a server ragdoll on death or a client one.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if ragdoll will be created on server, false if on client

GetSkin.DESCRIPTION: Returns the skin index of the current skin. Can be manipulated via [Entity:SetSkin](/gmod/Entity:SetSkin).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Current skin index.

GetSolid.DESCRIPTION: Returns solid type of an entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The solid type. See the [SOLID](/gmod/Enums/SOLID).

GetSolidFlags.DESCRIPTION: Returns solid flag(s) of an entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The flag(s) of the entity, see [FSOLID](/gmod/Enums/FSOLID).

GetSpawnEffect.DESCRIPTION: Returns if we should show a spawn effect on spawn on this entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The flag to allow or disallow the spawn effect.

GetSpawnFlags.DESCRIPTION: Returns the bitwise spawn flags used by the entity. These can be set by [Entity:SetKeyValue](/gmod/Entity:SetKeyValue).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The spawn flags of the entity, see [SF_Enums](/gmod/Enums/SF).

GetSubMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the material override for the given index. 

Returns "" if no material override exists. Use [Entity:GetMaterials](/gmod/Entity:GetMaterials) to list it's default materials.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The server's value takes priority on the client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the sub material. Acceptable values are from 0 to 31.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The material that overrides this index, if any.

GetSubModels.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of models included into the entity's model in the .qc file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The list of models included into the entity's model in the .qc file.

GetSurroundingBounds.DESCRIPTION: Returns two vectors representing the minimum and maximum extent of the entity's axis-aligned bounding box for hitbox detection. In most cases, this will return the same bounding box as [Entity:WorldSpaceAABB](/gmod/Entity:WorldSpaceAABB) unless it was changed by [Entity:SetSurroundingBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetSurroundingBounds) or [Entity:SetSurroundingBoundsType](/gmod/Entity:SetSurroundingBoundsType).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector for the entity's bounding box in world space.
The maximum vector for the entity's bounding box in world space.

GetTable.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a [table](/gmod/table) that contains all lua-based key-value pairs saved on the [Entity](/gmod/Entity).

		For retrieving engine-based key-value pairs, see [Entity:GetSaveTable](/gmod/Entity:GetSaveTable)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of the lua data stored on the Entity, or `nil` if the Entity is NULL.

GetTouchTrace.DESCRIPTION: Returns the last trace used in the collision callbacks such as [ENTITY:StartTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:StartTouch), [ENTITY:Touch](/gmod/ENTITY:Touch) and [ENTITY:EndTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:EndTouch).
NOTES: This returns the last collision trace used, regardless of the entity that caused it. As such, it's only reliable when used in the hooks mentioned above

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult)

GetTransmitWithParent.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the TransmitWithParent flag is set or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the TransmitWithParent flag is set or not

GetUnFreezable.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the entity is unfreezable, meaning it can't be frozen with the physgun. By default props are freezable, so this function will typically return false.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: True if the entity is unfreezable, false otherwise.

GetUp.DESCRIPTION: Returns the upward vector of the entity, as a normalized direction vector

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: upDir

GetVar.DESCRIPTION: Retrieves a value from entity's [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable). Set by [Entity:SetVar](/gmod/Entity:SetVar).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Key of the value to retrieve

ARGUMENTS.NAME: default
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A default value to fallback to if we couldn't retrieve the value from entity

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Retrieved value

GetVelocity.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the entity's velocity.

This returns the total velocity of the entity and is equal to local velocity + base velocity.

Clientside the velocity may be estimated for certain entities, such as physics based entities, instead of returning the "real" velocity from the server.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This can become out-of-sync on the client if the server has been up for a long time.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The velocity of the entity.

GetWorkshopID.DESCRIPTION: Returns ID of workshop addon that the entity is from.
DEPRECATED: The function **currently** does nothing and always returns nil

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The workshop ID

GetWorldTransformMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position and angle of the entity as a 3x4 matrix ([VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) is 4x4 so the fourth row goes unused). The first three columns store the angle as a [rotation matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix), and the fourth column stores the position vector.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This returns incorrect results for the angular component (columns 1-3) for the local player clientside.
This will use the local player's [EyeAngles](/gmod/Global.EyeAngles) in [rendering hooks](/gmod/3D_Rendering_Hooks).
Columns 1-3 will be all 0 (angular component) in [rendering hooks](/gmod/3D_Rendering_Hooks) while paused in single-player.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position and angle matrix.

GibBreakClient.DESCRIPTION:
Causes the entity to break into its current models gibs, if it has any.

You must call [Entity:PrecacheGibs](/gmod/Entity:PrecacheGibs) on the entity before using this function, or it will not create any gibs.

If called on server, the gibs will be spawned on the currently connected clients and will not be synchronized. Otherwise the gibs will be spawned only for the client the function is called on.
NOTES:
this function will not remove or hide the entity it is called on.
	For more expensive version of this function see [Entity:GibBreakServer](/gmod/Entity:GibBreakServer).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: force
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The force to apply to the created gibs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: clr
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, this will be color of the broken gibs instead of the entity's color.

GibBreakServer.DESCRIPTION:
Causes the entity to break into its current models gibs, if it has any.

You must call [Entity:PrecacheGibs](/gmod/Entity:PrecacheGibs) on the entity before using this function, or it will not create any gibs.

The gibs will be spawned on the server and be synchronized with all clients.

Note, that this function will not remove or hide the entity it is called on.

This function is affected by `props_break_max_pieces_perframe`, `props_break_max_pieces`, `prop_active_gib_limit` and `prop_active_gib_max_fade_time` console variables.
NOTES: Despite existing on client, it doesn't actually do anything on client.
WARNINGS:
Large numbers of serverside gibs will cause lag.

You can avoid this cost by spawning the gibs on the client using [Entity:GibBreakClient](/gmod/Entity:GibBreakClient)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: force
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The force to apply to the created gibs

HasBoneManipulations.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether or not the bone manipulation functions have ever been called on given  entity.

Related functions are [Entity:ManipulateBonePosition](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBonePosition), [Entity:ManipulateBoneAngles](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneAngles), [Entity:ManipulateBoneJiggle](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneJiggle), and [Entity:ManipulateBoneScale](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneScale).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will return true if the entity's bones have ever been manipulated. Resetting the position/angles/jiggle/scaling to 0,0,0 will not affect this function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: True if the entity has been bone manipulated, false otherwise.

HasFlexManipulatior.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether or not the the entity has had flex manipulations performed with [Entity:SetFlexWeight](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexWeight) or [Entity:SetFlexScale](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexScale).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: True if the entity has flex manipulations, false otherwise.

HasSpawnFlags.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether this entity has the specified spawnflags bits set.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: spawnFlags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The spawnflag bits to check, see [SF](/gmod/Enums/SF).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity has that spawnflag set or not.

HeadTarget.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position of the head of this entity, NPCs use this internally to aim at their targets.
NOTES: This only works on players and NPCs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector of where the attack comes from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The head position.

Health.DESCRIPTION: Returns the health of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: health

Ignite.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the entity on fire.

See also [Entity:Extinguish](/gmod/Entity:Extinguish).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long to keep the entity ignited, in seconds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the ignition, will ignite everything around the entity that is in this radius.

InitializeAsClientEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes this entity as being clientside only.

Only works on entities fully created clientside, and as such it currently has no use due to this being automatically called by [ents.CreateClientProp](/gmod/ents.CreateClientProp), [ents.CreateClientside](/gmod/ents.CreateClientside), [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) and [ClientsideScene](/gmod/Global.ClientsideScene).
DEPRECATED:
This function got disabled and will always throw an error if it's used. This is the error: 
```
[ERROR] InitializeAsClientEntity is deprecated and should no longer be used.
```

Input.DESCRIPTION:
Fires input to the entity with the ability to make another entity responsible, bypassing the event queue system.

You should only use this function over [Entity:Fire](/gmod/Entity:Fire) if you know what you are doing.

See [Entity:Fire](/gmod/Entity:Fire) for a function that conforms to the internal map IO event queue and [GM:AcceptInput](/gmod/GM:AcceptInput) for a hook that can intercept inputs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the input to fire

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that caused this input (i.e. the player who pushed a button)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: caller
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that is triggering this input (i.e. the button that was pushed)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: param
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to give to the input. Can be either a [string](/gmod/string), a [number](/gmod/number) or a [boolean](/gmod/boolean).

InstallDataTable.DESCRIPTION: Sets up Data Tables from entity to use with [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar).

InvalidateBoneCache.DESCRIPTION:
Resets the entity's bone cache values in order to prepare for a model change.

This should be called after calling [Entity:SetPoseParameter](/gmod/Entity:SetPoseParameter).

IsConstrained.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the entity has constraints attached to it

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
This will only update clientside if the server calls it first. This only checks constraints added through the [constraint](/gmod/constraint) so this will not react to map constraints.

For a serverside alternative, see [constraint.HasConstraints](/gmod/constraint.HasConstraints)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is constrained or not.

IsConstraint.DESCRIPTION:
Returns if entity is constraint or not.

This also means that [Entity:GetConstrainedPhysObjects](/gmod/Entity:GetConstrainedPhysObjects). [Entity:GetConstrainedEntities](/gmod/Entity:GetConstrainedEntities) and  [Entity:SetPhysConstraintObjects](/gmod/Entity:SetPhysConstraintObjects) can be used on this entity.
WARNINGS: For some constraint entities, such as `phys_spring`, `phys_slideconstraint`, `phys_torque` and `logic_collision_pair`, this function will return `false`!

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the entity a constraint or not

IsDormant.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the entity is dormant or not.

Networked entities become dormant clientside when they leave the [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community"). This typically means they are no longer visible by the local player, and will not receive updates from the server.

Server side, entities can only be dormant during level transitions by default.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is dormant or not.

IsEffectActive.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether an entity has engine effect applied or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: effect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The effect to check for, see [EF](/gmod/Enums/EF).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity has the engine effect applied or not.

IsEFlagSet.DESCRIPTION: Checks if given flag is set or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The engine flag to test, see [EFL](/gmod/Enums/EFL)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is set or not

IsFlagSet.DESCRIPTION: Checks if given flag(s) is set or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The engine flag(s) to test, see [FL](/gmod/Enums/FL)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is set or not

IsInWorld.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity is in the world (not inside a wall or outside of the map).
NOTES: Internally this function uses [util.IsInWorld](/gmod/util.IsInWorld), that means that this function only checks [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos) of the entity. If an entity is only partially inside a wall, or has a weird GetPos offset, this function may not give reliable output.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: False if the entity is inside a wall or outside of the map, true otherwise.

IsLagCompensated.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity is lag compensated or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is lag compensated or not.

IsLineOfSightClear.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the target is in line of sight.
NOTES: This will only work when called on CBaseCombatCharacter entities. This includes players, NPCs, grenades, RPG rockets, crossbow bolts, and physics cannisters.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The target to test. You can also supply an [Entity](/gmod/Entity) instead of a [Vector](/gmod/Vector)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the line of sight is clear

IsMarkedForDeletion.DESCRIPTION:
Determines if a given Entity is going to be removed at the start of the next tick.

		This will return `true` for an [Entity](/gmod/Entity) after [Entity:Remove](/gmod/Entity:Remove) is called on it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the Entity is going to be removed, `false` otherwise.

IsNextBot.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot) or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is an NextBot entity or not.

IsNPC.DESCRIPTION:
Checks if the entity is an [NPC](/gmod/NPC) or not.

This will return false for [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot)s, see [Entity:IsNextBot](/gmod/Entity:IsNextBot) for that.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is an NPC.

IsOnFire.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity is on fire.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is on fire or not.

IsOnGround.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the entity is on ground or not.

Internally, this checks if [FL_ONGROUND](/gmod/Enums/FL) is set on the entity.

This function is an alias of [Entity:OnGround](/gmod/Entity:OnGround).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is on ground or not.

IsPlayer.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a player or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is a player.

IsPlayerHolding.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the entity is being held by a player. Either by physics gun, gravity gun or use-key (+use).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: If multiple players are holding an object and one drops it, this will return false despite the object still being held.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: IsBeingHeld

IsPlayingGesture.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether there's a gesture with the given activity being played.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity to test. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether there's a gesture is given activity being played.

IsPointInBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether a given point is within the entity's Orientated Bounding Box.

This relies on the entity having a collision mesh (not a physics object) and will be affected by `SOLID_NONE`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: point
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The point to test, in world space coordinates.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the point is within the entity's bounds.

IsRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a ragdoll, or became a ragdoll. Internally checks whether [kRenderFXRagdoll](kRenderFX) is set.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is ragdoll or not

IsScripted.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a SENT or a built-in entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if entity is scripted ( SENT ), false if not ( A built-in engine entity )

IsSequenceFinished.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity's current sequence is finished or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity's sequence is finished or not.

IsSolid.DESCRIPTION:
Returns if the entity is solid or not.
Very useful for determining if the entity is a trigger or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is solid or not.

IsValid.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the entity is a valid entity or not.

An entity is valid if:
* It is not a [NULL](/gmod/Global_Variables) entity
* It is not the worldspawn entity ([game.GetWorld](/gmod/game.GetWorld))



It will check whether the given variable contains an object (an Entity) or nothing at all for you. See examples.


This might be a cause for a lot of headache. Usually happening during networking etc., when completely valid entities suddenly become invalid on the client, but are never filtered with IsValid(). See [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) for more details.
NOTES: Instead of calling this method directly, it's a good idea to call the global [IsValid](/gmod/Global.IsValid) instead, however if you're sure the variable you're using is always an entity object it's better to use this method
WARNINGS: NULL entities can still be assigned with key/value pairs, but they will be instantly negated. See example 3

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true if the entity is valid, false otherwise

IsValidLayer.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the given layer ID is valid and exists on this entity.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the given layer ID is valid and exists on this entity.

IsVehicle.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a vehicle or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is a vehicle.

IsWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the entity is a weapon or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is a weapon

IsWidget.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the entity is a widget or not.

This is used by the "Edit Bones" context menu property.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is a widget or not.

IsWorld.DESCRIPTION: Returns if this entity is the map entity `Entity[0] worldspawn`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether this entity is the world entity.

LocalToWorld.DESCRIPTION: Translates a vector relative to the entity's coordinate system into a worldspace vector.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lpos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A local space vector.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding worldspace vector.

LocalToWorldAngles.DESCRIPTION: Translates an angle relative to the entity's coordinate system to a worldspace angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A local space angle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding worldspace angle.

LookupAttachment.DESCRIPTION: Returns the attachment index of the given attachment name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachmentName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the attachment.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment index, or 0 if the attachment does not exist and -1 if the model is invalid.

LookupBone.DESCRIPTION:
Gets the bone index of the given bone name, returns `nil` if the bone does not exist. 


See [Entity:GetBoneName](/gmod/Entity:GetBoneName) for the inverse of this function.
NOTES: When called on [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon)s equipped by any Player, this will return their viewmodel's bone index instead of worldmodel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the bone.

Common generic bones ( for player models and some HL2 models ): 
* ValveBiped.Bip01_Head1
* ValveBiped.Bip01_Spine
* ValveBiped.Anim_Attachment_RH

Common hand bones (left hand equivalents also available, replace _R_ with _L_)
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Hand
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Forearm
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Foot
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Thigh
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Calf
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Shoulder
* ValveBiped.Bip01_R_Elbow

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the given bone name, or `nil` if the bone doesn't exist on the Entity.

LookupPoseParameter.DESCRIPTION: Returns pose parameter ID from its name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Pose parameter name

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the given pose parameter name, if it exists, -1 otherwise

LookupSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Returns sequence ID from either sequence name or activity name. See [Entity:GetSequenceName](/gmod/Entity:GetSequenceName) for a function that does the opposite.

**Sequences** are animations tied to a specific model. Different models can have sequences with same names, but have different IDs.  
Sequences can also be tied to certain activities ([ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT)), see [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sequence name. Input string can alternatively be an activity name, to lookup an activity from its name and get a sequence as result.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Sequence ID for that name. This **will** differ for models with same sequence names. Will be `-1` when the sequence is invalid or not found.
The sequence duration, or `0` if the sequence is invalid or there's no sequence with given name on entity's current model.

MakePhysicsObjectAShadow.DESCRIPTION:
Turns the [Entity:GetPhysicsObject](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObject) into a physics shadow.
It's used internally for the Player's and NPC's physics object, and certain HL2 entities such as the crane.

A physics shadow can be used to have static entities that never move by setting both arguments to false.
NOTES: Unlike [Entity:PhysicsInitShadow](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitShadow), this function doesn't remove the current physics object.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: allowPhysicsMovement
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to allow the physics shadow to move under stress.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: allowPhysicsRotation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to allow the physics shadow to rotate under stress.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
When used repeatedly serverside, this method is strongly discouraged due to the huge network traffic produced

As of update `2024.10.29` this has been resolved. However, network traffic is still generated and should be taken into consideration.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the bone you want to manipulate

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Angle to apply.

The angle is relative to the original bone angle, not relative to the world or the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: networking
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: boolean to network these changes (if called from server)

ManipulateBoneJiggle.DESCRIPTION: Manipulates the bone's jiggle status. This allows non jiggly bones to become jiggly.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the bone you want to manipulate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The jiggle bone type. There are currently the following options:
* `0` = No jiggle override, use model default
* `1` = Force jiggle, with hardcoded settings
* `2` = Force disable jiggle bone

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the bone you want to manipulate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position vector to apply. Note that the position is relative to the original bone position, not relative to the world or the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: networking
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: boolean to network these changes (if called from server)

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not scale procedural bones.

NOTES: This silently fails when given a Vector with nan values, hiding the vertices associated with the bone. See example below.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the bone you want to manipulate

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Scale vector to apply. Note that the scale is relative to the original bone scale, not relative to the world or the entity.

MapCreationID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns entity's map creation ID. Unlike [Entity:EntIndex](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex) or [Entity:GetCreationID](/gmod/Entity:GetCreationID), it will always be the same on same map, no matter how much you clean up or restart it.

It may change if the map is recompiled, even if no edits were made. It will definitely change if entities are added or removed from the map file.

To be used in conjunction with [ents.GetMapCreatedEntity](/gmod/ents.GetMapCreatedEntity). See also [Entity:CreatedByMap](/gmod/Entity:CreatedByMap).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The map creation ID or -1 if the entity is not compiled into the map.
NOTES: If the ID exists, it is identical to the entity's order number as it appears in Lump 1 of the BSP file. It is believed to start at 1234 for some reason.

MarkShadowAsDirty.DESCRIPTION: Refreshes the shadow of the entity.

MuzzleFlash.DESCRIPTION: Fires the muzzle flash effect of the weapon the entity is carrying. This only creates a light effect and is often called alongside [Weapon:SendWeaponAnim](/gmod/Weapon:SendWeaponAnim)

NearestPoint.DESCRIPTION:
Performs a Ray-Orientated Bounding Box intersection from the given position to the origin of the OBBox with the entity and returns the hit position on the OBBox.

This relies on the entity having a collision mesh (not a physics object) and will be affected by `SOLID_NONE`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to start the intersection from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The nearest hit point of the entity's bounding box in world coordinates.

NetworkVar.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a network variable on the entity and adds Set/Get functions for it. This function should only be called in [ENTITY:SetupDataTables](/gmod/ENTITY:SetupDataTables).

See [Entity:NetworkVarNotify](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVarNotify) for a function to hook NetworkVar changes.




Combining this function with [util.TableToJSON](/gmod/util.TableToJSON) can also provide a way to network tables as serialized strings.
NOTES:
Entity NetworkVars are influenced by the return value of [ENTITY:UpdateTransmitState](/gmod/ENTITY:UpdateTransmitState).  
	So if you use the **PVS**(**default**), then the NetworkVars can be different for each client.
WARNINGS: Make sure to not call the SetDT* and your custom set methods on the client realm unless you know exactly what you are doing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Supported choices:

* `String` (up to 511 characters)
* `Bool`
* `Float`
* `Int` (32-bit signed integer)
* `Vector`
* `Angle`
* `Entity`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: slot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Each network variable has to have a unique slot. The slot is per type - so you can have an int in slot `0`, a bool in slot `0` and a float in slot `0` etc. You can't have two ints in slot `0`, instead you would do a int in slot `0` and another int in slot `1`.

The max slots for strings `4` - so you should pick a number between `0` and `3`.

The max slots for everything else `32` - so you should pick a number between `0` and `31`.

This can be omitted entirely (arguments will shift) and it will use the next available slot.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name will affect how you access it. If you call it `Foo` you would add two new functions on your entity - `SetFoo()` and `GetFoo()`. So be careful that what you call it won't collide with any existing functions (don't call it `Pos` for example).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extended
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of extended information.

`KeyName`
* Allows the NetworkVar to be set using [Entity:SetKeyValue](/gmod/Entity:SetKeyValue).
* This is **required** for the entity editing to work.

This is useful if you're making an entity that you want to be loaded in a map. The sky entity uses this.

`Edit`
* The edit key lets you mark this variable as editable. See [Editable Entities](/gmod/Editable%20Entities) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Supported choices:

* `String` (up to 511 characters)
* `Bool`
* `Float`
* `Int` (32-bit signed integer)
* `Vector`
* `Angle`
* `Entity`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name will affect how you access it. If you call it `Foo` you would add two new functions on your entity - `SetFoo()` and `GetFoo()`. So be careful that what you call it won't collide with any existing functions (don't call it `Pos` for example).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extended
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of extended information.

`KeyName`
* Allows the NetworkVar to be set using [Entity:SetKeyValue](/gmod/Entity:SetKeyValue).
* This is **required** for the entity editing to work.

This is useful if you're making an entity that you want to be loaded in a map. The sky entity uses this.

`Edit`
* The edit key lets you mark this variable as editable. See [Editable Entities](/gmod/Editable%20Entities) for more information.

NetworkVarElement.DESCRIPTION:
Similarly to [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar), creates a network variable on the entity and adds Set/Get functions for it. This method stores it's value as a member value of a vector or an angle. This allows to go beyond the normal variable limit of [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) for `Int` and `Float` types, at the expense of `Vector` and `Angle` limit.

This function should only be called in [ENTITY:SetupDataTables](/gmod/ENTITY:SetupDataTables).
WARNINGS: Make sure to not call the SetDT* and your custom set methods on the client realm unless you know exactly what you are doing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Supported choices:
* `Vector`
* `Angle`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: slot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The slot for this `Vector` or `Angle`, from `0` to `31`. See [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) for more detailed explanation.

This can be omitted entirely (arguments will shift) and it will use the next available slot.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: element
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Which element of a `Vector` or an `Angle` to store the value on. This can be `p`, `y`, `r` for [Angle](/gmod/Angle)s, and `x`, `y`, `z` for [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name will affect how you access it. If you call it `Foo` you would add two new functions on your entity - `SetFoo()` and `GetFoo()`. So be careful that what you call it won't collide with any existing functions (don't call it "Pos" for example).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extended
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of extra information. See [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) for details.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Supported choices:
* `Vector`
* `Angle`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: element
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Which element of a `Vector` or an `Angle` to store the value on. This can be `p`, `y`, `r` for [Angle](/gmod/Angle)s, and `x`, `y`, `z` for [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name will affect how you access it. If you call it `Foo` you would add two new functions on your entity - `SetFoo()` and `GetFoo()`. So be careful that what you call it won't collide with any existing functions (don't call it "Pos" for example).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extended
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of extra information. See [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) for details.

NetworkVarNotify.DESCRIPTION: Creates a callback that will execute when the given network variable changes - that is, when the `Set

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of variable to track changes of.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to call when the variable changes.

NextThink.DESCRIPTION:
Controls when, relative to [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime), the [Entity](/gmod/Entity) will next run its Think function.

For Scripted Entities, this is the [ENTITY:Think](/gmod/ENTITY:Think) function.  
For engine Entities, this is an internal function whose behavior will depend on the specific Entity type.


For a Client-side equivalent, see [Entity:SetNextClientThink](/gmod/Entity:SetNextClientThink).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not work with SWEPs or Nextbots.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: timestamp
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The timestamp, relative to [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime), when the next think should occur.

OBBCenter.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the center of an entity's collision bounding box as a local vector.

See also [Entity:GetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetCollisionBounds), [Entity:OBBMins](/gmod/Entity:OBBMins) and [Entity:OBBMaxs](/gmod/Entity:OBBMaxs).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The center of an entity's bounding box relative to its [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos).

OBBMaxs.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the highest corner of an entity's collision bounding box as a local vector.

See also [Entity:GetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetCollisionBounds), [Entity:OBBMins](/gmod/Entity:OBBMins) and [Entity:OBBCenter](/gmod/Entity:OBBCenter).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The local position of the highest corner of the entity's oriented bounding box.

OBBMins.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the lowest corner of an entity's collision bounding box as a local vector.

See also [Entity:GetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetCollisionBounds), [Entity:OBBMaxs](/gmod/Entity:OBBMaxs) and [Entity:OBBCenter](/gmod/Entity:OBBCenter).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The local position of the lowest corner of the entity's oriented bounding box.

ObjectCaps.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the entity's capabilities as a bitfield.

In the engine this function is mostly used to check the use type, the save/restore system and level transitions flags.

Even though the function is defined shared, it is not guaranteed to return the same value across states.
NOTES: The enums for this are not currently implemented in Lua, however you can access the defines [here](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/shared/baseentity_shared.h#L21-L38).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The bitfield, a combination of the [FCAP_](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/55ed12f8d1eb6887d348be03aee5573d44177ffb/mp/src/game/shared/baseentity_shared.h#L21-L38) flags.

OnGround.DESCRIPTION:
Returns true if the entity is on the ground, and false if it isn't.

Internally, this checks if [FL_ONGROUND](/gmod/Enums/FL) is set on the entity. This is only updated for players and NPCs, and thus won't inherently work for other entities.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity is on the ground or not.

PassesDamageFilter.DESCRIPTION:
Tests whether the damage passes the entity filter.

This will call [ENTITY:PassesDamageFilter](/gmod/ENTITY:PassesDamageFilter) on scripted entities of the type "filter".
NOTES: This function only works on entities of the type "filter". ( filter_* entities, including base game filter entites )

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dmg
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage info to test

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the damage info passes the entity filter.

PassesFilter.DESCRIPTION:
Tests whether the entity passes the entity filter.

This will call [ENTITY:PassesFilter](/gmod/ENTITY:PassesFilter) on scripted entities of the type "filter".
NOTES: This function only works on entities of the type "filter". ( filter_* entities, including base game filter entites )

ARGUMENTS.NAME: caller
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The initiator of the test.

For example the trigger this filter entity is used in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to test against the entity filter.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity info passes the entity filter.

PhysicsDestroy.DESCRIPTION: Destroys the current physics object of an entity.
NOTES: Cannot be used on a ragdoll or the world entity.
WARNINGS: This function cannot be used when called from a physics callback.

PhysicsFromMesh.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes the physics mesh of the entity from a triangle soup defined by a table of vertices. The resulting mesh is hollow, may contain holes, and always has a volume of 0.

While this is very useful for static geometry such as terrain displacements, it is advised to use [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) or [Entity:PhysicsInitMultiConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitMultiConvex) for moving solid objects instead.

[Entity:EnableCustomCollisions](/gmod/Entity:EnableCustomCollisions) needs to be called if you want players to collide with the entity correctly.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertices
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of Vectors. Every 3 vertices define a triangle in the physics mesh

Alternatively, you can input a table consisting of [Structures/MeshVertex](/gmod/Structures/MeshVertex) (only the `pos` element is taken into account).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceprop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: massCenterOveride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `nil` otherwise.

PhysicsInit.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes the [physics object](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObject) of the entity using its current [model](/gmod/Entity:GetModel). Deletes the previous physics object if it existed and the new object creation was successful.

If the entity's current model has no physics mesh associated to it, no physics object will be created and the previous object will still exist, if applicable.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

NOTES:
When called clientside, this will not create a valid [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) if the model hasn't been [precached](/gmod/util.PrecacheModel) serverside.

If successful, this function will automatically call [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid)( solidType ) and [Entity:SetSolidFlags](/gmod/Entity:SetSolidFlags)( 0 ).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: solidType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The solid type of the physics object to create, see [SOLID](/gmod/Enums/SOLID). Should be `SOLID_VPHYSICS` in most cases.
NOTES: Using `SOLID_NONE` will only delete the current physics object - it does not create a new one.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: massCenterOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `false` otherwise.

PhysicsInitBox.DESCRIPTION:
Makes the physics object of the entity a AABB.

This function will automatically destroy any previous physics objects and do the following:
* [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid)( `SOLID_BBOX` )
* [Entity:SetMoveType](/gmod/Entity:SetMoveType)( `MOVETYPE_VPHYSICS` )
* [Entity:SetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetCollisionBounds)( `mins`, `maxs` )

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

NOTES: If the volume of the resulting box is 0 (the mins and maxs are the same), the mins and maxs will be changed to [Vector](/gmod/Global.Vector)( -1, -1, -1 ) and [Vector](/gmod/Global.Vector)( 1, 1, 1 ), respectively.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum position of the box. This is automatically ordered with the maxs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum position of the box. This is automatically ordered with the mins.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceprop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: massCenterOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `nil` otherwise. This fails when the game cannot create any more [PhysCollide](/gmod/PhysCollide)s.

PhysicsInitConvex.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes the physics mesh of the entity with a convex mesh defined by a table of points. The resulting mesh is the  of all the input points. If successful, the previous physics object will be removed.

This is the standard way of creating moving physics objects with a custom convex shape. For more complex, concave shapes, see [Entity:PhysicsInitMultiConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitMultiConvex).

You may be expected to call [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid) with desired solid type **before** calling this function.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

You can use the following workaround for movement, though clientside collisions will still be broken.
```
function ENT:Think()
	if ( CLIENT ) then
		local physobj = self:GetPhysicsObject()

		if ( IsValid( physobj ) ) then
			physobj:SetPos( self:GetPos() )
			physobj:SetAngles( self:GetAngles() )
		end
	end
end
```

ARGUMENTS.NAME: points
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of eight [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s, in local coordinates, to be used in the computation of the convex mesh. Order does not matter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceprop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: massCenterOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `false` otherwise.

PhysicsInitMultiConvex.DESCRIPTION:
An advanced version of [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) which initializes a physics object from multiple convex meshes. This should be used for physics objects with a custom shape which cannot be represented by a single convex mesh.

If successful, the previous physics object will be removed.

You may be expected to call [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid) with desired solid type **before** calling this function.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertices
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table consisting of tables of [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s. Each sub-table defines a set of points to be used in the computation of one convex mesh.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceprop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: massCenterOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, overwrites the center of mass for the created physics object.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `nil` otherwise.

PhysicsInitShadow.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes the entity's [physics object](/gmod/PhysObj) as a *physics shadow*. Physics shadows can react to the environment physically (see the arguments to the function), and can push other physics objects around, but are ultimately constrained to the entity's position and angles: the physics object will attempt to return to the entity's coordinates every simulation tick.

Internally, this creates a new physics object, copies the properties of the current physics object to it if one exists, and replaces the entity's physics object with the shadow. This is used internally for Player and NPC physics objects, certain HL2 entities such as the crane and barnacle tongue, parented physics entities, etc.

A physics shadow can be used to have static physics entities that never move by setting both arguments to false.

The created physics object will depend on the entity's solidity `SOLID_NONE` will not create a physics object, `SOLID_BBOX` will create a Axis-Aligned BBox one, `SOLID_OBB` will create Orientated Bounding Box one, and anything else will use the models' physics mesh.

See also [Structures/ShadowControlParams](/gmod/Structures/ShadowControlParams).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: allowPhysicsMovement
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to allow the physics shadow to move under stress.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: allowPhysicsRotation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to allow the physics shadow to rotate under stress.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return `true` on success, `false` otherwise.

PhysicsInitSphere.DESCRIPTION:
Makes the physics object of the entity a sphere.

This function will automatically destroy any previous physics objects and do the following:
* [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid)( `SOLID_BBOX` )
* [Entity:SetMoveType](/gmod/Entity:SetMoveType)( `MOVETYPE_VPHYSICS` )

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physmat
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physical material from [surfaceproperties.txt](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/scripts/surfaceproperties.txt) or added with [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `false` otherwise

PhysicsInitStatic.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes a static physics object of the entity using its [current model](/gmod/Entity:GetModel). If successful, the previous physics object is removed.

This is what used by entities such as `func_breakable`, `prop_dynamic`, `item_suitcharger`, `prop_thumper` and `npc_rollermine` while it is in its "buried" state in the Half-Life 2 Campaign.

If the entity's current model has no physics mesh associated to it, no physics object will be created.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Clientside physics objects on serverside entities do not move properly in some cases. Physics objects should only created on the server or you will experience incorrect physgun beam position, prediction issues, and other unexpected behavior.

A workaround is available on the [Entity:PhysicsInitConvex](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitConvex) page.

NOTES: This function will automatically call [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid)( `solidType` ).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: solidType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The solid type of the physics object to create, see [SOLID](/gmod/Enums/SOLID). Should be `SOLID_VPHYSICS` in most cases.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` on success, `false` otherwise. This will fail if the entity's current model has no associated physics mesh.

PhysWake.DESCRIPTION: Wakes up the entity's physics object

PlayScene.DESCRIPTION: Makes the entity play a .vcd scene. [All scenes from Half-Life 2](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Half-Life_2_Scenes_List).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scene
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Filepath to scene.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay in seconds until the scene starts playing.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Estimated length of the scene.
The scene entity, removing which will stop the scene from continuing to play.

PointAtEntity.DESCRIPTION: Changes an entities angles so that it faces the target entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to face.

PrecacheGibs.DESCRIPTION:
Precaches gibs for the entity's model.

Normally this function should be ran when the entity is spawned, for example the [ENTITY:Initialize](/gmod/ENTITY:Initialize), after [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel) is called.

This is required for [Entity:GibBreakServer](/gmod/Entity:GibBreakServer) and [Entity:GibBreakClient](/gmod/Entity:GibBreakClient) to work.

RETURNS.NAME: gibCount
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of gibs the prop has

RagdollSolve.DESCRIPTION: Normalizes the ragdoll. This is used alongside Kinect in [Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction](/gmod/Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction), for more info see ragdoll_motion entity.

RagdollStopControlling.DESCRIPTION: Sets the function to build the ragdoll. This is used alongside Kinect in [Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction](/gmod/Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction), for more info see ragdoll_motion entity.

RagdollUpdatePhysics.DESCRIPTION: Makes the physics objects follow the set bone positions. This is used alongside Kinect in [Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction](/gmod/Entity:SetRagdollBuildFunction), for more info see ragdoll_motion entity.

Remove.DESCRIPTION:
Removes (or deletes) a given [Entity](/gmod/Entity). 

		The Entity will continue to exist until the start of the next tick.  

		To check if an Entity will be removed in the next tick, see [Entity:IsMarkedForDeletion](/gmod/Entity:IsMarkedForDeletion)

RemoveAllDecals.DESCRIPTION: Removes all decals from the entities surface.

NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

Layer removal procedures aren't immediate. Layer removal functions actually manipulate [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight) down to 0, then remove the layer in next intervals. If the targeted layer's weight keeps changing, your layer will not be removed.

RemoveCallback.DESCRIPTION: Removes a callback previously added with [Entity:AddCallback](/gmod/Entity:AddCallback)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hook
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hook name to remove. See [Entity Callbacks](/gmod/Entity%20Callbacks)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callbackid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The callback id previously retrieved with the return of [Entity:AddCallback](/gmod/Entity:AddCallback) or [Entity:GetCallbacks](/gmod/Entity:GetCallbacks)

RemoveCallOnRemove.DESCRIPTION: Removes a function previously added via [Entity:CallOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:CallOnRemove).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Identifier of the function given to [Entity:CallOnRemove](/gmod/Entity:CallOnRemove).

RemoveEffects.DESCRIPTION: Removes an engine effect applied to an entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: effect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The effect to remove, see [EF](/gmod/Enums/EF).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag to remove, see [EFL](/gmod/Enums/EFL)

RemoveFlags.DESCRIPTION: Removes specified flag(s) from the entity

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag(s) to remove, see [FL](/gmod/Enums/FL)

RemoveFromMotionController.DESCRIPTION:
Removes a [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ect from the entity's motion controller so that [ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate](/gmod/ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate) will no longer be called for given [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ect.

You must first create a motion controller with [Entity:StartMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StartMotionController).
NOTES: Only works on a scripted [Entity](/gmod/Entity) of anim type

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physObj
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) to remove from the motion controller.

RemoveGesture.DESCRIPTION: Removes and stops the gesture with given activity. Same as [Entity:RemoveLayer](/gmod/Entity:RemoveLayer) with [Entity:FindGestureLayer](/gmod/Entity:FindGestureLayer).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

Layer removal procedures aren't immediate. Layer removal functions actually manipulate [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight) down to 0, then remove the layer in next intervals. If the targeted layer's weight keeps changing, your layer will not be removed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity remove. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

RemoveInternalConstraint.DESCRIPTION:
Breaks internal Ragdoll constrains, so you can for example separate an arm from the body of a ragdoll and preserve all physics.

The visual mesh will still stretch as if it was properly connected unless the ragdoll model is specifically designed to avoid that.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: num
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Which constraint to break, values below 0 mean break them all

RemoveLayer.DESCRIPTION: Removes the given layer by ID. See also [Entity:RemoveGesture](/gmod/Entity:RemoveGesture).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

Layer removal procedures aren't immediate. Layer removal functions actually manipulate [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight) down to 0, then remove the layer in next intervals. If the targeted layer's weight keeps changing, your layer will not be removed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The layer ID to remove.

RemoveSolidFlags.DESCRIPTION: Removes solid flag(s) from the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag(s) to remove, see [FSOLID](/gmod/Enums/FSOLID).

RemoveSpawnFlags.DESCRIPTION:
Removes a SpawnFlag from the current SpawnFlags of an Entity.

SpawnFlags can easily be found on https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/.
NOTES:
See also [Entity:AddSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:AddSpawnFlags), [Entity:SetSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:SetSpawnFlags)

	Using [SF Enumerations](/gmod/Enums/SF) won't work, if this function is ran clientside due to the enumerations being defined only Serverside. Use the actual SpawnFlag number.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flag
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The SpawnFlag to remove from the Entity

ResetSequence.DESCRIPTION: Plays an animation on the entity. This may not always work on engine entities.
NOTES:
This will not work properly if called directly after calling [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel). Consider waiting until the next Tick.

Will not work on players due to the animations being reset every frame by the base gamemode animation system. See [GM:CalcMainActivity](/gmod/GM:CalcMainActivity).

For custom scripted entities you will want to apply example from [ENTITY:Think](/gmod/ENTITY:Think) to make animations work.
WARNINGS: This will not reset the animation on viewmodels, use [Entity:SendViewModelMatchingSequence](/gmod/Entity:SendViewModelMatchingSequence) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence to play. Also accepts strings.
NOTES: If set to a string, the function will automatically call [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence) to retrieve the sequence ID as a number.

ResetSequenceInfo.DESCRIPTION: Reset entity sequence info such as playback rate, ground speed, last event check, etc.

Respawn.DESCRIPTION:
Makes the entity/weapon respawn.

Only usable on HL2/HL:S pickups and any weapons. Seems to be buggy with weapons.
Very unreliable.

RestartGesture.DESCRIPTION: Restarts the entity's animation gesture. If the given gesture is already playing, it will reset it and play it from the beginning.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity number to send to the entity. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT) and [Entity:GetSequenceActivity](/gmod/Entity:GetSequenceActivity)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: addIfMissing
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Add/start the gesture to if it has not been yet started.

RestoreNetworkVars.DESCRIPTION: Calls the associated `Entity:Set*` function for each network var provided.
NOTES: This function will only work on entities which had [Entity:InstallDataTable](/gmod/Entity:InstallDataTable) called on them, which is done automatically for players and all [Scripted Entities](/gmod/Scripted%20Entities)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The data from [Entity:GetNetworkVars](/gmod/Entity:GetNetworkVars).

SelectWeightedSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Returns sequence ID corresponding to given activity ID.

Multiple sequences can be assigned to a single [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT), in which case a random one will be selected. This can be used for example to randomize idle animations (and is used for that by built-in weapons) without the need to code logic for this.  
See also [Entity:SelectWeightedSequenceSeeded](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequenceSeeded).

Opposite of [Entity:GetSequenceActivity](/gmod/Entity:GetSequenceActivity).

Similar to [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity ID, see [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID, or `-1` if not found.

SelectWeightedSequenceSeeded.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the sequence ID corresponding to given activity ID, and uses the provided seed for random selection. The seed should be the same server-side and client-side if used in a predicted environment.

See [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence) for a provided-seed version of this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The activity ID, see [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The seed to use for randomly selecting a sequence in the case the activity ID has multiple sequences bound to it. [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence) uses the same seed as [util.SharedRandom](/gmod/util.SharedRandom) internally for this.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID, or `-1` if not found.

SendViewModelMatchingSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Sends sequence animation to the view model. It is recommended to use this for view model animations, instead of [Entity:ResetSequence](/gmod/Entity:ResetSequence).

This function is only usable on view models.
NOTES: Predicted viewmodels will have their sequence and cycle reset during prediction checks, making this function appear to do nothing unless also called on the server.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seq
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence ID returned by [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence) or  [Entity:SelectWeightedSequence](/gmod/Entity:SelectWeightedSequence).

SequenceDuration.DESCRIPTION: Returns length of currently played sequence.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will return incorrect results for weapons and viewmodels clientside in thirdperson.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seqid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A sequence ID to return the length specific sequence of instead of the entity's main/currently playing sequence.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The length of the sequence

NOTES: Actually binds to CBaseEntity::SetLocalVelocity() which sets the entity's velocity due to movement in the world from forces such as gravity. Does not include velocity from entity-on-entity collision or other world movement.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: velocity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new velocity to set.

SetAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets the angles of the entity.
NOTES: To set a player's angles, use [Player:SetEyeAngles](/gmod/Player:SetEyeAngles) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new angles.

SetAnimation.DESCRIPTION: Sets a player's third-person animation. Mainly used by [Weapon](/gmod/Weapon)s to start the player's weapon attack and reload animations.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: playerAnim
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Player animation, see [PLAYER](/gmod/Enums/PLAYER).

SetAnimTime.DESCRIPTION: Sets the start time (relative to [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime)) of the current animation, which is used to determine [Entity:GetCycle](/gmod/Entity:GetCycle). Should be less than CurTime to play an animation from the middle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: time
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The time the animation was supposed to begin.

SetAttachment.DESCRIPTION:
Parents the sprite to an attachment on another model.

Works only on `env_sprite` entities.

Despite existing on client, it doesn't actually do anything on client.
DEPRECATED: You should be using Entity:SetParent instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to attach/parent to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachment
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment ID to parent to

SetBloodColor.DESCRIPTION: Sets the blood color this entity uses.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bloodColor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An integer corresponding to [BLOOD_COLOR](/gmod/Enums/BLOOD_COLOR).

SetBodygroup.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the currently active [Sub Model ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#submodels) for the Body Group corresponding to the given [Body Group ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#id) of the [Entity's](/gmod/Entity) model.

Bodygroups, for which [Entity:GetBodygroupCount](/gmod/Entity:GetBodygroupCount) returns `1` or less are considered invalid, and will have no effect in-game.
NOTES: When used on a Weapon, this will modify its viewmodel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bodyGroupId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Body Group ID to set the Sub Model ID of.  
			Body Group IDs start at `0`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: subModelId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Sub Model ID to set as active for this Body Group.  
			Sub Model IDs start at `0`.

SetBodyGroups.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the [Entity's](/gmod/Entity) active Sub Models via a string of [Sub Model IDs](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#submodels) in order from the first [Body Group ID](/gmod/Structures/BodyGroupData#id) to the last.

This is a convenience function for [Entity:SetBodygroup](/gmod/Entity:SetBodygroup).
NOTES: When used on a Weapon, this will modify its viewmodel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: subModelIds
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Sub Model IDs to activate for each Body Group on the Entity's model.

			The first character corresponds with Body Group ID `0`, the second character coressponds to Body Group ID `1`, etc.	

			To support Body Groups with more than `0`-`9` options, values above `9` are represented using alphabetical characters starting with `a` and ending with `z`.

SetBoneController.DESCRIPTION: Sets the specified value on the bone controller with the given ID of this entity, it's used in HL1 to change the head rotation of NPCs, turret aiming and so on.
NOTES: This is the precursor of pose parameters, and only works for Half Life 1: Source models supporting it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneControllerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The ID of the bone controller to set the value to.
Goes from 0 to 3.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set on the specified bone controller.

SetBoneMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Sets the bone matrix of given bone to given matrix. See also [Entity:GetBoneMatrix](/gmod/Entity:GetBoneMatrix). Will cause a uncatchable error when used on `__INVALIDBONE__` bones, see the examples on a way to prevent this.
NOTES: Despite existing serverside, it does nothing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the bone

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrix
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to set.

SetBonePosition.DESCRIPTION: Sets the bone position and angles.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone ID to manipulate

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to set

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angles to set

SetCollisionBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the collision bounds for the entity, which are used for triggers ([Entity:SetTrigger](/gmod/Entity:SetTrigger), [ENTITY:Touch](/gmod/ENTITY:Touch)), and collision (If [Entity:SetSolid](/gmod/Entity:SetSolid) set as [SOLID_BBOX](/gmod/Enums/SOLID)).

Input bounds are relative to [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos)! 
See also [Entity:SetCollisionBoundsWS](/gmod/Entity:SetCollisionBoundsWS).
NOTES: Player collision bounds are reset every frame to player's [Player:SetHull](/gmod/Player:SetHull) values.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector of the bounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum vector of the bounds.

SetCollisionBoundsWS.DESCRIPTION: A convenience function that sets the collision bounds for the entity in world space coordinates by transforming given vectors to entity's local space and passing them to [Entity:SetCollisionBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetCollisionBounds)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vec1
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first vector of the bounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vec2
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The second vector of the bounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: group
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Collision group of the entity, see [COLLISION_GROUP](/gmod/Enums/COLLISION_GROUP)

SetColor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the color of an entity.

Some entities may need a custom [render mode](Enums/RENDERMODE) set for transparency to work. See example 2.
Entities also must have a proper [render group](Enums/RENDERGROUP) set for transparency to work.

When rendering a model manually via [Entity:SetNoDraw](/gmod/Entity:SetNoDraw) inside [ENTITY:Draw](/gmod/ENTITY:Draw), you may need to use [render.SetColorModulation](/gmod/render.SetColorModulation) in the render hook (where you call [Entity:DrawModel](/gmod/Entity:DrawModel)) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The color to set. Uses the [Color](/gmod/Color).

SetColor4Part.DESCRIPTION: Sets the color of an entity without usage of a [Color](/gmod/Global.Color) object.

SetCreator.DESCRIPTION: Sets the creator of this entity. This is set automatically in Sandbox gamemode when spawning SENTs, but is never used/read by default.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The creator

SetCustomCollisionCheck.DESCRIPTION: Marks the entity to call [GM:ShouldCollide](/gmod/GM:ShouldCollide). Not to be confused with [Entity:EnableCustomCollisions](/gmod/Entity:EnableCustomCollisions).
NOTES:
Make sure to use [Entity:CollisionRulesChanged](/gmod/Entity:CollisionRulesChanged) after changing this value.
			Otherwise it can cause crashes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the custom collision check

SetCycle.DESCRIPTION: Sets the progress of the current animation to a specific value between 0 and 1.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Viewmodels overwrite their animation cycle every frame, for prediction/interpolation purposes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The desired cycle value

SetDTAngle.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified angle on the entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to write on the entity's datatable.

SetDTBool.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified bool on the entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bool
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The boolean to write on the entity's metatable.

SetDTEntity.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified entity on this entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to write on this entity's datatable.

SetDTFloat.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified float on the entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: float
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The float to write on the entity's datatable.

SetDTInt.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified integer on the entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: integer
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The integer to write on the entity's datatable. This will be cast to a 32-bit signed integer internally.

SetDTString.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified string on the entity's datatable.
NOTES: The length of these strings are capped at 512 characters.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 3.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: str
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The string to write on the entity's datatable, can't be more than 512 characters per string.

SetDTVector.DESCRIPTION:
This is called internally by the [Entity:NetworkVar](/gmod/Entity:NetworkVar) system, you can use this in cases where using NetworkVar is not possible.

Sets the specified vector on the entity's datatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Goes from 0 to 31.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vec
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to write on the entity's datatable.

SetElasticity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the elasticity of this entity, used by some flying entities such as the Helicopter NPC to determine how much it should bounce around when colliding.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: elasticity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The elasticity to set.

SetEntity.DESCRIPTION: Allows you to set the Start or End entity attachment for the rope.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the variable to modify.
Accepted names are StartEntity and EndEntity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to apply to the specific attachment.

SetEyeTarget.DESCRIPTION: Sets the position an entity's eyes look toward. This works as an override for default behavior. Set to `0,0,0` to disable the override.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
For NPCs and all other entities except ragdolls - the **world position** for the entity to look towards

For ragdolls specifically - a **local position** in front of their `eyes` attachment.

SetFlexScale.DESCRIPTION: Sets the scale of all the flexes of this entity. See [Entity:SetFlexWeight](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexWeight).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new flex scale to set to

SetFlexWeight.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the weight/value of given flex controller.

Setting flex weights spawns an internal networked entity (one per entity face posed) to accommodate networking to clients.
NOTES: Only `96` flex controllers can be set! Flex controllers on models with higher amounts will not be accessible.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the flex to modify weight of.  The range is between `0` and [Entity:GetFlexNum](/gmod/Entity:GetFlexNum) - 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The new weight to set.

The range is [0,1] for entities with [Entity:HasFlexManipulatior](/gmod/Entity:HasFlexManipulatior), and the model-defined input range otherwise ([Entity:GetFlexBounds](/gmod/Entity:GetFlexBounds))

Exceeding the range is allowed, and will amplify the effect (to possibly bad results), exactly like [Entity:SetFlexScale](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexScale) does.

SetFriction.DESCRIPTION:
Sets friction multiplier for this entity when sliding against a surface. Entities default to 1 (100%) and can be higher.

This may not affect all entities, but does work for players (the range is 0 to 10), as well as other entities using [MOVETYPE_STEP](/gmod/Enums/MOVETYPE#MOVETYPE_STEP)

This only multiplies the friction of the entity, to change the value itself use [PhysObj:SetMaterial](/gmod/PhysObj:SetMaterial).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: friction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Friction multiplier

SetGravity.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the gravity multiplier of the entity.

This may not affect affect all entities, but does affect players, and entities with [MOVETYPE_FLYGRAVITY](/gmod/Enums/MOVETYPE#MOVETYPE_FLYGRAVITY), such as projectiles.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: multiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: By how much to multiply the gravity. `1` is normal gravity, `0.5` is half-gravity, etc.

SetGroundEntity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the ground the entity is standing on.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ground
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ground entity.

SetHealth.DESCRIPTION: Sets the health of the entity.
NOTES:
You may want to take [Entity:GetMaxHealth](/gmod/Entity:GetMaxHealth) into account when calculating what to set health to, in case a gamemode has a different max health than 100.  
In some cases, setting health only serverside can cause hitches in movement, for example if something is modifying the player speed based on health.  
To solve this issue, it is better to set it shared in a predicted hook.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: newHealth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New health value.

SetHitboxSet.DESCRIPTION: Sets the current Hitbox set for the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The new hitbox set to set. Can be a name as a [string](/gmod/string), or the ID as a [number](/gmod/number).

If the operation failed, the function will silently fail.

SetIK.DESCRIPTION: Enables or disable the inverse kinematic usage of this entity.
WARNINGS: Calling this with false outside of [ENTITY:Initialize](/gmod/ENTITY:Initialize) requires a model change to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: useIK
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The state of the IK.

SetKeyValue.DESCRIPTION:
Sets Hammer key values on an entity.

You can look up which entities have what key values on the [Valve Developer Community](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/) on entity pages. A  list of basic entities can be found [here](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/List_of_entities).

Alternatively you can look at the `.fgd` files shipped with Garry's Mod in the `bin/` folder with a text editor to see the key values as they appear in Hammer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal key name

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set

SetLagCompensated.DESCRIPTION:
This allows the entity to be lag compensated during [Player:LagCompensation](/gmod/Player:LagCompensation).



As a side note for parented entities, if your entity can be shot at, keep in mind that its collision bounds need to be bigger than the bone's hitbox the entity is parented to, or hull/line traces ( such as the crowbar attack or bullets ) might not hit at all.
NOTES:
Players are lag compensated by default and there's no need to call this function for them.

It's best to not enable lag compensation on parented entities, as the system does not handle it that well ( they will be moved back but then the entity will lag behind ).
Parented entities move back with the parent if it's lag compensated, so if you are making some kind of armor piece you shouldn't do anything.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity should be lag compensated or not.
