SetLayerAutokill.DESCRIPTION: Sets the autokill flag on the layer, making the layer be automatically removed once the animation playback finishes.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The layer ID to change.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: autoKill
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to set or unset the autokill flag.

SetLayerBlendIn.DESCRIPTION: Sets the interval the layer will fully blend in since startup, based on [Entity:GetLayerCycle](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerCycle). Setting this above 0 will enable internal blending of [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Enabling this will prevent looping gestures with autokill disabled to be removed with [Entity:RemoveGesture](/gmod/Entity:RemoveGesture) or [Entity:RemoveAllGestures](/gmod/Entity:RemoveAllGestures) because layer removal functions mark the layer to decrement [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight) and unallocate layer ID in next frames if the layer weight is `0`, but blending functions will still keep manipulating layer weight. 

Therefore; before calling layer cleanup functions, make sure both [Entity:SetLayerBlendIn](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendIn) and [Entity:SetLayerBlendOut](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendOut) are set to `0`.

NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blendIn
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Blend range from 0 to 1.

SetLayerBlendOut.DESCRIPTION: Sets the interval the layer will fully blend out, based on [Entity:GetLayerCycle](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerCycle). Setting this above 0 will enable internal blending of [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION:
Enabling this will prevent looping gestures with autokill disabled to be removed with [Entity:RemoveGesture](/gmod/Entity:RemoveGesture) or [Entity:RemoveAllGestures](/gmod/Entity:RemoveAllGestures) because layer removal functions mark the layer to decrement [Entity:GetLayerWeight](/gmod/Entity:GetLayerWeight) and unallocate layer ID in next frames if the layer weight is `0`, but blending functions will still keep manipulating layer weight. 

Therefore; before calling layer cleanup functions, make sure both [Entity:SetLayerBlendIn](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendIn) and [Entity:SetLayerBlendOut](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendOut) are set to `0`.

NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blendOut
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Blend range from 0 to 1.

SetLayerCycle.DESCRIPTION: Sets the animation cycle/frame of given layer.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cycle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new animation cycle/frame for given layer.

SetLayerDuration.DESCRIPTION: Sets the duration of given layer. This internally overrides the [Entity:SetLayerPlaybackRate](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerPlaybackRate).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This stops layer playback if layer sequence conists of 1 frame. Use `Entity:SetLayerPlaybackRate(layerID,1/duration)` instead.

NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duration
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new duration of the layer in seconds.

SetLayerLooping.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether the layer should loop or not.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: loop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the layer should loop or not.

SetLayerPlaybackRate.DESCRIPTION: Sets the layer playback rate. See also [Entity:SetLayerDuration](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerDuration).
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rate
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new playback rate.

SetLayerPriority.DESCRIPTION: Sets the priority of given layer.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entites!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: priority
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new priority of the layer.

SetLayerSequence.DESCRIPTION: Sets the sequence of given layer.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: seq
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequenceID to set. See [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence).

SetLayerWeight.DESCRIPTION: Sets the layer weight. This influences how strongly the animation should be overriding the normal animations of the entity.
NOTES: This function only works on [BaseAnimatingOverlay](/gmod/BaseAnimatingOverlay) entities.

Setting either [Entity:SetLayerBlendIn](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendIn) or [Entity:SetLayerBlendOut](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerBlendOut) above 0 will turn on automatic weight blending, so you shouldn't be using this if you use any of above.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: layerID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Layer ID

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new layer weight.

SetLegacyTransform.DESCRIPTION:
This forces an entity to use the bone transformation behaviour from versions prior to **8 July 2014**.

This behaviour affects [Entity:EnableMatrix](/gmod/Entity:EnableMatrix) and [Entity:SetModelScale](/gmod/Entity:SetModelScale) and is incorrect, therefore this function be used exclusively as a quick fix for old scripts that rely on it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the entity should use the old bone transformation behaviour or not.

SetLightingOriginEntity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity to be used as the light origin position for this entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The lighting entity.

SetLocalAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets angles relative to angles of [Entity:GetParent](/gmod/Entity:GetParent)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The local angle

SetLocalAngularVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity's angular velocity (rotation speed).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angVel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angular velocity to set.

SetLocalPos.DESCRIPTION:
Sets local position relative to the parented position. This is for use with [Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent) to offset position.
	
This is also used by NPCs for interpolated movement. If you use [Entity:SetPos](/gmod/Entity:SetPos) for step movement, your NPC will snap to position instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The local position

SetLocalVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity's local velocity which is their velocity due to movement in the world from forces such as gravity. Does not include velocity from entity-on-entity collision or other world movement.
WARNINGS: Same as [Entity:SetAbsVelocity](/gmod/Entity:SetAbsVelocity), but clamps the given velocity, and is not recommended to be used because of that.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: velocity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new velocity to set.

SetLOD.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Level Of Detail model to use with this entity. This may not work for all models if the model doesn't include any LOD sub models.

This function works exactly like the clientside r_lod convar and takes priority over it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lod
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Level Of Detail model ID to use. -1 leaves the engine to automatically set the Level of Detail.

The Level Of Detail may range from 0 to 8, with 0 being the highest quality and 8 the lowest.

SetMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the rendering material override of the entity.

To set a Lua material created with [CreateMaterial](/gmod/Global.CreateMaterial), just prepend a "!" to the material name.

If you wish to override a single material on the model, use [Entity:SetSubMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetSubMaterial) instead.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The server's value takes priority on the client.

NOTES: To apply materials to models, that material **must** have **VertexLitGeneric** shader. For that reason you cannot apply map textures onto models, map textures use a different material shader - **LightmappedGeneric**, which can be used on brush entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: materialName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New material name. Use an empty string ("") to reset to the default materials.

SetMaxHealth.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum health for entity. Note, that you can still set entity's health above this amount with [Entity:SetHealth](/gmod/Entity:SetHealth).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxhealth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: What the max health should be

SetMaxYawSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Sets the NPC max yaw speed. Internally sets the `m_fMaxYawSpeed` variable which is polled by the engine.
NOTES: This is a helper function only available if your SENT is based on `base_ai`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxyaw
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new max yaw value to set

SetModel.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the model of the entity.

This does not update the physics of the entity - see [Entity:PhysicsInit](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInit).
WARNINGS: This silently fails when given an empty string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New model value.

SetModelName.DESCRIPTION: Alter the model name returned by [Entity:GetModel](/gmod/Entity:GetModel). Does not affect the entity's actual model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new model name.

SetModelScale.DESCRIPTION:
Uniformly scales the model of the entity, if the entity is a [Player](/gmod/Player) or an [NPC](/gmod/NPC) the hitboxes will be scaled as well.

To resize the entity non-uniformly, along any axis, use [Entity:EnableMatrix](/gmod/Entity:EnableMatrix) instead.

For some entities (Such as `prop_physics` and `anim` type [Scripted Entities](/gmod/Scripted%20Entities)), calling [Entity:Activate](/gmod/Entity:Activate) after this will scale the collision bounds and [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) as well; be wary as there's no optimization being done internally and highly complex collision models might crash the server.

Client-side trace detection seems to mess up if `deltaTime` is set to anything but zero. A very small decimal can be used instead of zero to solve this issue.

If your old scales are wrong, use [Entity:SetLegacyTransform](/gmod/Entity:SetLegacyTransform) as a quick fix.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: On the client, `anim` types' collision testing prediction fails for changed model scales: you can use `cl_showerror 2` to see by how much. Essentially, the client will freak out when you stand/run past on a Scripted Entity or prop that has been modified using this method.

NOTES: If you do not want the physics to be affected by [Entity:Activate](/gmod/Entity:Activate), you can use [Entity:ManipulateBoneScale](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneScale)`( 0, Vector( scale, scale, scale ) )` instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A float to scale the model by. 0 will not draw anything. A number less than 0 will draw the model inverted.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: deltaTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Transition time of the scale change, set to 0 to modify the scale right away. To avoid issues with client-side trace detection this must be set, and can be an extremely low number to mimic a value of 0 such as .000001.

SetMoveCollide.DESCRIPTION: Sets the move collide type of the entity. The move collide is the way a physics object reacts to hitting an object - will it bounce, slide?

ARGUMENTS.NAME: moveCollideType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The move collide type, see [MOVECOLLIDE](/gmod/Enums/MOVECOLLIDE)

SetMoveParent.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Movement Parent of an entity to another entity.

Similar to [Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent), except the object's coordinates are not translated automatically before parenting.

Does nothing on client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Parent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to change this entity's Movement Parent to.

SetMoveType.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the entity's move type. This should be called before initializing the physics object on the entity, unless it will override SetMoveType such as [Entity:PhysicsInitBox](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInitBox).

Despite existing on client, it doesn't actually do anything on client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: movetype
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new movetype, see [MOVETYPE](/gmod/Enums/MOVETYPE)

SetName.DESCRIPTION: Sets the mapping name of the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mappingName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name to set for the entity.

SetNetworkAngles.DESCRIPTION: Alters the entity's perceived serverside angle on the client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Networked angle.

SetNetworked2Angle.DESCRIPTION:
Sets a networked angle value on the entity.

The value can then be accessed with [Entity:GetNetworked2Angle](/gmod/Entity:GetNetworked2Angle) both from client and server.
DEPRECATED: You should be using Entity:SetNW2Angle instead.
NOTES:
Running this function clientside will only set it for the client it is called on.  
The value will only be networked if it isn't the same as the current value and unlike SetNW*
the value will only be networked once and not every 10 seconds.
WARNINGS: The value will only be updated clientside if the entity is or enters the clients PVS. use [Entity:SetNWAngle](/gmod/Entity:SetNWAngle) instead

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value

SetOwner.DESCRIPTION: Sets the owner of this entity, disabling all physics interaction with it.
NOTES: This function is generally used to disable physics interactions on projectiles being fired by their owner, but can also be used for normal ownership in case physics interactions are not involved at all. The Gravity gun will be able to pick up the entity even if the owner can't collide with it, the Physics gun however will not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: owner
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be set as owner.

SetParent.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the parent of this entity, making it move with its parent. This will make the child entity non solid, nothing can interact with them, including traces (but [util.TraceHull](/gmod/util.TraceHull) will work).

All children of the parent get removed whenever it gets removed.
NOTES: This does not work on [the world](/gmod/game.GetWorld).
WARNINGS: This can cause undefined physics behavior when used on entities that don't support parenting. See the [Valve developer wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Entity_Hierarchy_(parenting)) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: parent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to parent to. Setting this to nil will clear the parent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachmentOrBoneId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The attachment or bone id to use when parenting. Defaults to -1 or whatever the parent had set previously.

Use [Entity:AddEffects](/gmod/Entity:AddEffects)( EF_FOLLOWBONE ) to treat this argument as a Bone ID instead of an Attachment ID. Similar to [Entity:FollowBone](/gmod/Entity:FollowBone).
NOTES: Parenting to attachment IDs more than `255` is unsupported and will output a LUA error.
You must call [Entity:SetMoveType](/gmod/Entity:SetMoveType)( MOVETYPE_NONE ) on the child for this argument to have any effect!

SetParentPhysNum.DESCRIPTION: Sets the parent of an entity to another entity with the given physics bone number. Similar to [Entity:SetParent](/gmod/Entity:SetParent), except it is parented to a physbone. This function is useful mainly for ragdolls.
NOTES: Despite this function being available server side, it doesn't actually do anything server side.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Physics bone number to attach to. Use 0 for objects with only one physics bone. (See [Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum))

SetPersistent.DESCRIPTION:
Sets whether or not the given entity is persistent. A persistent entity will be saved on server shutdown and loaded back when the server starts up. Additionally, by default persistent entities cannot be grabbed with the physgun and tools cannot be used on them.

In sandbox, this can be set on an entity by opening the context menu, right clicking the entity, and choosing `"Make Persistent"`.
NOTES: Persistence can only be enabled with the sbox_persist convar, which works as an identifier for the current set of persistent entities. An empty identifier (which is the default value) disables this feature.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: persist
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not the entity should be persistent.

SetPhysConstraintObjects.DESCRIPTION:
When called on a constraint entity, sets the two physics objects to be constrained.

Usage is not recommended as the Constraint library provides easier ways to deal with constraints.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Phys1
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first physics object to be constrained.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Phys2
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The second physics object to be constrained.

NOTES:
This function does not affect gestures.
			Use [Entity:SetLayerPlaybackRate](/gmod/Entity:SetLayerPlaybackRate) instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fSpeed

SetPos.DESCRIPTION:
Moves the entity to the specified position.

Some entities, such as ragdolls, will continually reset their position. Consider using [PhysObj:SetPos](/gmod/PhysObj:SetPos) on every physics object to move ragdolls.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will fail inside of predicted functions called during player movement processing. This includes [WEAPON:PrimaryAttack](/gmod/WEAPON:PrimaryAttack) and [WEAPON:Think](/gmod/WEAPON:Think).

NOTES: If the new position doesn't take effect right away, you can use [Entity:SetupBones](/gmod/Entity:SetupBones) to force it to do so. This issue is especially common when trying to render the same entity twice or more in a single frame at different positions.
WARNINGS: Entities with [Entity:GetSolid](/gmod/Entity:GetSolid) of `SOLID_BBOX` will have their angles reset!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to move the entity to.

SetPoseParameter.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the specified pose parameter to the specified value.

You should call [Entity:InvalidateBoneCache](/gmod/Entity:InvalidateBoneCache) after calling this function.
NOTES: Avoid calling this in draw hooks, especially when animating things, as it might cause visual artifacts.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: poseName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Name of the pose parameter. [Entity:GetPoseParameterName](/gmod/Entity:GetPoseParameterName) might come in handy here.

Can also be a pose parameter ID.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: poseValue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set the pose to.

SetPredictable.DESCRIPTION:
Sets whether an entity should be predictable or not.
When an entity is set as predictable, its DT vars can be changed during predicted hooks. This is useful for entities which can be controlled by player input.

Any datatable value that mismatches from the server will be overridden and a prediction error will be spewed.

Weapons are predictable by default, and the drive system uses this function to make the controlled prop predictable as well.

Visit  for a list of all predicted hooks, and the [Prediction](/gmod/Prediction) page.
For further technical information on the subject, visit [valve's wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Prediction).
NOTES: This function resets the datatable variables everytime it's called, it should ideally be called when a player starts using the entity and when he stops

Entities set as predictable with this function will be unmarked when the user lags and receives a full packet update, to handle such case visit [GM:NotifyShouldTransmit](/gmod/GM:NotifyShouldTransmit)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: setPredictable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: whether to make this entity predictable or not.

SetPreventTransmit.DESCRIPTION: Prevents the server from sending any further information about the entity to a player.
NOTES:
You must also call this function on all entity's children. See [Entity:GetChildren](/gmod/Entity:GetChildren).

[issue tracker](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/1736)

[Entity:SetFlexScale](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexScale) and other flex/bone manipulation functions will create a child entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: player
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player to stop networking the entity to. Can also be a [CRecipientFilter](/gmod/CRecipientFilter) or a [table](/gmod/table) as of March 2024 to affect multiple players at once.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stopTransmitting
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: true to stop the entity from networking, false to make it network again.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum corner of the bounds, relative to origin of the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: add
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If defined, adds this vector to maxs and subtracts this vector from mins.

SetRenderBoundsWS.DESCRIPTION: Sets the render bounds for the entity in world space coordinates. For relative coordinates see [Entity:SetRenderBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetRenderBounds).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum corner of the bounds, relative to origin of the world/map.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum corner of the bounds, relative to origin of the world/map.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: add
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If defined, adds this vector to maxs and subtracts this vector from mins.

SetRenderClipPlane.DESCRIPTION: Used to specify a plane, past which an object will be visually clipped.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: planeNormal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal of the plane. Anything behind the normal will be clipped.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: planePosition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the plane.

SetRenderClipPlaneEnabled.DESCRIPTION: Enables the use of clipping planes to "cut" objects.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable clipping planes

SetRenderFX.DESCRIPTION: Sets entity's render FX. Requires the entitys rendermode to support transparency.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: renderFX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new render FX to set, see [kRenderFx](/gmod/Enums/kRenderFx)

SetRenderMode.DESCRIPTION: Sets the render mode of the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: renderMode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: New render mode to set, see [RENDERMODE](/gmod/Enums/RENDERMODE).

SetRenderOrigin.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the render origin override, a position where the entity will be rendered at. [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos) will return the value set by this function until the override is disabled. (This is all this does internally)

See [Entity:SetRenderAngles](/gmod/Entity:SetRenderAngles) for the function to manipulate angles.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: newOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new origin in world coordinates where the entity's model will now be rendered at. To disable the override, set to [nil](/gmod/nil).

SetSaveValue.DESCRIPTION:
Sets a save value for an entity. You can see a full list of an entity's save values by creating it and printing [Entity:GetSaveTable](/gmod/Entity:GetSaveTable).

See [Entity:GetInternalVariable](/gmod/Entity:GetInternalVariable) for the opposite of this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the save value to set

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to set

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Key successfully set

SetSequence.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the entity's model sequence.

If the specified sequence is already active, the animation will not be restarted. See [Entity:ResetSequence](/gmod/Entity:ResetSequence) for a function that restarts the animation even if it is already playing.

In some cases you want to run [Entity:ResetSequenceInfo](/gmod/Entity:ResetSequenceInfo) to make this function run.
NOTES:
This will not work properly if called directly after calling [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel). Consider waiting until the next Tick.

Will not work on players due to the animations being reset every frame by the base gamemode animation system. See [GM:CalcMainActivity](/gmod/GM:CalcMainActivity).

For custom scripted entities you will want to apply example from [ENTITY:Think](/gmod/ENTITY:Think) to make animations work.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequence
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The sequence to play.

If set to a number, the input is treated as the sequence ID.  
If set to a string, the function will automatically call [Entity:LookupSequence](/gmod/Entity:LookupSequence) to retrieve the sequence ID.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The length of the sequence.

SetShouldPlayPickupSound.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether or not the entity should make a physics contact sound when it's been picked up by a player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: playsound
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: True to play the pickup sound, false otherwise.

SetShouldServerRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Sets if entity should create a server ragdoll on death or a client one.
NOTES:
This is reset for players when they respawn ([Entity:Spawn](/gmod/Entity:Spawn)).

Player ragdolls created with this enabled will have an owner set, see [Entity:SetOwner](/gmod/Entity:SetOwner) for more information on what effects this has.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: serverragdoll
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set `true` if ragdoll should be created on server, `false` if on client.

SetSkin.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the skin of the entity.

[Entity:GetSkin](/gmod/Entity:GetSkin) returns current skin and [Entity:SkinCount](/gmod/Entity:SkinCount) returns amount of skins.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: skinIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: 0-based index of the skin to use.

SetSolid.DESCRIPTION: Sets the solidity of an entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: solidType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The solid type. See the [SOLID](/gmod/Enums/SOLID).

SetSolidFlags.DESCRIPTION:
Sets solid flag(s) for the entity.

This overrides any other flags the entity might have had. See [Entity:AddSolidFlags](/gmod/Entity:AddSolidFlags) for adding flags.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flag(s) to set, see [FSOLID](/gmod/Enums/FSOLID).

SetSpawnEffect.DESCRIPTION:
Sets whether the entity should use a spawn effect when it is created on the client.

See [Entity:GetSpawnEffect](/gmod/Entity:GetSpawnEffect) for more information on how the effect is applied.
NOTES: This function will only have an effect when the entity spawns. After that it will do nothing even is set to true.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: spawnEffect
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sets if we should show a spawn effect.

SetSpawnFlags.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the SpawnFlags to set of an Entity

SpawnFlags can easily be found on https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/.
NOTES:
See also [Entity:RemoveSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:RemoveSpawnFlags), [Entity:AddSpawnFlags](/gmod/Entity:AddSpawnFlags) 

		Using [SF Enumerations](/gmod/Enums/SF) won't work, if this function is ran clientside due to the enumerations being defined only Serverside. Use the actual SpawnFlag number.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The SpawnFlag to remove from the Entity

SetSubMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Overrides a single material on the model of this entity.

To set a Lua material created with [CreateMaterial](/gmod/Global.CreateMaterial), just prepend a `!` to the material name.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The server's value takes priority on the client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Index of the material to override, acceptable values are from `0` to `31`.

Indexes are by [Entity:GetMaterials](/gmod/Entity:GetMaterials), but you have to subtract `1` from them.
NOTES: If called with no arguments, all sub materials will be reset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material to override the default one with. Set to [nil](/gmod/nil) to revert to default material.

SetSurroundingBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) for an entity's hitbox detection.

	See also [Entity:SetSurroundingBoundsType](/gmod/Entity:SetSurroundingBoundsType) (mutually exclusive).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Minimum extent of the AABB relative to entity's position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Maximum extent of the AABB relative to entity's position.

SetSurroundingBoundsType.DESCRIPTION:
Automatically sets the axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) for an entity's hitbox detection.

	See also [Entity:SetSurroundingBounds](/gmod/Entity:SetSurroundingBounds) (mutually exclusive).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bounds
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bounds type of the entity, see [BOUNDS](/gmod/Enums/BOUNDS)

SetTable.DESCRIPTION: Changes the table that can be accessed by indexing an entity. Each entity starts with its own table by default.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table for the entity to use

SetTransmitWithParent.DESCRIPTION: When this flag is set the entity will only transmit to the player when its parent is transmitted. This is useful for things like viewmodel attachments since without this flag they will transmit to everyone (and cause the viewmodels to transmit to everyone too).
NOTES: In the case of scripted entities, this will override [ENTITY:UpdateTransmitState](/gmod/ENTITY:UpdateTransmitState)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: onoff
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Will set the TransmitWithParent flag on or off

SetTrigger.DESCRIPTION:
Marks the entity as a trigger, so it will generate [ENTITY:StartTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:StartTouch), [ENTITY:Touch](/gmod/ENTITY:Touch) and [ENTITY:EndTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:EndTouch) callbacks.

Internally this is stored as [FSOLID_TRIGGER](/gmod/Enums/FSOLID) flag.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maketrigger
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Make the entity trigger or not

SetUnFreezable.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether an entity can be unfrozen, meaning that it cannot be unfrozen using the physgun.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: freezable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: True to make the entity unfreezable, false otherwise.

SetupBones.DESCRIPTION: Forces the entity to reconfigure its bones. You might need to call this after changing your model's scales or when manually drawing the entity multiple times at different positions.
NOTES: This calls the BuildBonePositions callback added via [Entity:AddCallback](/gmod/Entity:AddCallback), so avoid calling this function inside it to prevent an infinite loop.

SetupPhonemeMappings.DESCRIPTION: Initializes the class names of an entity's phoneme mappings (mouth movement data). This is called by default with argument "phonemes" when a flex-based entity (such as an [NPC](/gmod/NPC)) is created.
NOTES: TF2 phonemes can be accessed by using a path such as "player/scout/phonemes/phonemes" , check TF2's "tf2_misc_dir.vpk" with GCFScape for other paths, however it seems that TF2 sounds don't contain phoneme definitions anymore after being converted to mp3 and only rely on VCD animations, this needs to be further investigated

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileRoot
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file prefix of the phoneme mappings (relative to "garrysmod/expressions/").

SetUseType.DESCRIPTION: Sets the use type of an entity, affecting how often [ENTITY:Use](/gmod/ENTITY:Use) will be called for Lua entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: useType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The use type to apply to the entity. Uses [_USE](/gmod/Enums/_USE).

SetVar.DESCRIPTION: Allows to quickly set variable to entity's [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable).
NOTES: This will not network the variable to client(s). You want [Entity:SetNWString](/gmod/Entity:SetNWString) and similar functions for that

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Key of the value to set

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to set the variable to

SetVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the entity's velocity. For entities with physics, consider using [PhysObj:SetVelocity](/gmod/PhysObj:SetVelocity) on the [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) of the entity.
NOTES: Actually binds to CBaseEntity::SetBaseVelocity() which sets the entity's velocity due to forces applied by other entities.
WARNINGS: If applied to a player, this will actually **ADD** velocity, not set it. (due to how movement code handles base velocity)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: velocity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new velocity to set.

SetWeaponModel.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the model and associated weapon to this viewmodel entity.

This is used internally when the player switches weapon.
NOTES: View models are not drawn without a weapons associated to them.
WARNINGS: This will silently fail if the entity is not a viewmodel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewModel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The model string to give to this viewmodel.
Example: "models/weapons/c_smg1.mdl"

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weapon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The weapon entity to associate this viewmodel to.

SkinCount.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the amount of skins the entity has.

To set the entity's skin, use [Entity:SetSkin](/gmod/Entity:SetSkin).
To retrieve the total number of skins without an entity, see [util.GetModelInfo](/gmod/util.GetModelInfo).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of skins the entity's model has.

SnatchModelInstance.DESCRIPTION:
Moves the model instance from the source entity to this entity. This can be used to transfer decals that have been applied on one entity to another.

Both entities must have the same model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: srcEntity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to move the model instance from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the operation was successful or not

Spawn.DESCRIPTION:
Initializes the entity and starts its networking. If called on a player, it will respawn them.

This calls [ENTITY:Initialize](/gmod/ENTITY:Initialize) on Lua-defined entities.

StartLoopingSound.DESCRIPTION:
Starts a "looping" sound. As with any other sound playing methods, this function expects the sound file to be looping itself and will not automatically loop a non looping sound file as one might expect.

This function is almost identical to [CreateSound](/gmod/Global.CreateSound), with the exception of the sound being created in the STATIC channel and with normal attenuation.

See also [Entity:StopLoopingSound](/gmod/Entity:StopLoopingSound)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sound
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sound to play. Can be either a sound script or a filepath.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ID number of started sound starting with 0, or -1 if we failed for some reason.

StartMotionController.DESCRIPTION:
Starts a motion controller in the physics engine tied to this entity's [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj), which enables the use of [ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate](/gmod/ENTITY:PhysicsSimulate).

The motion controller can later be destroyed via [Entity:StopMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StopMotionController).

Motion controllers are used internally to control other Entities' [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj)ects, such as the Gravity Gun, +use pickup and the Physics Gun.

This function should be called every time you recreate the Entity's [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj). Or alternatively you should call [Entity:AddToMotionController](/gmod/Entity:AddToMotionController) on the new [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj).

Also see [Entity:AddToMotionController](/gmod/Entity:AddToMotionController) and [Entity:RemoveFromMotionController](/gmod/Entity:RemoveFromMotionController).
NOTES: Only works on a scripted [Entity](/gmod/Entity) of anim type.

StopAndDestroyParticles.DESCRIPTION: Stops all particle effects parented to the entity and immediately destroys them.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound ID returned by [Entity:StartLoopingSound](/gmod/Entity:StartLoopingSound)

StopMotionController.DESCRIPTION: Stops the motion controller created with [Entity:StartMotionController](/gmod/Entity:StartMotionController).

StopParticleEmission.DESCRIPTION:
Stops all particle effects parented to the entity.

This is ran automatically on every client by [Entity:StopParticles](/gmod/Entity:StopParticles) if called on the server.

StopParticles.DESCRIPTION:
Stops any attached to the entity .pcf particles using [ParticleEffectAttach](/gmod/Global.ParticleEffectAttach) or [ParticleEffect](/gmod/Global.ParticleEffect).

On client, this is the same as [Entity:StopParticleEmission](/gmod/Entity:StopParticleEmission). ( and you should use StopParticleEmission instead )


On server, this is the same as running [Entity:StopParticleEmission](/gmod/Entity:StopParticleEmission) on every client.

StopParticlesNamed.DESCRIPTION: Stops all particle effects parented to the entity with given name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the particle to stop.

StopParticlesWithNameAndAttachment.DESCRIPTION: Stops all particle effects parented to the entity with given name on given attachment.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the particle to stop.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachment
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment of the entity to stop particles on.

StopSound.DESCRIPTION:
Stops emitting the given sound from the entity, especially useful for looping sounds.

Internally plays the sound with the [SND_STOP](/gmod/Enums/SND#SND_STOP) flag to stop the sound.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sound
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the sound script or the filepath to stop playback of.

TakeDamage.DESCRIPTION: Applies the specified amount of damage to the entity with [DMG_GENERIC](/gmod/Enums/DMG) flag.
WARNINGS: Calling this function on the victim entity in [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage) can cause infinite loops.
This function does not seem to do any damage if you apply it to a player who is driving a prop_vehicle_jeep or prop_vehicle_jeep_old vehicle. You need to call it on the vehicle instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageAmount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of damage to be applied.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attacker
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that initiated the attack that caused the damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: inflictor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that applied the damage, eg. a weapon.

TakeDamageInfo.DESCRIPTION: Applies the damage specified by the damage info to the entity.
NOTES: This function does not apply damage to [func_breakable_surf](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Func_breakable_surf) entities correctly. To do this, you will need to use [Entity:DispatchTraceAttack](/gmod/Entity:DispatchTraceAttack) instead.
WARNINGS: Calling this function on the victim entity in [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage) can cause infinite loops.
This function does not seem to do any damage if you apply it to a player who is driving a prop_vehicle_jeep or prop_vehicle_jeep_old vehicle. You need to call it on the vehicle instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damageInfo
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damage to apply.

TakePhysicsDamage.DESCRIPTION: Applies forces to our physics object in response to damage.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dmginfo
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The damageinfo to apply. Only [CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamageForce](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamageForce) and [CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamagePosition](/gmod/CTakeDamageInfo:GetDamagePosition) are used.

TestPVS.DESCRIPTION:
Check if the given position or entity is within this entity's [PVS(Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community").

See also [Entity:IsDormant](/gmod/Entity:IsDormant).
NOTES: The function won't take in to account [AddOriginToPVS](/gmod/Global.AddOriginToPVS) and the like.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: testPoint
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: [Entity](/gmod/Entity) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector) to test against. If an entity is given, this function will test using its bounding box.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the testPoint is within our PVS.

TranslateBoneToPhysBone.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ID of a [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) attached to the given bone.

See [Entity:TranslatePhysBoneToBone](/gmod/Entity:TranslatePhysBoneToBone) for reverse function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of a bone to look up the "physics root" bone of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) ID of the given bone to be used with [Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum) or `-1` if we cannot translate for some reason, such as a model bone having no physics object associated with it.

TranslatePhysBoneToBone.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the boneID of the bone the given [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) is attached to.

See [Entity:TranslateBoneToPhysBone](/gmod/Entity:TranslateBoneToPhysBone) for reverse function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physNum
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) number on the entity

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The boneID of the bone the [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) is attached to.

UpdateBoneFollowers.DESCRIPTION:
Updates positions of bone followers created by [Entity:CreateBoneFollowers](/gmod/Entity:CreateBoneFollowers).

This should be called every tick.
NOTES: This function only works on `anim`, `nextbot` and `ai` type entities.

UpdateShadow.DESCRIPTION: Marks the render-to-texture (RTT) shadow of this entity as dirty, as well as any potential projected texture shadows related to this entity, so they will be updated as soon as possible.

Use.DESCRIPTION: Simulates a `+use` action on an entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity that caused this input. This will usually be the player who pressed their use key

ARGUMENTS.NAME: caller
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity responsible for the input. This will typically be the same as `activator` unless some other entity is acting as a proxy

ARGUMENTS.NAME: useType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Use type, see [USE](/gmod/Enums/USE).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any value.

UseClientSideAnimation.DESCRIPTION: Animations will be handled purely clientside instead of a fixed animtime, enabling interpolation. This does not affect layers and gestures.
NOTES: Does nothing on server.

UseTriggerBounds.DESCRIPTION:
Enables or disables trigger bounds.

This will give the entity a "trigger box" that extends around its bounding box by boundSize units in X/Y and (boundSize / 2) in +Z (-Z remains the same).
The trigger box is world aligned and will work regardless of the object's solidity and collision group.

Valve use trigger boxes for all pickup items. Their bloat size is 24, a surprisingly large figure.
NOTES:
The trigger boxes can be made visible as a light blue box by using the **ent_bbox** console command while looking at the entity. Alternatively a classname or entity index can be used as the first argument.

This requires **developer** to be set to **1**.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the bounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boundSize
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The distance/size of the trigger bounds.

ViewModelIndex.DESCRIPTION: Returns the index of this view model, it can be used to identify which one of the player's view models this entity is.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: View model index, ranges from 0 to 2, nil if the entity is not a view model

Visible.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the target/given entity is visible from the this entity.

This is meant to be used only with NPCs.

Differences from a simple trace include:
* If target has `FL_NOTARGET`, returns `false`
* If `ai_ignoreplayers` is turned on and target is a player, returns `false`
* Reacts to `ai_LOS_mode`:
* * If `1`, does a simple trace with `COLLISION_GROUP_NONE` and `MASK_BLOCKLOS`
* * If not, does a trace with `MASK_BLOCKLOS_AND_NPCS` (- `CONTENTS_BLOCKLOS` is target is player) and a custom LOS filter (`CTraceFilterLOS`)
* Returns `true` if hits a vehicle the target is driving

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to check for visibility to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the entities can see each other.

VisibleVec.DESCRIPTION:
Returns true if supplied vector is visible from the entity's line of sight.

This is achieved similarly to a trace.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to check for visibility

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Within line of sight

WaterLevel.DESCRIPTION: Returns an integer that represents how deep in water the entity is.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The water level.
* **0** - The entity isn't in water.
* **1** - Slightly submerged (at least to the feet).
* **2** - The majority of the entity is submerged (at least to the waist).
* **3** - Completely submerged.

Weapon_SetActivity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the activity of the entity's active weapon.
NOTES: This does nothing on the client.
Only works for CBaseCombatCharacter entities, which includes players and NPCs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Activity number. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duration
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long the animation should take in seconds.

Weapon_TranslateActivity.DESCRIPTION: Calls and returns [WEAPON:TranslateActivity](/gmod/WEAPON:TranslateActivity) on the weapon the entity (player or NPC) carries.
NOTES: Doesn't return anything on client, despite existing there.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The NPC activity to translate

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The translated activity. Defaults to `act` input when a translation doesn't exist.

WorldSpaceAABB.DESCRIPTION: Returns two vectors representing the minimum and maximum extent of the entity's axis-aligned bounding box (which is calculated from entity's collision bounds.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum vector for the entity's bounding box in world space.
The maximum vector for the entity's bounding box in world space.

WorldSpaceCenter.DESCRIPTION: Returns the center of the entity according to its collision model.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the entity

WorldToLocal.DESCRIPTION: Translates a worldspace vector into a vector relative to the entity's coordinate system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: wpos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A worldspace vector.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding local space vector.

WorldToLocalAngles.DESCRIPTION: Translates a worldspace angle into an angle relative to the entity's coordinate system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A worldspace angle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding local space angle.

Entity.DESCRIPTION:
This is a list of all available methods for all entities, which includes [Players](/gmod/Player), [Weapons](/gmod/Weapon), [NPCs](/gmod/NPC) and [Vehicles](/gmod/Vehicle).

For a list of possible members of [Scripted Entities](/gmod/Scripted%20Entities) see [ENT Structure](/gmod/Structures/ENT).

Close.DESCRIPTION: Dumps the file changes to disk and closes the file handle which makes the handle useless.

EndOfFile.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the [File](/gmod/File) object has reached the end of file or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the file has reached end or not.

Flush.DESCRIPTION: Dumps the file changes to disk and saves the file.

Read.DESCRIPTION: Reads the specified amount of chars and returns them as a binary string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Reads the specified amount of chars. If not set, will read the entire file.

RETURNS.NAME: data
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read data.

ReadBool.DESCRIPTION: Reads one byte of the file and returns whether that byte was not 0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: val

ReadByte.DESCRIPTION: Reads one unsigned 8-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The unsigned 8-bit integer from the file.

ReadDouble.DESCRIPTION: Reads an 8-byte little-endian IEEE-754 floating point double from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The double-precision floating point value read from the file.

ReadFloat.DESCRIPTION: Reads an IEEE 754 little-endian 4-byte float from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read value

ReadLine.DESCRIPTION: Returns the contents of the file from the current position up until the end of the current line.
NOTES:
This function will look specifically for `Line Feed` characters `\n` and will **completely ignore `Carriage Return` characters** `\r`.

It will also stop at a `\0` or `NULL` character, but will add a new line instead.

This function will not return more than 8192 characters. The return value will include the `\n` character.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The string of data from the read line.

ReadLong.DESCRIPTION: Reads a signed little-endian 32-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A signed 32-bit integer

ReadShort.DESCRIPTION: Reads a signed little-endian 16-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: int16

ReadUInt64.DESCRIPTION: Reads an unsigned 64-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: An unsigned 64-bit integer.
NOTES: Since Lua cannot store full 64-bit integers, this function returns a string. It is mainly aimed at usage with [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64).

ReadULong.DESCRIPTION: Reads an unsigned little-endian 32-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: An unsigned 32-bit integer

ReadUShort.DESCRIPTION: Reads an unsigned little-endian 16-bit integer from the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The 16-bit integer

Seek.DESCRIPTION: Sets the file pointer to the specified position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Pointer position, in bytes.

Size.DESCRIPTION: Returns the size of the file in bytes.

Skip.DESCRIPTION: Moves the file pointer by the specified amount of chars.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: amount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of chars to skip, can be negative to skip backwards.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: amount

Tell.DESCRIPTION: Returns the current position of the file pointer.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: pos

Write.DESCRIPTION: Writes the given string into the file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Binary data to write to the file.

WriteBool.DESCRIPTION: Writes a boolean value to the file as one **byte**.

FFT.DESCRIPTION:
Computes the [DFT (discrete Fourier transform)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform) of the sound channel.

The size parameter specifies the number of consecutive audio samples to use as the input to the DFT and is restricted to a power of two. A [Hann window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hann_function) is applied to the input data.

The computed DFT has the same number of frequency bins as the number of samples. Only half of this DFT is returned, since [the DFT magnitudes are symmetric for real input data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform#The_real-input_DFT). The magnitudes of the DFT (values from 0 to 1) are used to fill the output table, starting at index 1.

**Visualization protip:** For a size N DFT, bin k (1-indexed) corresponds to a frequency of (k - 1) / N * sampleRate.

**Visualization protip:** Sound energy is proportional to the square of the magnitudes. Adding magnitudes together makes no sense physically, but adding energies does.

**Visualization protip:** The human ear works on a logarithmic amplitude scale. You can convert to [decibels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decibel) by taking 20 * [math.log10](/gmod/math.log10) of frequency magnitudes, or 10 * [math.log10](/gmod/math.log10) of energy. The decibel values will range from -infinity to 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to output the DFT magnitudes (numbers between 0 and 1) into. Indices start from 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: size
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The number of samples to use. See [FFT](/gmod/Enums/FFT)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The number of frequency bins that have been filled in the output table.

... other headers

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:

The table will always have the following keys, filled out based on what is available:

IMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
A Material object. It represents a game material, similarly to how a `.vmt` file does, which are in fact loaded into an **IMaterial** object.

In most cases the game works with materials as far as file paths go. Materials then point to different [ITexture](/gmod/ITexture)s (`.vtf` files) they might be using.  
They are not the same and cannot be interchanged.

A material object can be created with [Material](/gmod/Global.Material) or [CreateMaterial](/gmod/Global.CreateMaterial).

BuildFromTriangles.DESCRIPTION:
Builds the mesh from a table mesh vertexes.

When modifying a previously built mesh, your new mesh must match the vertex count!

See [Mesh](/gmod/Global.Mesh) and [util.GetModelMeshes](/gmod/util.GetModelMeshes) for examples.
WARNINGS:
[IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) appears to have a limit of 65535 vertices. You should split your mesh into multiple meshes when above this limit. 

Exceeding the limit may lead to undefined rendering behavior.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertexes
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table consisting of [Structures/MeshVertex](/gmod/Structures/MeshVertex)s.

Destroy.DESCRIPTION: Deletes the mesh and frees the memory used by it.

Draw.DESCRIPTION: Renders the mesh with the active matrix.

DrawSkinned.DESCRIPTION: Renders the mesh with the active matrix and given bone matrices.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bones
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A list of matrices to use as bones. Up to 52 of them.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: multiply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, multiplies given matrices with currently active model matrix ([cam.GetModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.GetModelMatrix)). This incurs a performance hit.

IsValid.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether this [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) is valid or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether this [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) is valid or not.

IMesh.DESCRIPTION:
Renderable mesh object, can be used to create models on the fly. 
		The only way to create your own IMesh object is to call [Mesh](/gmod/Global.Mesh).
NOTES:
IMeshes only respond to one projected texture.  
			See the [render.RenderFlashlights](/gmod/render.RenderFlashlights) function and example that solves this problem.

The object used in the [saverestore](/gmod/saverestore), mainly in [saverestore.AddSaveHook](/gmod/saverestore.AddSaveHook).

It allows you to write blocks directly into the save game files used by Half-Life 2 save system when such save is being saved.

Download.DESCRIPTION: Invokes the generator of the texture. Reloads file based textures from disk and clears render target textures.

GetColor.DESCRIPTION: Returns the color of the specified pixel, only works for textures created from PNG files.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X coordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y coordinate.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The color of the pixel as a [Color](/gmod/Color).

GetMappingHeight.DESCRIPTION: Returns the true unmodified height of the texture.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: height

GetMappingWidth.DESCRIPTION: Returns the true unmodified width of the texture.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: width

GetName.DESCRIPTION: Returns the name of the texture, in most cases the path.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: name

GetNumAnimationFrames.DESCRIPTION: Returns the number of animation frames in this texture.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The number of animation frames in this texture.

Height.DESCRIPTION: Returns the modified height of the texture, this value may be affected by mipmapping and other factors.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: height

IsError.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the texture is valid. (i.e. was loaded successfully or not)
NOTES: The "error" texture is a valid texture, and therefore this function will return false when used on it. Use [ITexture:IsErrorTexture](/gmod/ITexture:IsErrorTexture), instead.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the texture was loaded successfully or not.

IsErrorTexture.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the texture is the error texture (pink and black checkerboard pattern).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the texture is the error texture or not.

Width.DESCRIPTION: Returns the modified width of the texture, this value may be affected by mipmapping and other factors.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: width

ITexture.DESCRIPTION:
An object representing game texture, such as those loaded from a `.vtf` file.

Do not confuse with [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial). Materials use textures. Game uses materials.

Returned by [IMaterial:GetTexture](/gmod/IMaterial:GetTexture)

AddFrame.DESCRIPTION: Adds the current framebuffer to the video stream.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: frameTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Usually set to what [FrameTime](/gmod/Global.FrameTime) is, or simply 1/fps.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: downsample
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If true it will downsample the whole screenspace to the videos width and height, otherwise it will just record from the top left corner to the given width and height and therefore not the whole screen.

Finish.DESCRIPTION: Ends the video recording and dumps it to disk.

Height.DESCRIPTION: Returns the height of the video stream.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: height

SetRecordSound.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether to record sound or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: record
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Record.

Width.DESCRIPTION: Returns the width of the video stream.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: width

Draw.DESCRIPTION: Draws the computed markupobject to the screen. See [markup.Parse](/gmod/markup.Parse).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: xOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X coordinate on the screen.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: yOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y coordinate on the screen.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: xAlign
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The alignment of the x coordinate within the text using [TEXT_ALIGN](/gmod/Enums/TEXT_ALIGN)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: yAlign
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The alignment of the y coordinate within the text using [TEXT_ALIGN](/gmod/Enums/TEXT_ALIGN)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: alphaoverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sets the alpha of all drawn objects to this value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: textAlign
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The alignment of the text horizontally using [TEXT_ALIGN](/gmod/Enums/TEXT_ALIGN)

GetHeight.DESCRIPTION: Gets computed the height of the markupobject.

RETURNS.NAME: Height
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The computed height.

GetMaxWidth.DESCRIPTION: Gets maximum width for this markup object as defined in [markup.Parse](/gmod/markup.Parse).

RETURNS.NAME: maxWidth
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The max width.

GetWidth.DESCRIPTION: Gets computed the width of the markupobject.

RETURNS.NAME: Width
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The computed width.

Size.DESCRIPTION: Gets computed the width and height of the markupobject.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The computed width.
The computed height.

MarkupObject.DESCRIPTION: Object containing parsed markup for later rendering. Created by [markup.Parse](/gmod/markup.Parse).

BecomeRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Become a ragdoll and remove the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: info
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Damage info passed from an onkilled event

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created ragdoll, if any.

BodyMoveXY.DESCRIPTION: Should only be called in [NEXTBOT:BodyUpdate](/gmod/NEXTBOT:BodyUpdate). This sets the `move_x` and `move_y` pose parameters of the bot to fit how they're currently moving, sets the animation speed ([Entity:GetPlaybackRate](/gmod/Entity:GetPlaybackRate)) to suit the ground speed, and calls [Entity:FrameAdvance](/gmod/Entity:FrameAdvance).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This function might cause crashes with some activities.

ClearLastKnownArea.DESCRIPTION: Clears this bot's last known area. See [NextBot:GetLastKnownArea](/gmod/NextBot:GetLastKnownArea).

FindSpot.DESCRIPTION: Like [NextBot:FindSpots](/gmod/NextBot:FindSpots) but only returns a vector.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Either `"random"`, `"near"`, `"far"`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: options
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This table should contain the search info.
* [string](/gmod/string) type - The type (Only `hiding` for now)
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) pos - the position to search.
* [number](/gmod/number) radius - the radius to search.
* [number](/gmod/number) stepup - the highest step to step up.
* [number](/gmod/number) stepdown - the highest we can step down without being hurt.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If it finds a spot it will return a vector. If not it will return nil.

FindSpots.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of hiding spots.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: specs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This table should contain the search info.
* [string](/gmod/string) type - The type (optional, only `hiding` supported)
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) pos - the position to search.
* [number](/gmod/number) radius - the radius to search.
* [number](/gmod/number) stepup - the highest step to step up.
* [number](/gmod/number) stepdown - the highest we can step down without being hurt.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
An unsorted table of tables containing:
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) vector - The position of the hiding spot
* [number](/gmod/number) distance - the distance to that position
The current activity

GetFOV.DESCRIPTION: Returns the Field of View of the Nextbot NPC, used for its vision functionality, such as [NextBot:IsAbleToSee](/gmod/NextBot:IsAbleToSee).

RETURNS.NAME: fov
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current FOV of the nextbot

GetLastKnownArea.DESCRIPTION: Returns this bots last known area. See also [NextBot:ClearLastKnownArea](/gmod/NextBot:ClearLastKnownArea).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The last area the bot is known to have been in.

GetMaxVisionRange.DESCRIPTION: Returns the maximum range the nextbot can see other nextbots/players at. See [NextBot:IsAbleToSee](/gmod/NextBot:IsAbleToSee).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current vision range

GetRangeSquaredTo.DESCRIPTION:
Returns squared distance to an entity or a position.

See also [NextBot:GetRangeTo](/gmod/NextBot:GetRangeTo).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to measure distance to. Can be an entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The squared distance

GetRangeTo.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the distance to an entity or position.

See also [NextBot:GetRangeSquaredTo](/gmod/NextBot:GetRangeSquaredTo).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to measure distance to. Can be an entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The distance

GetSolidMask.DESCRIPTION: Returns the solid mask for given NextBot.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The solid mask, see [CONTENTS](/gmod/Enums/CONTENTS) and [MASK](/gmod/Enums/MASK)

HandleStuck.DESCRIPTION:
Called from Lua when the NPC is stuck. This should only be called from the behaviour coroutine - so if you want to override this function and do something special that yields - then go for it.

You should always call self.loco:ClearStuck() in this function to reset the stuck status - so it knows it's unstuck. See [CLuaLocomotion:ClearStuck](/gmod/CLuaLocomotion:ClearStuck).

IsAbleToSee.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the Nextbot NPC can see the give entity or not.
WARNINGS: Using this function creates the nextbot vision interface which will cause a significant performance hit!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to test if we can see

ARGUMENTS.NAME: useFOV
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to use the Field of View of the Nextbot

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the nextbot can see or not

MoveToPos.DESCRIPTION: To be called in the behaviour coroutine only! Will yield until the bot has reached the goal or is stuck

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position we want to get to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: options
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing a bunch of tweakable options.
* [number](/gmod/number) lookahead - Minimum look ahead distance.
* [number](/gmod/number) tolerance - How close we must be to the goal before it can be considered complete.
* [boolean](/gmod/boolean) draw - Draw the path. Only visible on listen servers and single player.
* [number](/gmod/number) maxage - Maximum age of the path before it times out.
* [number](/gmod/number) repath - Rebuilds the path after this number of seconds.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Either `"failed"`, `"stuck"`, `"timeout"` or `"ok"` - depending on how the NPC got on

PlaySequenceAndWait.DESCRIPTION: To be called in the behaviour coroutine only! Plays an animation sequence and waits for it to end before returning.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sequence name

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Playback Rate of that sequence

SetFOV.DESCRIPTION: Sets the Field of View for the Nextbot NPC, used for its vision functionality, such as [NextBot:IsAbleToSee](/gmod/NextBot:IsAbleToSee).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fov
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new FOV

SetMaxVisionRange.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum range the nextbot can see other nextbots/players at. See [NextBot:IsAbleToSee](/gmod/NextBot:IsAbleToSee).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: range
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new vision range to set.

SetSolidMask.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the solid mask for given NextBot.

The default solid mask of a NextBot is [MASK_NPCSOLID](/gmod/Enums/MASK).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new mask, see [CONTENTS](/gmod/Enums/CONTENTS) and [MASK](/gmod/Enums/MASK)

StartActivity.DESCRIPTION:
Start doing an activity (animation).

This function may not produce the desired result if [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel) has not yet been called on the nextbot entity

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: One of the [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT)

NextBot.DESCRIPTION:
NextBots are a new system to create NPCs in the Source Engine, utilizing the more powerful [navmesh](/gmod/navmesh) system for navigation over the old node based system.

This page lists all possible functions usable with NextBots.

See [NextBot NPC Creation](/gmod/NextBot%20NPC%20Creation) for more information on how to create NextBot NPCs.

AddEntityRelationship.DESCRIPTION: Makes the NPC like, hate, feel neutral towards, or fear the entity in question. If you want to setup relationship towards a certain entity `class`, use [NPC:AddRelationship](/gmod/NPC:AddRelationship).
NOTES: NPCs do not see [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot)s by default. This can be fixed by adding the [FL_OBJECT](/gmod/Enums/FL) flag to the NextBot.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity for the relationship to be applied to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: disposition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A [D](/gmod/Enums/D) representing the relationship type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: priority
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How strong the relationship is. Higher values mean higher priority over relationships with lower priority.

AddRelationship.DESCRIPTION: Changes how an NPC feels towards another NPC.  If you want to setup relationship towards a certain `entity`, use [NPC:AddEntityRelationship](/gmod/NPC:AddEntityRelationship).
WARNINGS: Avoid using this in [GM:OnEntityCreated](/gmod/GM:OnEntityCreated) to prevent crashing due to infinite loops. This function may create an entity with given class and delete it immediately after.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: relationstring
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A string representing how the relationship should be set up.
Should be formatted as `"npc_class `[D](/gmod/Enums/D)` numberPriority"`.

AdvancePath.DESCRIPTION: Advances the NPC on its path to the next waypoint.
WARNINGS: Calling this on an NPC without any route will result in an instant crash.

AlertSound.DESCRIPTION: Force an NPC to play their Alert sound.

AutoMovement.DESCRIPTION: Executes any movement the current sequence may have.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: interval
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This is a good place to use [Entity:GetAnimTimeInterval](/gmod/Entity:GetAnimTimeInterval).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if any movement was performed.

BecomeRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Become a ragdoll and remove the entity. Internally handles serverside/clientside ragdoll creation, momentum calculation, triggering ragdoll creation hooks / events and cloning entity's bone transforms to the created ragdoll.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: info
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Damage info passed from an onkilled event

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created serverside ragdoll, nil if failed or a clientside ragdoll created.

CapabilitiesAdd.DESCRIPTION: Adds a capability to the NPC.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: capabilities
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Capabilities to add, see [CAP](/gmod/Enums/CAP).

CapabilitiesClear.DESCRIPTION: Removes all of Capabilities the NPC has.

CapabilitiesGet.DESCRIPTION: Returns the NPC's capabilities along the ones defined on its weapon.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The capabilities as a bitflag.
See [CAP](/gmod/Enums/CAP)

CapabilitiesHas.DESCRIPTION: Checks whether the NPC has the specified capabilities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: capabilities
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Capabilities to check, see [CAP](/gmod/Enums/CAP).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: capabilities
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Capabilities to remove, see [CAP](/gmod/Enums/CAP)

Classify.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the NPC relationship class. This is mostly used to tell NPCs who should be attacking who.

Do not confuse with [Entity:GetClass](/gmod/Entity:GetClass)!

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: See [CLASS](/gmod/Enums/CLASS)

ClearCondition.DESCRIPTION: Clears out the specified [COND](/gmod/Enums/COND) on this NPC.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: condition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [COND](/gmod/Enums/COND) to clear out.

ClearEnemyMemory.DESCRIPTION: Clears the Enemy from the NPC's memory, effectively forgetting it until met again with either the NPC vision or with [NPC:UpdateEnemyMemory](/gmod/NPC:UpdateEnemyMemory).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to mark

ClearExpression.DESCRIPTION: Clears the NPC's current expression which can be set with [NPC:SetExpression](/gmod/NPC:SetExpression).

ClearGoal.DESCRIPTION: Clears the current NPC goal or target.

ClearSchedule.DESCRIPTION: Stops the current schedule that the NPC is doing.

ConditionID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ID of a given condition by name. Opposite of [NPC:ConditionName](/gmod/NPC:ConditionName).

This is useful for custom conditions defined by engine NPCs, such as `COND_ZOMBIE_RELEASECRAB` for zombies, and `COND_COMBINE_ON_FIRE` for Combine Soldiers.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: conditionName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The condition name.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The condition ID, see [COND](/gmod/Enums/COND). Custom conditions will have a "randomly" assigned IDs, which will change with each game session.

ConditionName.DESCRIPTION: Translates condition ID to a string. For the opposite process, see [NPC:ConditionID](/gmod/NPC:ConditionID).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cond
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The NPCs condition ID, see [COND](/gmod/Enums/COND)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A human understandable string equivalent of that condition.

Disposition.DESCRIPTION: Returns the way the NPC "feels" about a given entity. See [NPC:AddEntityRelationship](/gmod/NPC:AddEntityRelationship).
NOTES: For `ai` type entities, this will return [ENTITY:GetRelationship](/gmod/ENTITY:GetRelationship). If it returns `nil` or for engine NPCs, this will return whatever was last set by [NPC:AddEntityRelationship](/gmod/NPC:AddEntityRelationship). As a last resort, engine will decide on the disposition based on this NPC's [NPC:Classify](/gmod/NPC:Classify).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to test our disposition towards.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The NPCs disposition, see [D](/gmod/Enums/D).
The NPCs disposition priority.

DropWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Forces the NPC to drop the specified weapon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weapon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Weapon to be dropped. If unset, will default to the currently equipped weapon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, launches the weapon at given position. There is a limit to how far it is willing to throw the weapon. Overrides velocity argument.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: velocity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set and previous argument is unset, launches the weapon with given velocity. If the velocity is higher than 400, it will be clamped to 400.

ExitScriptedSequence.DESCRIPTION: Makes an NPC exit a scripted sequence, if one is playing.

FearSound.DESCRIPTION: Force an NPC to play its Fear sound.

FoundEnemySound.DESCRIPTION: Force an NPC to play its FoundEnemy sound.

GetActiveWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Returns the weapon the NPC is currently carrying, or [NULL](/gmod/Global_Variables).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The NPCs current weapon
Current activity, see [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

GetAimVector.DESCRIPTION: Returns the aim vector of the NPC. NPC alternative of [Player:GetAimVector](/gmod/Player:GetAimVector).
NOTES: If the NPC has both [NPC:GetEnemy](/gmod/NPC:GetEnemy) and [NPC:GetActiveWeapon](/gmod/NPC:GetActiveWeapon), engine will automatically call [ENTITY:GetAttackSpread](/gmod/ENTITY:GetAttackSpread) to add random spread degrees to the return value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The aim direction of the NPC, usually a noisy direction to it's [NPC:GetEnemy](/gmod/NPC:GetEnemy). This will default to [Entity:GetForward](/gmod/Entity:GetForward) when there's no enemy. Thus, [NPC:GetCurrentWeaponProficiency](/gmod/NPC:GetCurrentWeaponProficiency) will be used.

GetArrivalActivity.DESCRIPTION: Returns the activity to be played when the NPC arrives at its goal

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The arrival activity. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

GetArrivalDirection.DESCRIPTION: Returns the direction from the NPC origin to its current navigational destination.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The arrival direction.

GetArrivalDistance.DESCRIPTION: Returns NPC arrival distance, set by [NPC:SetArrivalDistance](/gmod/NPC:SetArrivalDistance).

RETURNS.NAME: dist
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current arrival distance.

GetArrivalSequence.DESCRIPTION: Returns the sequence to be played when the NPC arrives at its goal.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Sequence ID to be played, or -1 if there's no sequence.

GetArrivalSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Returns NPC arrival speed, set by [NPC:SetArrivalSpeed](/gmod/NPC:SetArrivalSpeed).

RETURNS.NAME: speed
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current arrival peed.

GetBestSoundHint.DESCRIPTION: Returns the most dangerous/closest sound hint based on the NPCs location and the types of sounds it can sense.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: types
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The types of sounds to choose from. See [SOUND_ enums](/gmod/Enums/SOUND)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table with [SoundHintData](/gmod/Structures/SoundHintData) structure or `nil` if no sound hints are nearby.

GetBlockingEntity.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity blocking the NPC along its path.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Blocking entity

GetCurGoalType.DESCRIPTION: Returns the goal type for current navigation path.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The goal type. See [GOALTYPE](/gmod/Enums/GOALTYPE).
The NPCs schedule, see [SCHED](/gmod/Enums/SCHED) or -1 if we failed for some reason

GetCurrentWeaponProficiency.DESCRIPTION: Returns how proficient (skilled) an NPC is with its current weapon.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: NPC's proficiency for current weapon. See [WEAPON_PROFICIENCY](/gmod/Enums/WEAPON_PROFICIENCY).

GetCurWaypointPos.DESCRIPTION: Gets the NPC's current waypoint position (where NPC is currently moving towards), if any is available.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the current NPC waypoint.

GetEnemy.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity that this NPC is trying to fight.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This returns nil if the NPC has no enemy. You should use [IsValid](/gmod/Global.IsValid) (which accounts for nil and NULL) on the return to verify validity of the enemy.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Enemy NPC.

GetEnemyFirstTimeSeen.DESCRIPTION: Returns the first time an NPC's enemy was seen by the NPC.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to check.

RETURNS.NAME: time
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: First time the given enemy was seen.

GetEnemyLastKnownPos.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the last known position of an NPC's enemy.

Similar to [NPC:GetEnemyLastSeenPos](/gmod/NPC:GetEnemyLastSeenPos), but the known position will be a few seconds ahead of the last seen position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to check.

RETURNS.NAME: pos
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The last known position.

GetEnemyLastSeenPos.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the last seen position of an NPC's enemy.

Similar to [NPC:GetEnemyLastKnownPos](/gmod/NPC:GetEnemyLastKnownPos), but the known position will be a few seconds ahead of the last seen position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to check.

RETURNS.NAME: pos
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The last seen position.

GetEnemyLastTimeSeen.DESCRIPTION: Returns the last time an NPC's enemy was seen by the NPC.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to check.

RETURNS.NAME: time
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Last time the given enemy was seen.

GetExpression.DESCRIPTION: Returns the expression file the NPC is currently playing.

RETURNS.NAME: m_iszExpressionScene
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The file path of the expression.

GetEyeDirection.DESCRIPTION: Returns the eye direction of the NPC.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The eye direction.

GetFOV.DESCRIPTION: Returns the Field Of View of the NPC. See [NPC:SetFOV](/gmod/NPC:SetFOV).

RETURNS.NAME: fov
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The FOV for the NPC in degrees.

GetGoalPos.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position we are trying to reach, if any.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position we are trying to reach.

GetGoalTarget.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity we are trying to reach, if any.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entity we are trying to reach, or `NULL`.

GetHeadDirection.DESCRIPTION: Returns the 2D head direction of the NPC.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The head direction.

GetHullType.DESCRIPTION: Returns NPCs hull type set by [NPC:SetHullType](/gmod/NPC:SetHullType).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Hull type, see [HULL](/gmod/Enums/HULL)

GetIdealActivity.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ideal activity the NPC currently wants to achieve.
NOTES: By default, base NPCs will automatically attempt to play a sequence bound to the ideal activity. To prevent ideal activity from overriding NPC's active sequence, set this to `ACT_DO_NOT_DISTURB`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ideal activity. [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

GetIdealMoveAcceleration.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ideal move acceleration of the NPC.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ideal move acceleration.

GetIdealMoveSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ideal move speed of the NPC.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ideal move speed.

GetIdealSequence.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ideal sequence the NPC currently wants to achieve.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ideal sequence, specific to the NPCs model.

GetIdealYaw.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ideal yaw (left right rotation) for this NPC at this moment.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ideal yaw.

GetKnownEnemies.DESCRIPTION:
Returns all known enemies this NPC has. The enemy table is updated with [NPC:UpdateEnemyMemory](/gmod/NPC:UpdateEnemyMemory) and [NPC:ClearEnemyMemory](/gmod/NPC:ClearEnemyMemory), meaning other entities may be in enemies list even though your NPC doesn't hate it. 

See also [NPC:GetKnownEnemyCount](/gmod/NPC:GetKnownEnemyCount)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of entities that this NPC knows as enemies.

GetKnownEnemyCount.DESCRIPTION:
Returns known enemy count of this NPC.

See also [NPC:GetKnownEnemies](/gmod/NPC:GetKnownEnemies)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Amount of entities that this NPC knows as enemies.

GetLastPosition.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the last registered or memorized position of the NPC. When using scheduling, the NPC will focus on navigating to the last position via nodes.

See [NPC:SetLastPosition](/gmod/NPC:SetLastPosition).

RETURNS.NAME: position
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Where the NPC's last position was set to.

GetLastTimeTookDamageFromEnemy.DESCRIPTION: Returns [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime) based time since this NPC last received damage from given enemy. The last damage time is set when [NPC:MarkTookDamageFromEnemy](/gmod/NPC:MarkTookDamageFromEnemy) is called.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enemy
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The enemy to test. Defaults to currently active enemy ([NPC:GetEnemy](/gmod/NPC:GetEnemy))

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Time since this NPC last received damage from given enemy.

GetMaxLookDistance.DESCRIPTION: Returns NPCs max view distance. An NPC will not be able to see enemies outside of this distance.

RETURNS.NAME: dist
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum distance the NPC can see at.

GetMinMoveCheckDist.DESCRIPTION: Returns how far should the NPC look ahead in its route.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: How far the NPC checks ahead of its route.

GetMinMoveStopDist.DESCRIPTION: Returns how far before the NPC can come to a complete stop.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: minResult
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum value that will be returned by this function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum stop distance.

GetMoveDelay.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the movement delay for given NPC.

See [NPC:SetMoveDelay](/gmod/NPC:SetMoveDelay).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The movement delay.

GetMoveInterval.DESCRIPTION: Returns the current timestep the internal NPC motor is working on.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current timestep.

GetMovementActivity.DESCRIPTION: Returns the NPC's current movement activity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Current NPC movement activity, see [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).
