Returns the 64-bit SteamID aka CommunityID of the Steam Account that owns the Garry's Mod license this player is using. This is useful for detecting players using Steam Family Sharing.

If player is not using Steam Family Sharing, this will return the player's actual SteamID64().
NOTES: This data will only be available after the player has fully authenticated with Steam. See [Player:IsFullyAuthenticated](/gmod/Player:IsFullyAuthenticated).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The 64bit SteamID

PacketLoss.DESCRIPTION: Returns the percentage of packets lost by the client. It is not networked so it only returns 0 when run clientside.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Percentage of packets lost (0-100)

PhysgunUnfreeze.DESCRIPTION:
Unfreezes the props player is looking at. This is essentially the same as pressing reload with the physics gun, including double press for unfreeze all.

For freezing props, use [PhysObj:EnableMotion](/gmod/PhysObj:EnableMotion).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of props unfrozen.

PickupObject.DESCRIPTION:
This makes the player hold (same as pressing  on a small prop) given entity.

Not to be confused with picking up items like ammo or health kits.

This picks up the passed entity regardless of its mass or distance from the player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to pick up.

PickupWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Forces the player to pickup an existing weapon entity. The player will not pick up the weapon if they already own a weapon of given type, or if the player could not normally have this weapon in their inventory.

This function **will** bypass [GM:PlayerCanPickupWeapon](/gmod/GM:PlayerCanPickupWeapon).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: wep
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The weapon to try to pick up.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoOnly
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to true, the player will only attempt to pick up the ammo from the weapon. The weapon will not be picked up even if the player doesn't have a weapon of this type, and the weapon will be removed if the player picks up any ammo from it.

RETURNS.NAME: result
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the player succeeded in picking up the weapon or not.

Ping.DESCRIPTION: Returns the player's ping to server.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The player's ping.

PlayStepSound.DESCRIPTION: Plays the correct step sound according to what the player is staying on.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Volume for the sound, in range from 0 to 1

PrintMessage.DESCRIPTION: Displays a message either in their chat, console, or center of the screen. See also [PrintMessage](/gmod/Global.PrintMessage).
NOTES:
When called serverside, this uses the archaic user message system (the [umsg](/gmod/umsg)) and hence is limited to ≈250 characters.

`HUD_PRINTCENTER` will not work when this is called clientside.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Which type of message should be sent to the player ([HUD](/gmod/Enums/HUD)).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: message
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Message to be sent to the player.

RemoveAllAmmo.DESCRIPTION: Removes all ammo from a certain player

RemoveAllItems.DESCRIPTION: Removes all weapons and ammo from the player.

RemoveAmmo.DESCRIPTION: Removes the amount of the specified ammo from the player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of ammunition to remove.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the ammunition to remove from. This can also be a [number](/gmod/number) ammoID.

RemovePData.DESCRIPTION:
Removes a **P**ersistent **Data** key-value pair from the SQL database. (`sv.db` when called on server, `cl.db` when called on client)

Internally uses the [sql](/gmod/sql) library. See [util.RemovePData](/gmod/util.RemovePData) for cases when the player is not currently on the server.
NOTES: PData is not networked from servers to clients!

This function internally uses [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which can cause collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry). [Player:SetPData](/gmod/Player:SetPData) now replaces all instances of [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) with [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) when running [Player:SetPData](/gmod/Player:SetPData)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Key to remove

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true is succeeded, false otherwise

ResetHull.DESCRIPTION: Resets both normal and duck hulls to their default values.

Say.DESCRIPTION: Forces the player to say whatever the first argument is. Works on bots too.
NOTES: This function ignores the default chat message cooldown
WARNINGS: The argument can only contain 126 characters. [Source SDK 2013](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/0d8dceea4310fde5706b3ce1c70609d72a38efdf/sp/src/game/server/client.cpp#L84-L86)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: text
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The text to force the player to say.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: teamOnly
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to send this message to our own team only.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Fade flags defined with [SCREENFADE](/gmod/Enums/SCREENFADE).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The color of the screenfade

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fadeTime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Fade(in/out) effect transition time ( From no fade to full fade and vice versa ).

This is limited to 7 bits integer part and 9 bits fractional part.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fadeHold
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Fade effect hold time.

This is limited to 7 bits integer part and 9 bits fractional part.

SelectWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Sets the active weapon of the player by its class name.
NOTES: This will trigger the weapon switch event and associated animations. To switch weapons silently, use [Player:SetActiveWeapon](/gmod/Player:SetActiveWeapon).
WARNINGS: This will switch the weapon out of prediction, causing delay on the client and [WEAPON:Deploy](/gmod/WEAPON:Deploy) and [WEAPON:Holster](/gmod/WEAPON:Holster) to be called out of prediction. Try using [CUserCmd:SelectWeapon](/gmod/CUserCmd:SelectWeapon) or [input.SelectWeapon](/gmod/input.SelectWeapon), instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: className
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The class name of the weapon to switch to.

If the player doesn't have the specified weapon, nothing will happen. You can use [Player:Give](/gmod/Player:Give) to give the weapon first.

SendHint.DESCRIPTION: Sends a hint to a player.
NOTES: This function is only available in Sandbox and its derivatives. Since this adds `#Hint_` to the beginning of each message, you should only use it with default hint messages, or those cached with [language.Add](/gmod/language.Add). For hints with custom text, look at [notification.AddLegacy](/gmod/notification.AddLegacy).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name/class/index of the hint. You can find a list of hint names for this function [here](/gmod/List_of_Hint_Classes).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay in seconds before showing the hint

SendLua.DESCRIPTION: Executes a simple Lua string on the player.
NOTES: If you need to use this function more than once consider using [net](/gmod/net) library. Send net message and make the entire code you want to execute in [net.Receive](/gmod/net.Receive) on client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: script
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The script to execute, limited to 6000 bytes.

SetActiveWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player's active weapon. You should use [CUserCmd:SelectWeapon](/gmod/CUserCmd:SelectWeapon) or [Player:SelectWeapon](/gmod/Player:SelectWeapon), instead in most cases.

This function will not trigger the weapon switch events or associated equip animations. It will bypass 
 [GM:PlayerSwitchWeapon](/gmod/GM:PlayerSwitchWeapon) and the currently active weapon's [WEAPON:Holster](/gmod/WEAPON:Holster) return value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weapon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The weapon to equip.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: act
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new activity to set. See [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

SetAllowFullRotation.DESCRIPTION: Set if the players' model is allowed to rotate around the pitch and roll axis.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Allowed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Allowed to rotate

SetAllowWeaponsInVehicle.DESCRIPTION: Allows player to use their weapons in a vehicle. You need to call this before entering a vehicle.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Shooting in a vehicle fires two bullets.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: allow
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Show we allow player to use their weapons in a vehicle or not.

SetAmmo.DESCRIPTION: Sets the amount of the specified ammo for the player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of ammunition to set.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ammunition type. Can be either number ammo ID or string ammo name. See [Default Ammo Types](/gmod/Default%20Ammo%20Types) for default values.

SetArmor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player armor value.

See [GM:HandlePlayerArmorReduction](/gmod/GM:HandlePlayerArmorReduction) for a hook that allows manipulating what armor does.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: amount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount to set the armor value of the player to.

SetAvoidPlayers.DESCRIPTION:
Pushes the player away from other players whenever the player inside another players' bounding box.

This avoidance is performed clientside by altering movement sent to server.

This applies to players within a single team. ([Player:Team](/gmod/Player:Team))

ARGUMENTS.NAME: avoidPlayers
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to avoid teammates, or not.

SetCanWalk.DESCRIPTION: Set if the player should be allowed to walk using the (default) alt key. (`+walk` keybind)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: canWalk
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `true` allows the player to walk.

SetCanZoom.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether the player can use the HL2 suit zoom (`+zoom` bind) or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: canZoom
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to make the player able or unable to zoom.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The class id the player is being set with.

SetCrouchedWalkSpeed.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the crouched walk speed multiplier.

Has no effect for values above 1.

See also [Player:SetWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetWalkSpeed) and [Player:GetCrouchedWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:GetCrouchedWalkSpeed).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The walk speed multiplier that crouch speed should be.

SetCurrentViewOffset.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the **actual** view offset which equals the difference between the players actual position and their view when standing.

Do not confuse with [Player:SetViewOffset](/gmod/Player:SetViewOffset) and [Player:SetViewOffsetDucked](/gmod/Player:SetViewOffsetDucked)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new view offset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: deathCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Number of deaths (positive or negative)

SetDrivingEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the driving entity and driving mode.

Use [drive.PlayerStartDriving](/gmod/drive.PlayerStartDriving) instead, see [Entity Driving](/gmod/Entity%20Driving).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: drivingEntity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity the player should drive.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: drivingMode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The driving mode index.

SetDSP.DESCRIPTION:
Activates a given DSP (Digital Signal Processor) effect on all sounds that the player hears. This is equivalent to setting `dsp_player` convar on the player.

		To apply a DSP effect to individual sounds, see [CSoundPatch:SetDSP](/gmod/CSoundPatch:SetDSP)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dspEffectId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The index of the DSP sound filter to apply.

			For a list of the available IDs and their meaning, see [DSP Presets](/gmod/DSP_Presets).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fastReset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to true the sound filter will be removed faster.
NOTES:
**This only works clientside**  
				If used serverside, a message will be displayed (`SetPlayerDSP: fastReset only valid from client`) in the server console.

SetDuckSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Sets how quickly a player ducks.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will not work for values >= 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duckSpeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How quickly the player will duck.

SetEyeAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets the local angle of the player's view (may rotate body too if angular difference is large)
NOTES: This function works differently when the player is in a vehicle. In that case passing `Angle(0, 90, 0)` will have the player look forward (out the windshield) and `Angle(0, 0, 0)` will have them look to the right.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angle to set the view to

SetFlashlightColor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the color of a player's flashlight. 
		Can be used on other players.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Flashlight color

SetFOV.DESCRIPTION:
Set a player's FOV (Field Of View) over a certain amount of time.

This is meant to be called on the server or shared (for prediction), it will have no effect if called clientside only. You may want to use [GM:CalcView](/gmod/GM:CalcView) for that instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fov
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: the angle of perception (FOV). Set to 0 to return to default user FOV. ( Which is ranging from 75 to 100, depending on user settings )

ARGUMENTS.NAME: time
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: the time it takes to transition to the FOV expressed in a floating point.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: requester
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The requester or "owner" of the zoom event. Only this entity will be able to change the player's FOV until it is set back to 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fragCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Number of frags (positive or negative)

SetHands.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the hands entity of a player.

The hands entity is an entity introduced in Garry's Mod 13 and it's used to show the player's hands attached to the viewmodel.
This is similar to the approach used in L4D and CS:GO, for more information on how to implement this system in your gamemode visit [Using Viewmodel Hands](/gmod/Using%20Viewmodel%20Hands).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hands
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hands entity to set

SetHoveredWidget.DESCRIPTION: Sets the widget that is currently hovered by the player's mouse.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: widget
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The widget entity that the player is hovering.

SetHull.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the size of the [Player's](/gmod/Player) [Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box) used for physics and movement [Hull Traces](/gmod/util.TraceHull).

		See also: [Player:GetHull](/gmod/Player:GetHull), [Player:SetHullDuck](/gmod/Player:SetHullDuck), [Player:GetHullDuck](/gmod/Player:GetHullDuck)
NOTES: This value is **not** replicated automatically to clients and must be manually called in both the Server and Client [Realms](/gmod/States).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hull mins, the lowest corner of the Player's bounding box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hull maxs, the highest corner of the Player's bounding box, opposite of the mins.

SetHullDuck.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the size of the [Player's](/gmod/Player) [Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box) used for physics and movement [Hull Traces](/gmod/util.TraceHull) while they are crouching (or "Ducking").

		See also: [Player:GetHullDuck](/gmod/Player:GetHullDuck), [Player:GetHull](/gmod/Player:GetHull), [Player:SetHull](/gmod/Player:SetHull)
NOTES: This value is **not** replicated automatically to clients and must be manually called in both the Server and Client [Realms](/gmod/States).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hull mins, the lowest corner of the Player's bounding box while crouching.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hull maxs, the highest corner of the Player's crouching bounding box, opposite of the mins.

SetJumpPower.DESCRIPTION: Sets the jump power, eg. the velocity that will be applied to the player when they jump.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: jumpPower
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new jump velocity.

SetLadderClimbSpeed.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player's ladder climbing speed.

See [Player:SetWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetWalkSpeed) for normal walking speed, [Player:SetRunSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetRunSpeed) for sprinting speed and [Player:SetSlowWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetSlowWalkSpeed) for slow walking speed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ladder climbing speed.

SetLaggedMovementValue.DESCRIPTION:
Slows down the player movement simulation by the timescale, this is used internally in the HL2 weapon stripping sequence.

It achieves such behavior by multiplying the [FrameTime](/gmod/Global.FrameTime) by the specified timescale at the start of the movement simulation and then restoring it afterwards.
NOTES:
This is reset to 1 on spawn.

There is no weapon counterpart to this, you'll have to hardcode the multiplier in the weapon or call [Weapon:SetNextPrimaryFire](/gmod/Weapon:SetNextPrimaryFire) / [Weapon:SetNextSecondaryFire](/gmod/Weapon:SetNextSecondaryFire) manually.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: timescale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The timescale multiplier.

SetLastHitGroup.DESCRIPTION: Sets the hitgroup where the player was last hit.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hitgroup
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hitgroup to set as the "last hit", see [HITGROUP](/gmod/Enums/HITGROUP).

SetMaxArmor.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum amount of armor the player should have. This affects default built-in armor pickups, but not [Player:SetArmor](/gmod/Player:SetArmor).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxarmor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new max armor value.

SetMaxSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum speed which the player can move at.
NOTES: This is called automatically by the engine. If you wish to limit player speed without setting their run/sprint speeds, see [CMoveData:SetMaxClientSpeed](/gmod/CMoveData:SetMaxClientSpeed).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: walkSpeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum speed.

SetMuted.DESCRIPTION: Sets if the player should be voicechat muted locally.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mute
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Mute or unmute.

SetNoCollideWithTeammates.DESCRIPTION: Sets whenever the player should not collide with their teammates, based on their [Player:Team](/gmod/Player:Team).
NOTES: This will only work for teams with ID 1 to 4 due to internal Engine limitations.
This causes traces with [COLLISION_GROUP_PLAYER](/gmod/Enums/COLLISION_GROUP) to pass through players.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldNotCollide
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `true` to disable, `false` to enable collision.

SetNoTarget.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the players visibility towards NPCs.

Internally this toggles the [FL_NOTARGET](/gmod/Enums/FL) flag, which you can manually test for using [Entity:IsFlagSet](/gmod/Entity:IsFlagSet)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: visibility
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The visibility.

SetObserverMode.DESCRIPTION: Sets the players observer mode. You must start the spectating first with [Player:Spectate](/gmod/Player:Spectate).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Spectator mode using [OBS_MODE](/gmod/Enums/OBS_MODE).

SetPData.DESCRIPTION:
Writes a **P**ersistent **Data** key-value pair to the SQL database. (`sv.db` when called on server, `cl.db` when called on client)

Internally uses the [sql](/gmod/sql) library. See [util.SetPData](/gmod/util.SetPData) for cases when the player is not currently on the server.
NOTES: PData is not networked from servers to clients!

This function internally uses [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which could have caused collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry). [Player:SetPData](/gmod/Player:SetPData) now replaces all instances of [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) with [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) when running [Player:SetPData](/gmod/Player:SetPData)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the PData key

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to write to the key (**must** be an SQL valid data type, such as a string or integer)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the operation was successful or not

SetPlayerColor.DESCRIPTION: Sets the player model's color. The part of the model that is colored is determined by the model itself, and is different for each model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This is the color to be set. The format is Vector(r, g, b), and each color should be between 0 and 1.

SetPressedWidget.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the widget that is currently in use by the player's mouse.

Having a pressed widget stops the player from firing their weapon to allow input to be passed onto the widget.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pressedWidget
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The widget the player is currently using.

SetRenderAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets the render angles of a player. Value set by this function is reset to player's angles ([Entity:GetAngles](/gmod/Entity:GetAngles)) right after [GM:UpdateAnimation](/gmod/GM:UpdateAnimation).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ang
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new render angles to set

SetRunSpeed.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player's sprint speed.

See also [Player:GetRunSpeed](/gmod/Player:GetRunSpeed), [Player:SetWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetWalkSpeed) and [Player:SetMaxSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetMaxSpeed).
NOTES: player_default class run speed is: `400`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: runSpeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The new sprint speed when `sv_friction` is below `10`. Higher `sv_friction` values will result in slower speed.

Has to be `7` or above or the player **won't** be able to move.

SetSlowWalkSpeed.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player's slow walking speed, which is activated via  keybind.

See [Player:SetWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetWalkSpeed) for normal walking speed, [Player:SetRunSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetRunSpeed) for sprinting speed and [Player:SetLadderClimbSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetLadderClimbSpeed) for ladder climb speed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new slow walking speed.

SetStepSize.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum height a player can step onto without jumping.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stepHeight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new maximum height the player can step onto without jumping

SetSuitPower.DESCRIPTION: Sets the player's HEV suit power.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will only work for the local player when used clientside.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: power
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new suit power.

SetSuppressPickupNotices.DESCRIPTION: Sets whenever to suppress the pickup notification for the player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: doSuppress
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whenever to suppress the notice or not.

SetTeam.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player to the chosen team. The value is networked to clients at reduced bit count (16 bits) as as a signed value, so the real range is [-32768, 32767].

Can be retrieved via [Player:Team](/gmod/Player:Team)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: team
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The team that the player is being set to.

SetUnDuckSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Sets how quickly a player un-ducks

ARGUMENTS.NAME: UnDuckSpeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How quickly the player will un-duck

SetupHands.DESCRIPTION: Sets up the player's hands for the viewmodel. Calls [GM:PlayerSetHandsModel](/gmod/GM:PlayerSetHandsModel) to determine the model. If no entity is provided, uses the player's own hands model. If spectating another entity, pass that entity to use its hands model instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the player is spectating an entity, this should be the entity the player is spectating, so we can use its hands model instead.

SetUserGroup.DESCRIPTION: Sets the usergroup of the player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: groupName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The user group of the player.

SetViewEntity.DESCRIPTION: Attaches the players view to the position and angles of the specified entity.
NOTES: By default, the view is in first person and its model will not be rendered. [Player:SetObserverMode](/gmod/Player:SetObserverMode) can be used to enable drawing of view entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewEntity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to attach the player view to.

SetViewOffset.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the **desired** view offset which equals the difference between the players actual position and their view when standing.

If you want to set **actual** view offset, use [Player:SetCurrentViewOffset](/gmod/Player:SetCurrentViewOffset)

See also [Player:SetViewOffsetDucked](/gmod/Player:SetViewOffsetDucked) for **desired** view offset when crouching.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new desired view offset when standing.

SetViewOffsetDucked.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the **desired** view offset which equals the difference between the players actual position and their view when crouching.

If you want to set **actual** view offset, use [Player:SetCurrentViewOffset](/gmod/Player:SetCurrentViewOffset)

See also [Player:SetViewOffset](/gmod/Player:SetViewOffset) for **desired** view offset when standing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new desired view offset when crouching.

SetViewPunchAngles.DESCRIPTION: Sets client's view punch angle, but not the velocity. See [Player:ViewPunch](/gmod/Player:ViewPunch)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: punchAngle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to set.

SetViewPunchVelocity.DESCRIPTION: Sets client's view punch velocity. See [Player:ViewPunch](/gmod/Player:ViewPunch) and [Player:SetViewPunchAngles](/gmod/Player:SetViewPunchAngles)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: punchVel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle velocity to set.

SetVoiceVolumeScale.DESCRIPTION: Sets the voice volume scale for given player on client. This value will persist from server to server, but will be reset when the game is shut down.
NOTES: This doesn't work on bots, their scale will always be `1`. Does not work with multiruns.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The voice volume scale, where `0` is 0% and `1` is 100%.

SetWalkSpeed.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the player's normal walking speed. Not sprinting, not slow walking .

See also [Player:SetSlowWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetSlowWalkSpeed), [Player:GetWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:GetWalkSpeed), [Player:SetCrouchedWalkSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetCrouchedWalkSpeed), [Player:SetMaxSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetMaxSpeed) and [Player:SetRunSpeed](/gmod/Player:SetRunSpeed).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Using a speed of `0` can lead to prediction errors, and can cause players to move at sv_maxvelocity

NOTES: `player_default` class walk speed is: `200`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: walkSpeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The new walk speed when `sv_friction` is below `10`. Higher `sv_friction` values will result in slower speed.

Has to be `7` or above or the player **won't** be able to move.

SetWeaponColor.DESCRIPTION: Sets the player weapon's color. The part of the model that is colored is determined by the model itself, and is different for each model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This is the color to be set. The format is Vector(r,g,b), and each color should be between 0 and 1.

ShouldDrawLocalPlayer.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the **local player's** player model will be drawn at the time the function is called.

Despite this being a method on a player object, this will always represent the state of the [local player](/gmod/Global.LocalPlayer), not of the player entity this method is used on.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the player's playermodel is visible

ShouldDropWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether the player's current weapon should drop on death.
NOTES: This is reset on spawn to the [player class](/gmod/Player_Classes)'s **DropWeaponOnDie** field by [player_manager.OnPlayerSpawn](/gmod/player_manager.OnPlayerSpawn).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: drop
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to drop the player's current weapon or not

ShowProfile.DESCRIPTION: Opens the player steam profile page in the steam overlay browser.

SimulateGravGunDrop.DESCRIPTION: Signals the entity that it was dropped by the gravity gun.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity that was dropped.

SimulateGravGunPickup.DESCRIPTION: Signals the entity that it was picked up by the gravity gun. This call is only required if you want to simulate the situation of picking up objects.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity picked up

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightning
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to show lightning effects around the entity

Spectate.DESCRIPTION:
Starts spectate mode for given player. This will also affect the players movetype in some cases.

[Player:UnSpectate](/gmod/Player:UnSpectate) should be used to remove the player from spectate mode, or call this with `OBS_MODE_NONE`.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The player must be respawned, otherwise they will be able to walk through doors and become invincible. This will be fixed in a future update.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Spectate mode, see [OBS_MODE](/gmod/Enums/OBS_MODE).

SpectateEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Makes the player spectate the entity.

To get the applied spectated entity, use [Player:GetObserverTarget](/gmod/Player:GetObserverTarget).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to spectate.

SprayDecal.DESCRIPTION: Makes a player spray their decal.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sprayOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The location to spray from

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sprayEndPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The location to spray to

SprintDisable.DESCRIPTION: Disables the sprint on the player.

SprintEnable.DESCRIPTION: Enables the sprint on the player.

DEPRECATED: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

StartWalking.DESCRIPTION: When used in a [GM:SetupMove](/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function will force the player to walk, as well as preventing the player from sprinting.
DEPRECATED: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

SteamID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the player's SteamID.

See [Player:AccountID](/gmod/Player:AccountID) for a shorter version of the SteamID and [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) for the full SteamID.

It is recommended to use [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) over the other SteamID formats whenever possible.
NOTES:
In a `-multirun` environment, this will return `STEAM_ID_LAN` for all "copies" of a player because they are not authenticated with Steam.

For Bots this will return `BOT`.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: "Text" representation of the player's SteamID.

SteamID64.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the player's full **64-bit SteamID**, also known as **CommunityID**. Information on how data is packed into this value can be found [here](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamID).

See [Player:AccountID](/gmod/Player:AccountID) for a function that returns only the Account ID part of the SteamID and [Player:SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID) for the text version of the SteamID.
NOTES:
In a `-multirun` environment, this will return `"0"` for all "copies" of a player because they are not authenticated with Steam.

For bots, this will return `90071996842377216` (equivalent to `STEAM_0:0:0`) for the first bot to join.

For each additional bot, the number increases by 1. So the next bot will be `90071996842377217` (`STEAM_0:1:0`) then `90071996842377218` (`STEAM_0:0:1`) and so on.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Player's 64-bit SteamID aka CommunityID.
NOTES: The return value is a string, not a number, since Lua's numbers are unable to store the entire 64bit numbers without data loss.

StopSprinting.DESCRIPTION:
When used in a [GM:SetupMove](/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function will prevent the player from sprinting.

When +walk is engaged, the player will still be able to sprint to half speed (normal run speed) as opposed to full sprint speed without this function.
DEPRECATED: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

StopWalking.DESCRIPTION: When used in a [GM:SetupMove](/gmod/GM:SetupMove) hook, this function behaves unexpectedly by preventing the player from sprinting similar to [Player:StopSprinting](/gmod/Player:StopSprinting).
DEPRECATED: This appears to be a direct binding to internal functionality that is overridden by the engine every frame so calling these functions may not have any or expected effect.

StopZooming.DESCRIPTION:
Turns off the zoom mode of the player. (+zoom console command)

Basically equivalent of entering "-zoom" into player's console.

StripAmmo.DESCRIPTION: Removes all ammo from the player.
DEPRECATED: Alias of Player:RemoveAllAmmo

StripWeapon.DESCRIPTION: Removes the specified weapon class from a certain player
NOTES: this function will call the [Entity:OnRemove](/gmod/Entity:OnRemove) but if you try use [Entity:GetOwner](/gmod/Entity:GetOwner) it will return nil

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weapon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The weapon class to remove

StripWeapons.DESCRIPTION: Removes all weapons from a certain player

SuppressHint.DESCRIPTION: Prevents a hint from showing up.
NOTES: This function is only available in Sandbox and its derivatives

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Hint name/class/index to prevent from showing up. You can find a list of hint names for this function [here](/gmod/List_of_Hint_Classes).

SwitchToDefaultWeapon.DESCRIPTION:
Attempts to switch the player weapon to the one specified in the "cl_defaultweapon" convar, if the player does not own the specified weapon nothing will happen.

If you want to switch to a specific weapon, use: [Player:SetActiveWeapon](/gmod/Player:SetActiveWeapon)

Team.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the player's team ID, set by [Player:SetTeam](/gmod/Player:SetTeam)

Returns 0 clientside when the game is not fully loaded.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The player's team's index number, as in the [TEAM](/gmod/Enums/TEAM) or a custom team defined in [team.SetUp](/gmod/team.SetUp).

TimeConnected.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the time in seconds since the player connected.

Bots will always return value 0.

RETURNS.NAME: connectedTime
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: How long this player was connected to the server for, in seconds.

TraceHullAttack.DESCRIPTION: Performs a trace hull and applies damage to the entities hit, returns the first entity hit.
WARNINGS: Hitting the victim entity with this function in [ENTITY:OnTakeDamage](/gmod/ENTITY:OnTakeDamage) can cause infinite loops.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the hull trace.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the hull trace.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum coordinates of the hull.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum coordinates of the hull.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: damage

IsValid.DESCRIPTION:
Returns true if the projected texture is valid (i.e. has not been removed), false otherwise.

Instead of calling this directly it's a good idea to call [IsValid](/gmod/Global.IsValid) in case the variable is nil.

```
IsValid( ptexture )
```

This not only checks whether the projected texture is valid - but also checks whether it's nil.

Remove.DESCRIPTION: Removes the projected texture. After calling this, [ProjectedTexture:IsValid](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:IsValid) will return false, and any hooks with the projected texture as the identifier will be automatically deleted.

SetAngles.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the angles (direction) of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetBrightness.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the brightness of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: brightness
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The brightness to give the projected texture. A float from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100% brightness. Can be higher.

SetColor.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the color of the projected texture.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Unlike other projected textures, this color can only go up to 255.

SetConstantAttenuation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the constant attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetEnableShadows.DESCRIPTION:
Enable or disable shadows cast from the projected texture.



You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.
NOTES: As with all types of projected textures (including the player's flashlight and env_projectedtexture), there can only be 8 projected textures with shadows enabled in total.This limit can be increased with the launch parameter `-numshadowtextures LIMIT` where `LIMIT` is the new limit.Naturally, many projected lights with shadows enabled will drastically decrease framerate.

SetFarZ.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the distance at which the projected texture ends.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetFOV.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the angle of projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fov
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Must be higher than 0 and lower than 180

SetHorizontalFOV.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the horizontal angle of projection without affecting the vertical angle.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hFOV
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new horizontal Field Of View for the projected texture. Must be in range between 0 and 180.

SetLightWorld.DESCRIPTION: Set whenever or not the Texture should light up world geometry.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightworld
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set it to `true` if the Texture should light up world geometry.

SetLinearAttenuation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the linear attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetQuadraticAttenuation).

The default value of linear attenuation when the projected texture is created is 100. (others are 0, as you are not supposed to mix them)

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetNearZ.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the distance at which the projected texture begins its projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.
NOTES: Setting this to 0 will disable the projected texture completely! This may be useful if you want to disable a projected texture without actually removing it

This seems to affect the rendering of shadows - a higher Near Z value will have shadows begin to render closer to their casting object. Comparing a low Near Z value (like 1) with a normal one (12) or high one (1000) is the easiest way to understand this artifact

SetNoCull.DESCRIPTION:
Allows disabling of projected texture view-frustum culling for cases where said culling creates unwanted side effects. Disabling culling will have a negative effect on performance.

Culling makes projected textures off screen to stop rendering/updating.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `false` to enable culling (default), `true` to disable.

SetOrthographic.DESCRIPTION:
Changes the current projected texture between orthographic and perspective projection.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

Shadows dont work. (For non static props and for most map brushes)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: orthographic
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: When false, all other arguments are ignored and the texture is reset to perspective projection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: left
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of units left from the projected texture's origin to project.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: top
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of units upwards from the projected texture's origin to project.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: right
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of units right from the projected texture's origin to project.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bottom
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of units downwards from the projected texture's origin to project.

SetPos.DESCRIPTION:
Move the Projected Texture to the specified position.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetQuadraticAttenuation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the quadratic attenuation of the projected texture.

See also [ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetLinearAttenuation) and [ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:SetConstantAttenuation).

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

SetShadowDepthBias.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the shadow depth bias of the projected texture.

The initial value is `0.0001`. Normal projected textures obey the value of the `mat_depthbias_shadowmap` [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bias
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The shadow depth bias to set.

SetShadowFilter.DESCRIPTION: Sets the shadow "filter size" of the projected texture. `0` is fully pixelated, higher values will blur the shadow more. The initial value is the value of `r_projectedtexture_filter` [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The shadow filter size to set.

SetShadowSlopeScaleDepthBias.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the shadow depth slope scale bias of the projected texture.

The initial value is `2`. Normal projected textures obey the value of the `mat_slopescaledepthbias_shadowmap` [ConVar](/gmod/ConVar).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bias
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The shadow depth slope scale bias to set.

SetSkipShadowUpdates.DESCRIPTION: Sets whether shadow updates are disabled for this ProjectedTexture. This can be useful to save up on performance, but it will inevitably cause graphical glitches if left not updating for long.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether future shadow updates should be skipped.

SetTargetEntity.DESCRIPTION: Sets the target entity for this projected texture, meaning it will only be lighting the given entity and the world.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The target entity, or `NULL` to reset.

SetTexture.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the texture to be projected.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texture
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the texture. Can also be an [ITexture](/gmod/ITexture).

SetTextureFrame.DESCRIPTION:
For animated textures, this will choose which frame in the animation will be projected.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: frame
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The frame index to use.

SetVerticalFOV.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the vertical angle of projection without affecting the horizontal angle.

You must call [ProjectedTexture:Update](/gmod/ProjectedTexture:Update) after using this function for it to take effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vFOV
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new vertical Field Of View for the projected texture. Must be in range between 0 and 180.

The best place to call this function is in [GM:PreDrawOpaqueRenderables](/gmod/GM:PreDrawOpaqueRenderables).

Stack.DESCRIPTION:
An object returned by [util.Stack](/gmod/util.Stack).

Like a Lua table, a Stack is a container. It follows the principle of LIFO (last in, first out).

The Stack works like a stack of papers: the first page you put down (push) will be the last one you remove (pop). That also means that the last page you put down, will be the first to be removed.

* * Stage 3
* Operation 2
* * Stage 1
* * Stage 2
* * Stage ...

UpdateGhostEntity.DESCRIPTION:

This should be called in the tool's [TOOL:Think](/gmod/TOOL:Think) hook.

This command is only used for tools that move props, such as easy weld, axis and motor. If you want to update a ghost like the thruster tool does it for example, check its [source code](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/gamemodes/sandbox/entities/weapons/gmod_tool/stools/thruster.lua#L179).

Add.DESCRIPTION: Adds the values of the argument vector to the original vector. This function is the same as vector1 + vector2 without creating a new vector object, skipping object construction and garbage collection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to add.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The angle/direction of the vector.

AngleEx.DESCRIPTION: Returns the angle of this vector (normalized), but instead of assuming that up is [Vector](/gmod/Global.Vector)( 0, 0, 1 ) (Like [Vector:Angle](/gmod/Vector:Angle) does) you can specify which direction is 'up' for the angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: up
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The up direction vector

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The angle

Cross.DESCRIPTION:
Calculates the cross product of this vector and the passed one.

The cross product of two vectors is a 3-dimensional vector with a direction perpendicular (at right angles) to both of them (according to the [right-hand rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-hand_rule)), and magnitude equal to the area of parallelogram they span. This is defined as the product of the magnitudes, the sine of the angle between them, and unit (normal) vector `n` defined by the right-hand rule:
:**a** × **b** = |**a**| |**b**| sin(θ) **n̂**
where **a** and **b** are vectors, and **n̂** is a unit vector (magnitude of 1) perpendicular to both.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Vector to calculate the cross product with.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The cross product of the two vectors.

Distance.DESCRIPTION: Returns the Euclidean distance between the vector and the other vector.
NOTES: This function is more expensive than [Vector:DistToSqr](/gmod/Vector:DistToSqr). However, please see the notes for [Vector:DistToSqr](/gmod/Vector:DistToSqr) before using it as squared distances are not the same as euclidean distances.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to get the distance to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Distance between the vectors.

Distance2D.DESCRIPTION: Returns the Euclidean distance between the vector and the other vector in 2D space. The Z axis is ignored.
NOTES: This function is more expensive than [Vector:Distance2DSqr](/gmod/Vector:Distance2DSqr). However, please see the notes for [Vector:Distance2DSqr](/gmod/Vector:Distance2DSqr) before using it as squared distances are not the same as Euclidean distances.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to get the distance to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Distance between the vectors in 2D space.

Distance2DSqr.DESCRIPTION: Returns the squared distance between 2 vectors in 2D space, ignoring the Z axis. This is faster than [Vector:Distance2D](/gmod/Vector:Distance2D) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.
NOTES:
Squared distances should not be summed. If you need to sum distances, use [Vector:Distance2D](/gmod/Vector:Distance2D).

When performing a distance check, ensure the distance being checked against is squared.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVec
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to calculate the distance to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Squared distance to the vector in 2D space.

DistToSqr.DESCRIPTION: Returns the squared distance of 2 vectors, this is quicker to call than [Vector:Distance](/gmod/Vector:Distance) as DistToSqr does not need to calculate the square root, which is an expensive process.
NOTES:
Squared distances should not be summed. If you need to sum distances, use [Vector:Distance](/gmod/Vector:Distance).

When performing a distance check, ensure the distance being checked against is squared. See example code below.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVec
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to calculate the distance to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Squared distance to the vector.

Div.DESCRIPTION: Divide the vector by the given number, that means x, y and z are divided by that value. This will change the value of the original vector, see example 2 for division without changing the value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: divisor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to divide the vector with.

Dot.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the [dot product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_product#Geometric_definition)  of this vector and the passed one.

The dot product of two vectors is the product of their magnitudes (lengths), and the cosine of the angle between them:
**a · b** = |**a**| |**b**| cos(θ) 
where **a** and **b** are vectors.
See [Vector:Length](/gmod/Vector:Length) for obtaining magnitudes.

A dot product returns just the cosine of the angle if both vectors are normalized, and zero if the vectors are at right angles to each other.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: otherVector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to calculate the dot product with

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The dot product between the two vectors

DotProduct.DESCRIPTION: Returns the dot product of the two vectors.
DEPRECATED: This is an alias of Vector:Dot. Use that instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Vector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The other vector.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Dot Product

Length2DSqr.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the squared length of the vectors x and y value, x² + y².

This is faster than [Vector:Length2D](/gmod/Vector:Length2D) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Squared length of the vector in two dimensions

LengthSqr.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the squared length of the vector, x² + y² + z².

This is faster than [Vector:Length](/gmod/Vector:Length) as calculating the square root is an expensive process.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Squared length of the vector

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrix
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to transform the vector by.

y * 255 -> g

This is the opposite of [Color:ToVector](/gmod/Color:ToVector)

ToScreen.DESCRIPTION: Returns where on the screen the specified position vector would appear. A related function is [gui.ScreenToVector](/gmod/gui.ScreenToVector), which converts a 2D coordinate to a 3D direction.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Errors in a render hook can make this value incorrect until the player restarts their game.

[cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D) or 3D context [cam.Start](/gmod/cam.Start) with non-default parameters incorrectly sets the reference FOV for this function, causing incorrect return values. This can be fixed by creating and ending a default 3D context ([cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D) with no arguments).

NOTES: Should be called from a 3D rendering environment or after [cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D) or it may not work correctly.

Vector.DESCRIPTION:
List of all possible functions to manipulate vectors.

Created by [Vector](/gmod/Global.Vector).

 Type   | Name           | Description                    
 ------ | -------------- | ------------------------------ 
 [number](/gmod/number) | `x`, `X`, `r` or `1` | The X component of the vector. 
 [number](/gmod/number) | `y`, `Y`, `g` or `2` | The Y component of the vector. 
 [number](/gmod/number) | `z`, `Z`, `b` or `3` | The Z component of the vector.

Metamethod | Second Operand | Description
---------- | -------------- | -----------
`__add` | [Vector](/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of addition.
`__div` | [number](/gmod/number) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of division.
`__eq` | [any](/gmod/any) | Compares 2 operands, if they both are [Vector](/gmod/Vector), compares each individual component.
`__index` | [number](/gmod/number) or [string](/gmod/string) | Gets the component of the [Vector](/gmod/Vector). Returns a [number](/gmod/number).
`__mul` | [number](/gmod/number) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector)| Returns new [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of multiplication.
`__newindex` | [number](/gmod/number) or [string](/gmod/string) | Sets the component of the [Vector](/gmod/Vector). Accepts [number](/gmod/number) and [string](/gmod/string).
`__sub` | [Vector](/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of subtraction.
`__tostring` | | Returns `x y z`.
`__unm` | | Returns new [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of negation.

GetInverse.DESCRIPTION:

Inverting the matrix will fail if its [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) is 0 or close to 0. (ie. its "scale" in any direction is 0.)

See also [VMatrix:GetInverseTR](/gmod/VMatrix:GetInverseTR).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The inverted matrix if possible, nil otherwise

GetInverseTR.DESCRIPTION:
Returns an inverted matrix without modifying the original matrix. This function will not fail, but only works correctly on matrices that contain only translation and/or rotation.

Using this function on a matrix with modified scale may return an incorrect inverted matrix.

To get the inverse of a matrix that contains other modifications, see [VMatrix:GetInverse](/gmod/VMatrix:GetInverse).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The inverted matrix.

GetRight.DESCRIPTION:
Gets the right direction of the matrix.

ie. The second column of the matrix, negated, excluding the w coordinate.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The right direction of the matrix.

GetScale.DESCRIPTION: Returns the absolute scale of the matrix.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Absolute scale of the matrix

GetTranslation.DESCRIPTION: Returns the absolute translation of the matrix.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Absolute translation of the matrix

GetTransposed.DESCRIPTION: Returns the transpose (each row becomes a column) of this matrix.

RETURNS.NAME: transposed
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The transposed matrix.

GetUp.DESCRIPTION:
Gets the up direction of the matrix.

ie. The third column of the matrix, excluding the w coordinate.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The up direction of the matrix.

Identity.DESCRIPTION: Initializes the matrix as Identity matrix.

Invert.DESCRIPTION:
Inverts the matrix.

Inverting the matrix will fail if its [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) is 0 or close to 0. (ie. its "scale" in any direction is 0.)

If the matrix cannot be inverted, it does not get modified.

See also [VMatrix:InvertTR](/gmod/VMatrix:InvertTR).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the matrix was inverted or not

InvertTR.DESCRIPTION:
Quickly inverts the matrix. This function will not fail, but only works correctly on matrices that contain only translation and/or rotation.

Using this function on a matrix with modified scale may return an incorrect inverted matrix.

To invert a matrix that contains other modifications, see [VMatrix:Invert](/gmod/VMatrix:Invert). This function is faster.

IsIdentity.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the matrix is equal to Identity matrix or not.

IsRotationMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the matrix is a rotation matrix or not.

Technically it checks if the forward, right and up vectors are orthogonal and normalized.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the matrix a rotation matrix or not

IsZero.DESCRIPTION: Checks whenever all fields of the matrix are 0, aka if this is a [null matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_matrix).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the matrix is a null matrix.

Zero.DESCRIPTION:

VMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
A 4x4 matrix.

This page lists all possible functions to manipulate matrices.

This object can be created by [Matrix](/gmod/Global.Matrix).

Metamethod | Second Operand | Description
---------- | -------------- | -----------
`__add` | [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) | Returns new [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of addition.
`__eq` | [any](/gmod/any) | Compares 2 operands, if they both are [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix), compares each individual component.
`__mul` | [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector) | Returns new [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector) with the result of multiplication.
`__sub` | [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) | Returns new [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of subtraction.
`__tostring` |  | Returns a [string](/gmod/string) in format `[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]\n[%f,\t%f,\t%f,\t%f]`.
`__unm` | | Returns new [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) with the result of negation.

Get.DESCRIPTION:
Gets the base class of an an object.

	This is used not just by entities, but also by widgets, panels, drive modes, weapons and gamemodes (with "gamemode_" prefix).

	The keyword **DEFINE_BASECLASS** translates into a call to this function. In the engine, it is replaced with:

	```lua
	local BaseClass = baseclass.Get
	```

	

	For more information, including usage examples, see the [BaseClasses](/gmod/BaseClasses) reference page.
NOTES: You should prefer using this instead of `self.BaseClass` to avoid infinite recursion.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The child class.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The base class's meta table.

* [panels](vgui.Register)
* [drive modes](drive.Register)
* [entities and widgets](scripted_ents.Register)
* [weapons](weapons.Register)
* [gamemodes](gamemode.Register) (with prefix "gamemode_")

For more information, including usage examples, see the [BaseClasses](/gmod/BaseClasses) reference page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shiftCount

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to be manipulated.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shiftCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Amounts of bits to rotate left by.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The shifted value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The shifted value.

NOTES: The returned value will be clamped to a signed 32-bit integer, even on 64-bit builds.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to be manipulated.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shiftCount

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The shifted value.

tobit.DESCRIPTION: Normalizes the specified value and clamps it in the range of a signed 32bit integer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The 32 bits of the provided value.

tohex.DESCRIPTION: Returns the hexadecimal representation of the number with the specified number of characters.

bit.DESCRIPTION:
The bitwise library contains useful functions for bitwise operations.
Make sure you're familiar with [Bitwise Operators](https://code.tutsplus.com/articles/understanding-bitwise-operators--active-11301)

ApplyShake.DESCRIPTION: Shakes the screen at a certain position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Angles of the shake.

End.DESCRIPTION:
Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 3D context.

This function is an alias of [cam.End3D](/gmod/cam.End3D).

End2D.DESCRIPTION: Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 2D context.

End3D.DESCRIPTION: Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 3D context.

End3D2D.DESCRIPTION: Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 3D2D context.

EndOrthoView.DESCRIPTION: Switches the renderer back to the previous drawing mode from a 3D orthographic rendering context.

GetModelMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Returns a copy of the model matrix that is at the top of the stack.
NOTES: Editing the matrix **will not** edit the current view. To do so, you will have to use [cam.PushModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.PushModelMatrix).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently active model matrix.

GetProjectionMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a copy of the projection matrix. Also see [cam.GetViewMatrix](/gmod/cam.GetViewMatrix).

Will return Identity matrix in 2D Render context. In this case use [cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D). See [Render Hook Order](/gmod/Render_Order).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently active projection matrix.

GetViewMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a copy of the view matrix. Also see [cam.GetProjectionMatrix](/gmod/cam.GetProjectionMatrix).

Will return Identity matrix in 2D Render context. In this case use [cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D). See [Render Hook Order](/gmod/Render_Order).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently active view matrix.

IgnoreZ.DESCRIPTION:
Tells the renderer to ignore the depth buffer and draw any upcoming operation "ontop" of everything that was drawn yet.

This is identical to calling `render.DepthRange( 0, 0.01 )` for `true` and  `render.DepthRange( 0, 1 )` for `false`. See [render.DepthRange](/gmod/render.DepthRange).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ignoreZ
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Determines whenever to ignore the depth buffer or not.

PopModelMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Removes the currently active model matrix (pushed previously with [cam.PushModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.PushModelMatrix)) from the stack and reinstates the previous one.

PushModelMatrix.DESCRIPTION:
Pushes the specified matrix onto the render matrix stack. Each pushed matrix must be popped via [cam.PopModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.PopModelMatrix).

When used in [PANEL:Paint](/gmod/PANEL:Paint), if you want to rely on the top-left position of the panel, you must use [VMatrix:Translate](/gmod/VMatrix:Translate) with the (0, 0) position of the panel relative to the screen.

If trying to use it with with [cam.Start3D2D](/gmod/cam.Start3D2D), set `multiply` to `true`, since **cam.Start3D2D** pushes its own model matrix.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrix
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to push.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: multiply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, multiplies given matrix with currently active matrix ([cam.GetModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.GetModelMatrix)) before pushing.

Start.DESCRIPTION: Sets up a new rendering context. This is an extended version of [cam.Start3D](/gmod/cam.Start3D) and [cam.Start2D](/gmod/cam.Start2D). Must be finished by [cam.End3D](/gmod/cam.End3D) or [cam.End2D](/gmod/cam.End2D).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will not update current view properties for 3D contexts.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dataTbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Render context config. See [Structures/RenderCamData](/gmod/Structures/RenderCamData).

Start2D.DESCRIPTION:
Sets up a new 2D rendering context. Must be finished by [cam.End2D](/gmod/cam.End2D).

This is almost always used with a render target from the [render](/gmod/render). To set its position use [render.SetViewPort](/gmod/render.SetViewPort) with a target already stored.
NOTES: This will put an identity matrix at the top of the model matrix stack. If you are trying to use [cam.PushModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.PushModelMatrix), call it after this function and not before.

Start3D.DESCRIPTION:
Sets up a new 3D rendering context. Must be finished by [cam.End3D](/gmod/cam.End3D).

For more advanced settings such as an orthographic view, use [cam.Start](/gmod/cam.Start) instead, which this is an alias of basically.

All parameters are optional, and fall back parameters that of the "current" or "last" render operation.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Negative x/y values won't work.
This will not update current view properties.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Render cam position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Render cam angles.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fov
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Field of view.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X coordinate of where to start the new view port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y coordinate of where to start the new view port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: w
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Width of the new viewport.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: h
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Height of the new viewport.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: zNear
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Distance to near clipping plane.
NOTES:
Both `zNear` and `zFar` need a value before any of them work.

zNear also requires a value higher than 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: zFar
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Distance to far clipping plane.

Start3D2D.DESCRIPTION:
Sets up the model transformation matrix to draw 2D content in 3D space and pushes it into the stack ([cam.PushModelMatrix](/gmod/cam.PushModelMatrix)).

Matrix formula:
```
local m = Matrix()
m:SetAngles( angles )
m:SetTranslation( pos )
m:SetScale( Vector( scale, -scale, 1 ) )
```


[render.SetToneMappingScaleLinear](/gmod/render.SetToneMappingScaleLinear) may of use when dealing with bloom.
WARNINGS: This must be closed by [cam.End3D2D](/gmod/cam.End3D2D). If not done so, unexpected issues might arise.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin of the 3D2D context, ie. the top left corner, (0, 0).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Angles of the 3D2D context.
+x in the 2d context corresponds to +x of the angle (its forward direction).
+y in the 2d context corresponds to -y of the angle (its right direction).

If (dx, dy) are your desired (+x, +y) unit vectors, the angle you want is dx:AngleEx(dx:Cross(-dy)).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The scale of the render context.
If scale is 1 then 1 pixel in 2D context will equal to 1 unit in 3D context.

StartOrthoView.DESCRIPTION: Sets up a new 3d context using orthographic projection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: leftOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The left plane offset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: topOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The top plane offset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rightOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The right plane offset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bottomOffset
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bottom plane offset.

cam.DESCRIPTION:
This directs all drawing to be done to a certain 2D or 3D plane or position, until the corresponding "End" function is called.

The matrix functions exist, but are mostly unusable unless you're familiar with the source engine's layout for each aspect.

AddText.DESCRIPTION: Adds text to the local player's chat box (which only they can read).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: arguments
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The message to be added to the chat box.  

Arguments can be:
* [Color](/gmod/Color) - Will set the color for all following strings until the next Color argument.
* [string](/gmod/string) - Text to be added to the chat box.
* [Player](/gmod/Player) - Adds the name of the player in the player's team color to the chat box.
* [any](/gmod/any) - Any other type, such as [Entity](/gmod/Entity) will be converted to string and added as text.

These argument types can be combined to create formatted messages.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The X coordinate of the chatbox's position.
The Y coordinate of the chatbox's position.
The width of the chatbox.
The height of the chatbox.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If equals 1, opens public chat, otherwise opens team chat.

chat.DESCRIPTION: The chat library's purpose is to interface with the default chatbox.

Add.DESCRIPTION: Creates a console command that runs a function in lua with optional autocompletion function and help text.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This will fail if the concommand was previously removed with [concommand.Remove](/gmod/concommand.Remove) in a different realm (creating a command on the client that was removed from the server and vice-versa).

WARNINGS: Clients can still run commands created only on the server. Always check permissions in the callback.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The command name to be used in console.

This cannot be a name of existing console command or console variable. It will silently fail if it is.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to run when the concommand is executed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: autoComplete
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The function to call which should return a table of options for autocompletion. ([Autocompletion Tutorial](/gmod/Console_Command_Auto-completion))

This only properly works on the client since it is **not** networked.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: helpText
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The text to display should a user run 'help cmdName'.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Console command modifier flags. Either a bitflag, or a table of enums. See [FCVAR](/gmod/Enums/FCVAR).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Possibilities for auto-completion. This is the return value of the auto-complete callback.

GetTable.DESCRIPTION: Returns the tables of all console command callbacks, and autocomplete functions, that were added to the game with [concommand.Add](/gmod/concommand.Add).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of command callback functions.
Table of command autocomplete functions.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: [concommand.Add](/gmod/concommand.Add) will fail if the concommand was previously removed with this function in a different realm (creating a command on the client that was removed from the server and vice-versa).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the command to be removed.

Run.DESCRIPTION:
Used by the engine to run a console command's callback function. This will only be called for commands that were added with [AddConsoleCommand](/gmod/Global.AddConsoleCommand), which [concommand.Add](/gmod/concommand.Add) calls internally. An error is sent to the player's console if no callback is found.

This will still be called for concommands removed with [concommand.Remove](/gmod/concommand.Remove) but will return false. This will not be called for concommands added by the engine, only those made from Lua.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Player to run concommand on.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Command name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Command arguments.
Can be table or string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: argumentString
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: string of all arguments sent to the command.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the console command with the given name exists, and `false` if it doesn't.

concommand.DESCRIPTION: The concommand library is used to create console commands which can be used to network (basic) information & events between the client and the server.

It consists of 3 rope segments, 2 of which have variable length, visually connected by a 3rd. Reducing length of one end will increase the length of the other end.

```
WPos2 --- WPos3
  |			|
  |			|
 Ent1	   Ent4
```

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position relative to the the second physics object to constrain to.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: World position constrain the first entity to. This point will be static.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: worldPos3
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: World position constrain the second entity to. This point will be static.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: forceLimit
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Amount of force until it breaks (0 = unbreakable).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the constraint is rigid, i.e. cannot bend.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Width of the rope. If below or at `0`, visual rope segments will not be created.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Material of the rope. If unset, will be solid black.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The color of the rope.

The first rope segment. ([keyframe_rope](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Keyframe_rope)) Will return `nil` if the constraint or this rope segment could not be created.
The second rope segment. ([keyframe_rope](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Keyframe_rope)) Will return `nil` if the constraint or this rope segment could not be created.
The third rope segment. ([keyframe_rope](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Keyframe_rope)) Will return `nil` if the constraint or this rope segment could not be created.

Enters an interactive mode with the user, running each string that the user enters. Using simple commands and other debug facilities, the user can inspect global and local variables, change their values, evaluate expressions, and so on. * Commands for debug.debug are not lexically nested within any function, and so have no direct access to local variables.
* To exit this interactive mode, you can press Ctrl + Z then Enter OR type the word 'cont' on a single line and press enter.

getinfo.DESCRIPTION: Returns debug information about a function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: funcOrStackLevel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Takes either a function or a number representing the stack level as an argument. Stack level 0 always corresponds to the debug.getinfo call, 1 would be the function calling debug.getinfo in most cases, and so on.

Returns useful information about that function in a table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fields
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A string whose characters specify the information to be retrieved.

* `f` - Populates the func field.
* `l` - Populates the currentline field.
* `L` - Populates the activelines field.
* `n` - Populates the name and namewhat fields - only works if stack level is passed rather than function pointer.
* `S` - Populates the location fields (lastlinedefined, linedefined, short_src, source and what).
* `u` - Populates the argument and upvalue fields (isvararg, nparams, nups).
* `>` - Causes this function to use the last argument to get the data from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: function
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to use. (Only used by the `>` field)

getlocal.DESCRIPTION: Gets the name and value of a local variable indexed from the level.
WARNINGS: When a function has a tailcall return, you cannot access the locals of this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: thread
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The thread.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: level
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The level above the thread. 
* 0 = the function that was called (most always this function)'s arguments.
* 1 = the thread that had called this function.
* 2 = the thread that had called the function that started the thread that called this function.

A function defined in Lua can also be passed as the level. The index will specify the parameter's name to be returned (a parameter will have a value of nil).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The variable's index you want to get.
* 1 = the first local defined in the thread.
* 2 = the second local defined in the thread.
* etc...

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the variable.

Sometimes this will be `(*temporary)` if the local variable had no name.
NOTES: Variables with names starting with **(** are **internal variables**.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The value of the local variable.

getregistry.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the internal Lua registry table.

The Lua registry is used by the engine and binary modules to create references to Lua values. The registry contains every global ran and used in the Lua environment. Avoid creating entries into the registry with a number as the key, as they are reserved for the reference system.
DEPRECATED:
This function now returns a table that serves as a proxy to Global.FindMetaTable and Global.RegisterMetaTable. If you previously used the registry to get/add metatables, you should use those functions directly instead.
```lua
--
-- Hack for debug.getregistry
--
local meta = {}
function meta.__index( self, key )
	return FindMetaTable( key )
end
function meta.__newindex( self, key, value )
	rawset( self, key, value )

	if ( isstring( key ) and istable( value ) ) then
		RegisterMetaTable( key, value )
	end
end

local tbl = {}
setmetatable( tbl, meta )
function debug.getregistry() return tbl end
```
WARNINGS: Improper editing of the registry can result in unintended side effects, including crashing the game.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The Lua registry.

Unlike [setfenv](/gmod/Global.setfenv), this also works on **any** userdata, allowing you to save data stored to it which can be accessed using [debug.getfenv](/gmod/debug.getfenv).  
Userdata seem to intentionally support this & setting/changing it does not affect anything (though unused by gmod / Entities and such don't this)  
This can be useful when trying to store data on a [IGModAudioChannel](/gmod/IGModAudioChannel), [Vector](/gmod/Vector), [Angle](/gmod/Angle) or any other that doesn't already allow you to store data on it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: object

ARGUMENTS.NAME: env
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Environment to set.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The object.

sethook.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the given function as a Lua hook. This is completely different to gamemode hooks. The thread argument can be completely omitted and calling this function with no arguments will remove the current hook. This is used by default for infinite loop detection. More information on hooks can be found at http://www.lua.org/pil/23.2.html and https://www.gammon.com.au/scripts/doc.php?lua=debug.sethook

Hooks are not always ran when code that has been compiled by LuaJIT's JIT compiler is being executed, this is due to Intermediate Representation internally storing constantly running bytecode for performance reasons.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: thread
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Thread to set the hook on. This argument can be omitted.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hook
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function for the hook to call. First argument in this function will be the mask event that called the hook as a full string (not as 'c' but instead as 'call').

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The hook's mask. Can be one or more of the following events: 
* c - Triggers the hook on each function call made from Lua.
* r - Triggers the hook on each function return made from Lua.
* l - Triggers the hook on each line compiled of code.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: count
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How often to call the hook (in instructions). 0 for every instruction. Can be omitted.

DEPRECATED: This function was removed due to security concerns.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: thread
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The thread.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: level
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The level above the thread.  

0 is the function that was called (most always this function)'s arguments.

1 is the thread that had called this function.

2 is the thread that had called the function that started the thread that called this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The variable's index you want to get.

1 = the first local defined in the thread.

2 = the second local defined in the thread.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set the local to.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the local variable if the local at the index exists, otherwise nil is returned.

DefineControl.DESCRIPTION:
Defines a new Derma control with an optional base.

This calls [vgui.Register](/gmod/vgui.Register) internally, but also does the following:
* Adds the control to [derma.GetControlList](/gmod/derma.GetControlList)
* Adds a key "Derma" - This is returned by [derma.GetControlList](/gmod/derma.GetControlList)
* Makes a global table with the name of the control (This is technically deprecated and should not be relied upon)
* If reloading (i.e. called this function with name of an existing panel), updates all existing instances of panels with this name. (Updates functions, calls [PANEL:PreAutoRefresh](/gmod/PANEL:PreAutoRefresh) and [PANEL:PostAutoRefresh](/gmod/PANEL:PostAutoRefresh), etc.)

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table containing control methods and properties.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Derma control to base the new control off of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing the new control's methods and properties.

Allow.DESCRIPTION:
Allow entities with given class name to be duplicated. See [duplicator.Disallow](/gmod/duplicator.Disallow) for the opposite effect.

[duplicator.IsAllowed](/gmod/duplicator.IsAllowed) can be used to poll the status of a particular entity class. 

`duplicator.Allow` is automatically called by [scripted_ents.Register](/gmod/scripted_ents.Register) and [weapons.Register](/gmod/weapons.Register), unless the associated entity table has `ENT.DisableDuplicator` set to `true`.

This is also automatically called by [duplicator.RegisterEntityClass](/gmod/duplicator.RegisterEntityClass).

In addition to that most spawnmenu content, such as engine weapons and pickup-ables, as well as most engine NPCs in Sandbox-derived gamemodes are also allowed by default.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An entity's classname to allow duplicating.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity in question.

Uses the same table format as the table returned from this function.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing duplication info which includes the following members:
