* [table](/gmod/table) Constraints
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) Mins
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) Maxs

The values of Mins & Maxs from the table are returned from [duplicator.WorkoutSize](/gmod/duplicator.WorkoutSize).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table containing duplication info which includes the following members:

* [table](/gmod/table) Constraints
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) Mins
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) Maxs

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity table to save.

CreateConstraintFromTable.DESCRIPTION: Creates a constraint from a saved/copied constraint table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: constraint
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Saved/copied constraint table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entityList
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The list of entities that are to be constrained.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The newly created constraint entity, if any.

For example, an entity of class `phys_pulleyconstraint` or `phys_spring`, etc., the functional entity of the constraint.

The second constraint related entity, if any.

For a most constraints, this would be a `keyframe_rope` for the visual part of a constraint.

The third constraint related entity, if any.

For example, a Hydraulic constraint would return the `gmod_winch_controller` entity here. A pulley would have another `keyframe_rope`.

The fourth constraint related entity, if any.

For example, a Hydraulic constraint would return the `phys_slideconstraint` entity here. A pulley would have yet another `keyframe_rope`.

CreateEntityFromTable.DESCRIPTION:
"Create an entity from a table." 


This creates an entity using the data in EntTable.


If an entity factory has been registered for the entity's Class, it will be called. 


Otherwise, [duplicator.GenericDuplicatorFunction](/gmod/duplicator.GenericDuplicatorFunction) will be called instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player who wants to create something.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The duplication data to build the entity with. See [Structures/EntityCopyData](/gmod/Structures/EntityCopyData).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created entity.

Disallow.DESCRIPTION:
Disallow this entity to be duplicated. Opposite of [duplicator.Allow](/gmod/duplicator.Allow).

This function is useful for temporarily disabling duplication of certain entity classes that may have been previously allowed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An entity's classname to disallow duplicating.

DoBoneManipulator.DESCRIPTION:
"Restores the bone's data."


Loops through Bones and calls [Entity:ManipulateBoneScale](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneScale), [Entity:ManipulateBoneAngles](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBoneAngles) and [Entity:ManipulateBonePosition](/gmod/Entity:ManipulateBonePosition) on ent with the table keys and the subtable values s, a and p respectively.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be bone manipulated.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bones
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table with a [Structures/BoneManipulationData](/gmod/Structures/BoneManipulationData) for every bone (that has manipulations applied) using the bone ID as the table index.

DoFlex.DESCRIPTION: Restores the flex data using [Entity:SetFlexWeight](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexWeight) and [Entity:SetFlexScale](/gmod/Entity:SetFlexScale).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to restore the flexes on.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flexes to restore.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The flex scale to apply. (Flex scale is unchanged if omitted)

DoGeneric.DESCRIPTION:
"Applies generic every-day entity stuff for ent from table data."


Depending on the values of Model, Angle, Pos, Skin, Flex, Bonemanip, ModelScale, ColGroup, Name, and BodyG ([table](/gmod/table) of multiple values) in the data table, this calls [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel), [Entity:SetAngles](/gmod/Entity:SetAngles), [Entity:SetPos](/gmod/Entity:SetPos), [Entity:SetSkin](/gmod/Entity:SetSkin), [duplicator.DoFlex](/gmod/duplicator.DoFlex), [duplicator.DoBoneManipulator](/gmod/duplicator.DoBoneManipulator), [Entity:SetModelScale](/gmod/Entity:SetModelScale), [Entity:SetCollisionGroup](/gmod/Entity:SetCollisionGroup), [Entity:SetName](/gmod/Entity:SetName), [Entity:SetBodygroup](/gmod/Entity:SetBodygroup) on ent.


If ent has a RestoreNetworkVars function, it is called with data.DT.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be applied upon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The data to be applied onto the entity.

DoGenericPhysics.DESCRIPTION:
"Applies bone data, generically."


If data contains a PhysicsObjects table, it moves, re-angles and if relevent freezes all specified bones, first converting from local coordinates to world coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be applied upon.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply

FigureOutRequiredAddons.DESCRIPTION: Checks the given duplication table and tries to figure out any addons that might be required to correctly spawn the duplication. Currently this is limited to models and material overrides saved in the duplication.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dupe
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The duplication table to process, for example from [duplicator.Copy](/gmod/duplicator.Copy).

The provided table will have `RequiredAddons` key added.

FindEntityClass.DESCRIPTION: Returns the entity class factory registered with [duplicator.RegisterEntityClass](/gmod/duplicator.RegisterEntityClass).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the entity class factory.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Is compromised of the following members:
* [function](/gmod/function) Func - The function that creates the entity.
* [table](/gmod/table) Args - Arguments to pass to the function.

GenericDuplicatorFunction.DESCRIPTION:
"Generic function for duplicating stuff" 


This is called when [duplicator.CreateEntityFromTable](/gmod/duplicator.CreateEntityFromTable) can't find an entity factory to build with. It calls [duplicator.DoGeneric](/gmod/duplicator.DoGeneric) and [duplicator.DoGenericPhysics](/gmod/duplicator.DoGenericPhysics) to apply standard duplicator stored things such as the model and position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created entity.

GetAllConstrainedEntitiesAndConstraints.DESCRIPTION: Fills entStorageTable with all of the entities in a group connected with constraints. Fills constraintStorageTable with all of the constraints constraining the group.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to start from

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entStorageTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table the entities will be inserted into.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: constraintStorageTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table the constraints will be inserted into.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: entStorageTable
constraintStorageTable

IsAllowed.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the entity can be duplicated or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An entity's classname.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the entity can be duplicated (nil otherwise).

Paste.DESCRIPTION:
"Given entity list and constraint list, create all entities and return their tables"

Calls [duplicator.CreateEntityFromTable](/gmod/duplicator.CreateEntityFromTable) on each sub-table of EntityList. If an entity is actually created, it calls [ENTITY:OnDuplicated](/gmod/ENTITY:OnDuplicated) with the entity's duplicator data, then [duplicator.ApplyEntityModifiers](/gmod/duplicator.ApplyEntityModifiers), [duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers](/gmod/duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers) and finally  [ENTITY:PostEntityPaste](/gmod/ENTITY:PostEntityPaste) is called.

The constraints are then created with [duplicator.CreateConstraintFromTable](/gmod/duplicator.CreateConstraintFromTable).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Player
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player who wants to create something.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: EntityList
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of duplicator data to create the entities from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ConstraintList
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of duplicator data to create the constraints from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: List of created entities.
List of created constraints.

RegisterBoneModifier.DESCRIPTION: Registers a function to be called on each of an entity's bones when [duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers](/gmod/duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers) is called.
NOTES: This function is available to call on the client, but registered functions aren't used anywhere!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The type of the key doesn't appear to matter, but it is preferable to use a string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneModifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function called on each bone that an ent has. Called during [duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers](/gmod/duplicator.ApplyBoneModifiers).

RegisterConstraint.DESCRIPTION: Register a function used for creating a duplicator-supported constraint.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique name of the new constraint. It will be used to identify which constraint to apply on duplicator load.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Function to be called when this constraint is created.

It is a good idea to check [constraint.CanConstrain](/gmod/constraint.CanConstrain) before doing anything else.


You must also call [constraint.AddConstraintTable](/gmod/constraint.AddConstraintTable) if creating custom constraint entities.
  * This is what stores the constraint for duplicator to save and load, as well as for [constraint.GetTable](/gmod/constraint.GetTable).
  * The constraint entity must have `Type` key on it. This means that a single entity can only represent one constraint.

Optionally, the callback can return up to 4 entities, which are considered the "constraint" entities.
* Each of those is added to `"ropeconstraints"` or `"constraints"` cleanup list based on entity's classname ([Player:AddCleanup](/gmod/Player:AddCleanup))
* The first entity is added to the player's entity count ([Player:AddCount](/gmod/Player:AddCount)) in Sandbox.
* None of these entities **should** be the 2 entities being constraint (i.e. a `prop_physics`), but it can be one one of them if you know what you are doing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: customData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Arguments to be passed to the callback function when the constraint is created via [duplicator.CreateConstraintFromTable](/gmod/duplicator.CreateConstraintFromTable).

The data would be taken the constraint entity table added via [constraint.AddConstraintTable](/gmod/constraint.AddConstraintTable). All [constraint](/gmod/constraint) library constraints call it on the appropriate entity for you. (Typically its the first entity returned by the callback)

RegisterEntityClass.DESCRIPTION: This allows you to specify a specific function to be run when your SENT is pasted with the duplicator, instead of relying on the generic automatic functions.
NOTES: Automatically calls [duplicator.Allow](/gmod/duplicator.Allow) for the entity class.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ClassName of the entity you wish to register a factory for.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: function
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The factory function you want to have called.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: args
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Strings of the names of arguments you want passed to function the from the [Structures/EntityCopyData](/gmod/Structures/EntityCopyData). As a special case, "Data" will pass the whole structure.

RegisterEntityModifier.DESCRIPTION:
This allows you to register tweaks to entities. For instance, if you were making an "unbreakable" addon, you would use this to enable saving the "unbreakable" state of entities between duplications.

This function registers a piece of generic code that is run on all entities with this modifier. In order to have it actually run, use [duplicator.StoreEntityModifier](/gmod/duplicator.StoreEntityModifier).

This function does nothing when run clientside.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An identifier for your modification. This is not limited, so be verbose. `Person's 'Unbreakable' mod` is far less likely to cause conflicts than `unbreakable`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to be called for your modification.

RemoveMapCreatedEntities.DESCRIPTION:
Help to remove certain map created entities before creating the saved entities
This is obviously so we don't get duplicate props everywhere.
It should be called before calling Paste.

SetLocalAng.DESCRIPTION:
"When a copy is copied it will be translated according to these.
If you set them - make sure to set them back to 0 0 0!"

ARGUMENTS.NAME: v
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to offset all pastes from.

SetLocalPos.DESCRIPTION:
"When a copy is copied it will be translated according to these.
If you set them - make sure to set them back to 0 0 0!"

ARGUMENTS.NAME: v
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to offset all pastes from.

StoreBoneModifier.DESCRIPTION: Stores bone mod data for a registered bone modification function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to add bone mod data to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boneID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The bone ID.
See [Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum](/gmod/Entity:GetPhysicsObjectNum).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: key
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key for the bone modification.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bone modification data that is passed to the bone modification function.

StoreEntityModifier.DESCRIPTION: Stores an entity modifier into an entity for saving.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to store modifier in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Unique modifier name as defined in [duplicator.RegisterEntityModifier](/gmod/duplicator.RegisterEntityModifier).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Modifier data.

WorkoutSize.DESCRIPTION: Works out the AABB size of the duplication.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Ents
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of entity duplication datums.

RETURNS.NAME: Mins
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: AABB mins vector.

RETURNS.NAME: Maxs
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: AABB maxs vector.

duplicator.DESCRIPTION: The duplicator library allows you to specify what should be saved when someone attempts to duplicate your custom entity with the duplicator tool. It can also be used by 3rd party duplicator tools to make use of the built in system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The origin position of the effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lifetime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long the effect will be drawing for, in seconds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startRad
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Initial radius of the effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endRad
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Final radius of the effect, at the end of the effect's lifetime.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: width
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How thick the beam should be.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: amplitude
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How noisy the beam should be.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Beam's [Color](/gmod/Color).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extra
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Extra info, all optional. A table with the following keys: (any combination)
* [number](/gmod/number) speed - ?
* [number](/gmod/number) spread - ?
* [number](/gmod/number) delay - Delay in seconds after which the effect should appear.
* [number](/gmod/number) flags- Beam flags.
* [number](/gmod/number) framerate - texture framerate.
* [string](/gmod/string) material - The material to use instead of the default one.

Bubbles.DESCRIPTION: Creates a bunch of bubbles inside a defined box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The lowest extents of the box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The highest extents of the box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: count
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How many bubbles to spawn. There's a hard limit of 500 tempents at any time.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: height
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How high the bubbles can fly up before disappearing.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How quickly the bubbles move.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay in seconds after the function call and before the effect actually spawns.

BubbleTrail.DESCRIPTION: Creates a bubble trail effect, the very same you get when shooting underwater.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the effects.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: count
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How many bubbles to spawn. There's a hard limit of 500 tempents at any time.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: speed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How quickly the bubbles move.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Delay in seconds after the function call and before the effect actually spawns.

Create.DESCRIPTION: Returns the table of the effect specified.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Effect name.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The effect table.

GetList.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of all Lua-defined effects.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The effects table.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Effect table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Effect name.

TracerSound.DESCRIPTION:
Imitates the "near miss" tracer sound, with the ability to override the sound played.

The frequency of the sound is limited internally, as to not overwhelm the player. (same as normal tracers)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: start
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endpos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: End position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tracerType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Tracer type. Acceptable values are:
* 1 - Normal bullet.
* 2 - Gunship bullet.
* 4 - Strider bullet.
* 8 - Underwater bullet.

This affects the default sound, as well as the distance from which the sound can be heard compared to the closest point on the tracer line to the [player's eyes](/gmod/Player:GetShootPos).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, this sound will be played instead of the default sound.

effects.DESCRIPTION: The effects library allows you to manually add scripted effects.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Frame time.

ActiveGamemode.DESCRIPTION: Returns the name of the currently running gamemode.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The active gamemode's name. This is the name of the gamemode's folder.

CloseServer.DESCRIPTION:
Closes the server and completely exits.

To enable this function for use on your server, add `-allowquit` to your commandline, which will make this function run `quit keep_players` when executed, this also does not forcibly disconnect players.

This is also available when running in server test mode (launch option `-systemtest`). Server test mode is used internally at Facepunch as part of the build process to make sure that the dedicated servers aren't crashing on startup.

GetAddons.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a list of addons the player have subscribed to on the workshop.

This list will also include "Floating" .gma addons that are mounted by the game, but not the folder addons.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of tables containing 8 keys (downloaded, models, title, file, mounted, wsid, size, updated).

GetDemoPlaybackStartTick.DESCRIPTION: When starting playing a demo, [engine.GetDemoPlaybackTick](/gmod/engine.GetDemoPlaybackTick) will be reset and its old value will be added to this functions return value.

GetDemoPlaybackTick.DESCRIPTION:
Current tick of currently loaded demo.

If not playing a demo, it will return amount of ticks since last demo playback.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of ticks of currently loaded demo.

GetDemoPlaybackTimeScale.DESCRIPTION:
Returns time scale of demo playback.

If not during demo playback, returns 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The time scale of demo playback, value of demo_timescale console variable.

GetDemoPlaybackTotalTicks.DESCRIPTION:
Returns total amount of ticks of currently loaded demo.

If not playing a demo, returns 0 or the value of last played demo.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Total amount of ticks of currently loaded demo.

GetGamemodes.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table containing info for all installed gamemodes.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The gamemodes.

GetGames.DESCRIPTION: Returns an array of tables corresponding to all games from which Garry's Mod supports mounting content.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of tables containing all mountable games.

GetUserContent.DESCRIPTION: Returns the UGC (demos, saves and dupes) the player have subscribed to on the workshop.
DEPRECATED: Used internally for in-game menus, may be merged in the future into engine.GetAddons.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table with 5 keys (title, type, tags, wsid, timeadded).

IsPlayingDemo.DESCRIPTION:
Returns true if we're currently playing a demo.

You will notice that there's no server-side version of this. That's because there is no server when playing a demo. Demos are both recorded and played back purely clientside.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the game is currently playing a demo or not.

IsRecordingDemo.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the game is currently recording a demo file (.dem) using gm_demo.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the game is currently recording a demo or not.

LightStyle.DESCRIPTION: This is a direct binding to the function `engine->LightStyle`. This function allows you to change the default light style of the map - so you can make lighting lighter or darker. You’ll need to call [render.RedownloadAllLightmaps](/gmod/render.RedownloadAllLightmaps) clientside to refresh the lightmaps to this new color.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Calling this function with arguments 0 and "a" will cause dynamic lights such as those produced by the Light tool to stop working.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightstyle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The lightstyle to edit. 0 to 63. If you want to edit map lighting, you want to set this to 0.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pattern
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The pattern to change the lightstyle to. `a` is the darkest, `z` is the brightest. You can use stuff like "abcxyz" to make flashing patterns. The normal brightness for a map is `m`. Values over `z` are allowed, `~` for instance.

OpenDupe.DESCRIPTION: Loads a duplication from the local filesystem.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dupeName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the file. (e.g, `engine.OpenDupe("dupes/8b809dd7a1a9a375e75be01cdc12e61f.dupe")`).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table with a simple field:
* [string](/gmod/string) `data` - Compressed dupe data. Use util.JSONToTable to make it into a format useable by the duplicator tool.

ServerFrameTime.DESCRIPTION: Returns an estimate of the server's performance. Equivalent to calling [FrameTime](/gmod/Global.FrameTime) from the server, according to source code.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Frame time.
Server framerate [standard deviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_deviation).

SetMounted.DESCRIPTION: Sets the mounting options for mountable content.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: depotID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The depot id of the game to mount.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: doMount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The mount state, true to mount, false to unmount

TickCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the number of ticks since the game server started.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of ticks since the game server started.

TickInterval.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the time interval between each game tick in seconds.

This function is useful for making animations (usually serverside, such as doors rotating) and similar things to be independent of the tickrate in hooks that run at the tick rate, such as [GM:Tick](/gmod/GM:Tick).

Clientside you'd want to use [FrameTime](/gmod/Global.FrameTime) for this purpose in hooks that run every frame.

The default tickrate is `66.6666`, aka `15` milliseconds interval between each game tick.  
The tickrate can be adjusted via the `-tickrate` [command line option](Command_Line_Parameters).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of seconds between each gametick.

VideoSettings.DESCRIPTION: Returns video recording settings set by [video.Record](/gmod/video.Record). Used by Demo-To-Video feature.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The video recording settings, see [Structures/VideoData](/gmod/Structures/VideoData).

WriteDupe.DESCRIPTION: Saves a duplication as a file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dupe
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Dupe table, encoded by [util.TableToJSON](/gmod/util.TableToJSON) and compressed by [util.Compress](/gmod/util.Compress).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: jpeg
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The dupe icon, created by [render.Capture](/gmod/render.Capture).

WriteSave.DESCRIPTION: Stores savedata into the game. (can be loaded using the LoadGame menu)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: saveData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Data generated by [gmsave.SaveMap](/gmod/gmsave.SaveMap), compressed by [util.Compress](/gmod/util.Compress).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name the save will have.

engine.DESCRIPTION: The engine library provides functions to access various features in the game's engine, most are related to the demo and save systems.

Create.DESCRIPTION: Creates an entity. This function will fail and return `NULL` if the networked-edict limit is hit (around **8176**), or the provided entity class doesn't exist.
WARNINGS:
Do not use before [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) has been called, otherwise the server will crash!
If you need to perform entity creation when the game starts, create a hook for [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) and do it there.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of the entity to create.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The created entity, or `NULL` if failed.

CreateClientProp.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a clientside only prop with optional physics. See also [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) if physics is not needed.

For physics to work you're expected to use the `model` argument. A simple [Entity:SetModel](/gmod/Entity:SetModel) will not be enough — the [Entity:PhysicsInit](/gmod/Entity:PhysicsInit)* function will be needed.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Parented clientside prop will become detached if the parent entity leaves the PVS. **A workaround is available on its github page.**

ARGUMENTS.NAME: model
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The model for the entity to be created.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created entity (`C_PhysPropClientside`).

CreateClientRope.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a clientside only rope, similar to those used by the Dog and Fast Zombie models from Half-Life 2.

Created ropes will be automatically cleaned up when one of the attached entities is removed.
WARNINGS: It doesn’t work exactly the same way as [constraint.CreateKeyframeRope](/gmod/constraint.CreateKeyframeRope) or [constraint.Rope](/gmod/constraint.Rope), you can see it when you try to use Slack with [constraint.CreateKeyframeRope](/gmod/constraint.CreateKeyframeRope) or addlength on [constraint.Rope](/gmod/constraint.Rope).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent1
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first entity to attach the rope to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent1attach
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment ID on the first entity to attach the rope to, or a local Vector relative to the first entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent2
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The second entity to attach the rope to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent2attach
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attachment ID on the second entity to attach the rope to, or a local Vector relative to the second entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extra
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Extra optional settings for the rope. Possible values are:
* slack - How much extra rope to add to the length. (default: 0)
* width - Width of the rope. (default: 2)
* segments - How many segments the rope should have (default: 8, valid range is [2,10])
* material - Which material should the rope have. (default: `"cable/cable"`)
* nogravity - If set, the rope should have no gravity. (default: 0)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created entity (`C_RopeKeyframe`).

CreateClientside.DESCRIPTION: Creates a clientside only scripted entity. The scripted entity must be of "anim" type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The class name of the entity to create.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Created entity.

FindAlongRay.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table of all entities along the ray. The ray does not stop on collisions, meaning it will go through walls/entities.

This function is capable of detecting clientside only entities by default.

This internally uses [spatial partitioning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_partitioning) to avoid looping through all entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: start
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: end
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The mins corner of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maxs corner of the ray.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of the found entities. There's a limit of 1024 entities.

FindByClass.DESCRIPTION:
Gets all entities with the given class, supports wildcards.

This function returns a sequential table, meaning it should be looped with [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs) instead of [pairs](/gmod/Global.pairs) for efficiency reasons.

This works internally by iterating over [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll). `ents.FindByClass` is always faster than [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll) or [ents.Iterator](/gmod/ents.Iterator).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The class of the entities to find, supports wildcards.

Asterisks (`*`) are the only wildcard supported.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing all found entities.

FindByClassAndParent.DESCRIPTION: Finds all entities that are of given class and are children of given entity. This works internally by iterating over [ents.FindByClass](/gmod/ents.FindByClass).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The class of entities to search for.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: parent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Parent of entities that are being searched for.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of found entities or nil if none are found.

FindByModel.DESCRIPTION:
Gets all entities with the given model, supports wildcards.

This works internally by iterating over [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: model
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The model of the entities to find.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all found entities.

FindByName.DESCRIPTION:
Gets all entities with the given hammer targetname. This works internally by iterating over [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll).

Doesn't do anything on client.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The targetname to look for.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all found entities.

FindInBox.DESCRIPTION:
Returns all entities within the specified box.

This internally uses a Spatial Partition to avoid looping through all entities, so it is more efficient than using [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll) for this purpose.
NOTES: Clientside entities will not be returned by this function. Serverside only entities without networked edicts (entity indexes), such as point logic or Constraints are not returned either

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The box minimum coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMaxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The box maximum coordinates.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all found entities.

FindInCone.DESCRIPTION:
Finds and returns all entities within the specified cone. Only entities whose [Entity:WorldSpaceCenter](/gmod/Entity:WorldSpaceCenter) is within the cone are considered to be in it.

The "cone" is actually a conical "slice" of an axis-aligned box (see: [ents.FindInBox](/gmod/ents.FindInBox)). The image to the right shows approximately how this function would look in 2D. Due to this, the entity may be farther than the specified range!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The tip of the cone.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Direction of the cone.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: range
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The range of the cone/box around the origin.
NOTES: The function internally adds 1 to this argument before using it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle_cos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The [cosine](/gmod/math.cos) of the angle between the center of the cone to its edges, which is half the overall angle of the cone.

1 makes a 0° cone, 0.707 makes approximately 90°, 0 makes 180°, and so on.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all found [Entity](/gmod/Entity)s.

FindInPVS.DESCRIPTION: Finds all entities that lie within a [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community").
NOTES: The function won't take in to account [AddOriginToPVS](/gmod/Global.AddOriginToPVS) and the like.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: viewPoint
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: [Entity](/gmod/Entity) or [Vector](/gmod/Vector) to find entities within the PVS of. If a player is given, this function will use the player's view entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The found [Entity](/gmod/Entity)s.

FindInSphere.DESCRIPTION:
Gets all entities within the specified sphere.

This function internally calls [util.IsBoxIntersectingSphere](/gmod/util.IsBoxIntersectingSphere) for every entity on the map based on their Orientated Bounding Box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Center of the sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Radius of the sphere.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all found [Entity](/gmod/Entity)s.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the target entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: activator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Activator of the event.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: caller
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Caller of the event.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: usetype
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Use type. See the [USE](/gmod/Enums/USE).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This value is passed to [ENTITY:Use](/gmod/ENTITY:Use), but isn't used by any default entities in the engine.

GetAll.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table of all existing entities.

Consider using [ents.Iterator](/gmod/ents.Iterator) instead for better performance.

This function returns a sequential table, meaning it should be looped with [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs) instead of [pairs](/gmod/Global.pairs) for efficiency reasons.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of all existing [Entity](/gmod/Entity)s.

GetByIndex.DESCRIPTION: Returns an entity by its index. Same as [Entity](/gmod/Global.Entity).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entIdx
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entity if it exists, or `NULL` if it doesn't.

GetCount.DESCRIPTION:
Gives you the amount of currently existing entities.

Similar to **#**[ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll)() but with better performance since the entity table doesn't have to be generated.  
If [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll) is already being called for iteration, than using the **#** operator on the table will be faster than calling this function since it is JITted.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: IncludeKillMe
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Include entities with the FL_KILLME flag. This will skip an internal loop, and the function will be more efficient as a byproduct.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of entities.

GetEdictCount.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the amount of networked entities, which is limited to 8192.

[ents.Create](/gmod/ents.Create) will fail somewhere between 8064 and 8176 - this can vary based on the amount of player slots on the server and other entities.

See also [MAX_EDICT_BITS](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Global_Variables#maxedictbits) global variable.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of networked entities.

GetMapCreatedEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Returns entity that has given [Entity:MapCreationID](/gmod/Entity:MapCreationID).


	This works internally by iterating over [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity's creation id.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Found entity, `nil` otherwise.

Iterator.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a [Stateless Iterator](https://www.lua.org/pil/7.3.html) for all entities.
		Intended for use in [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).  
		See [player.Iterator](/gmod/player.Iterator) for a similar function for all players.
NOTES:
Internally, this function uses cached values that are stored in Lua, as opposed to [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll), which is a C++ function.
		Because a call operation from Lua to C++ *and* with a return back to Lua is quite costly, this function will be more efficient than [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The Iterator Function from [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs).
Table of all existing [Entities](/gmod/Entity).  This is a cached copy of [ents.GetAll](/gmod/ents.GetAll).
WARNINGS:
This table is intended to be read-only.

Modifying the return table will affect all subsequent calls to this function until the cache is refreshed, replacing all of your ents.GetAll usages may come with unintended side effects because of this.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The starting index for the table of players.  
			This is always `0` and is returned for the benefit of [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).

ents.DESCRIPTION: The ents library provides functions for creating and finding entities in the game.

Append.DESCRIPTION: Appends data to a file in the `data/` folder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file's name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: content
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The content which should be appended to the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the operation was successful.

AsyncRead.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the content of a file asynchronously.

All limitations of [file.Read](/gmod/file.Read) also apply.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A callback function that will be called when the file read operation finishes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sync
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If `true` the file will be read synchronously.

RETURNS.NAME: status
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: [FSASYNC_OK](/gmod/Enums/FSASYNC) on success, [FSASYNC_ERR_](/gmod/Enums/FSASYNC) on failure.

CreateDir.DESCRIPTION: Creates a directory that is relative to the `data` folder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The directory's name.

Delete.DESCRIPTION: Deletes a file or `empty` folder that is relative to the **data** folder. You can't remove any files outside of **data** folder.
NOTES: You are able to delete **any** file in the Menu state.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.
NOTES: This is only available in the menu state.

Exists.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a boolean of whether the file or directory exists or not.    
		If you want to check for a directory, [file.IsDir](/gmod/file.IsDir) will be faster since it won't check for files.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file or directory's name. ( You must include the file extension for files, for example "data.txt" )

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns `true` if the file exists and `false` if it does not.

Find.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of files and directories inside a single folder.
WARNINGS: It seems that paths with capital letters (e.g. lua/MyFolder/*) don't work as expected on Linux.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The wildcard to search for. `models/*.mdl` will list **.mdl** files in the `models/` folder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sorting
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The sorting to be used, **optional**.

* `nameasc` sort the files ascending by name.
* `namedesc` sort the files descending by name.
* `dateasc` sort the files ascending by date.
* `datedesc` sort the files descending by date.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of found files, or `nil` if the path is invalid.
A table of found directories, or `nil` if the path is invalid.

IsDir.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the given file is a directory or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file or directory's name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the given path is a directory or `false` if it's a file.

Open.DESCRIPTION: Attempts to open a file with the given mode.
WARNINGS:
When trying to open files with the following characteristics, it returns nil:

the file extension is ".db; .mdmp; .dmp" or
the file is "server.cfg; autoexec.cfg; config.cfg; listenserver.cfg; mount.cfg"

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The files name. See [file.Write](/gmod/file.Write) for details on filename restrictions when writing to files.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileMode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The mode to open the file in. Possible values are:
* **r** - read mode.
* **w** - write mode.
* **a** - append mode.
* **rb** - binary read mode.
* **wb** - binary write mode.
* **ab** - binary append mode.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.NAME: File
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The opened file object, or `nil` if it failed to open due to it not existing or being used by another process.

Read.DESCRIPTION: Returns the content of a file.
WARNINGS: Beware of casing -- some filesystems are case-sensitive. SRCDS on Linux seems to force file/directory creation to lowercase, but will not modify read operations.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The data from the file as a string, or `nil` if the file isn't found.

Rename.DESCRIPTION:
Attempts to rename a file with the given name to another given name.

This function is constrained to the `data/` folder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: orignalFileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The original file or folder name. See [file.Write](/gmod/file.Write) for details on filename restrictions when writing to files.

**This argument will be forced lowercase.**

ARGUMENTS.NAME: targetFileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The target file or folder name. See [file.Write](/gmod/file.Write) for details on filename restrictions when writing to files.

**This argument will be forced lowercase.**

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` on success, `false` otherwise.

Size.DESCRIPTION: Returns the file's size in bytes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file's name.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The file size in bytes, or `-1` if the file is not found.

Time.DESCRIPTION: Returns when the file or folder was last modified in Unix time.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The **file** or **folder** path.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gamePath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Seconds passed since Unix epoch, or `0` if the file is not found.  
			For workshop content `1` is returned.

Write.DESCRIPTION: Writes the given string to a file. Erases all previous data in the file. To add data without deleting previous data, use [file.Append](/gmod/file.Append).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the file being written into. The path is relative to the `data/` folder.

This argument will be forced lowercase.

The filename **must** end with one of the following:
* .txt
* .dat
* .json
* .xml
* .csv
* .dem
* .vcd
* .gma
* .mdl
* .phy
* .vvd
* .vtx
* .ani
* .vtf
* .vmt
* .png
* .jpg
* .jpeg
* .mp3
* .wav
* .ogg

Restricted symbols are: `":`, and multiple consecutive spaces, as well as pretty much every other non Latin (a-Z) character

ARGUMENTS.NAME: content
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The content that will be written into the file.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: If the operation was successful.

file.DESCRIPTION:
The file library provides functions for finding, reading and writing to files. 
The following path values are most commonly used:
* `LUA` searches the lua files (in /lua/, in your gamemodes, in all the addons).
* `GAME` searches all the mounted content (main folder, addons, mounted games etc).
* `MOD` searches only the garrysmod folder.
* `DATA` searches in the data folder.

See [File Search Paths](/gmod/File%20Search%20Paths) for the descriptive list of path values.
For the full list of path values, type `path` in the console.

AddFrame.DESCRIPTION: Adds a frame to the blend. Calls [frame_blend.CompleteFrame](/gmod/frame_blend.CompleteFrame) once enough frames have passed since last [frame_blend.CompleteFrame](/gmod/frame_blend.CompleteFrame) call.

CompleteFrame.DESCRIPTION: Renders the frame onto internal render target.

DrawPreview.DESCRIPTION: Actually draws the frame blend effect.

IsActive.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether frame blend post processing effect is enabled or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is frame blend enabled or not.

IsLastFrame.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the current frame is the last frame?

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the current frame is the last frame?

RenderableFrames.DESCRIPTION: Returns amount of frames needed to render?

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Amount of frames needed to render?

ShouldSkipFrame.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether we should skip frame or not.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Should the frame be skipped or not.

AddAmmoType.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a new ammo type to the game.

You can find a list of default ammo types [here](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Default_Ammo_Types).
NOTES: There is a limit of 256 ammo types, including the default ones.
WARNINGS: This function **must** be called on both the client and server in [GM:Initialize](/gmod/GM:Initialize) or you will have unexpected problems.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ammoData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The attributes of the ammo. See the [Structures/AmmoData](/gmod/Structures/AmmoData).

WARNINGS: There's a rather low limit of around 256 for decal materials that may be registered and they are not cleared on map load.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: decalName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the decal.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: materialName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material to be used for the decal. May also be a list of material names, in which case a random material from that list will be chosen every time the decal is placed.

AddParticles.DESCRIPTION: Loads a particle file. Individual particle systems will still need to be precached with [PrecacheParticleSystem](/gmod/Global.PrecacheParticleSystem).
NOTES: You will still need to call this function clientside regardless if you create the particle effects serverside.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: particleFileName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path of the file to add. Must be `(file).pcf`.

BuildAmmoTypes.DESCRIPTION: Called by the engine to retrieve the ammo types.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: All ammo types registered via [game.AddAmmoType](/gmod/game.AddAmmoType), sorted by its name value.

CleanUpMap.DESCRIPTION:
Removes most entities, and then respawns entities created by the map, as if the map was just loaded.

There are certain exclusions, such as players or weapons held by players, soundscapes and others.  
[EFL_KEEP_ON_RECREATE_ENTITIES](/gmod/enums/EFL) can be set on entities to preserve them through a map cleanup.

On the client it will remove decals, sounds, gibs, dead NPCs, and entities created via [ents.CreateClientProp](/gmod/ents.CreateClientProp). This function is ran on all clients from server automatically, when it is called on the server.

This function calls [GM:PreCleanupMap](/gmod/GM:PreCleanupMap) before cleaning up the map and [GM:PostCleanupMap](/gmod/GM:PostCleanupMap) after cleaning up the map.

Beware of calling this function in hooks that may be called on map clean up (such as [ENTITY:StartTouch](/gmod/ENTITY:StartTouch)) to avoid infinite loops.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Calling this destroys all BASS streams.
The EFL_KEEP_ON_RECREATE_ENTITIES flag doesn't prevent an entity from being recreated, which means flagged entities will be duplicated since they are both kept and recreated.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dontSendToClients
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to `true`, don't run this functions on all clients.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: extraFilters
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity classes not to reset during cleanup.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
If set, delays the map cleanup until the end of a server tick, allowing bypassing the entity limit on maps with large amounts of them. Otherwise the entities will not be cleaned up until the end of the server tick.

The callback function will be called after the map cleanup has been performed.

ConsoleCommand.DESCRIPTION:
Runs a console command.
Make sure to add a newline ("\n") at the end of the command.
WARNINGS:
If you use data that were received from a client, you should avoid using this function because newline and semicolon (at least) allow the client to run arbitrary commands!

For safety, you are urged to prefer using [RunConsoleCommand](/gmod/Global.RunConsoleCommand) in this case.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stringCommand
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: String containing the command and arguments to be ran.

Get3DSkyboxInfo.DESCRIPTION: Returns information about the currently active 3D skybox.

RETURNS.NAME: sky3dparams
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The 3D skybox info, or `nil` if the map has no 3d skybox or the function is called too soon during server start up.

GetAmmoDamageType.DESCRIPTION: Returns the damage type of given ammo type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo ID to retrieve the damage type of. Starts from 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: See [DMG](/gmod/Enums/DMG).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID of the ammo type to look up the data for.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [Structures/AmmoData](/gmod/Structures/AmmoData) containing all ammo data.

GetAmmoForce.DESCRIPTION: Returns the ammo bullet force that is applied when an entity is hit by a bullet of given ammo type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo ID to retrieve the force of. Starts from 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ammo force.

GetAmmoID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ammo type ID for given ammo type name.

See [game.GetAmmoName](/gmod/game.GetAmmoName) for reverse.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the ammo type to look up ID of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ammo type ID of given ammo type name, or -1 if not found.

GetAmmoMax.DESCRIPTION: Returns the real maximum amount of ammo of given ammo ID, regardless of the setting of `gmod_maxammo` convar.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo type ID.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum amount of reserve ammo a player can hold of this ammo type.

GetAmmoName.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ammo name for given ammo type ID.

See [game.GetAmmoID](/gmod/game.GetAmmoID) for reverse.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo ID to retrieve the name of. Starts from 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The name of given ammo type ID or nil if ammo type ID is invalid.

GetAmmoNPCDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns the damage given ammo type should do to NPCs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo ID to retrieve the damage info of. Starts from 1.

GetAmmoPlayerDamage.DESCRIPTION: Returns the damage given ammo type should do to players.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Ammo ID to retrieve the damage info of. Starts from 1.

GetAmmoTypes.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of all ammo types currently registered.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing all ammo types. The keys are ammo IDs, the values are the names associated with those IDs.

GetGlobalCounter.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the counter of a Global State.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the Global State to set. 

If the Global State by that name does not exist, it will be created.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for a list of default global states.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The value of the given Global State, 0 if the global state doesn't exist.

GetGlobalState.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether a Global State is off, active or dead ( inactive ).

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the Global State to retrieve the state of. 

If the Global State by that name does not exist, **GLOBAL_DEAD** will be returned.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for a list of default global states.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The state of the Global State. See [GLOBAL](/gmod/Enums/GLOBAL).

GetIPAddress.DESCRIPTION: Returns the public IP address and port of the current server. This will return the IP/port that you are connecting through when ran clientside.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Returns "0.0.0.0:`port`" on the server when called too early, including in [GM:Initialize](/gmod/GM:Initialize) and [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity). This bug seems to only happen the first time a server is launched, and will return the correct value after switching maps.

NOTES: Returns "loopback" in singleplayer.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The IP address and port in the format "x.x.x.x:x".

GetMap.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the name of the current map, without a file extension.
On the menu state, returns "menu".
WARNINGS: In Multiplayer this does not return the current map in the CLIENT realm before [GM:Initialize](/gmod/GM:Initialize).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the current map, without a file extension.

GetMapChangeCount.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the current map change count for the server.

This is useful to determine whether the current map is the initial map, or whether a `changelevel` (using `map` command is also detected) has occurred at any point in the server's session.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The current map change count. Will start at `1`.

GetMapNext.DESCRIPTION: Returns the next map that would be loaded according to the file that is set by the mapcyclefile convar.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: nextMap or nil if called too early.

GetMapVersion.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the revision (Not to be confused with [VBSP Version](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Source_BSP_File_Format#Versions)) and BSP version of the current map.

Map revision is the amount of times the map file was saved in Hammer at the time of the map being compiled. This is useful to detect when a map has changed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Revision of the currently loaded map.
BSP version.

GetSkillLevel.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the difficulty level of the game.

**TIP:** You can use this function in your scripted NPCs or Nextbots to make them stronger, however, it is a good idea to lock powerful attacks behind the highest difficulty instead of just increasing the health.
NOTES: Internally this is tied to the gamerules entity, so you'll have to wait until [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) is called to return the skill level.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The difficulty level, Easy (1), Normal (2), Hard (3).

GetTimeScale.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the time scale set with [game.SetTimeScale](/gmod/game.SetTimeScale).

		If you want to get the value of `host_timescale`, use:
		```lua
local timescale = GetConVar( "host_timescale" ):GetFloat()
		```

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The time scale.

GetWindSpeed.DESCRIPTION: Returns the wind's velocity at a given position, as influenced by current map's [env_wind](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Env_wind) entities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The point to get wind speed at.

If specified, wind controllers with `windradius` other than `-1` will be taken into account, if the point is within their radius.  
If omitted, only the global wind controller will be used (if one exists).
NOTES: This argument will be ignored on the `CLIENT` [realm](/gmod/States) and will be treated as `nil` because the position of `env_wind` is not currently networked to clients.

RETURNS.NAME: windVelocity
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
`windDir * windSpeed` — the current wind direction multiplied by the current total wind speed.

See [env_wind_shared.cpp#L255-L258](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/master/src/game/shared/env_wind_shared.cpp#L255-L258) for how it's calculated.
The world.

IsDedicated.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the server is a dedicated server, false if it is a listen server or a singleplayer game.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the server dedicated or not.

KickID.DESCRIPTION: Kicks a player from the server. This can be ran before the player has spawned.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: [UserID](/gmod/Player:UserID), [SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID) or [SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) of the player to kick. Uses SteamID32 eg STEAM_0:0:00000000.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: reason
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Reason to display to the player. This can span across multiple lines.
WARNINGS: This will be shortened to ~512 chars, though this includes the command itself and the player index so will realistically be more around ~483. It is recommended to avoid going near the limit to avoid truncation.

LoadNextMap.DESCRIPTION: Loads the next map according to the `nextlevel` convar, or from the current `mapcyclefile` set by the respective convar.

MapLoadType.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the map load type of the current map.

After changing the map with the console command `changelevel`, "newgame" is returned. With `changelevel2` (single player only), "transition" is returned.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The load type. Possible values are: "newgame", "loadgame", "transition", "background".

MaxPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Returns the maximum amount of players (including bots) that the server can have.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum amount of players.

MountGMA.DESCRIPTION:
Mounts a GMA addon from the disk.
Can be used with [steamworks.DownloadUGC](/gmod/steamworks.DownloadUGC).
NOTES:
Any error models currently loaded that the mounted addon provides will be reloaded.


Any error materials currently loaded that the mounted addon provides will NOT be reloaded. That means that this cannot be used to fix missing map materials, as the map materials are loaded before you are able to call this.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Location of the GMA file to mount, retrieved from [steamworks.DownloadUGC](/gmod/steamworks.DownloadUGC) or relative to the `garrysmod/` directory (ignores mounting). This file does not have to end with the .gma extension, but will be interpreted as a GMA.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: success.
If successful, a table of files that have been mounted.

RemoveRagdolls.DESCRIPTION: Removes all the clientside ragdolls. On server, it will remove all `prop_ragdolls` that have the `SF_RAGDOLLPROP_USE_LRU_RETIREMENT` (4096) spawnflag.

SetGlobalCounter.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the counter of a Global State.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the Global State to set. 

If the Global State by that name does not exist, it will be created.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for a list of default global states.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: count
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to set for that Global State.

SetGlobalState.DESCRIPTION:
Sets whether a Global State is off, active or dead ( inactive ).

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for more information.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the Global State to set. 

If the Global State by that name does not exist, it will be created.

See [Global States](/gmod/Global%20States) for a list of default global states.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: state
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The state of the Global State. See [GLOBAL](/gmod/Enums/GLOBAL).

SetSkillLevel.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the difficulty level of the game, can be retrieved with [game.GetSkillLevel](/gmod/game.GetSkillLevel).

This will automatically change whenever the "skill" convar is modified serverside.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: level
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The difficulty level, Easy( 1 ), Normal( 2 ), Hard( 3 ).

SetTimeScale.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the time scale of the game logic.

To slow down or speed up the movement of a specific player, use [Player:SetLaggedMovementValue](/gmod/Player:SetLaggedMovementValue) instead.

See [physenv.SetTimeScale](/gmod/physenv.SetTimeScale) if you wish to only scale the physics timescale.

This function is meant to remove the need of using the `host_timescale` convar, which is cheat protected.  
The true timescale will be `host_timescale` multiplied by [game.GetTimeScale](/gmod/game.GetTimeScale).

Like `host_timescale`, this method does not affect sounds, if you wish to change that, look into [GM:EntityEmitSound](/gmod/GM:EntityEmitSound).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: timeScale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new timescale, minimum value is 0.001 and maximum is 5.

SendCommand.DESCRIPTION: Sends command to Hammer, if Hammer is running with the current map loaded.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cmd
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Command to send including arguments.

All commands are in the format `"command var1 var2 etc"`.

All commands that pick an entity with `x y z`, must use the exact position including decimals (i.e. `-354.4523 123.4 213.33`). 

# List of commands
| Command       | Description   |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| "session_begin mapName mapVersion" | Starts a hammer edit, locking the editor. mapName is the current map without path or suffix, mapVersion is the current version in the .vmf file |
| "session_end" | Ends a hammer edit, unlocking the editor. |
| "map_check_version mapName mapVersion" | This only works after session_begin, so you'd know the right version already and this only returns ok, this function is apparently useless. |
| "entity_create entityClass x y z" | Creates an entity of entityClass at position x y z. |
| "entity_delete entityClass x y z" | Deletes an entity of entityClass at position x y z. |
| "entity_set_keyvalue entityClass x y z "key" "value"" | Set's the KeyValue pair of an entity of entityClass at x y z. The Key name and Value String must be in quotes. |
| "entity_rotate_incremental entityClass x y z incX incY incZ" | Rotates an entity of entityClass at x y z by incX incY incZ. |
| "node_create nodeClass nodeID x y z" | Creates an AI node of nodeClass with nodeID at x y z you should keep nodeID unique or you will have issues. |
| "node_delete nodeID" | Deletes node(s) with nodeID, this will delete multiple nodes if they have the same nodeID. |
| "nodelink_create startNodeID endNodeID" | Creates a link between AI nodes startNodeID and endNodeID. |
| "nodelink_delete startNodeID endNodeID" | Removes a link between AI nodes startNodeID and endNodeID. |

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Returns `"ok"` if command succeeded, otherwise returns `"badcommand"` or `"notrunning"` if Hammer is not running.

**All changes only happen in Hammer, there is *NO* in game representation/feedback**

Add.DESCRIPTION: Registers a function (or "callback") with the [Hook](/gmod/Hook) system so that it will be called automatically whenever a specific event (or "hook") occurs.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: eventName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The event to hook on to. This can be any [GM](/gmod/GM_Hooks) hook, gameevent after using [gameevent.Listen](/gmod/gameevent.Listen), or custom hook run with [hook.Call](/gmod/hook.Call) or [hook.Run](/gmod/hook.Run).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The unique identifier, usually a string. This can be used elsewhere in the code to replace or remove the hook. The identifier **should** be unique so that you do not accidentally override some other mods hook, unless that's what you are trying to do.

			The identifier can be either a [string](/gmod/string), or a [table](/gmod/table)/object with an IsValid function defined such as an [Entity](/gmod/Entity) or [Panel](/gmod/Panel). [number](/gmod/number)s and [boolean](/gmod/boolean)s, for example, are not allowed.

			If the identifier is a table/object, it will be inserted in front of the other arguments in the callback and the hook will be called as long as it's valid. However, if IsValid( identifier ) returns false when **any** eventName hook is called, the hook will be removed.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to be called, arguments given to it depend on the identifier used.
WARNINGS:
Returning any value besides nil from the hook's function will stop other hooks of the same event down the loop from being executed. Only return a value when absolutely necessary and when you know what you are doing.

				It will also prevent the associated `GM:*` hook from being called on the gamemode.

				It WILL break other addons.

Fetch.DESCRIPTION:
Launches an asynchronous **GET** request to an HTTP server. Internally calls [HTTP](/gmod/Global.HTTP).

HTTP requests returning a status code >= `400` are still considered a success and will call the [onSuccess](/gmod/Structures/HTTPRequest) callback.

The [onFailure](/gmod/Structures/HTTPRequest) callback is usually only called on DNS or TCP errors (e.g. the website is unavailable or the domain does not exist).

A rough overview of possible [onFailure](/gmod/Structures/HTTPRequest) messages:
* `invalid url` - Invalid/empty url. ( no request was attempted )
* `invalid request` - Steam HTTP lib failed to create a HTTP request.
* `error` - OnComplete callback's second argument, `bError`, is `true`.
* `unsuccessful` - OnComplete's first argument, `pResult->m_bRequestSuccessful`, returned `false`.





Not all headers are allowed to be set, here is a list of known blacklisted headers:
```
host
expect
content-length
proxy-authenticate
accept-charset
connection
accept-encoding
origin
date
```

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This cannot send or receive multiple headers with the same name.

NOTES: HTTP-requests that respond with a large body may return an `unsuccessful` error. Try using the [Range](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Range) header to download the file in chunks.

HTTP-requests to destinations on private networks (such as `192.168.0.1`, or `127.0.0.1`) won't work.
	
	To enable HTTP-requests to destinations on private networks use [Command Line Parameters](/gmod/Command%20Line%20Parameters) `-allowlocalhttp`. (Dedicated servers only)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: url
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The URL of the website to fetch.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: onSuccess
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be called on success.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: onFailure
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be called on failure.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: headers
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: KeyValue table for headers.

Post.DESCRIPTION:
Sends an asynchronous **POST** request to an HTTP server. Internally calls [HTTP](/gmod/Global.HTTP).

HTTP requests returning a status code >= `400` are still considered a success and will call the [onSuccess](/gmod/Structures/HTTPRequest) callback.

The [onFailure](/gmod/Structures/HTTPRequest) callback is usually only called on DNS or TCP errors (e.g. the website is unavailable or the domain does not exist).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This cannot send or receive multiple headers with the same name.

NOTES: HTTP-requests that respond with a large body may return an `unsuccessful` error. Try using the [Range](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Range) header to download the file in chunks.

HTTP-requests to destinations on private networks (such as `192.168.0.1`, or `127.0.0.1`) won't work.
	
	To enable HTTP-requests to destinations on private networks use [Command Line Parameters](/gmod/Command%20Line%20Parameters) `-allowlocalhttp`. (Dedicated servers only)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: url
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The url to of the website to post.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: parameters
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The post parameters (x-www-form-urlencoded) to be send to the server. **Keys and values must be strings**.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: onSuccess
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be called on success.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: onFailure
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function to be called on failure.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: headers
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: KeyValue table for headers.

GetAnalogValue.DESCRIPTION: Returns the digital value of an analog stick on the current (set up via convars) controller.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: axis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The analog axis to poll. See [ANALOG](/gmod/Enums/ANALOG).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The digital value.
NOTES:
A joystick axis returns `-32768` when it's pushed completely up/completely left, & returns `32767` when it's pushed completely down/completely right.

A mouse wheel starts @ `0` & increases by `1` for every unit of scroll up/decreases by `1` for every unit of scroll down.

A mouse axis is `0` when the arrow is @ the top or left of the screen; When the arrow is @ the bottom right of the screen, the mouse y axis is the height of the screen & the mouse x axis is the width of the screen (in pixels). Note that in game, the “arrow” stays near the middle of the screen.

Trigger axis always return `0` (verify).

You can also use it programmatically, e.g.:

funcinfo.DESCRIPTION:
Retrieves LuaJIT information about a given function, similarly to [debug.getinfo](/gmod/debug.getinfo). Possible table fields:
* linedefined: as for [debug.getinfo](/gmod/debug.getinfo)
* lastlinedefined: as for [debug.getinfo](/gmod/debug.getinfo)
* params: the number of parameters the function takes
* stackslots: the number of stack slots the function's local variable use
* upvalues: the number of upvalues the function uses
* bytecodes: the number of bytecodes it the compiled function
* gcconsts: the number of garbage collectable constants
* nconsts: the number of lua_Number (double) constants
* children: Boolean representing whether the function creates closures
* currentline: as for [debug.getinfo](/gmod/debug.getinfo)
* isvararg: if the function is a vararg function
* source: as for [debug.getinfo](/gmod/debug.getinfo)
* loc: a string describing the source and currentline, like "<source>:<line>"
* ffid: the fast function id of the function (if it is one). In this case only upvalues above and addr below are valid
* addr: the address of the function (if it is not a Lua function). If it's a C function rather than a fast function, only upvalues above is valid*

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Function or Proto to retrieve info about.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Information about the supplied function/proto.

Return table fields:
* 0 (ref) (number): first IR ref for the snapshot
* 1 (nslots) (number): the number of valid slots

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The callback function.

The arguments passed to the callback depend on the event being reported:

* `"bc"`:
  * [function](/gmod/function) **func** - The function that's just been recorded
* `"trace"`:
  * [string](/gmod/string) **what** - description of the trace event: "flush", "start", "stop", "abort". Available for all events.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
  * [function](/gmod/function) **func** - The function being traced. Available for start and abort.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **pc** - The program counter - the bytecode number of the function being recorded (if this a Lua function). Available for start and abort.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **otr** - start: the parent trace number if this is a side trace, abort: abort code
  * [string](/gmod/string) **oex** - start: the exit number for the parent trace, abort: abort reason (string)
* `"record"`:
  * [number](/gmod/number) **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
  * [function](/gmod/function) **func** - The function being traced. Available for start and abort.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **pc** - The program counter - the bytecode number of the function being recorded (if this a Lua function). Available for start and abort.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **depth** - The depth of the inlining of the current bytecode.
* `"texit"`:
  * [number](/gmod/number) **tr** - The trace number. Not available for flush.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **ex** - The exit number
  * [number](/gmod/number) **ngpr** - The number of general-purpose and floating point registers that are active at the exit.
  * [number](/gmod/number) **nfpr** - The number of general-purpose and floating point registers that are active at the exit.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: event
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The event to hook into.

fmod.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the modulus of the specified values.

While this is similar to the `%` operator, **it will return a negative value if the first argument is negative**, whereas the % operator will return a **positive** value **even if the first operand is negative**.

This function is also slower than the `%` operator.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The calculated modulus.

frexp.DESCRIPTION:
**Lua reference description**: Returns `m` and `e` such that `x = m2e`, `e` is an integer and the absolute value of `m` is in the range ((0.5, 1) (or zero when x is zero).

Used to split the number value into a normalized fraction and an exponent. Two values are returned: the first is a multiplier in the range `1/2` (**inclusive**) to `1` (**exclusive**) and the second is an integer exponent.

The result is such that `x = m*2^e`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to get the normalized fraction and the exponent from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: m, multiplier - between `0.5` and `1`.
e, exponent - **always** an integer.

When called with an integer number m, returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range 1 to m inclusive.

See also [math.Rand](/gmod/math.Rand)

If n is also provided: lower limit.

If provided, this must be an integer.

randomseed.DESCRIPTION:

For shared random values across predicted realms, use [util.SharedRandom](/gmod/util.SharedRandom).
WARNINGS:
Usage of this function affects **ALL** random numbers in the game. This means that improper use (such as setting the seed to a static value that doesn't change with time) can negatively affect other addons or the base game.

It is a good idea to set the seed back to at least something like [SysTime](/gmod/Global.SysTime) in those cases.
