AdvanceVertex.DESCRIPTION: Pushes the currently set vertex data (via other `mesh.*` functions) into the mesh stack. See example on [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

Begin.DESCRIPTION:
Begins creating or modifying a 3D mesh constructed from a given quantity and type of primitive 3D shapes such as triangles and quads.

		The resulting mesh can be stored in an [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) if it is intended to be drawn multiple times or on multiple frames.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mesh
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) that the created mesh will be stored in.
			
			If the mesh has already been built, it will instead have its existing vertices modified but cannot have the quantity of vertices changed.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: primitiveType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
An enum that indicates what the format of the mesh's primitives will be.  
			For a full list of the available options, see the [MATERIAL](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: primitiveCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The quantity of primitives this mesh will contain as a whole integer number.

			The total number of vertices must not exceed the limit of `65535`.  
			The number of vertices created by each primitive will depend on the type of primitive used to construct the mesh.

			The expected value of this argument is dependent on the primitive type used.  
			For a full list of the primitive counts expected by each primitive type, see [MATERIAL](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: primitiveType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
An enum that indicates what the format of the mesh's primitives will be.  
			For a full list of the available options, see the [MATERIAL](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: primitiveCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The quantity of primitives this mesh will contain as a whole integer number.

			The total number of vertices must not exceed the limit of `65535`.  
			The number of vertices created by each primitive will depend on the type of primitive used to construct the mesh.

			The expected value of this argument is dependent on the primitive type used.  
			For a full list of the primitive counts expected by each primitive type, see [MATERIAL](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL).

BoneData.DESCRIPTION: Sets the bone matrix ID and bone weight to be used for the next vertex. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The slot index for the vertex, either 0 or 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrixId
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix index for the vertex, in the range of 0 -> 52. This is the index into [IMesh:DrawSkinned](/gmod/IMesh:DrawSkinned)'s ``bones`` argument, minus 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: weight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How much influence that matrix will have on this vertex, in the range of 0 -> 1.

Color.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the color to be used for the next vertex. This is `COLOR0` semantic of 
Vertex Shader. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Red component.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Green component.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Blue component.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: a
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Alpha component.

End.DESCRIPTION: Ends the mesh (Started with [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin)) and renders it.

Normal.DESCRIPTION: Sets the normal to be used for the next vertex. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal of the vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X part of the vertex normal.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y part of the vertex normal.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: z
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Z part of the vertex normal.

Position.DESCRIPTION: Sets the position to be used for the next vertex. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X position of the vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y position of the vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: z
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Z position of the vertex.

Quad.DESCRIPTION: Adds a quad (4 vertices) to the currently built mesh. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertex1
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertex2
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The second vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertex3
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The third vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vertex4
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The fourth vertex.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color) for the vertices.

QuadEasy.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a quad (4 vertices) to the currently built mesh, by using position, normal and sizes. See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

See also [mesh.Quad](/gmod/mesh.Quad).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the quad.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal of the quad.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sizeX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X size in pixels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sizeY
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y size in pixels.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color) for the vertices.

Specular.DESCRIPTION: Sets the specular map values. This is `COLOR1` semantic of Vertex Shader. Allows to blend textures of [Lightmapped_4WayBlend](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Lightmapped_4WayBlend). Requires the `VERTEX_SPECULAR` flag to be set in the C++ code of a shader.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red channel multiplier of the specular map.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The green channel multiplier of the specular map.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The blue channel multiplier of the specular map.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: a
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The alpha channel multiplier of the specular map.

TangentS.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the `S` tangent to be used, also known as "binormal".

Tangents and binormals are using in bumpmap rendering.

See also [mesh.TangentT](/gmod/mesh.TangentT) and [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tangentS
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The S tangent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X part of the vertex' tangent S.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y part of the vertex' tangent S.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: z
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Z part of the vertex' tangent S.

TangentT.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the `T` tangent to be used.

Tangents and binormals are using in bumpmap rendering.

See also [mesh.TangentS](/gmod/mesh.TangentS) and [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tangentT
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The T tangent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X part of the vertex' tangent T.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y part of the vertex' tangent T.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: z
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Z part of the vertex' tangent T.

TexCoord.DESCRIPTION: Sets the texture coordinates for the next vertex for the current mesh. (See [mesh.Begin](/gmod/mesh.Begin))

ARGUMENTS.NAME: set
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The texture coordinate set, 0 to 7.

Non-zero values require the currently bound material to support it. For example, any `LightmappedGeneric` material supports sets 1 and 2 (lightmap texture coordinates and bump map texture coords?).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: s
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: S coordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: t
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: T coordinate. Will be optional in the next update.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: u
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: U coordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: v
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: V coordinate.

UserData.DESCRIPTION:
A set of four numbers that can be used for arbitrary purposes by [Material](/gmod/Material) shaders.  
		This is most commonly used to provide tangent information about each vertex to the Material's shader.

VertexCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of vertices that have been pushed via [mesh.AdvanceVertex](/gmod/mesh.AdvanceVertex).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of vertices.

mesh.DESCRIPTION: The mesh library allows you to create meshes. A mesh is a set of vertices that define a 3D shape, for constant meshes you should use the [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh) object instead.

BuildSkeleton.DESCRIPTION: Called to build the skeleton. See [Using The Kinect](/gmod/Using%20The%20Kinect) and [Kinect developing](/gmod/Kinect%20developing).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: translator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `list.Get( "SkeletonConvertor" )` and [motionsensor.ChooseBuilderFromEntity](/gmod/motionsensor.ChooseBuilderFromEntity).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: player
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player to get motion sensor positions from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rotation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Global rotation of the player?

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Position
Angles
Sensor

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to choose builder for

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Chosen builder. The builders are stored in `list.Get( "SkeletonConvertor" )`
The material

GetSkeleton.DESCRIPTION: Returns players skeletal data if they are using Kinect. See [Using The Kinect](/gmod/Using%20The%20Kinect) and [Kinect developing](/gmod/Kinect%20developing).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The skeleton data.

IsActive.DESCRIPTION: Return whether a kinect is connected - and active (ie - Start has been called).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Connected and active or not

IsAvailable.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if we have detected that there's a kinect connected to the PC

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Connected or not

ProcessAngle.DESCRIPTION: Used internally by [motionsensor.ProcessAnglesTable](/gmod/motionsensor.ProcessAnglesTable). See [Using The Kinect](/gmod/Using%20The%20Kinect) and [Kinect developing](/gmod/Kinect%20developing).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Return nil on failure

ProcessAnglesTable.DESCRIPTION: Used internally by [motionsensor.BuildSkeleton](/gmod/motionsensor.BuildSkeleton). See [Using The Kinect](/gmod/Using%20The%20Kinect) and [Kinect developing](/gmod/Kinect%20developing).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Ang. If `!translator.AnglesTable` then `return {}`

ProcessPositionTable.DESCRIPTION: Used internally by [motionsensor.BuildSkeleton](/gmod/motionsensor.BuildSkeleton). See [Using The Kinect](/gmod/Using%20The%20Kinect) and [Kinect developing](/gmod/Kinect%20developing).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Positions. if `!translator.PositionTable` then return - `{}`

Start.DESCRIPTION: This starts access to the kinect sensor. Note that this usually freezes the game for a couple of seconds.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the access has been started

motionsensor.DESCRIPTION: Functions related to Kinect for Windows usage in GMod.
WARNINGS: Kinect feature works only on 32-bit version of the game.

AddWalkableSeed.DESCRIPTION: Add this position and normal to the list of walkable positions, used before map generation with [navmesh.BeginGeneration](/gmod/navmesh.BeginGeneration)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The terrain position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dir
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal of this terrain position.

BeginGeneration.DESCRIPTION: Starts the generation of a new navmesh.
NOTES: This process is highly resource intensive and it's not wise to use during normal gameplay

ClearWalkableSeeds.DESCRIPTION: Clears all the walkable positions, used before calling [navmesh.BeginGeneration](/gmod/navmesh.BeginGeneration).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: corner
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first corner of the new [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: opposite_corner
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The opposite (diagonally) corner of the new [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) or [nil](/gmod/nil) if we failed for some reason.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: top
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The top position of the ladder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bottom
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The bottom position of the ladder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: width
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Width for the new ladder.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dir
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Directional vector in which way the ladder should be facing. Please note that ladders can only face in the 4 cardinal directions - NORTH, SOUTH, WEST, EAST.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxHeightAboveTopArea
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If above 0, will limit how much the top of the ladder can be adjusted to the closest [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) when automatically connecting the newly created ladder to pre-existing nav areas.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The new [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) or [nil](/gmod/nil) if we failed for some reason.

Find.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of areas within distance, used to find hiding spots by [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot)s for example.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to search around. This position will be used to find the closest area to search from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Radius to search within

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stepHeight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Maximum step up height allowed

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dropHeight
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Maximum step down (fall distance) allowed

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A list of found [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s.

FindInBox.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s overlapping the given cube extents.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos1
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the cube to search in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos2
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The "end" position of the cube to search in. This is the opposite corner of the cube, diagonally.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A list of found [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s.

GetAllNavAreas.DESCRIPTION: Returns an integer indexed table of all [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s on the current map. If the map doesn't have a navmesh generated then this will return an empty table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all the [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s on the current map.

GetBlockedAreas.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of all blocked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s on the current map. See [CNavArea:MarkAsBlocked](/gmod/CNavArea:MarkAsBlocked).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of all the blocked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s on the current map.

GetEditCursorPosition.DESCRIPTION: Returns the position of the edit cursor when nav_edit is set to 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the edit cursor.

GetGroundHeight.DESCRIPTION: Finds the closest standable ground at, above, or below the provided position.
NOTES: The ground must have at least 32 units of empty space above it to be considered by this function, unless 16 layers are tested without finding valid ground.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position to find the closest ground for.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The height of the ground layer.
The normal of the ground layer.

GetMarkedArea.DESCRIPTION: Returns the currently marked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea), for use with editing console commands.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently marked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea).

GetMarkedLadder.DESCRIPTION: Returns the currently marked [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder), for use with editing console commands.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently marked [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder).

GetNavArea.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the Nav Area contained in this position that also satisfies the elevation limit.

This function will properly see blocked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s. See [navmesh.GetNearestNavArea](/gmod/navmesh.GetNearestNavArea).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to search for.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: beneathLimit
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The elevation limit at which the Nav Area will be searched.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The nav area.

GetNavAreaByID.DESCRIPTION: Returns a [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) by the given ID.
NOTES: Avoid calling this function every frame, as internally it does a lookup trough all the [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s, call this once and store the result

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID of the [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) to get. Starts with 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) with given ID.

GetNavAreaCount.DESCRIPTION: Returns the total count of nav areas on the map. If you want to get all nav areas, use [navmesh.GetAllNavAreas](/gmod/navmesh.GetAllNavAreas) instead as nav areas IDs are not always sequential.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The total count of nav areas on the map.

GetNavLadderByID.DESCRIPTION: Returns a [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) by the given ID.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID of the [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) to get. Starts with 1.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) with given ID.

GetNearestNavArea.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the closest [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) to given position at the same height, or beneath it.

This function will ignore blocked [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)s. See [navmesh.GetNavArea](/gmod/navmesh.GetNavArea) for a function that does see blocked areas.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to look from

ARGUMENTS.NAME: anyZ
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This argument is ignored and has no effect

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxDist
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This is the maximum distance from the given position that the function will look for a [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: checkLOS
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
If this is set to true then the function will internally do a [util.TraceLine](/gmod/util.TraceLine) from the starting position to each potential [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) with a [MASK_NPCSOLID_BRUSHONLY](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Enums/MASK). If the trace fails then the [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) is ignored.

If this is set to false then the function will find the closest [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) through anything, including the world.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: checkGround
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If checkGround is true then this function will internally call [navmesh.GetNavArea](/gmod/navmesh.GetNavArea) to check if there is a [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) directly below the position, and return it if so, before checking anywhere else.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: team
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: This will internally call [CNavArea:IsBlocked](/gmod/CNavArea:IsBlocked) to check if the target [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) is not to be navigated by the given team. Currently this appears to do nothing.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The closest [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) found with the given parameters, or a NULL [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) if one was not found.

GetPlayerSpawnName.DESCRIPTION: Returns the classname of the player spawn entity.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of the spawn point entity. By default returns "info_player_start"

IsGenerating.DESCRIPTION: Whether we're currently generating a new navmesh with [navmesh.BeginGeneration](/gmod/navmesh.BeginGeneration).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether we're generating a nav mesh or not.

IsLoaded.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if a navmesh has been loaded when loading the map.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether a navmesh has been loaded when loading the map.

Load.DESCRIPTION: Loads a new navmesh from the .nav file for current map discarding any changes made to the navmesh previously.
WARNINGS: Calling this function too soon, causes the Server to crash!

Reset.DESCRIPTION: Deletes every [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) and [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) on the map **without saving the changes**.

Save.DESCRIPTION: Saves any changes made to navmesh to the .nav file.

SetMarkedArea.DESCRIPTION: Sets the [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) as marked, so it can be used with editing console commands.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: area
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea) to set as the marked area.

SetMarkedLadder.DESCRIPTION: Sets the [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) as marked, so it can be used with editing console commands.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: area
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [CNavLadder](/gmod/CNavLadder) to set as the marked ladder.

SetPlayerSpawnName.DESCRIPTION: Sets the classname of the default spawn point entity, used before generating a new navmesh with [navmesh.BeginGeneration](/gmod/navmesh.BeginGeneration).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: spawnPointClass
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of what the player uses to spawn, automatically adds it to the walkable positions during map generation.

navmesh.DESCRIPTION:
The navigation mesh library. To be used with [CNavArea](/gmod/CNavArea).

The navigation mesh is used by [NextBot](/gmod/NextBot) to calculate path to its target.

Abort.DESCRIPTION: Cancels a net message started by [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start), so you can immediately start a new one without any errors.

Broadcast.DESCRIPTION:
Sends the currently built net message (see [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start)) to all connected players.
More information can be found in [Net Library Usage](/gmod/Net%20Library%20Usage).
NOTES: This is equivalent to: net.Send(player.GetAll())

BytesLeft.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of data left to read in the current message. Does nothing when sending data.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The amount of data left to read in the current net message in **bytes**.
Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.

The amount of data left to read in the current net message in **bits**.
Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.

BytesWritten.DESCRIPTION: Returns the size of the current message.
NOTES: This will include 3 extra bytes (24 bits) used by the engine internally to send the data over the network.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The amount of **bytes** written to the current net message.
Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.

The amount of **bits** written to the current net message.
Returns `nil` if no net message has been started.

Incoming.DESCRIPTION: Function called by the engine to tell the Lua state a message arrived.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The message length, in **bits**.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: client
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player that sent the message. This will be `nil` in the client state.

ReadAngle.DESCRIPTION: Reads an angle from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read angle, or `Angle( 0, 0, 0 )` if no angle could be read

ReadBit.DESCRIPTION: Reads a bit from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `0` or `1`, or `0` if the bit could not be read.

ReadBool.DESCRIPTION: Reads a boolean from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` or `false`, or `false` if the bool could not be read.

ReadColor.DESCRIPTION: Reads a [Color](/gmod/Color) from the current net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hasAlpha
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the color has alpha written or not. **Must match what was given to [net.WriteColor](/gmod/net.WriteColor).**

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color) read from the current net message, or `Color( 0, 0, 0, 0 )` if the color could not be read.

ReadData.DESCRIPTION: Reads pure binary data from the message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The length of the data to be read, in **bytes**.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The binary data read, or a string containing one character with a byte of `0` if no data could be read.

ReadDouble.DESCRIPTION: Reads a double-precision number from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The double-precision number, or `0` if no number could be read.

ReadEntity.DESCRIPTION: Reads an entity from the received net message. You should always check if the specified entity exists as it may have been removed and therefore `NULL` if it is outside of the players [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community") or was already removed.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The entity, or `nil` if no entity could be read.

ReadFloat.DESCRIPTION: Reads a floating point number from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The floating point number, or `0` if no number could be read.

ReadHeader.DESCRIPTION: Reads a word, basically unsigned short. This is used internally to read the "header" of the message which is an unsigned short which can be converted to the corresponding message name via [util.NetworkIDToString](/gmod/util.NetworkIDToString).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The header number

ReadInt.DESCRIPTION: Reads an integer from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bitCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The amount of bits to be read.

This must be set to what you set to [net.WriteInt](/gmod/net.WriteInt). Read more information at [net.WriteInt](/gmod/net.WriteInt).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read integer number, or `0` if no integer could be read.

ReadMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Reads a [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix, or an empty matrix if no matrix could be read.

ReadNormal.DESCRIPTION: Reads a normal vector from the net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The normalized vector ( length = `1` ), or `Vector( 0, 0, 1 )` if no normal could be read.

ReadPlayer.DESCRIPTION:
Reads a player entity that was written with [net.WritePlayer](/gmod/net.WritePlayer) from the received net message.

You should always check if the specified entity exists as it may have been removed and therefore `NULL` if it is outside of the local players [PVS](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS) or was already removed.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The player, or `Entity(0)` if no entity could be read.

ReadString.DESCRIPTION: Reads a [null-terminated string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Null-terminated_string) from the net stream. The size of the string is 8 bits plus 8 bits for every ASCII character in the string.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read string, or a string with `0` length if no string could be read.

ReadTable.DESCRIPTION:
Reads a table from the received net message.

See [net.WriteTable](/gmod/net.WriteTable) for extra info.
NOTES:
Sometimes when sending a table through the net library, the order of the keys may be switched. So be cautious when comparing (See example 1).

You may get `net.ReadType: Couldn't read type X` during the execution of the function, the problem is that you are sending objects that **cannot** be serialized/sent over the network.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequential
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set to `true` if the input table is sequential. This saves on bandwidth.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table received via the net message, or a blank table if no table could be read.

ReadType.DESCRIPTION: Reads a value from the net message with the specified type, written by [net.WriteType](/gmod/net.WriteType).
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: typeID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The type of value to be read, using [TYPE](/gmod/Enums/TYPE).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The value, or the respective blank value based on the type you're reading if the value could not be read.

ReadUInt.DESCRIPTION: Reads an unsigned integer with the specified number of bits from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bitCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The size of the integer to be read, in bits.

This must be set to what you set to [net.WriteUInt](/gmod/net.WriteUInt). Read more information at [net.WriteUInt](/gmod/net.WriteUInt).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The unsigned integer read, or `0` if the integer could not be read.

ReadUInt64.DESCRIPTION: Reads a unsigned integer with 64 bits from the received net message.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The uint64 number.
NOTES: Since Lua cannot store full 64-bit integers, this function returns a string. It is mainly aimed at usage with [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64).

ReadVector.DESCRIPTION: Reads a vector from the received net message. Vectors sent by this function are **compressed**, which may result in precision loss. See [net.WriteVector](/gmod/net.WriteVector) for more information.
WARNINGS: You **must** read information in same order as you write it.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The read vector, or `Vector( 0, 0, 0 )` if no vector could be read.

Receive.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a net message handler. Only one receiver can be used to receive the net message.

You can use the `net.Read*` functions within the message handler callback.
WARNINGS:
You **should** put this function **outside** of any other function or hook for it to work properly unless you know what you are doing!

You **must** read information in the same order as you write it.

Each net message has a length limit of **64KB**!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: messageName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The message name to hook to.
NOTES: The message-name is converted to lower-case so the message-names "`BigBlue`" and "`bigblue`" would be equal.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to be called if the specified message was received.

Send.DESCRIPTION: Sends the current net message to the specified player(s). It is then received via [net.Receive](/gmod/net.Receive) on the client realm of each of those players.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player to send the message to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: plys
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of players to send the message to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A recipient filter specifying message targets.

SendOmit.DESCRIPTION: Sends the current message (see [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start)) to all except the player or players specified.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player to **NOT** send the message to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: plys
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of players to **NOT** send the message to.

SendPAS.DESCRIPTION: Sends current net message (see [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start)) to all players that are in the same [Potentially Audible Set (PAS)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PAS) as the position, or simply said, it adds all players that can potentially hear sounds from this position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: PAS position.

SendPVS.DESCRIPTION: Sends current net message (see [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start)) to all players in the [PVS (Potential Visibility Set)](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/PVS "PVS - Valve Developer Community") of the position, or, more simply said, sends the message to players that can potentially see this position.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position that must be in players' visibility set.

SendToServer.DESCRIPTION: Sends the current net message (see [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start)) to the server. The player object must exist on the server for the net message to be received successfully by the server.
WARNINGS:
Each net message has a length limit of 65,533 bytes (approximately 64 KiB) and your net message will error and fail to send if it is larger than this.

The message name must be pooled with [util.AddNetworkString](/gmod/util.AddNetworkString) beforehand!

Start.DESCRIPTION:
Begins a new net message. If another net message is already started and hasn't been sent yet, it will be discarded.

After calling this function, you will want to call `net.Write` functions to write your data, if any, and then finish with a call to one of the following functions:
* [net.Send](/gmod/net.Send)
* [net.SendOmit](/gmod/net.SendOmit)
* [net.SendPAS](/gmod/net.SendPAS)
* [net.SendPVS](/gmod/net.SendPVS)
* [net.Broadcast](/gmod/net.Broadcast)
* [net.SendToServer](/gmod/net.SendToServer)
WARNINGS:
Each net message has a length limit of 65,533 bytes (approximately 64 KiB) and your net message will error and fail to send if it is larger than this.

The net library has an internal buffer that sent messages are added to that is capable of holding roughly 256 kb at a time. Trying to send more will lead to the client being kicked because of a buffer overflow. [More information on net library limits can be found here.](/gmod/Networking_Usage#netlimits)

The message name must be pooled with [util.AddNetworkString](/gmod/util.AddNetworkString) beforehand!

Net messages will not reliably reach the client until the client's [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) hook is called.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: messageName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the message to send

ARGUMENTS.NAME: unreliable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to `true`, the message is not guaranteed to reach its destination

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the message has been started.

WriteAngle.DESCRIPTION: Writes an angle to the current net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: angle
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle to be sent.

WriteBit.DESCRIPTION:
Appends a boolean (as `1` or `0`) to the current net message.

Please note that the bit is written here from a [boolean](/gmod/boolean) (`true/false`) but [net.ReadBit](/gmod/net.ReadBit) returns a number.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boolean
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Bit status (false = `0`, true = `1`).

WriteBool.DESCRIPTION: Appends a boolean to the current net message. Alias of [net.WriteBit](/gmod/net.WriteBit).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boolean
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Boolean value to write.

WriteColor.DESCRIPTION: Appends a [Color](/gmod/Color) to the current net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Color](/gmod/Color) you want to append to the net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: writeAlpha
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If we should write the alpha of the color or not.

WriteData.DESCRIPTION: Writes a chunk of binary data to the message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: binaryData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The binary data to be sent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The length of the binary data to be sent, in bytes.

WriteDouble.DESCRIPTION: Appends a double-precision number to the current net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: double
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The double to be sent

WriteEntity.DESCRIPTION:
Appends an entity to the current net message using its [Entity:EntIndex](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex).

See [net.ReadEntity](/gmod/net.ReadEntity) for the function to read the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entity
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to be sent.

WriteFloat.DESCRIPTION: Appends a float (number with decimals) to the current net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: float
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The float to be sent.

WriteInt.DESCRIPTION:
Appends a signed integer - a whole number, positive/negative - to the current net message. Can be read back with [net.ReadInt](/gmod/net.ReadInt) on the receiving end.

Use [net.WriteUInt](/gmod/net.WriteUInt) to send an unsigned number (that you know will **never** be negative). Use [net.WriteFloat](/gmod/net.WriteFloat) for a non-whole number (e.g. `2.25`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: integer
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The integer to be sent.

WriteMatrix.DESCRIPTION: Writes a [VMatrix](/gmod/VMatrix) to the current net message.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: matrix
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The matrix to be sent.

WriteNormal.DESCRIPTION:
Writes a normalized/direction vector ( Vector with length of 1 ) to the net message.

This function uses less bandwidth compared to [net.WriteVector](/gmod/net.WriteVector) and will not send vectors with length of > 1 properly.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normalized/direction vector to be send.

WritePlayer.DESCRIPTION:
Appends a player entity to the current net message using its [Entity:EntIndex](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex). This saves a small amount of network bandwidth over [net.WriteEntity](/gmod/net.WriteEntity).

See [net.ReadPlayer](/gmod/net.ReadPlayer) for the function to read the entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player to be sent.

WriteString.DESCRIPTION:
Appends a string to the current net message. The size of the written data is 8 bits for every ASCII character in the string + 8 bits for the null terminator.

The maximum allowed length of a single written string is **65532 characters**. (aka the limit of the net message itself)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: string
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The string to be sent.

The input will be terminated at the first null byte if one is present. See [net.WriteData](/gmod/net.WriteData) if you wish to write binary data.

WriteTable.DESCRIPTION: Appends a table to the current net message. Adds **16 extra bits** per key/value pair, so you're better off writing each individual key/value as the exact type if possible.
WARNINGS: All net messages have a **64kb** buffer. This function will not check or error when that buffer is overflown. You might want to consider using [util.TableToJSON](/gmod/util.TableToJSON) and [util.Compress](/gmod/util.Compress) and send the resulting string in **60kb** chunks, doing the opposite on the receiving end.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to be sent.
WARNINGS:
If the table contains a `nil` key the table may not be read correctly.

Not all objects can be sent over the network. Things like functions, [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial)s, etc will cause errors when reading the table from a net message.

Each element is also limited by the constraint of the `net.Write

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sequential
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set to `true` if the input table is sequential. This saves on bandwidth, adding **8 extra bits** per key/value pair instead of 16 bits.
NOTES: To read the table you need to give [net.ReadTable](/gmod/net.ReadTable) the same value!

WriteType.DESCRIPTION: Appends any type of value to the current net message.
NOTES: An additional 8-bit unsigned integer indicating the type will automatically be written to the packet before the value, in order to facilitate reading with [net.ReadType](/gmod/net.ReadType). If you know the data type you are writing, use a function meant for that specific data type to reduce amount of data sent.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The data to be sent.

WriteUInt.DESCRIPTION:
Appends an unsigned integer with the specified number of bits to the current net message.

Use [net.WriteInt](/gmod/net.WriteInt) if you want to send negative and positive numbers. Use [net.WriteFloat](/gmod/net.WriteFloat) for a non-whole number (e.g. `2.25`).
NOTES: Unsigned numbers **do not** support negative numbers.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: unsignedInteger
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unsigned integer to be sent.

WriteUInt64.DESCRIPTION:
Appends an unsigned integer with 64 bits to the current net message.

		The limit for an uint64 is 18'446'744'073'709'551'615.  
		Everything above the limit will be set to the limit.  

		Unsigned numbers **do not** support negative numbers.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: uint64
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The 64 bit value to be sent. Can be a number.
WARNINGS:
Since Lua cannot store full 64-bit integers, this function takes a string. It is mainly aimed at usage with [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64).

				If your input is a number and not a string, it won't be networked correctly as soon as it has more than 13 digits.  
				This is because Lua represents numbers over 13 digits as `1e+14`(`100 000 000 000 000`)  
				You can do something like this to convert it to a string: `string.format("%.0f", number)`.  
				If you try to use [tostring](/gmod/Global.tostring) it will fail because it will create a result something like `1e+14` which doesn't work.

WriteVector.DESCRIPTION:
Appends a vector to the current net message.
Vectors sent by this function are compressed, which may result in precision loss. XYZ components greater than `16384` or less than `-16384` are irrecoverably altered (most significant bits are trimmed) and precision after the decimal point is 1 digit (5 bits).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: vector
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The vector to be sent.

net.DESCRIPTION:
The net library is one of a number of ways to send data between the client and server. 

The major advantages of the net library are the large size limit (64kb/message) and the ability to send data backwards - from the client to the server.

Refer to [Net Library Usage](/gmod/Net%20Library%20Usage) for a short introduction.

date.DESCRIPTION: Returns the date/time as a formatted string or in a table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: format
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The format string.

If this is equal to `*t` or `!*t` then this function will return a [Structures/DateData](/gmod/Structures/DateData), otherwise it will return a string.

If this starts with an `!`, the returned data will use the UTC timezone rather than the local timezone.

See http://www.mkssoftware.com/docs/man3/strftime.3.asp for available format flags.



Known formats that work on all platforms:

| Format | Description | Example of the output |
|:------:|:-----------:|:---------------------:|
| `%a` | Abbreviated weekday name | `Wed` |
| `%A` | Full weekday name | `Wednesday` |
| `%b` | Abbreviated month name | `Sep` |
| `%B` | Full month name | `September` |
| `%c` | Locale-appropriate date and time | Varies by platform and language settings |
| `%d` | Day of the month [01-31] | `16` |
| `%H` | Hour, using a 24-hour clock [00-23] | `23` |
| `%I` | Hour, using a 12-hour clock [01-12] | `11` |
| `%j` | Day of the year [001-365] | `259` |
| `%m` | Month [01-12] | `09` |
| `%M` | Minute [00-59] | `48` |
| `%p` | Either `am` or `pm` | `pm` |
| `%S` | Second [00-60] | `10` |
| `%w` | Weekday [0-6 = Sunday-Saturday] | `3` |
| `%W` | Week of the year [00-53] | `37` |
| `%x` | Date (Same as `%m/%d/%y`) | `09/16/98` |
| `%X` | Time (Same as `%H:%M:%S`) | `23:48:10` |
| `%y` | Two-digit year [00-99] | `98` |
| `%Y` | Full year | `1998` |
| `%z` | Timezone | `-0300` |
| `%%` | A percent sign | `%` |

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: **Not all flags are available on all operating systems** and the result of using an invalid flag is undefined. This currently crashes the game on Windows. Most or all flags are available on OS X and Linux but considerably fewer are available on Windows. See http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/fe06s4ak.aspx for a list of available flags on Windows. Note that the **#** flags also crashes the game on Windows.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: time
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Time to use for the format.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Formatted date
NOTES: This will be a [Structures/DateData](/gmod/Structures/DateData) if the first argument equals to `*t` or `!*t`

difftime.DESCRIPTION: Subtracts the second from the first value and rounds the result.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: timeA
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: timeB
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to subtract.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: diffTime

time.DESCRIPTION: Returns the system time in seconds past the unix epoch. If a table is supplied, the function attempts to build a system time with the specified table members.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dateData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to generate the time from. This table's data is interpreted as being in the local timezone. See [Structures/DateData](/gmod/Structures/DateData)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Seconds passed since Unix epoch

package.DESCRIPTION: The package library is a standard Lua library, it's mainly for use with the module system built into Lua.

Adds a [material surface property](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Material_surface_properties) type to the game's physics environment.

CreateNextBot.DESCRIPTION:
Similar to the serverside command "bot", this function creates a new Player bot with the given name. This bot will not obey to the usual `bot_*` commands, and it's the same bot base used in TF2 and CS:S.

The best way to control the behaviour of a Player bot right now is to use the [GM:StartCommand](/gmod/GM:StartCommand) hook and modify its input serverside.
NOTES: Any Bot created using this method will be considered UnAuthed by Garry's Mod

Despite this Player being fake, it has to be removed from the server by using [Player:Kick](/gmod/Player:Kick) and **NOT** [Entity:Remove](/gmod/Entity:Remove).
Also keep in mind that these bots still use player slots, so you won't be able to spawn them in singleplayer!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: botName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the bot, using an already existing name will append brackets at the end of it with a number pertaining it.

Example: "Bot name test", "Bot name test(1)".

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The newly created Player bot. Returns NULL if there's no Player slots available to host it.

WARNINGS: Internally this function iterates over all players in the server, meaning it can be quite expensive in a performance-critical context.

GetByUniqueID.DESCRIPTION: Gets the player with the specified uniqueID (not recommended way to identify players).
DEPRECATED: Use player.GetBySteamID64, player.GetBySteamID or player.GetByAccountID to get a player by a unique identifier instead.
WARNINGS: Internally this function iterates over all players in the server, meaning it can be quite expensive in a performance-critical context.

It is highly recommended to use [player.GetByAccountID](/gmod/player.GetByAccountID), [player.GetBySteamID](/gmod/player.GetBySteamID) or [player.GetBySteamID64](/gmod/player.GetBySteamID64) instead as this function can have collisions ( be same for different people ) while SteamID is guaranteed to unique to each player.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: uniqueID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) to find the player by.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Player if one is found, `false` otherwise.

NOTES: Players who are currently connecting to the server will not be counted. See function: [player.GetCountConnecting](/gmod/player.GetCountConnecting)

Similar to **#**[player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll)() but with better performance since the player table doesn't have to be generated. If [player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll) is already being called for iteration, then using the **#** operator on the table will be faster than calling this function since it is JITted.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of players.

GetCountConnecting.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the amount of players connecting to the server, but not yet spawned in.

`player.GetCountConnecting() + player.GetCount()` would result in the total player count on this server.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Number of players still connecting.

GetHumans.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table containing all human players (non-bot/AI).

Unlike [player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll), this does not include bots.
NOTES: This function returns a sequential table, meaning it should be looped with [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs) instead of [pairs](/gmod/Global.pairs) for efficiency reasons.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing all human (non-bot/AI) players.

Iterator.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a [Stateless Iterator](https://www.lua.org/pil/7.3.html) for all players on the server.
		Intended for use in [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).  
		See [ents.Iterator](/gmod/ents.Iterator) for a similar function for all entities.
NOTES:
Internally, this function uses cached values that are stored in Lua, as opposed to [player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll), which is a C++ function.
		Because a call operation from Lua to C++ *and* with a return back to Lua is quite costly, this function will be more efficient than [player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The Iterator Function from [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs).
Table of all existing [Players](/gmod/Player).  This is a cached copy of [player.GetAll](/gmod/player.GetAll).
WARNINGS:
This table is intended to be read-only.

Modifying the return table will affect all subsequent calls to this function until the cache is refreshed, replacing all of your player.GetAll usages may come with unintended side effects because of this.

An example:
```
-- Bad code.
local scan_ents = select( 2, player.Iterator() )
table.Add( scan_ents, ents.FindByClass( "ttt_decoy" ) )

-- Fine code. A copy of the table is being made and used.
local scan_ents = table.Copy( select( 2, player.Iterator() ) )
table.Add( scan_ents, ents.FindByClass( "ttt_decoy" ) )
```

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The starting index for the table of players.  
			This is always `0` and is returned for the benefit of [Generic For-Loops](https://www.lua.org/pil/4.3.5.html).

BindLocalCubemap.DESCRIPTION:

BrushMaterialOverride.DESCRIPTION: This function overrides the brush material for next render operations. It can be used with [Entity:DrawModel](/gmod/Entity:DrawModel).

Capture.DESCRIPTION:
Captures a part of the current render target and returns the data as a binary string in the given format.

Since the pixel buffer clears itself every frame, this will return a black screen outside of render hooks. To capture the user's final view, use [GM:PostRender](/gmod/GM:PostRender). This will not capture the Steam overlay or third-party injections (such as the Discord overlay, Overwolf, and advanced cheats) on the user's screen.
WARNINGS: This function will return nil if escape menu is open.

In PNG mode, this function can produce unexpected result where foreground is rendered as transparent.
This is caused by [render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha](/gmod/render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha) set to `true` when doing most of render operations, including rendering in `_rt_fullframefb`. If you want to capture render target's content as PNG image only for output quality, set [Structures/RenderCaptureData](/gmod/Structures/RenderCaptureData)'s `alpha` to `false` when capturing render targets with [render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha](/gmod/render.SetWriteDepthToDestAlpha) set to `true`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: captureData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Parameters of the capture. See [Structures/RenderCaptureData](/gmod/Structures/RenderCaptureData).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The binary data.

CapturePixels.DESCRIPTION:
Dumps the current render target and allows the pixels to be accessed by [render.ReadPixel](/gmod/render.ReadPixel). 

	Capturing outside a render hook will return an image filled with `0 0 0 255`.

	See also [render.Capture](/gmod/render.Capture).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Blue component to clear to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: a
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Alpha component to clear to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: clearDepth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Clear the depth.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: clearStencil
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Clear the stencil.

ClearBuffersObeyStencil.DESCRIPTION:
Tests every pixel of the active [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets) against the current Stencil configuration and sets the Color Channel values and, optionally, the Depth Buffer values for every pixel that passes.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page
NOTES:
This function does **not** clear the Stencil Buffer on its own.  
			If you would like to clear the Stencil Buffer, you can use [render.ClearStencil](/gmod/render.ClearStencil).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: red
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The red Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: green
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The green Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The blue Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: alpha
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The alpha (translucency) Color Channel value for each pixel that is cleared.  
			Must be an integer value in the range 0-255 (`byte`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: clearDepth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If true, reset the Depth Buffer values.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: clearStencil
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to also clear the stencil buffer.

ClearRenderTarget.DESCRIPTION:
Clears a render target.

It uses [render.Clear](/gmod/render.Clear) then [render.SetRenderTarget](/gmod/render.SetRenderTarget) on the modified render target.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The color.

ClearStencil.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Stencil Buffer value to `0` for all pixels in the currently active [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets).
		
		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ClearStencilBufferRectangle.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Stencil Buffer value for every pixel in a given rectangle to a given value.

This is **not** affected by [render.SetStencilWriteMask](/gmod/render.SetStencilWriteMask).

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle to be cleared.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startY
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle to be cleared.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The X coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle to be cleared.  
			**Note:** Unlike some other rectangle-based functions, this is **not** the width of the rectangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endY
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The Y coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle to be cleared.  
			**Note:** Unlike some other rectangle-based functions, this is **not** the height of the rectangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stencilBufferValue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Stencil Buffer value that all pixels within the rectangle will be set to.

Pointing away from walls will get the lighting the wall receives. Pointing towards walls will not.

GetAmbientLightColor.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ambient color intensity of the map, basically the color the sky emits.

This is used by the engine to calculate shadow color using the following formula: `ambientLight * 3 + Vector( 0.3, 0.3, 0.3 )`

See also [render.ComputeLighting](/gmod/render.ComputeLighting).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
The ambient color intensity of the map.

This is computed at map compile time and is stored in "linear color space".
Current alpha blending in range 0 to 1.

Depth is written using the [Shaders/DepthWrite](/gmod/Shaders/DepthWrite) by rendering scene a second time, using [SSAO_DepthPass function](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/blob/11a677c349b149b2f77184dc903e6bb17f8df69b/src/game/client/viewrender.cpp#L5576).

MaterialOverride.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the render material override for all next calls of [Entity:DrawModel](/gmod/Entity:DrawModel). Also overrides [render.MaterialOverrideByIndex](/gmod/render.MaterialOverrideByIndex).

See [render.WorldMaterialOverride](/gmod/render.WorldMaterialOverride), [render.BrushMaterialOverride](/gmod/render.BrushMaterialOverride) and [render.ModelMaterialOverride](/gmod/render.ModelMaterialOverride) for similar functions.
WARNINGS: In certain scenarios such as during entity's shadow pass, using this function can cause unexpected side effects. See example below on how to deal with this.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material to use as override, use `nil` to disable.

MaterialOverrideByIndex.DESCRIPTION:
Similar to [render.MaterialOverride](/gmod/render.MaterialOverride), but overrides the materials per index. For simple entities you may want to just use [Entity:SetSubMaterial](/gmod/Entity:SetSubMaterial).

[render.MaterialOverride](/gmod/render.MaterialOverride) overrides effects of this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the material to override, in range of 0 to 31. `nil` will reset all overrides.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material to override with, `nil` will reset the override for given index.

MaxTextureWidth.DESCRIPTION: Returns the maximum texture width the renderer can handle.

Model.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel), renders it at the specified pos/ang, and removes it. Can also be given an existing [CSEnt](/gmod/CSEnt) to reuse instead.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Using this with a map model ([game.GetWorld](/gmod/game.GetWorld)():[GetModel](/gmod/Entity:GetModel)()) crashes the game.

NOTES: This function is only meant to be used in a single render pass kind of scenario, if you need to render a model continuously, use a cached [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel) and provide it as a second argument.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: settings
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Requires:
* [string](/gmod/string) model - The model to draw.
* [Vector](/gmod/Vector) pos - The position to draw the model at.
* [Angle](/gmod/Angle) angle - The angles to draw the model at.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If provided, this entity will be reused instead of creating a new one with [ClientsideModel](/gmod/Global.ClientsideModel). Note that the ent's model, position and angles will be changed, and [Entity:SetNoDraw](/gmod/Entity:SetNoDraw) will be set to true.

ModelMaterialOverride.DESCRIPTION:
Forces all future draw operations to use a specific [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial).  
		
		Because this is independent of a specific [Entity](/gmod/Entity), it can be used to change materials on static models that are part of maps.
WARNINGS: In certain scenarios such as during entity's shadow pass, using this function can cause unexpected side effects. See example on [render.MaterialOverride](/gmod/render.MaterialOverride) about dealing with this.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial) that will be used for all upcoming draw operations, or `nil` to stop overriding.

OverrideAlphaWriteEnable.DESCRIPTION:
Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the alpha channel of the current render target.

See also [render.OverrideBlend](/gmod/render.OverrideBlend).
NOTES: Doing [surface](/gmod/surface) draw calls with alpha set to 0 is a no-op and will never have any effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the override.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldWrite
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the alpha channel or not. Has no effect if the previous argument is false.

OverrideBlend.DESCRIPTION:
Overrides the way that the final color and alpha is calculated for each pixel affected by upcoming draw operations.

When a draw operation is performed, the rendering system examines each pixel that is affected by the draw operation and determines its new color by combining (or "Blending") the pixel's current color (Called the "Destination" or "Dst" color) with the new color produced by the draw operation (Called the "Source" or "Src" color.)

This function allows you to control the way that those two colors (The Source and Destination) are combined to produce the final pixel color.

It's important to know that while [Colors](/gmod/Global.Color) use values in the range `(0-255)`, the color and alpha values used here are normalized to the range `(0-1)` so that they can be multiplied together to produce a value that is still in the range `(0-1)`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set to `true` to enable Blend Overrides.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sourceMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source color and alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: destinationMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination color and alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blendingFunction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
After the Source and Destination color and alpha have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Blending Function which combines them into the final color and alpha for the pixel.  
			One of the [BLENDFUNC](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set to `true` to enable Blend Overrides.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sourceColorMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source color** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Color Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: destinationColorMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination color** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Color Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: colorBlendingFunction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
After the Source and Destination colors have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Color Blending Function which combines them into the final color and alpha for the pixel.  
			One of the [BLENDFUNC](/gmod/Enums/BLENDFUNC) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sourceAlphaMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Source alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Alpha Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: destinationAlphaMultiplier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
This determines which value each affected pixel's **Destination alpha** will be multiplied by before they are sent to the Alpha Blending Function.  
			One of the [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND) enums.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: alphaBlendingFunction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: After the Source and Destination alphas have been multiplied against their corresponding multipliers, they are passed to the Alpha Blending Function which combines them into the final alpha for the pixel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Set to `false` to disable blend overrides.

OverrideBlendFunc.DESCRIPTION:
Overrides the internal graphical functions used to determine the final color and alpha of a rendered texture.

See also [render.OverrideAlphaWriteEnable](/gmod/render.OverrideAlphaWriteEnable).
DEPRECATED: Use render.OverrideBlend instead.
NOTES: Doing [surface](/gmod/surface) draw calls with alpha set to 0 is a no-op and will never have any effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enabled
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: true to enable, false to disable. No other arguments are required when disabling.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: srcBlend
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The source color blend function [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND). Determines how a rendered texture's final color should be calculated.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: srcBlendAlpha
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The source alpha blend function [BLEND](/gmod/Enums/BLEND). Determines how a rendered texture's final alpha should be calculated.

OverrideColorWriteEnable.DESCRIPTION: Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the color channel of the current render target.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the override.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldWrite
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the color channel or not. Anything drawn after will still write to depth if enabled and shouldWrite is false.

OverrideDepthEnable.DESCRIPTION: Overrides the write behaviour of all next rendering operations towards the depth buffer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the override.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shouldWrite
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If the previous argument is true, sets whether the next rendering operations should write to the depth buffer or not. Has no effect if the previous argument is false.

PerformFullScreenStencilOperation.DESCRIPTION:
Performs a Stencil operation on every pixel in the active [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets) without performing a draw operation.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

PopCustomClipPlane.DESCRIPTION: Removes the current active clipping plane from the clip plane stack.

PopFilterMag.DESCRIPTION:
Pops (Removes) the texture filter most recently pushed (Added) onto the magnification texture filter stack.  
		
		This function should only be called *after* a magnification filter has been pushed via [render.PushFilterMag](/gmod/render.PushFilterMag).

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

PopFilterMin.DESCRIPTION:
Pops (Removes) the texture filter most recently pushed (Added) onto the minification texture filter stack.  
		
		This function should only be called *after* a minification filter has been pushed via [render.PushFilterMin()](/gmod/render.PushFilterMin).

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

PopFlashlightMode.DESCRIPTION: Pops the current flashlight mode from the flashlight mode stack.

PopRenderTarget.DESCRIPTION:
Pops the last render target and viewport from the RT stack and sets them as the current render target and viewport.

This is should be called to restore the previous render target and viewport after a call to [render.PushRenderTarget](/gmod/render.PushRenderTarget).

PushCustomClipPlane.DESCRIPTION: Pushes a new clipping plane of the clip plane stack and sets it as active.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: A max of 2 clip planes are supported on Linux/POSIX, and 6 on Windows.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: normal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal of the clipping plane.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: distance
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The distance of the plane from the world origin. You can use [Vector:Dot](/gmod/Vector:Dot) between the normal and any point on the plane to find this.

PushFilterMag.DESCRIPTION:
Pushes (Adds) a texture filter onto the magnification texture filter stack.  
		This will modify how textures are stretched to sizes larger than their native resolution for upcoming rendering and drawing operations.  
		For a version of this same function that modifies filtering for texture sizes smaller than their native resolution, see [render.PushFilterMin](/gmod/render.PushFilterMin)

		Always be sure to call [render.PopFilterMag](/gmod/render.PopFilterMag) afterwards to avoid texture filtering problems.

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

If current texture has more than 1 mipmap, this also sets the mipmap filter.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texFilterType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The texture filter to use. For available options, see [TEXFILTER](/gmod/Enums/TEXFILTER).

PushFilterMin.DESCRIPTION:
Pushes (Adds) a texture filter onto the minification texture filter stack.  
		This will modify how textures are compressed to a lower resolution than their native resolution for upcoming rendering and drawing operations.  
		For a version of this same function that modifies filtering for texture sizes larger than their native resolution, see [render.PushFilterMag()](/gmod/render.PushFilterMag)

		Always be sure to call [render.PopFilterMin()](/gmod/render.PopFilterMin) afterwards to avoid texture filtering problems.

		For more detailed information and a usage example, see [the texture minification and magnification render reference.](/gmod/render_min_mag_filters)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texFilterType
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The texture filter to use. For available options, see [TEXFILTER](/gmod/Enums/TEXFILTER).

PushFlashlightMode.DESCRIPTION: Enables the flashlight projection for the upcoming rendering.
DEPRECATED: This will leave models lit under specific conditions. You should use render.RenderFlashlights which is meant as a direct replacement for this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the flashlight mode should be enabled or disabled.

PushRenderTarget.DESCRIPTION:
Pushes the current render target and viewport to the RT stack then sets a new current render target and viewport. If the viewport is not specified, the dimensions of the render target are used instead.

This is similar to a call to [render.SetRenderTarget](/gmod/render.SetRenderTarget) and [render.SetViewPort](/gmod/render.SetViewPort) where the current render target and viewport have been saved beforehand, except the viewport isn't clipped to screen bounds.

See also [render.PopRenderTarget](/gmod/render.PopRenderTarget).
NOTES: If you want to render to the render target in 2d mode and it is not the same size as the screen, use [cam.Start2D](/gmod/cam.Start2D) and [cam.End2D](/gmod/cam.End2D).
If the render target is bigger than the screen, rendering done with the surface library will be clipped to the screen bounds unless you call [DisableClipping](/gmod/Global.DisableClipping)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texture
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The new render target to be used.  
			Can be set to `nil` to push the main game frame buffer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X origin of the viewport.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y origin of the viewport.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: w
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Width of the viewport.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: h
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Height of the viewport.

ReadPixel.DESCRIPTION: Reads the color of the specified pixel from the RenderTarget sent by [render.CapturePixels](/gmod/render.CapturePixels)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The y coordinate.

RETURNS.NAME: r

RETURNS.NAME: g

RETURNS.NAME: b

RedownloadAllLightmaps.DESCRIPTION: This applies the changes made to map lighting using [engine.LightStyle](/gmod/engine.LightStyle).

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: When true, this will also apply lighting changes to static props. This is really slow on large maps.

RenderFlashlights.DESCRIPTION: Renders additive flashlights on an [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh), a direct replacement for [render.PushFlashlightMode](/gmod/render.PushFlashlightMode).

RenderView.DESCRIPTION: Renders the scene with the specified viewData to the current active render target.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Static props and LODs are rendered improperly due to incorrectly perceived distance.
Using render.RenderView on a RenderTarget texture in a 3d context like SWEP:PostDrawViewModel() while drawing the RenderTarget texture causes screen flickers.

ResetModelLighting.DESCRIPTION:
Resets the model lighting to the specified color.

It has the same effect as calling [render.SetModelLighting](/gmod/render.SetModelLighting) for every direction with given color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red part of the color, 0-1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
