Resets the HDR tone multiplier to the specified value.

This will only work on HDR maps, and the value will automatically fade to what it was ( or whatever [render.SetGoalToneMappingScale](/gmod/render.SetGoalToneMappingScale) is ) if called only once.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value which should be used as multiplier.

SetAmbientLight.DESCRIPTION: Sets the ambient lighting for any upcoming render operation.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red part of the color, 0-1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The green part of the color, 0-1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The blue part of the color, 0-1.

SetBlend.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the alpha blending (or transparency) for upcoming render operations.
	
See [render.SetColorModulation](/gmod/render.SetColorModulation) for the function to affect RGB color channels.

By itself, this will cause visible overlapping on parts of a model that are in front of other parts of the same model.  
For a solution to this, see the examples below.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not affect non-model `render.Draw*` functions.

NOTES: If a material has the [$alphatest](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/$alphatest) flag enabled then this function might not behave as expected because alpha will be binary, this has a default cutoff of `0.7`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blending
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The alpha (transparency) for upcoming draw operations.  
			A value in the range `(0-1)` where `0` is fully transparent, `0.5` is 50% visible, and `1` is fully opaque.

SetColorMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the current drawing material to "color".

The material is defined as:
```

 "UnlitGeneric"
 {
 	"$basetexture" "color/white"
 	"$model" 		1
 	"$translucent" 	1
 	"$vertexalpha" 	1
 	"$vertexcolor" 	1
 }
```

SetColorMaterialIgnoreZ.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the current drawing material to `color_ignorez`.

The material is defined as:
```

 "UnlitGeneric"
 {
 	"$basetexture" "color/white"
  	"$model" 		1
 	"$translucent" 	1
 	"$vertexalpha" 	1
 	"$vertexcolor" 	1
 	"$ignorez"		1
 }
```

SetColorModulation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the color modulation for upcoming render operations, such as rendering models.

The values can exceed 1 for stronger effect.

See [render.SetBlend](/gmod/render.SetBlend) for the function to affect alpha channel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: r
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red channel multiplier normal ranging from 0-1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: g
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The green channel multiplier normal ranging from 0-1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: b
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The blue channel multiplier normal ranging from 0-1.

SetFogZ.DESCRIPTION: If the [fog mode](/gmod/render.FogMode) is set to [MATERIAL_FOG_LINEAR_BELOW_FOG_Z](/gmod/Enums/MATERIAL_FOG), the fog will only be rendered below the specified height.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fogZ
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The fog Z.

SetGoalToneMappingScale.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the goal HDR tone mapping scale.

Use this in a rendering/think hook as it is reset every frame.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scale
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The target scale.

SetLightingMode.DESCRIPTION: Sets lighting mode when rendering something.
NOTES: **Do not forget to restore the default value** to avoid unexpected behavior, like the world and the HUD/UI being affected.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: Mode
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Lighting render mode.

Possible values are:
* 0 - Default.
* 1 - Total fullbright, similar to `mat_fullbright 1` but excluding some weapon view models.
* 2 - Increased brightness(?), models look fullbright.

SetLightingOrigin.DESCRIPTION: Sets lighting origin for the current model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightingOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position which will be used to calculate lighting for the current model.

SetLightmapTexture.DESCRIPTION: Sets the texture to be used as the lightmap in upcoming rendering operations. This is required when rendering meshes using a material with a lightmapped shader such as `LightmappedGeneric`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The texture to be used as the lightmap.

SetLocalModelLights.DESCRIPTION:
Sets up the local lighting for any upcoming render operation. Up to 4 local lights can be defined, with one of three different types (point, directional, spot).

Disables all local lights if called with no arguments.

See also [render.SetModelLighting](/gmod/render.SetModelLighting) for "lightbox" lighting. They are not mutually exclusive.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lights
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing up to 4 tables for each light source that should be set up. Each of these tables should contain the properties of its associated light source, see [Structures/LocalLight](/gmod/Structures/LocalLight).

SetMaterial.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the material to be used in any upcoming render operation using the [render](/gmod/render).

Not to be confused with [surface.SetMaterial](/gmod/surface.SetMaterial).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mat
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The material to be used.

SetModelLighting.DESCRIPTION:
Sets up the ambient lighting for any upcoming render operation. Ambient lighting can be seen as a cube enclosing the object to be drawn, each of its faces representing a directional light source that shines towards the object. Thus, there is a total of six different light sources that can be configured separately.

Light color components are not restricted to a specific range (i.e. 0-1), instead, higher values will result in a brighter light.

[render.ResetModelLighting](/gmod/render.ResetModelLighting) will set all 6 directions at once.
See also [render.SetLocalModelLights](/gmod/render.SetLocalModelLights).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lightDirection
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The light source to edit, see [BOX](/gmod/Enums/BOX).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: red
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

ARGUMENTS.NAME: green
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The green component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The blue component of the light color. In range of [0,1]

SetRenderTarget.DESCRIPTION: Sets the render target to the specified rt.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texture
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new render target to be used.

SetRenderTargetEx.DESCRIPTION: Sets the render target with the specified index of `COLOR[n]` to the specified rt, allowing you to work with [Multiple Render Targets (MRT)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d9/multiple-render-targets). Since standard shaders don't use MRT, you might find this useful at [Shaders/screenspace_general](/gmod/Shaders/screenspace_general).
NOTES: MRT doesn't work with 2D render functions like [render.DrawScreenQuad](/gmod/render.DrawScreenQuad). Instead, you can render a [render.DrawQuad](/gmod/render.DrawQuad) using [cam.Start2D](/gmod/cam.Start2D).
WARNINGS:
If you try to render with MSAA and set the main RenderTarget with another RenderTarget, nothing will be rendered.

[Link to Direct3D 9 documentation on MRT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d9/multiple-render-targets#:~:text=No%20antialiasing%20is%20supported)

`Multiple render targets have the following restrictions:`
* *No antialiasing is supported.*

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rtIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of output `COLOR[n]` [semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-semantics) from pixel-shader. Min: `0`, max: `3`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texture
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new render target to be used.

SetScissorRect.DESCRIPTION: Sets a scissoring rectangle which limits the drawing area. (otherwise known as clipping)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X start coordinate of the scissor rectangle in screen-space coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startY
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y start coordinate of the scissor rectangle in screen-space coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endX
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X end coordinate of the scissor rectangle in screen-space coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endY
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y end coordinate of the scissor rectangle in screen-space coordinates.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: enable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Enable or disable the scissor rect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: red
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The red channel of the shadow color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: green
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The green channel of the shadow color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: blue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The blue channel of the shadow color.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shadowDirections
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new shadow direction.

SetShadowDistance.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum shadow projection range.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shadowDistance
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new maximum shadow distance.

SetShadowsDisabled.DESCRIPTION:
Sets whether all shadow rendering should be disabled.

Internally sets `r_shadows_gamecontrol` convar, exactly like `shadow_control` does via its `SetShadowsDisabled` input.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: disable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `true` to disable shadows, `false` to enable.

SetStencilCompareFunction.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Compare Function that all pixels affected by a draw operation will have their Stencil Buffer value tested against.  

When not set to a static value like NEVER or ALWAYS, the Stencil Buffer value corresponding to each affected pixel will be compared against the current [Reference Value](/gmod/render.SetStencilReferenceValue).

Pixels that **Pass** the Compare Function check move on to the Depth Test, which determines if the draw operation will ultimately be allowed to overwrite the pixel's Color Channel, Stencil Buffer, and Depth Buffer values.

Pixels that **Fail** the Compare Function check have the [Fail Operation](/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation) performed on their Stencil Buffer value and do **not** have any of their Render Target layers modified by the draw operation.

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: compareFunction
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Compare Function that each affected pixel's Stencil Buffer value will be evaluated against during a draw operation.

SetStencilEnable.DESCRIPTION:
Enables or disables the Stencil system for future draw operations.

While enabled, all pixels affected by draw operations will have their corresponding values in the active [Render Target's](/gmod/render_rendertargets) Stencil Buffer compared against the current [Reference Value](/gmod/render.SetStencilReferenceValue) and their current Depth Buffer value compared against the depth of the corresponding pixel from the draw operation.  
Depending on the outcomes of these comparisons, one of either the [Pass](/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation), [Fail](/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation), or [Z-Fail](/gmod/render.SetStencilZFailOperation) operations is performed on the pixel's Stencil Buffer value.  
A pixel will only be updated in the active [Render Target](/gmod/render_rendertargets) if the [Pass Operation](/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation) is performed.

For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.
NOTES:
The Stencil system's configuration does **not** reset automatically.  
To prevent unexpected behavior, always manually ensure that the Stencil system is configured appropriately for your use-case after enabling it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: newState
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new state.

SetStencilFailOperation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) did **not** [Pass](/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation) the pixel.  

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: failOperation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function does not Pass a pixel.

SetStencilPassOperation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) Passes the pixel.  

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: passOperation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function Passes a pixel.

SetStencilReferenceValue.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the Stencil system's Reference Value which is compared against each pixel's corresponding Stencil Buffer value in the [Compare Function](/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) and can be used to modify the Stencil Buffer value of those same pixels in the [Pass](/gmod/render.SetStencilPassOperation), [Fail](/gmod/render.SetStencilFailOperation), and [Z Fail](/gmod/render.SetStencilZFailOperation) operations.
		
		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: referenceValue
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The value that the Compare function and the pass, fail, and z-fail operations will use.  
			This is an 8-bit (`byte`) unsigned integer value in the range [`0-255`].

SetStencilTestMask.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are read (tested) from the Stencil Buffer

		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.

		This is a companion function to [render.SetStencilWriteMask](/gmod/render.SetStencilWriteMask) which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are written.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bitMask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
			Set to `255` to make no change to read Stencil Buffer values.

SetStencilWriteMask.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the unsigned 8-bit (`byte`) bitflag mask that will be bitwise ANDed with all values as they are written to the Stencil Buffer

		This can be considered a "niche" Stencil function as it is not required for many Stencil use-cases.

		This is a companion function to [render.SetStencilTestMask](/gmod/render.SetStencilTestMask) which modifies Stencil Buffer values as they are read.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bitMask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The 8-bit (`byte`) mask.  
			Set to `255` to make no change to written Stencil Buffer values.

SetStencilZFailOperation.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the [Stencil Operation](/gmod/Enums/STENCILOPERATION) that will be performed on the Stencil Buffer values of pixels affected by draw operations if the [Compare Function](/gmod/render.SetStencilCompareFunction) Passed a given pixel, but it did **not** Pass the Depth Test.

		For more detailed information on the Stencil system, including usage examples, see the [Stencils Render Reference](/gmod/render_stencils) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: zFailOperation
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Stencil Operation to be performed if the Compare Function Passes a pixel, but the pixel fails the Depth Test.

SetToneMappingScaleLinear.DESCRIPTION: Sets the tone mapping scale for upcoming rendering operations.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: scales
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The tonemapping scales.
* X - Output scale.
* Y - Lightmap scale.
* Z - Reflection map scale.

SetViewPort.DESCRIPTION:
Changes the view port position and size. The values will be clamped to the game's screen resolution.

If you are looking to render something to a texture (render target), you should use [render.PushRenderTarget](/gmod/render.PushRenderTarget).
NOTES: This function will override values of [ScrW](/gmod/Global.ScrW) and [ScrH](/gmod/Global.ScrH) with the ones you set.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: X origin of the view port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Y origin of the view port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: w
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Width of the view port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: h
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Height of the view port.

Spin.DESCRIPTION:
Swaps the frame buffers/cycles the frame. In other words, this updates the screen.

If you take a really long time during a single frame render, it is a good idea to use this and let the user know that the game isn't stuck.

StartBeam.DESCRIPTION:
Begin drawing a multi-segment Beam.

			For more detailed information on Beams, as well as usage examples, see the [Beams Render Reference](/gmod/render_beams).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: segmentCount
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The number of Beam Segments that this multi-segment Beam will contain.

SupportsHDR.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the player's hardware supports HDR. (High Dynamic Range) HDR can still be disabled by the `mat_hdr_level` console variable or just not be supported by the map.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the player's hardware supports HDR.

SupportsPixelShaders_1_4.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the current settings and the system allow the usage of pixel shaders 1.4.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether Pixel Shaders 1.4 are supported or not.

SupportsPixelShaders_2_0.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the current settings and the system allow the usage of pixel shaders 2.0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether Pixel Shaders 2.0 are supported or not.

SupportsVertexShaders_2_0.DESCRIPTION: Returns if the current settings and the system allow the usage of vertex shaders 2.0.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether Vertex Shaders 2.0 are supported or not.

SuppressEngineLighting.DESCRIPTION:
Allows suppressing model lighting for any upcoming model render operation.  
Lighting then can be manually set up via various functions such as [render.SetModelLighting](/gmod/render.SetModelLighting).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This does not affect [IMesh](/gmod/IMesh)es.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: suppressLighting
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: True to suppress false to enable.

TurnOnToneMapping.DESCRIPTION: Enables HDR tone mapping which influences the brightness.

UpdateFullScreenDepthTexture.DESCRIPTION:
Updates the texture returned by [render.GetFullScreenDepthTexture](/gmod/render.GetFullScreenDepthTexture).

Silently fails if [render.SupportsPixelShaders_2_0](/gmod/render.SupportsPixelShaders_2_0) returns false.

UpdatePowerOfTwoTexture.DESCRIPTION: Updates the power of two texture.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The [render.GetPowerOfTwoTexture](/gmod/render.GetPowerOfTwoTexture).

UpdateRefractTexture.DESCRIPTION: Pretty much alias of [render.UpdatePowerOfTwoTexture](/gmod/render.UpdatePowerOfTwoTexture) but does not return the texture.

UpdateScreenEffectTexture.DESCRIPTION: Copies the entire screen to the screen effect texture, which can be acquired via [render.GetScreenEffectTexture](/gmod/render.GetScreenEffectTexture). This function is mainly intended to be used in [GM:RenderScreenspaceEffects](/gmod/GM:RenderScreenspaceEffects).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: textureIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Texture index to update. Max index is 3, but engine only creates the first two for you.

WorldMaterialOverride.DESCRIPTION: This function overrides all map materials for one frame.

render.DESCRIPTION: The render library is a powerful set of functions that let you control how the world and its contents are rendered. It can also be used to draw some 3D clientside effects such as beams, boxes and spheres.

AddFile.DESCRIPTION:
Adds the specified and all related files to the list of files the client should download from the server.

For convenience, this function will automatically add any other files that are related to the selected one, and throw an error if it can't find them. For example, a `.vmt` file will automatically add the `.vtf` with the same name, and a `.mdl` file will automatically add all `.vvd`, `.ani`, `.dx80.vtx`, `.dx90.vtx` and `.phy` files with the same name, with a separate error for each missing file.

If you do not want it to do this, use [resource.AddSingleFile](/gmod/resource.AddSingleFile).

See also [Serving Content](/gmod/Serving%20Content).
NOTES: The file must exist on the server it will not be added to the downloadables list!
WARNINGS: There's a 8192 downloadable file limit. If you need more, consider using Workshop addons - [resource.AddWorkshop](/gmod/resource.AddWorkshop). You should also consider the fact that you have way too many downloads. This limit is shared among all `resource.Add*` functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
**Virtual path** of the file to be added, relative to `garrysmod/`.  
Do not add `.bz2` to the filepath.  
Do not add `gamemodes/*gamemodename*/content/` or `addons/*addonname*/` to the path, since those paths are mounted virtually as if they are in the root `garrysmod/`.

AddSingleFile.DESCRIPTION:
Adds the specified file to the files the client should download from the server.

If you wish to add textures or models, consider using [resource.AddFile](/gmod/resource.AddFile) to add all the files required for a texture/model.





See also [Serving Content](/gmod/Serving%20Content).
NOTES: The file must exist on the server or players will not download it!
WARNINGS: There's a 8192 downloadable file limit. If you need more, consider using Workshop addons - [resource.AddWorkshop](/gmod/resource.AddWorkshop). You should also consider the fact that you have way too many downloads. This limit is shared among all `resource.Add*` functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path of the file to be added, relative to `garrysmod/`.

AddWorkshop.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a workshop addon for the client to download before entering the server. This will not "install" the addon on your server, see [Workshop for Dedicated Servers](/gmod/Workshop%20for%20Dedicated%20Servers) for installing Steam Workshop addons onto your servers.

Having the raw files from a workshop item does not count as having already downloaded it.
So players who previously downloaded a map through [FastDL](Serving_Content) will have to re-download it if it is part of a workshop addon.

You should try to only add addons that have custom content (models, sounds, etc). Lua files are not considered content, and are handled by a separate system. Adding workshop addons that only have Lua files is a waste, it will do nothing.

Gamemodes that are [workshop enabled](/gmod/Gamemode_Creation#Gamemode_Text_File) and the current map are automatically added to this list, if they come from the servers' workshop collection - so there's no need to manually add them.



See also [Serving Content](/gmod/Serving%20Content).
WARNINGS: There's a 8192 downloadable file limit. If you need more, consider the fact that you have way too many downloads. This limit is shared among all `resource.Add*` functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: workshopid
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The workshop id of the file. This cannot be a collection.

resource.DESCRIPTION: The resource library is used to control what files are sent to clients who join a server, this includes models, materials, sounds, text files but not Lua files.

AddRestoreHook.DESCRIPTION: Adds a restore/load hook for the Half-Life 2 save system.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique identifier for this hook.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The function to be called when an engine save is being loaded.



You can also use those functions to read data:
* [saverestore.ReadVar](/gmod/saverestore.ReadVar)
* [saverestore.ReadTable](/gmod/saverestore.ReadTable)
* [saverestore.LoadEntity](/gmod/saverestore.LoadEntity)

AddSaveHook.DESCRIPTION: Adds a save hook for the Half-Life 2 save system. You can use this to carry data through level transitions in Half-Life 2.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique identifier for this hook.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The function to be called when an engine save is being saved.



You can also use those functions to save data:
* [saverestore.WriteVar](/gmod/saverestore.WriteVar)
* [saverestore.WriteTable](/gmod/saverestore.WriteTable)
* [saverestore.SaveEntity](/gmod/saverestore.SaveEntity)

LoadEntity.DESCRIPTION: Loads [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) from the save game file that is being loaded and merges it with the given entitys [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity which will receive the loaded values from the save.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The restore object to read the [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) from.

LoadGlobal.DESCRIPTION:
Called by engine when a save is being loaded.

This handles loading gamemode and calls all of the hooks added with [saverestore.AddRestoreHook](/gmod/saverestore.AddRestoreHook).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The restore object to read data from the save file with.

PreRestore.DESCRIPTION: Called by the engine just before [saverestore.LoadGlobal](/gmod/saverestore.LoadGlobal) is.

PreSave.DESCRIPTION: Called by the engine just before [saverestore.SaveGlobal](/gmod/saverestore.SaveGlobal) is.

ReadTable.DESCRIPTION: Reads a table from the save game file that is being loaded.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The restore object to read the table from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The table that has been read, if any

ReadVar.DESCRIPTION:
Loads a variable from the save game file that is being loaded.

Variables will be read in the save order you have saved them.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The restore object to read variables from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The variable that was read, if any.

SaveEntity.DESCRIPTION: Saves entitys [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) to the save game file that is being saved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to save [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) of.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The save object to save [Entity:GetTable](/gmod/Entity:GetTable) to.

SaveGlobal.DESCRIPTION:
Called by engine when a save is being saved.

This handles saving gamemode and calls all of the hooks added with [saverestore.AddSaveHook](/gmod/saverestore.AddSaveHook).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The save object to write data into the save file.

WritableKeysInTable.DESCRIPTION: Returns how many writable keys are in the given table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to test.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The number of keys that can be written with [saverestore.WriteTable](/gmod/saverestore.WriteTable).

WriteTable.DESCRIPTION: Write a table to a save game file that is being saved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to write

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The save object to write the table to.

WriteVar.DESCRIPTION: Writes a variable to the save game file that is being saved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The value to save.

It can be one of the following types: [number](/gmod/number), [boolean](/gmod/boolean), [string](/gmod/string), [Entity](/gmod/Entity), [Angle](/gmod/Angle), [Vector](/gmod/Vector) or [table](/gmod/table).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: save
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The save object to write the variable to.

saverestore.DESCRIPTION: The saverestore library contains functions relating to the singleplayer save system built into the game.

Alias.DESCRIPTION: Defines an alias string that can be used to refer to another classname.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: alias
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A new string which can be used to refer to another classname.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname the alias should refer to.

Get.DESCRIPTION: Returns a copy of the ENT table for a class, including functions defined by the base class.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of the ENT table to return, can be an alias.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ENT table.

GetList.DESCRIPTION: Returns a copy of the list of all ENT tables registered.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of all SENTs where the key is the classname and the value is a table where:
* [table](/gmod/table) **t** — The [ENT](/gmod/Structures/ENT) table associated with the entity.
* [boolean](/gmod/boolean) **isBaseType** — Unused. Always `true`.
* [string](/gmod/string) **Base** — The entity base.
* [string](/gmod/string) **type** — The entity type.

GetMember.DESCRIPTION: Retrieves a member of entity's table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity's class name

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of member to retrieve

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The member or nil if failed

GetSpawnable.DESCRIPTION: Returns a list of all ENT tables which contain ENT.Spawnable

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of [Structures/ENT](/gmod/Structures/ENT)s

GetStored.DESCRIPTION: Returns the actual ENT table for a class. Modifying functions/variables in this table will change newly spawned entities

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname of the ENT table to return

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: entTable

GetType.DESCRIPTION: Returns the 'type' of a class, this will one of the following: 'anim', 'ai', 'brush', 'point'.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname to check

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: type

IsBasedOn.DESCRIPTION: Checks if name is based on base

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity's class name to be checked

ARGUMENTS.NAME: base
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Base class name to be checked

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if class name is based on base, else false.

OnLoaded.DESCRIPTION:
Called after all ENTS have been loaded and runs [baseclass.Set](/gmod/baseclass.Set) on each one.

You can retrieve all the currently registered ENTS with [scripted_ents.GetList](/gmod/scripted_ents.GetList).
NOTES: This is not called after an ENT auto refresh, and thus the inherited baseclass functions retrieved with [baseclass.Get](/gmod/baseclass.Get) will not be updated

Register.DESCRIPTION: Registers an ENT table with a classname. Reregistering an existing classname will automatically update the functions of all existing entities of that class.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Sub-tables provided in the first argument will not carry over their metatable, and will receive a BaseClass key if the table was merged with the base's. Userdata references, which includes Vectors, Angles, Entities, etc. will not be copied.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ENT
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The ENT table to register.  
			For the table's format and available options see the [Structures/ENT](/gmod/Structures/ENT) page.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The classname to register.

scripted_ents.DESCRIPTION: The scripted_ents library allows you to access information about any scripted entities loaded into the game, as well as register your own entities.

AddProvider.DESCRIPTION: Adds a search result provider. For examples, see [gamemodes/sandbox/gamemode/cl_search_models.lua](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/7c23addd2c35d3d046c80e3d0cb6052055eca3e2/garrysmod/gamemodes/sandbox/gamemode/cl_search_models.lua)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: provider
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Provider function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If provided, ensures that only one provider exists with the given ID at a time.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: query
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Search query

ARGUMENTS.NAME: types
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, only searches given provider type(s), instead of everything. For example `"tool"` will only search tools in Sandbox. Can be a table for multiple types.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxResults
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How many results to stop at

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of results

AddCurrentServerToFavorites.DESCRIPTION: Adds current server the player is on to their favorites.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: addOrRemove
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if to add, or `false` if to remove from favorites.

AddServerToFavorites.DESCRIPTION: Adds the given server address to their favorites.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: address
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Server Address. **IP:Port like "127.0.0.1:27015"**

IsCurrentServerFavorite.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the current server address is in their favorites.

RETURNS.NAME: favorite
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true if the current server is in their favorites

IsServerFavorite.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the given server address is in their favorites.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: address
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Server Address. **IP:Port like "127.0.0.1:27015"**

RETURNS.NAME: favorite
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: true if the server address is in their favorites

PingServer.DESCRIPTION: Queries a server for its information/ping.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ip
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The IP address of the server, including the port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The function to be called if and when the request finishes.

Callback has arguments described here: [Structures/ServerQueryData](/gmod/Structures/ServerQueryData).

PlayerList.DESCRIPTION: Queries a server for its player list.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ip
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The IP address of the server, including the port.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to be called if and when the request finishes.

Query.DESCRIPTION: Queries the master server for server list.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: data
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The information about what kind of servers we want. See [Structures/ServerQueryData](/gmod/Structures/ServerQueryData)

RemoveServerFromFavorites.DESCRIPTION: Removes the given server address from their favorites.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: address
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Server Address. **IP:Port like "127.0.0.1:27015"**

serverlist.DESCRIPTION: Menu state library to query the master server list.

Add.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a [sound scripts](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Soundscripts). It can also override sounds, which seems to only work when set on the server.

You can find a list of common sound scripts that are shipped with the game by default here: [Common Sounds](/gmod/Common%20Sounds).

A list of sound scripts can be retrieved with [sound.GetTable](/gmod/sound.GetTable).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sounds properties. See [Structures/SoundData](/gmod/Structures/SoundData)

AddSoundOverrides.DESCRIPTION: Overrides [sound scripts](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Soundscripts) defined inside of a `.txt` file; typically used for adding map-specific sounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filepath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the script file to load.

EmitHint.DESCRIPTION: Emits a sound hint to the game elements to react to, for example to repel or attract antlions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: hint
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The hint to emit. This can be a bit flag. See [SOUND](/gmod/Enums/SOUND)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to emit the hint at

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The volume or radius of the hint

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duration
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The duration of the hint in seconds

ARGUMENTS.NAME: owner
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, the sound hint will be ignored/deleted when the given entity is destroyed.

Generate.DESCRIPTION: Creates a sound from a function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A unique identifier for the sound.
WARNINGS: You cannot override already existing ones.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: samplerate
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sample rate of the sound. Must be `11025`, `22050` or `44100`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: length
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The length in seconds of the sound to generate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callbackOrData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A function which will be called to generate every sample on the sound. 

			

		This argument can also be given a table of samples, where values must range from `-1` to `1`.  
		This argument can also be a string of raw 16bit binary data, (each sample is unsigned short).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: loopStart
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sample ID of the loop start. If given, the sound will be looping and will restart playing at given position after reaching its end.

GetLoudestSoundHint.DESCRIPTION: Returns the most dangerous/closest sound hint based on given location and types of sounds to sense.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: types
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The types of sounds to choose from. See [SOUND_ enums](/gmod/Enums/SOUND).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to sense sounds at.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table with [SoundHintData](/gmod/Structures/SoundHintData) structure or `nil` if no sound hints are nearby.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the sound script

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The properties of the soundscript. See [Structures/SoundData](/gmod/Structures/SoundData)

GetTable.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a list of all registered [sound scripts](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Soundscripts).

New ones can be registered using [sound.Add](/gmod/sound.Add), and detailed information about each one can be retrieved via [sound.GetProperties](/gmod/sound.GetProperties).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The list/array of all registered sound scripts ( No other information is provided )

Play.DESCRIPTION:
Plays a sound from the specified position in the world.
If you want to play a sound without a position, such as a UI sound, use [surface.PlaySound](/gmod/surface.PlaySound) instead.

This function is similar to [EmitSound](/gmod/Global.EmitSound), but with less options.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: snd
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound to play. This should either be a sound script name ([sound.Add](/gmod/sound.Add)) or a file path relative to the `sound/` folder. (Make note that it's not sound**s**)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Where the sound should play.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: level
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Sound level in decibels. 75 is normal. Ranges from 20 to 180, where 180 is super loud. This affects how far away the sound will be heard, see [SNDLVL](/gmod/Enums/SNDLVL).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pitch
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound pitch. Range is from 0 to 255. 100 is normal pitch.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: volume
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Output volume of the sound in range 0 to 1.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dsp
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The DSP preset for this sound. [DSP Presets](/gmod/DSP_Presets)

PlayFile.DESCRIPTION:
Plays a file from GMod directory. You can find a list of all error codes [here](http://www.un4seen.com/doc/#bass/BASS_ErrorGetCode.html)

For external file/stream playback, see [sound.PlayURL](/gmod/sound.PlayURL).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: This fails for looping .wav files in 3D mode.
This fails with unicode file names.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: path
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The path to the file to play.

Unlike other sound functions and structures, the path is relative to `garrysmod/` instead of `garrysmod/sound/`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Flags for the sound. Can be one or more of following, separated by a space (" "):
* 3d - Makes the sound 3D, so you can set its position
* mono - Forces the sound to have only one channel
* noplay - Forces the sound not to play as soon as this function is called
* noblock - Disables streaming in blocks. It is more resource-intensive, but it is required for [IGModAudioChannel:SetTime](/gmod/IGModAudioChannel:SetTime).

If you don't want to use any of the above, you can just leave it as "".

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Callback function that is called as soon as the the stream is loaded.

PlayURL.DESCRIPTION:
Allows you to play external sound files, as well as online radio streams.
You can find a list of all error codes [here](http://www.un4seen.com/doc/#bass/BASS_ErrorGetCode.html)

For offline file playback, see [sound.PlayFile](/gmod/sound.PlayFile).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Due to a bug with [BASS](http://www.un4seen.com/), AAC codec streams cannot be played in 3D mode.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: url
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The URL of the sound to play

ARGUMENTS.NAME: flags
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Flags for the sound. Can be one or more of following, separated by a space (`" "`):
* 3d - Makes the sound 3D, so you can set its position
* mono - Forces the sound to have only one channel
* noplay - Forces the sound not to play as soon as this function is called
* noblock - Disables streaming in blocks. It is more resource-intensive, but it is required for [IGModAudioChannel:SetTime](/gmod/IGModAudioChannel:SetTime).

If you don't want to use any of the above, you can just leave it as `""`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Callback function that is called as soon as the the stream is loaded.

SetActorGender.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the gender of a specific actor (model). This is a system from [base Half-Life 2](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Global_actors) - `global_actors.txt`.

This will affect what voice lines `npc_citizen` will use when they have the given model set.

It is not limited to `npc_citizens` - any sound played on any entity with given model can have gender specific sounds playing, including soundscripts, by including `$gender` token in the sound file path.
WARNINGS: Internally the gender is stored by model file name only (i.e. `models/alyx.mdl` would be stored as `alyx`), not the full path! Be aware of potential collisions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelPath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the model file to set the gender of.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: gender
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Gender to set. Only 2 options are permitted: `female` and `male`. Any other option will be ignored.

sound.DESCRIPTION: Used primarily for adding new soundscript entries.

ActivateTool.DESCRIPTION: Activates a tool, opens context menu and brings up the tool gun.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tool
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Tool class/file name

ARGUMENTS.NAME: menu_only
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should we activate this tool in the menu only or also the toolgun? `true` = menu only,`false` = toolgun aswell

ActivateToolPanel.DESCRIPTION: Activates tools context menu in specified tool tab.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The tabID of the tab to open the context menu in

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cp
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The control panel to open

ActiveControlPanel.DESCRIPTION: Returns currently opened control panel of a tool, post process effect or some other menu in spawnmenu.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The currently opened control panel, if any.

AddContentType.DESCRIPTION:
Registers a new content type that is saveable into spawnlists.
Created/called by [spawnmenu.CreateContentIcon](/gmod/spawnmenu.CreateContentIcon).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: An unique name of the content type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: constructor
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A function that is called whenever we need create a new panel for this content type.

AddCreationTab.DESCRIPTION: Inserts a new tab into the CreationMenus table, which will be used by the creation menu to generate its tabs (Spawnlists, Weapons, Entities, etc.)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: What text will appear on the tab (i.e Spawnlists).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: function
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function called to generate the content of the tab.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: material
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the material that will be used as an icon on the tab. Should be a `.png` file. See [Silkicons](/gmod/Silkicons).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: order
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The order in which this tab should be shown relative to the other tabs on the creation menu.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tooltip
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The tooltip to be shown for this tab.

AddPropCategory.DESCRIPTION:
Used to add addon spawnlists to the spawnmenu tree. This function should be called within [SANDBOX:PopulatePropMenu](/gmod/SANDBOX:PopulatePropMenu).

Addon spawnlists will not save to disk if edited.
WARNINGS: You should never try to modify player customized spawnlists!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: classname
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A unique classname of the list.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the category displayed to the player, e.g. `Comic Props`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: contents
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of entries for the spawn menu. It must be numerically indexed.

Each member of the table is a sub-table containing a type member, and other members depending on the type.

New content types can be added via [spawnmenu.AddContentType](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddContentType).

| [string](/gmod/string) type | Description | Other members |
| ------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
| "header" | a simple header for organization | [string](/gmod/string) text - The text that the header will display |
| "model" | spawns a model where the player is looking | [string](/gmod/string) model - The path to the model file 	 [number](/gmod/number) skin - The skin for the model to use (optional)  [string](/gmod/string) body - The bodygroups for the model (optional)  [number](/gmod/number) wide - The width of the spawnicon (optional)  [number](/gmod/number) tall - The height of the spawnicon (optional) |
| "entity" | spawns an entity where the player is looking(appears in the Entities tab by default) | [string](/gmod/string) spawnname - The filename of the entity, for example "sent_ball"  [string](/gmod/string) nicename - The name of the entity to display  [string](/gmod/string) material - The icon to display, this should be set to `entities/[sent_name].png` 	[boolean](/gmod/boolean) admin - Whether the entity is only spawnable by admins (optional) |
| "vehicle" | spawns a vehicle where the player is looking  (appears in the Vehicles tab by default) | [string](/gmod/string) spawnname - The filename of the vehicle  [string](/gmod/string) nicename - The name of the vehicle to display  [string](/gmod/string) material - The icon to display  [boolean](/gmod/boolean) admin - Whether the vehicle is only spawnable by admins (optional) |
| "npc" | spawns an NPC where the player is looking  (appears in the NPCs tab by default) | [string](/gmod/string) spawnname - The spawn name of the NPC 	[string](/gmod/string) nicename - The name to display  [string](/gmod/string) material - The icon to display  [table](/gmod/table) weapon - A table of potential weapons (each a string) to give to the NPC. When spawned, one of these will be chosen randomly each time.  [boolean](/gmod/boolean) admin - Whether the NPC is only spawnable by admins (optional) |
| "weapon" | When clicked, gives the player a weapon;  When middle-clicked, spawns a weapon where the player is looking  (appears in the Weapons tab by default) |[string](/gmod/string) spawnname - The spawn name of the weapon  [string](/gmod/string) nicename - The name to display  [string](/gmod/string) material - The icon to display  [boolean](/gmod/boolean) admin - Whether the weapon is only spawnable by admins (optional) |

ARGUMENTS.NAME: icon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The icon to use in the tree.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique ID number for the spawnlist category. Used to make sub categories. See "parentID" parameter below. If not set, it will be automatically set to ever increasing number, starting with 1000.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: parentID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique ID of the parent category. This will make the created category a subcategory of category with given unique ID. `0` makes this a base category (such as `Builder`).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: needsApp
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The needed game for this prop category, if one is needed. If the specified game is not mounted, the category isn't shown. This uses the shortcut name, e.g. `cstrike`, and not the Steam AppID.

AddToolCategory.DESCRIPTION:
Used to create a new category in the list inside of a spawnmenu Tool Tab.

You must call this function from [SANDBOX:AddToolMenuCategories](/gmod/SANDBOX:AddToolMenuCategories) for it to work properly.

See [spawnmenu.AddToolTab](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolTab) to add new tool tabs.  
See [spawnmenu.AddToolMenuOption](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolMenuOption) to add new sub options to a newly created tool category.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tabName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The internal tool tab name, as created with [spawnmenu.AddToolTab](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolTab).

You can also use the default Tool Tab names `"Main"` and `"Utilities"`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: className
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The unique identifier name, which will be used to add tool option to this category.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: printName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The nice name to be displayed to the player. See [Addon Localization](/gmod/Addon%20Localization).

AddToolMenuOption.DESCRIPTION:
Adds an option to the right side of the spawnmenu.

See [spawnmenu.AddToolTab](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolTab) to add new right-side tabs. See [spawnmenu.AddToolCategory](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolCategory) to add new categories.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal name of the spawnmenu tab to add into (for example "Utilities")

ARGUMENTS.NAME: category
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal name of the category within the tab to add into (for example "Admin")

ARGUMENTS.NAME: class
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Unique internal identifier of the new option. This is used to reference this option by other code.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The nice name of item to show to the player. See [Addon Localization](/gmod/Addon%20Localization).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cmd
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Console command to execute when the item is selected.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: config
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Config name, used in older versions to load tool settings UI from a file.
DEPRECATED: Legacy argument, no longer works.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: cpanel
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A function to build the context panel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Allows to override the table that will be added to the tool list. Some of the fields will be overwritten by this function.

AddToolTab.DESCRIPTION:
Adds a new tool tab to the right side of the spawnmenu. (usually via the [SANDBOX:AddToolMenuTabs](/gmod/SANDBOX:AddToolMenuTabs) hook)

See [spawnmenu.GetToolMenu](/gmod/spawnmenu.GetToolMenu) for a function to retrieve existing tool tabs.

See [spawnmenu.AddCreationTab](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddCreationTab) for tabs on the left side of the spawnmenu.

See [spawnmenu.AddToolCategory](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolCategory) to add new categories to the newly created tool tab.  
See [spawnmenu.AddToolMenuOption](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddToolMenuOption) to add new options to the categories within a tool tab.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The internal name of the tab. This is used for sorting, as well as adding categories, so it should be unique.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: label
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The 'nice' name of the tab that is displayed to the player. See [Addon Localization](/gmod/Addon%20Localization).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: icon
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The file path to the icon of the tab. Should be a `.png` file. See [Silkicons](/gmod/Silkicons).

ClearToolMenus.DESCRIPTION:
Clears all the tools from the different tool categories and the categories itself, if ran at the correct place.

Seems to only work when ran at initialization.

CreateContentIcon.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new [ContentIcon](/gmod/ContentIcon) previously defined via [spawnmenu.AddContentType](/gmod/spawnmenu.AddContentType).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: type
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:

Begin.DESCRIPTION:
Tells the engine a set of queries is coming. Will wait until [sql.Commit](/gmod/sql.Commit) is called to run them.
This is most useful when you run more than 100+ queries.
This is equivalent to :
```
sql.Query( "BEGIN;" )
```

Commit.DESCRIPTION:
Tells the engine to execute a series of queries queued for execution, must be preceded by [sql.Begin](/gmod/sql.Begin).

Query.DESCRIPTION: Performs a query on the local SQLite database, returns a table as result set, nil if result is empty and false on error.
WARNINGS:
To run SQL queries with this function safely, it is crucial to ensure that the concatenated variables in the query string are safe to avoid vulnerabilities like SQL injections. For this, it is recommended to use the [sql.SQLStr](/gmod/sql.SQLStr), which allows arguments to be escaped correctly.

It's best to just use [sql.QueryTyped](/gmod/sql.QueryTyped) instead if possible.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: query

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `false` is returned if there is an error, `nil` if the query returned no data.

Performs the [sql.Query](/gmod/sql.Query) and returns the n'th row.

This function is equivalent to safely returning
```lua

```

QueryTyped.DESCRIPTION: Performs a query on the local SQLite database with proper type handling and parameter binding, returns a table as result set, empty table if no results, and false on error. Unlike [sql.Query](/gmod/sql.Query), this function properly handles SQLite data types and allows safe parameter binding to prevent SQL injection attacks.
WARNINGS:
* This function only executes a single SQL statement, unlike [sql.Query](/gmod/sql.Query) which can execute multiple statements separated by semicolons.

* Large INTEGER values (beyond ±9,007,199,254,740,991) are returned as strings to preserve exact values. This is because Lua represents all numbers as doubles, which lose precision for integers larger than 2⁵³-1. Returning them as strings prevents data corruption from rounding errors.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: query
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The query to execute with optional `?` parameter placeholders.
WARNINGS: * Always use parameter binding with `?` placeholders instead of string concatenation to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: queryParams
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Parameters to bind to the query placeholders. Supports [nil](/gmod/nil), [boolean](/gmod/boolean), [number](/gmod/number), and [string](/gmod/string) types.

The number of query parameters must match the number of `?` placeholders, or the query will fail. See examples.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `false` is returned if there is an error (See [sql.LastError](/gmod/sql.LastError)), otherwise a table with properly typed column values (empty table if no results).

QueryValue.DESCRIPTION: Performs the query like [sql.QueryRow](/gmod/sql.QueryRow), but returns the first value found.

sql.DESCRIPTION:
The SQL library allows you to access powerful database software included with Garry's Mod. It is the preferred and fastest method of storing large amounts of data. The database is located in sv.db serverside and cl.db clientside, both in the Garry's Mod base folder. SQL is a whole scripting language in itself although relatively simple, it's something you'll need to read up on before using this library.


Example of using sql.
```
-- Creating a table
sql.Query("CREATE TABLE my_db_table( id NUMBER , name TEXT )" )

-- Inserting a value to the table
sql.Query("INSERT INTO my_db_table( id , name ) VALUES( 1 , 'First') ")

-- Printing the tables data
PrintTable( sql.Query("SELECT * FROM my_db_table ") )

-- Deleting the table
sql.Query("DROP TABLE my_db_table") 
```

Known GMod [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html) settings:
* Temp files are stored in memory (`SQLITE_TEMP_STORE = 3`)
* No `ATTACH` and `DETACH` operations (`SQLITE_OMIT_ATTACH = 1`)
* No Virtual Tables (`SQLITE_OMIT_VIRTUALTABLE = 1`)
* No `VACUUM` operation (`SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM = 1`)
* No `LIMIT` and `ORDER BY` clauses in `DELETE` and `UPDATE` statements (`SQLITE_ENABLE_UPDATE_DELETE_LIMIT`)

string.DESCRIPTION:
The string *type* is a sequence of characters.

The string *library* is a standard Lua library which provides functions for the manipulation of strings.[[1]](https://www.lua.org/pil/20.html)

In Garry's Mod there are several extra useful functions and features added to this library.
Most notably all strings will access this library through the string metatable index function.[[2]](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod/blob/master/garrysmod/lua/includes/extensions/string.lua#L311-L322)

This means all strings are treated like table objects and the string library as its [Meta Table](/gmod/Meta_Tables)

```lua
local x = "Kittens"
function string.Foobar(self) return self:Right(4) end

string.Right(x,4) == x:Right(4) == x:Foobar() == ("Kittens"):Right(4) == x[-4]..x[-3]..x[-2]..x[-1]
```


The string *metatable* however is something else, and to access that you must use `getmetatable("")`.

The difference here is related to [Metamethods](/gmod/Metamethods), such as using (+) instead of (..) to concatenate strings.


```lua
local stringmeta = getmetatable("")
function stringmeta.__add(str,x) return str..x end -- This will work
function string.__add(str,x) return str..x end -- But this will not.

print("Kittens" + " And " + "Puppies")
```

See [Meta Tables](/gmod/Meta%20Tables) and [Metamethods](/gmod/Metamethods) for more information.


This category lists functions available in the string *library*.
WARNINGS: Making changes to the string *metatable* is not a good idea unless you know what you are doing. Use the string *library* instead.
Using `+` operator for concatenation breaks lua metamethod to sum string as numbers (Example: `"10" + "1"` return `11` (number)) and this is 400 times SLOWER!

DrawTexturedRectUV.DESCRIPTION:
Draws a textured rectangle with a repeated or partial texture.

`u` and `v` refer to texture coordinates.
* (u, v) = (0, 0) is the top left
* (u, v) = (1, 0) is the top right
* (u, v) = (1, 1) is the bottom right
* (u, v) = (0, 1) is the bottom left

Using a start point of (1, 0) and an end point to (0, 1), you can draw an image flipped horizontally, same goes with other directions. Going above 1 will tile the texture. Negative values are allowed as well.

Here's a helper image:


See also [surface.DrawTexturedRect](/gmod/surface.DrawTexturedRect) and [surface.DrawTexturedRectRotated](/gmod/surface.DrawTexturedRectRotated).

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: The UV offsets might require (sub-)pixel correction for accurate tiling results.

NOTES: If you are using a .png image, you need supply the "noclamp" flag as second parameter for [Material](/gmod/Global.Material) if you intend to use tiling.

If you find that `surface.DrawTexturedRectUV` is getting your texture coordinates (u0, v0), (u1, v1) wrong and you're rendering with a material created with [CreateMaterial](/gmod/Global.CreateMaterial), try adjusting them with the following code:

```
local du = 0.5 / 32 -- half pixel anticorrection
local dv = 0.5 / 32 -- half pixel anticorrection
local u0, v0 = (u0 - du) / (1 - 2 * du), (v0 - dv) / (1 - 2 * dv)
local u1, v1 = (u1 - du) / (1 - 2 * du), (v1 - dv) / (1 - 2 * dv)
```


**Explanation:**
`surface.DrawTexturedRectUV` tries to correct the texture coordinates by half a pixel (something to do with sampling) and computes the correction using `IMaterial::GetMappingWidth()`/`GetMappingHeight()`. If the material was created without a `$basetexture`, then `GetMappingWidth()`/`GetMappingHeight()` uses the width and height of the error material (which is 32x32).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X integer coordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y integer coordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: width
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The integer width of the rectangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: height
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The integer height of the rectangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startU
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The U texture mapping of the rectangle origin.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startV
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The V texture mapping of the rectangle origin.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endU
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The U texture mapping of the rectangle end.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endV
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The V texture mapping of the rectangle end.
