ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A [Color](/gmod/Color) object/table to read the color from. This is slower than providing four numbers. You could use [Color:Unpack](/gmod/Color:Unpack) to address this. You should also cache your color objects if you wish to use them, for performance reasons.

SetTextPos.DESCRIPTION: Set the top-left position to draw any future text at.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: x
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The X integer co-ordinate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: y
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Y integer co-ordinate.

SetTexture.DESCRIPTION:
Sets the texture to be used in all upcoming draw operations using the surface library.

This is a legacy method, and should probably not be used, see [surface.SetMaterial](/gmod/surface.SetMaterial) and [IMaterial](/gmod/IMaterial) for a better alternative.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: textureID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the texture to draw with returned by [surface.GetTextureID](/gmod/surface.GetTextureID).

surface.DESCRIPTION: The surface library allows you to draw text and shapes on the screen. Primarily used for making HUDs & custom GUI panels.

AppTime.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the total uptime of the current application as reported by Steam.

This will return a similar value to [SysTime](/gmod/Global.SysTime).
NOTES: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Seconds of game uptime as an integer.

0-100 if a battery (laptop, UPS, etc) is present.

Will instead return 255 if plugged in without a battery.

FlashWindow.DESCRIPTION: Flashes the window, turning the border to white briefly

GetCountry.DESCRIPTION: Returns the country code of this computer, determined by the IP of the client. Uses the steamworks API function `SteamUtils()->GetIPCountry()`.
NOTES: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Two-letter country code, using [ISO 3166-1](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) standard.

HasFocus.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether or not the game window has focus.
NOTES: This function does not work on dedicated servers and will instead return no value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not the game window has focus.

IsLinux.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the current OS is Linux.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not the game is running on Linux.

IsOSX.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the current OS is OSX.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not the game is running on OSX.

IsWindowed.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the game is being run in a window or in fullscreen (you can change this by opening the menu, clicking 'Options', then clicking the 'Video' tab, and changing the Display Mode using the dropdown menu):

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is the game running in a window?

IsWindows.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether the current OS is Windows.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the system the game runs on is Windows or not.

SteamTime.DESCRIPTION: Returns the synchronized Steam time. This is the number of seconds since the [Unix epoch](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).
NOTES: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Current Steam-synchronized Unix time.

UpTime.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the amount of seconds since the Steam user last moved their mouse.

This is a direct binding to ISteamUtils->GetSecondsSinceComputerActive, and is most likely related to Steam's automatic "Away" online status.
NOTES: This function does not work on Dedicated Servers and will instead return no value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The amount of seconds since the Steam user last moved their mouse.

system.DESCRIPTION: The system library provides functions that allow you to gather information about the system running the game, such as operating system, uptime and battery level.

Add.DESCRIPTION:
Adds all values from `source` table into the `target` table. This is most useful for sequential tables, not "dictionary" or "map" tables. See [table.Merge](/gmod/table.Merge) if you want to merge 2 tables into one.

See [table.insert](/gmod/table.insert) for a function that adds a single value, and [table.Inherit](/gmod/table.Inherit) for a function that inherits keys from one table to another.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to insert the new values into.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: source
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to retrieve the values from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The target table.

ClearKeys.DESCRIPTION: Changes all keys to sequential integers. This creates a new table object and does not affect the original.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The original table to modify.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: saveKeys
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Save the keys within each member table. This will insert a new field `__key` into each value, and should not be used if the table contains non-table values.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table with integer keys.

CollapseKeyValue.DESCRIPTION: Collapses a table with keyvalue structure

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Input table

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Output table

concat.DESCRIPTION: Concatenates the contents of a table to a string.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to concatenate.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: concatenator
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A separator to insert between strings

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key to start at

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key to end at

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Concatenated values

Copy.DESCRIPTION: Creates a deep copy and returns that copy.
WARNINGS: This function does NOT copy userdata, such as [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s and [Angle](/gmod/Angle)s!
This function is very slow! If you know the table structure, it is better to write your own copying mechanism

ARGUMENTS.NAME: originalTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to be copied.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A deep copy of the original table

CopyFromTo.DESCRIPTION: Empties the target table, and merges all values from the source table into it.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: source
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to copy from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to write to.

Count.DESCRIPTION:
Counts the amount of keys in a table. This should only be used when a table is not numerically and sequentially indexed. For those tables, consider the length (**#**) operator.

If you only want to test if the table is empty or not, use [table.IsEmpty](/gmod/table.IsEmpty) instead as it is a lot faster.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to count the keys of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The number of keyvalue pairs. This includes non-numeric and non-sequential keys, unlike the length (**#**) operator.

DeSanitise.DESCRIPTION: Converts a table that has been sanitised with [table.Sanitise](/gmod/table.Sanitise) back to its original form

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to be de-sanitised

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: De-sanitised table

Empty.DESCRIPTION: Removes all values from a table. If your table is not a metatable, it is almost always better to use `tab = {}` to preserve performance.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to empty.

FindNext.DESCRIPTION: Returns the value positioned after the supplied value in a table. If it isn't found then the first element in the table is returned
DEPRECATED: Instead, iterate the table using ipairs or increment from the previous index using Global.next. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to search

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to return element after

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Found element

FindPrev.DESCRIPTION: Returns the value positioned before the supplied value in a table. If it isn't found then the last element in the table is returned
DEPRECATED: Instead, iterate your table with ipairs, storing the previous value and checking for the target. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to search

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to return element before

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Found element

Flip.DESCRIPTION: Flips key-value pairs of each element within a table, so that each value becomes the key, and each key becomes the value.
WARNINGS:
Take care when using this function, as a Lua table cannot contain multiple instances of the same key. As such, data loss is possible when using this function on tables with duplicate values.

```
local test = { test = 1, test2 = 1 }
local f = table.Flip( test )
PrintTable( f )
-- Outputs "1	=	test2"
```

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to flip items of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The flipped table.

ForceInsert.DESCRIPTION: Inserts a value in to the given table even if the table is non-existent

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to insert value in to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to insert

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The supplied or created table

ForEach.DESCRIPTION:
Iterates for each key-value pair in the table, calling the function with the key and value of the pair. If the function returns anything, the loop is broken.

The GLua interpretation of this is [table.ForEach](/gmod/table.ForEach).
DEPRECATED: This was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and removed in 5.2. You should use Global.pairs instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to iterate over.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: callback
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to run for each key and value.

foreachi.DESCRIPTION:
Iterates for each numeric index in the table in order.

This is inherited from the original Lua implementation and is deprecated in Lua as of 5.1; see [here](http://lua-users.org/wiki/TableLibraryTutorial). You should use [ipairs](/gmod/Global.ipairs)() instead.
DEPRECATED: This was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and removed in 5.2. You should use Global.ipairs() instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to iterate over.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to run for each index.

GetFirstKey.DESCRIPTION: Returns the first key found in the given table
DEPRECATED:
Instead, expect the first key to be 1.

Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a first key.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to retrieve key from

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Key

GetFirstValue.DESCRIPTION: Returns the first value found in the given table
DEPRECATED:
Instead, index the table with a key of 1.

Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a first key.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to retrieve value from

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Value

GetKeys.DESCRIPTION: Returns all keys of a table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tabl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to get keys of

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Table of keys

GetLastKey.DESCRIPTION: Returns the last key found in the given table
DEPRECATED: Instead, use the result of the length (#) operator, ensuring it is not zero. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a last key.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to retrieve key from

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Key

GetLastValue.DESCRIPTION: Returns the last value found in the given table
DEPRECATED: Instead, index the table with the result of the length (#) operator, ensuring it is not zero. Non-numerically indexed tables are not ordered and do not have a last key.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to retrieve value from

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Value

getn.DESCRIPTION: Returns the length of the table.
DEPRECATED: This function was deprecated in Lua 5.1 and is removed in 5.2. Use the length (#) operator instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Sequential length.

GetWinningKey.DESCRIPTION: Returns a key of the supplied table with the highest number value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: inputTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to search in.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: winningKey

HasValue.DESCRIPTION: Checks if a table has a value.
NOTES: For optimization, functions that look for a value by sorting the table should never be needed if you work on a table that you built yourself.
WARNINGS: This function is **very inefficient for large tables** (O(n)) and should probably not be called in things that run each frame. Instead, consider a table structure such as example 2 below. Also see: [Tables: Bad Habits](/gmod/Tables:%20Bad%20Habits)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to check

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to search for

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the table has that value, false otherwise

Inherit.DESCRIPTION:
Copies any missing data from `base` to `target`, and sets the `target`'s `BaseClass` member to the `base` table's pointer.

See [table.Merge](/gmod/table.Merge), which overrides existing values and doesn't add a BaseClass member.


See also [table.Add](/gmod/table.Add), which simply adds values of one table to another.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Sub-tables aren't inherited. The target's table value will take priority.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to copy data to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: base
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to copy data from

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Target

insert.DESCRIPTION: Inserts a value into a table at the end of the table or at the given position.
NOTES: This function does not call the `__newindex` [metamethod](Metamethods).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to insert the variable into.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position in the table to insert the variable. If the third argument is nil this argument becomes the value to insert at the end of given table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The variable to insert into the table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The index the object was placed at.

IsEmpty.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether or not the given table is empty.

This works on both sequential and non-sequential tables, and is a lot faster for non-sequential tables than `table.Count(tbl) == 0`.

For sequential tables it is better to use `tab[1] == nil`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is empty?

IsSequential.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether or not the table's keys are sequential

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to check

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Is sequential

KeyFromValue.DESCRIPTION: Returns the first key found to be containing the supplied value

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to search

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to search for

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Key

KeysFromValue.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of keys containing the supplied value

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to search

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Value to search for

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Keys

LowerKeyNames.DESCRIPTION: Returns a copy of the input table with all string keys converted to be lowercase recursively

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to convert

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: New table

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to search.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The highest numerical key.

MemberValuesFromKey.DESCRIPTION:
Returns an array of values of given with given key from each table of given table.

See also [table.KeysFromValue](/gmod/table.KeysFromValue).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: inputTable
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to search in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: keyName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key to lookup.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A list of found values, or an empty table.

Merge.DESCRIPTION:
Recursively merges the key-value pairs of the `source` table with the key-value pairs in the `destination` table.

See [table.Inherit](/gmod/table.Inherit), which doesn't override existing values.


See also [table.Add](/gmod/table.Add), which simply adds values of one table to another.
NOTES: This function can cause a stack overflow under certain circumstances.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: destination
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table you want the source table to merge with.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: source
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table you want to merge with the destination table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: forceOverride
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If `true`, does not recursively merge sub-tables, and simply replaces them.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Destination table

move.DESCRIPTION: Moves elements from one part of a table to another part a given table. This is similar to assigning elements from the source table to the destination table in multiple assignments.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sourceTbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The source table from which the elements are to be moved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: from
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start index of the source range from which the elements are to be moved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: to
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end index of the source range until which the elements are to be moved.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dest
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index within the destination table where the moved elements should be inserted.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: destTbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The destination table to which the elements are to be moved. By default, this is the same as the source table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The modified destination table.

Pack.DESCRIPTION: Packs a set of items into a table and returns the new table. It is meant as an alternative implementation of `table.pack` from newer versions of Lua.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: items
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The items to pack into a table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table containing the `items`.
The amount of items that were added to the table.

Random.DESCRIPTION: Returns a random value from the supplied table.
WARNINGS:
This function iterates over the given table **twice**, therefore with sequential tables you should instead use following:

```
mytable[ math.random( #mytable ) ]
```

ARGUMENTS.NAME: haystack
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to choose from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A random value from the table.
The key associated with the random value.

remove.DESCRIPTION: Removes a value from a table and shifts any other values down to fill the gap.
NOTES: Does nothing if index is less than 1 or greater than `#tbl`

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to remove the value from.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: index
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The index of the value to remove.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The value that was removed.

RemoveByValue.DESCRIPTION: Removes the first instance of a given value from the specified table with [table.remove](/gmod/table.remove), then returns the key that the value was found at.
WARNINGS: Avoid usage of this function. It does not remove all instances of given value in the table, only the first found, and it does not work with non sequential tables!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table that will be searched.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: val
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to find within the table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The key at which the value was found, or false if the value was not found.

Reverse.DESCRIPTION: Returns a reversed copy of a sequential table. Any non-sequential and non-numeric keyvalue pairs will not be copied.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to reverse.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A reversed copy of the table.

Sanitise.DESCRIPTION:
Converts [Vector](/gmod/Vector)s, [Angle](/gmod/Angle)s and [boolean](/gmod/boolean)s to be able to be converted to and from key-values via [util.TableToKeyValues](/gmod/util.TableToKeyValues).

[table.DeSanitise](/gmod/table.DeSanitise) performs the opposite transformation.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to sanitise

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Sanitised table

Shuffle.DESCRIPTION: Performs an inline [Fisher-Yates shuffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Yates_shuffle) on the table in `O(n)` time

ARGUMENTS.NAME: target
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to shuffle.

sort.DESCRIPTION: Sorts a sequential table either ascending or by the given sort function.
NOTES: This function modifies the table you give to it and internally uses the [quick sort algorithm](http://www.lua.org/source/5.2/ltablib.c.html#sort).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to sort.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sorter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If specified, the sorting function.

SortByKey.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a list of keys sorted based on values of those keys.

For normal sorting see [table.sort](/gmod/table.sort).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to sort. All values of this table must be of same type.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: descending
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should the order be descending?

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A table of keys sorted by values from supplied table.

SortByMember.DESCRIPTION: Sorts a table by a named member.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tab
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to sort.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: memberKey
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The key used to identify the member.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ascending
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not the order should be ascending.

SortDesc.DESCRIPTION: Sorts a table in reverse order from [table.sort](/gmod/table.sort).
NOTES: This function modifies the table you give to it. Like table.sort, it does not return anything.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to sort in descending order.

ToString.DESCRIPTION: Converts a table into a string

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tbl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to iterate over.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: displayName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A name for the table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: niceFormatting
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Adds new lines and tabs to the string.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The table formatted as a string.

table.DESCRIPTION:
The [table](/gmod/Beginner_Tutorial_Tables) **type** is an object that can store multiple values.

The table **library** is a standard Lua library which provides functions to manipulate tables. In Garry's Mod there are several extra useful functions added to this library.

This category lists the functions available in the table `library`.

AddScore.DESCRIPTION: Increases the score of the given team

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Index of the team

GetAllTeams.DESCRIPTION: Returns the real table consisting of information on every defined team

GetClass.DESCRIPTION: Returns the selectable classes for the given team. This can be added to with [team.SetClass](/gmod/team.SetClass)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The team's color as a [Color](/gmod/Color).

GetScore.DESCRIPTION: Returns the score of the team.

GetSpawnPoints.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of valid spawnpoint entities the team can use. These are set with  [team.SetSpawnPoint](/gmod/team.SetSpawnPoint).

Joinable.DESCRIPTION: Returns if a team is joinable or not. This is set in [team.SetUp](/gmod/team.SetUp).

NumPlayers.DESCRIPTION: Returns the amount of players in a team.

SetClass.DESCRIPTION: Sets valid classes for use by a team. Classes can be created using [player_manager.RegisterClass](/gmod/player_manager.RegisterClass)

team.DESCRIPTION: The team library gives you access to the team system built into the Source engine, and allows you to create custom teams and get information about them.

Adjust.DESCRIPTION: Adjusts a previously created ([timer.Create](/gmod/timer.Create)) timer with the given identifier.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Identifier of the timer to adjust.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The delay interval in seconds. **Must be specified.**

ARGUMENTS.NAME: repetitions
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Repetitions. Use `0` for infinite or `nil` to keep previous value.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The new function. Use `nil` to keep previous value.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if succeeded.

DEPRECATED: If you want to check if whether or not a timer exists, use timer.Exists.

Create.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a new timer that will repeat its function given amount of times.
This function also requires the timer to be named, which allows you to control it after it was created via the [timer](/gmod/timer).

For a simple one-time timer with no identifiers, see [timer.Simple](/gmod/timer.Simple).
WARNINGS: Timers use [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime) internally. Due to this, they won't advance while the client is timing out from the server or on an empty dedicated server due to hibernation. (unless `sv_hibernate_think` is set to `1` or `delay` is set to `0` ).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: identifier
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Identifier of the timer to create. Must be unique. If a timer already exists with the same identifier, that timer will be updated to the new settings and reset.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay

Simple.DESCRIPTION:
Creates a simple timer that runs the given function after a specified delay.

For a more advanced version that you can control after creation, see [timer.Create](/gmod/timer.Create).
WARNINGS: Timers use [CurTime](/gmod/Global.CurTime) internally. Due to this, they won't advance while the client is timing out from the server or on an empty dedicated server due to hibernation. (unless `sv_hibernate_think` is set to `1`).

A previous message on this page stated that a delay of 0 would run the function on the next tick. This was partially an invalid assumption, and the true behavior is dependent on where `timer.Simple(0, func)` is called relative to `GarrysMod::Lua::Libraries::Timer::DoSimpleTimers`.



- If called *before* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the same frame.

- If called *during* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the same frame. **Note that calling timer.Simple(0, func) recursively (ie. a function that calls **`timer.simple(0, itself)`**) can lead to a hang!**

- If called *after* `DoSimpleTimers`, the callback will be executed on the next frame.

For more information on hook execution order, see [Lua Hooks Order](/gmod/Lua%20Hooks%20Order).

As of a commit on [2026.1.5](https://commits.facepunch.com/574654), simple timers are queued to the next frame.

As of a commit on [2026.1.8](https://commits.facepunch.com/575132), only timers with the same callback function are queued to the next frame. [Source](https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/6668#issuecomment-3725044829)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: delay
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long until the function should be ran (in seconds). A value of `0` differs in behavior, depending on where you're calling this function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: func
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The function to run after the specified delay.

WARNINGS: Timers won't advance while the client is timing out from the server.

AddNetworkString.DESCRIPTION:
Adds the specified string to a string table, which will cache it and network it to all clients automatically.
Whenever you want to create a net message with [net.Start](/gmod/net.Start), you must add the name of that message as a networked string via this function.

If the passed string already exists, nothing will happen and the ID of the existing item will be returned.
NOTES:
Each unique network name needs to be pooled once - do not put this function call into any other functions if you're using a constant string. Preferable place for this function is in a serverside lua file, or in a shared file with the [net.Receive](/gmod/net.Receive) function.

The string table used for this function does not interfere with the engine string tables and has 4095 slots.  
This limit is shared among all entities, SetNW* and SetGlobal* functions. If you exceed the limit, you cannot create new variables, and you will get the following warning:
```lua 
Warning:  Table networkstring is full, can't add [key]
```

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:

Compress.DESCRIPTION:
Compresses the given string using the [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm.

Use with [net.WriteData](/gmod/net.WriteData) and [net.ReadData](/gmod/net.ReadData) for networking and  [util.Decompress](/gmod/util.Decompress) to decompress the data.
NOTES:
The output of this function will have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L56-L63)

You may therefore experience issues using the output of this function **_outside of Garry's Mod_**. If you need to do this, you will need to manually strip the first 8 bytes from the compressed output, or use third-party tools such as [gmod-lzma](https://github.com/WilliamVenner/gmod-lzma-rs) to decompress the output instead.

It is possible for this function to generate "collisions", where two different strings will produce the same CRC. If you need a hashing function, use [util.SHA256](/gmod/util.SHA256).

Decompress.DESCRIPTION: Decompresses the given string using [LZMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZMA) algorithm. Used to decompress strings previously compressed with [util.Compress](/gmod/util.Compress).
NOTES:
This function expects the compressed input data to have the uncompressed size of the data prepended to it as an 8-byte little-endian integer. [Source](https://github.com/garrynewman/bootil/blob/beb4cec8ad29533965491b767b177dc549e62d23/src/Bootil/Utility/CompressionLZMA.cpp#L101)

If your compressed input data was compressed by [util.Compress](/gmod/util.Compress), you don't need to worry about this - the uncompressed size of the data is already prepended to its output.

However, if your compressed data was produced using standard tools **_outside of Garry's Mod_**, you will need to manually prepend the length of the uncompressed data to its compressed form as an 8-byte little endian integer.
WARNINGS: When reading user data, always try to specify `maxSize` argument, otherwise the server can be [decompression bombed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zip_bomb) with bad data that will fill up all Lua memory

ARGUMENTS.NAME: compressedString

ARGUMENTS.NAME: maxSize

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The original, decompressed string or `nil` on failure or invalid input. Also returns empty string if the input string was zero length ("").

		You can use [util.RelativePathToFull_Menu](/gmod/util.RelativePathToFull_Menu) to convert the relative path back to the full path.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fullPath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The **full** path to a file.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: fsPath
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The path to look for the files and directories in. See [this list](/gmod/File_Search_Paths) for a list of valid paths.

RETURNS.NAME: relativePath
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The relative path to the given file.

GetActivityIDByName.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ID of a custom model activity. This is useful for models that define custom ones.

See [util.GetActivityNameByID](/gmod/util.GetActivityNameByID) for a function that does the opposite.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of an activity, as defined in the model's `.qc` at compile time.

RETURNS.NAME: id
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of the activity. See also [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

GetActivityNameByID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a name for given activity ID. This is useful for models that define custom activities.

See [util.GetActivityIDByName](/gmod/util.GetActivityIDByName) for a function that does the opposite.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of an activity from some hook. See also [ACT](/gmod/Enums/ACT).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The associated name with given activity ID.

GetAnimEventIDByName.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the ID of a custom model animation event. This is useful for models that define custom animation events.

See [util.GetAnimEventNameByID](/gmod/util.GetAnimEventNameByID) for a function that does the opposite.

ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of an model animation event, as defined in the model's `.qc` at compile time.

RETURNS.NAME: id
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of an animation event, typically for usage with [ENTITY:HandleAnimEvent](/gmod/ENTITY:HandleAnimEvent).

GetAnimEventNameByID.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a name for given automatically generated numerical animation event ID. This is useful for models that define custom animation events.

See [util.GetAnimEventIDByName](/gmod/util.GetAnimEventIDByName) for a function that does the opposite.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The ID of an animation event, typically from [ENTITY:HandleAnimEvent](/gmod/ENTITY:HandleAnimEvent).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The associated name with given event ID.

GetModelInfo.DESCRIPTION:
Returns a table containing the info about the model. The model will be loaded and cached if it was not previously.

See also [util.GetModelMeshes](/gmod/util.GetModelMeshes)
NOTES:
This function will silently fail if used on models with following strings in them:
* _shared
* _anims
* _gestures
* _anim
* _postures
* _gst
* _pst
* _shd
* _ss
* _anm
* _include

ARGUMENTS.NAME: mdl
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The model path to retrieve information about.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The model info. See [Structures/ModelInfo](/gmod/Structures/ModelInfo) for details.

GetModelMeshes.DESCRIPTION: Retrieves vertex, triangle, and bone data for the visual meshes of a given model.
NOTES: This does not work on brush models (Models with names in the format `*number`)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: model
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The full path to the model to get the visual meshes of.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lod
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Which of the model's Level of Detail (LOD) models to retrieve.

			`0` is the best quality with higher numbers progressively lowering the quality.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bodygroupMask
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The combination of bodygroups to retrieve meshes for. This can also be a specially formatted bitflag.
			
			For more information, see [Entity:SetBodyGroups](/gmod/Entity:SetBodyGroups).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: skin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Skin index. Affects the `.material` of [Structures/ModelMeshData](/gmod/Structures/ModelMeshData).
			
			For more information, see [Entity:GetSkin](/gmod/Entity:GetSkin).

RETURNS.NAME: modelMeshes
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
Each index in this table corresponds to a mesh within the model passed as an argument to this function.

The mesh data is raw, and is not transformed via bone transformations. That's what the second return value is for.

RETURNS.NAME: modelBindPoses
RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: This tables indices are bone IDs for the [Structures/BoneBindPose](/gmod/Structures/BoneBindPose) stored at each index.

GetPData.DESCRIPTION:
Gets persistent data of an offline player using their SteamID.

See also [Player:GetPData](/gmod/Player:GetPData) for a more convenient version of this function for online players, [util.RemovePData](/gmod/util.RemovePData) and 
 [util.SetPData](/gmod/util.SetPData) for the other accompanying functions.
NOTES: This function internally uses [util.SteamIDTo64](/gmod/util.SteamIDTo64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which can cause collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry). This function now only uses the old method as a fallback if the name isn't found.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: steamID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: SteamID of the player, in the `STEAM_0:0:0` format. See [Player:SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Variable name to get the value of

ARGUMENTS.NAME: default
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The default value, in case there's nothing stored

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The stored value

GetPixelVisibleHandle.DESCRIPTION: Creates a new PixVis handle. See [util.PixelVisible](/gmod/util.PixelVisible).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: PixVis

GetPlayerTrace.DESCRIPTION:
Utility function to quickly generate a trace table that starts at the players view position, and ends `32768` units along a specified direction.

For usage with [util.TraceLine](/gmod/util.TraceLine) and similar functions.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ply
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The player the trace should be based on

ARGUMENTS.NAME: dir
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The direction of the trace. By default falls back to the direction the player is looking in.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The trace data. See [Structures/Trace](/gmod/Structures/Trace)

GetSunInfo.DESCRIPTION: Gets information about the sun position and obstruction or nil if there is no sun.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The sun info. See [Structures/SunInfo](/gmod/Structures/SunInfo)

GetSurfaceData.DESCRIPTION: Returns data of a [surface property](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Material_surface_properties) at given ID. New surface properties can be added via [physenv.AddSurfaceData](/gmod/physenv.AddSurfaceData).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Surface property ID. You can get it from [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult) or using [util.GetSurfaceIndex](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceIndex).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The data or no value if there is no valid surface property at given index.

GetSurfaceIndex.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the matching surface property index for the given surface property name.

See also [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData) and [util.GetSurfacePropName](/gmod/util.GetSurfacePropName) for opposite function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: surfaceName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the surface.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The surface property index, or -1 if name doesn't correspond to a valid surface property.

GetSurfacePropName.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the name of a surface property at given ID.

See also [util.GetSurfaceData](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceData) and [util.GetSurfaceIndex](/gmod/util.GetSurfaceIndex) for opposite function.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Surface property ID. You can get it from [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The name or an empty string if there is no valid surface property at given index.

GetUserGroups.DESCRIPTION: Returns a table of all SteamIDs that have a usergroup.
NOTES: This returns the original usergroups table, changes done to this table are not retroactive and will only affect newly connected users

This returns only groups that are registered in the **settings/users.txt** file of your server.  

In order to get the usergroup of a connected player, please use [Player:GetUserGroup](/gmod/Player:GetUserGroup) instead.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of users where the key is the SteamID of the user and the value is a table with 2 fields:  
* [string](/gmod/string) name - Player Steam name  
* [string](/gmod/string) group - Player usergroup name

IntersectRayWithOBB.DESCRIPTION: Performs a Ray-OBB (Orientated Bounding Box) intersection and returns position, normal and the fraction if there was an intersection.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayStart
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin or start position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayDelta
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The ray vector itself, the ray end point relative to the start point. Can be implemented as `direction * distance`

Note that in this implementation, the ray is not infinite - it's only a segment.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxAngles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angle of the box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The min position of the box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMaxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The max position of the box.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Hit position, nil if not hit.
Normal/direction vector, nil if not hit.
Fraction of trace used, nil if not hit.

IntersectRayWithPlane.DESCRIPTION: Performs a [ray-plane intersection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line%E2%80%93plane_intersection) and returns the hit position or nil.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin/start position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayDirection
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The direction of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: planePosition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any position of the plane.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: planeNormal
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The normal vector of the plane.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position of intersection, `nil` if not hit.
The distance from start position to the hit point, if there was a hit.

IntersectRayWithSphere.DESCRIPTION: Performs a ray-sphere intersection and returns the intersection positions or nil.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin/start position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayDelta
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the ray relative to the start position. Equivalent of `direction * distance`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: spherePosition
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any position of the sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphereRadius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the sphere.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The first intersection position along the ray, or `nil` if there is no intersection.
The second intersection position along the ray, or `nil` if there is no intersection.

IntersectRayWithTriangle.DESCRIPTION: Performs a ray-triangle intersection and returns the hit position or nil.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Origin/start position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rayEnd
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: triA
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The first vertex of the triangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: triB
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The second vertex of the triangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: triC
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The third vertex of the triangle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: oneSided
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the triangle can be hit from only one side (`true`) or from both sides (`false`).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The position of intersection, `nil` if not hit.
The fraction of start position to end position in range of [0,1] to the hit point, if there was a hit. i.e. 0.5 would be a hit in the exact middle of start and end positions.

IsBinaryModuleInstalled.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether a binary module is installed and is resolvable by [require](/gmod/Global.require).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name of the binary module, exactly the same as you would enter it as the argument to [require](/gmod/Global.require).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the binary module is installed and [require](/gmod/Global.require) can resolve it.

IsBoxIntersectingBox.DESCRIPTION: Performs a box-box intersection and returns whether there was an intersection or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum extents of the Axis-Aligned box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMax
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum extents of the Axis-Aligned box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum extents of the second Axis-Aligned box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum extents of the second Axis-Aligned box.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if there is an intersection, `false` otherwise.

IsBoxIntersectingSphere.DESCRIPTION: Performs a box-sphere intersection and returns whether there was an intersection or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum extents of the Axis-Aligned box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: boxMax
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum extents of the Axis-Aligned box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: shpere2Position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any position of the sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphere2Radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the sphere.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if there is an intersection, `false` otherwise.

IsInWorld.DESCRIPTION: Checks if a certain position is within the world bounds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the vector is in world.

IsModelLoaded.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the model is loaded in the game.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name/Path of the model to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the model is loaded in the game; otherwise false.

IsOBBIntersectingOBB.DESCRIPTION: Performs OBB on OBB intersection test.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box1Origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the first box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box1Angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angles of the first box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box1Mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The min position of the first box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box1Maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The max position of the first box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Origin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the second box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Angles
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The angles of the second box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Mins
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The min position of the second box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: box2Maxs
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The max position of the second box.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tolerance
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance for error. Leave at 0 if unsure.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether there is an intersection.

IsPlayerSpeaking.DESCRIPTION:
Returns whether the player at given index is speaking or not.

This is used internally by the voice chat HUD for players outside of the PVS.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [entity index](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex) of the player to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the player at given index is currently speaking.
The current voice volume ([Player:VoiceVolume](/gmod/Player:VoiceVolume)) of the player if they are speaking.

IsPointInCone.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether a point is within a cone or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: point
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the point to test.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the cone tip.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneAxis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The direction of the cone.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneSine
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sine of the cone's angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneLength
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Length of the cone's axis.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the point is within the cone, `false` otherwise.

IsRayIntersectingRay.DESCRIPTION: Performs a ray-ray intersection and returns whether there was an intersection or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ray1Start
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start position of the first ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ray1End
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: End position of the first ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ray2Start
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start position of the second ray.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ray2End
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: End position of the second ray.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if there is an intersection, `false` otherwise.
Distance from start of ray 1 to the intersection, if there was one.
Distance from start of ray 2 to the intersection, if there was one.

IsSkyboxVisibleFromPoint.DESCRIPTION: Check whether the skybox is visible from the point specified.
NOTES: This will always return true in fullbright maps.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position to check the skybox visibility from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the skybox is visible from the position.

IsSphereIntersectingCone.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether a sphere is intersecting a cone or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphereCenter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center position of the sphere to test.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphereRadius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the sphere to test.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneOrigin
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The position of the cone tip.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneAxis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The direction of the cone.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneSine
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [math.sin](/gmod/math.sin) of the cone's angle.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: coneCosine
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [math.cos](/gmod/math.cos) of the cone's angle.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if the sphere intersects the cone, `false` otherwise.

IsSphereIntersectingSphere.DESCRIPTION: Performs a sphere-sphere intersection and returns whether there was an intersection or not.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphere1Position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any position of the first sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphere1Radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the first sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphere2Position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Any position of the second sphere.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: sphere2Radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The radius of the second sphere.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` if there is an intersection, `false` otherwise.

IsValidModel.DESCRIPTION:
Checks if the specified model is valid.
 

A model is considered invalid in following cases:
* Starts with a space or **maps**
* Doesn't start with **models**
* Contains any of the following:
  * `_gestures`
  * `_animations`
  * `_postures`
  * `_gst`
  * `_pst`
  * `_shd`
  * `_ss`
  * `_anm`
  * `.bsp`
  * `cs_fix`
* If the model isn't precached on the server, AND if the model file doesn't exist on disk
* If precache failed
* Model is the error model

Running this function will also precache the model.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name/Path of the model to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Whether the model is valid or not. Returns false clientside if the model is not precached by the server.

IsValidPhysicsObject.DESCRIPTION: Checks whether the given numbered physics object of the given entity is valid or not. Most useful for ragdolls.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to take.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: physobj
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Number of the physics object to test.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: `true` that's valid, `false` otherwise.

IsValidProp.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the specified prop is valid (has valid physics object).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name/Path of the model to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the specified prop is valid; otherwise false.

IsValidRagdoll.DESCRIPTION: Checks if the specified model name points to a valid ragdoll.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ragdollName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Name/Path of the ragdoll model to check.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Returns true if the specified model name points to a valid ragdoll; otherwise false.

JSONToTable.DESCRIPTION:
Converts a JSON string to a Lua table. It supports comments and trailing commas.

See [util.TableToJSON](/gmod/util.TableToJSON) for the opposite function.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Colors will not have the color metatable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: json
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The JSON string to convert.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ignoreLimits
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ignore the depth and breadth limits, **use at your own risk!**.
WARNINGS: If this is false, there is a limit of 15,000 keys total.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ignoreConversions
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ignore string to number conversions for table keys.
WARNINGS: if this is false, keys are converted to numbers wherever possible. This means using [Player:SteamID64](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) as keys won't work.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The table containing converted information. Returns `nil` on failure.

KeyValuesToTable.DESCRIPTION: Converts a Valve KeyValue string (typically from [util.TableToKeyValues](/gmod/util.TableToKeyValues)) to a Lua table.
NOTES: Due to how [table](/gmod/table)s work in Lua, keys will not repeat within a table. See [util.KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder](/gmod/util.KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder) for alternative.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: keyValues
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The KeyValue string to convert.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: usesEscapeSequences
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to true, will replace `\t`, `\n`, `\"` and `\\` in the input text with their escaped variants

ARGUMENTS.NAME: preserveKeyCase
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether we should preserve key case (may fail) or not (always lowercase)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The converted table

KeyValuesToTablePreserveOrder.DESCRIPTION: Similar to [util.KeyValuesToTable](/gmod/util.KeyValuesToTable), but it also preserves order of keys (since Lua dictionary-style tables do not guarantee a specific order), and allows handling of repeated keys. (since each key can only appear once in a dictionary data structure)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: keyValues
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The Valve KeyValue formatted text.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: usesEscapeSequences
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set to true, will replace `\t`, `\n`, `\"` and `\\` in the input text with their escaped variants

ARGUMENTS.NAME: preserveKeyCase
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether we should preserve key case (may fail) or not (always lowercase)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The output table

LocalToWorld.DESCRIPTION: A convenience function around LocalToWorld-related functions.
NOTES: If [Entity:EntIndex](/gmod/Entity:EntIndex) returns `0`, the function will return the passed `lpos`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to take.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lpos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A local space vector.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: bone
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Actually to be treated as the number corresponding to a specific [PhysObj](/gmod/PhysObj) of the entity.

If that specific physics object is valid, then [PhysObj:LocalToWorld](/gmod/PhysObj:LocalToWorld) is used.

Otherwise, [Entity:LocalToWorld](/gmod/Entity:LocalToWorld).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The corresponding worldspace vector.

MD5.DESCRIPTION: Generates the [MD5 hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5) of the specified string.
WARNINGS: MD5 is considered cryptographically broken and is known to be vulnerable to a variety of attacks including duplicate return values. If security or duplicate returns is a concern, use [util.SHA256](/gmod/util.SHA256).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stringToHash
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The string to calculate the MD5 hash of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The MD5 hash of the string in hexadecimal form.

NetworkIDToString.DESCRIPTION: Returns the networked string associated with the given ID from the string table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stringTableID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: ID to get the associated string from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The networked string, or nil if it wasn't found.

NetworkStringToID.DESCRIPTION: Returns the networked ID associated with the given string from the string table.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: networkString
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: String to get the associated networked ID from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The networked ID of the string, or 0 if it hasn't been networked with [util.AddNetworkString](/gmod/util.AddNetworkString).

NiceFloat.DESCRIPTION: Formats a float by stripping off extra `0's` and `.'s`.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: float
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The float to format.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Formatted float.

ParticleTracer.DESCRIPTION:
Creates an orange box (.pcf) tracer effect with the given parameters. See [util.ParticleTracerEx](/gmod/util.ParticleTracerEx) for version with additional arguments.

Internally uses `ParticleTracer` engine effect. ([util.Effect](/gmod/util.Effect)) which then spawns in `ParticleEffect` effect.
NOTES: The default bullet effect is not in .pcf format, therefore it is not used with util.ParticleTracer.  Consider utilizing [util.Effect](/gmod/util.Effect) instead

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The name of the .pcf particle effect to use for the tracer.

Control Point 0 is the start location. Control Point 1 is the end pos.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: doWhiz
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Whether to play the hit near-miss (whiz) sound.

ParticleTracerEx.DESCRIPTION: Creates a tracer effect with the given parameters. Expanded version of [util.ParticleTracer](/gmod/util.ParticleTracer).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The name of the tracer effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The start position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endPos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The end position of the tracer.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: doWhiz
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Play the hit miss(whiz) sound.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: entityIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity index of the emitting entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachmentIndex
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Attachment index to be used as origin.

PixelVisible.DESCRIPTION:
Returns the visibility of a square that is always pointed at the camera in the world-space.

This is typically used for in-game sprites or "billboards". ([render.DrawSprite](/gmod/render.DrawSprite))

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The center of the visibility test.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: size
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The size of the square to check for visibility.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: PixVis
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The PixVis handle created with [util.GetPixelVisibleHandle](/gmod/util.GetPixelVisibleHandle).
WARNINGS: Don't use the same handle twice per tick or it will give unpredictable results.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Visibility percentage, in range of `[0-1]`. `0` when none of the area is visible, `0.5` when half the area is visible, `1` when all of it is visible, etc.

PointContents.DESCRIPTION: Returns the contents of the position specified.
NOTES: This function will sample only the world environments. It can be used to check if [Entity:GetPos](/gmod/Entity:GetPos) is underwater for example unlike [Entity:WaterLevel](/gmod/Entity:WaterLevel) which works for players only.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: position
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Position to get the contents sample from.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Contents bitflag, see [CONTENTS](/gmod/Enums/CONTENTS)

PrecacheModel.DESCRIPTION: Precaches a model for later use. Model is cached after being loaded once.
NOTES: Does nothing on the client.
WARNINGS: Modelprecache is limited to 8192 unique models. When it reaches the limit the game will crash.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: modelName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The model to precache.

PrecacheSound.DESCRIPTION: Precaches a sound for later use. Sound is cached after being loaded once.

BUGS.DESCRIPTION: Ultimately does nothing on client, and only works with sound scripts, not direct paths.

NOTES: Soundcache is limited to 16384 unique sounds on the server. Due to this fact this function is disabled on purpose, as exceeding the limit causes the server to shutdown.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: soundName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The sound to precache.

QuickTrace.DESCRIPTION: Performs a trace with the given origin, direction, and filter.
NOTES: This function will throw an error in the menu realm because it internally uses util.TraceLine which doesn't exist in the menu realm and thus error.

RelativePathToFull_Menu.DESCRIPTION:
Converts the relative path of a given file to the full path on disk.

RelativePathToGMA_Menu.DESCRIPTION: Returns which Workshop addon the given file belongs to.

Author	=	[Addon Author]

RemoveDecalsAt.DESCRIPTION: Removes world decals at given position, in given radius. Does not remove decals on models!

ARGUMENTS.NAME: limit

RemovePData.DESCRIPTION:
Removes persistent data of an offline player using their SteamID.

See also [Player:RemovePData](/gmod/Player:RemovePData) for a more convenient version of this function for online players, [util.SetPData](/gmod/util.SetPData) and 
 [util.GetPData](/gmod/util.GetPData) for the other accompanying functions.
NOTES: This function internally uses [util.SteamIDTo64](/gmod/util.SteamIDTo64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which can cause collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry). This function now tries to remove both old and new entries.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: steamID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: SteamID of the player to remove data of, in the `STEAM_0:0:0` format. See [Player:SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Variable name to remove

NOTES: The screen shake effect is rendered by modifying the view origin on the client. If you override the view origin in [GM:CalcView](/gmod/GM:CalcView) you may not be able to see the shake effect.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: pos
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The origin of the effect.
			
Used serverside only, to determine which clients the event should be networked to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: amplitude
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The strength of the effect. How far away from its origin the camera will move while shaking.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: frequency
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How many times per second to change the direction of the camera wobble. 40 is generally enough; values higher are hardly distinguishable.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duration
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The duration of the effect in seconds.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: radius
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
The range from the origin within which views will be affected, in Hammer units.

This is used when networking the event to clients only.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: airshake
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION:
Whether players in the air should also be affected.

Used serverside only to determine which clients to send the event to.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: filter
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: If set, will only network the screen shake event to players present in the filter.

SetPData.DESCRIPTION:
Sets persistent data for offline player using their SteamID.

See also [Player:SetPData](/gmod/Player:SetPData) for a more convenient version of this function for online players, [util.RemovePData](/gmod/util.RemovePData) and 
 [util.GetPData](/gmod/util.GetPData) for the other accompanying functions.
NOTES: This function internally uses [util.SteamIDTo64](/gmod/util.SteamIDTo64), it previously utilized [Player:UniqueID](/gmod/Player:UniqueID) which could have caused collisions (two or more players sharing the same PData entry).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: steamID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: SteamID of the player, in the `STEAM_0:0:0` format. See [Player:SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: name
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Variable name to store the value in.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: value
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The value to store.

SHA1.DESCRIPTION: Generates the [SHA-1 hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1) of the specified string.
WARNINGS: SHA-1 is considered cryptographically broken and is known to be vulnerable to a variety of attacks. If security is a concern, use [util.SHA256](/gmod/util.SHA256).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stringToHash
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The string to calculate the SHA-1 hash of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The SHA-1 hash of the string in hexadecimal form.

SHA256.DESCRIPTION: Generates the [SHA-256 hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) of the specified string. This is mostly unique and is astronomically unlikely to return the same hash for a different string unlike [util.CRC](/gmod/util.CRC) or [util.MD5](/gmod/util.MD5) which are both much more vulnerable to duplicate returns.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: stringToHash
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The string to calculate the SHA-256 hash of.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The SHA-256 hash of the string in hexadecimal form.

SharedRandom.DESCRIPTION:
Generates a random float value that should be the same on client and server.



This uses a different method of obtaining random numbers and is unaffected by [math.randomseed](/gmod/math.randomseed). Instead it uses an internal seed that is based on the player's current predicted command and is fixed to a value of -1 outside of prediction.
NOTES: This function is best used in a [predicted hook](/gmod/prediction).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: uniqueName
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The seed for the random value

ARGUMENTS.NAME: min
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The minimum value of the random range

ARGUMENTS.NAME: max
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The maximum value of the random range

ARGUMENTS.NAME: additionalSeed
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The additional seed

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The random float value

SpriteTrail.DESCRIPTION: Adds a trail to the specified entity.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Entity to attach trail to

ARGUMENTS.NAME: attachmentID
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Attachment ID of the entities model to attach trail to. If you are not sure, set this to 0

ARGUMENTS.NAME: color
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Color of the trail

ARGUMENTS.NAME: additive
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Should the trail be additive or not

ARGUMENTS.NAME: startWidth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Start width of the trail

ARGUMENTS.NAME: endWidth
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: End width of the trail

ARGUMENTS.NAME: lifetime
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long it takes to transition from startWidth to endWidth

ARGUMENTS.NAME: textureRes
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The resolution of trails texture. A good value can be calculated using this formula: 1 / ( startWidth + endWidth ) * 0.5

ARGUMENTS.NAME: texture
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Path to the texture to use as a trail.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Entity of created trail ([env_spritetrail](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Env_spritetrail))
A brand new stack object.

SteamIDFrom64.DESCRIPTION: Given a [64bit SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) will return a [STEAM_0:0:0](/gmod/Player:SteamID) style Steam ID.
NOTES: This operation induces data loss. Not all fields of a [64bit SteamID](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamID) can be represented using the `STEAM_0:0:0` format, specifically the "account type" and "account instance" fields.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The 64 bit Steam ID

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: String [STEAM_0:0:0](/gmod/Player:SteamID) style Steam ID representation.

SteamIDTo64.DESCRIPTION: Converts a [STEAM_0:0:0](/gmod/Player:SteamID) style SteamID to a [64bit SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID64).

ARGUMENTS.NAME: id
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The [STEAM_0:0:0](/gmod/Player:SteamID) format SteamID

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: [64bit SteamID](/gmod/Player:SteamID64) or 0 (as a string) on fail

StringToType.DESCRIPTION:
Converts a string to the specified type.

This can be useful when dealing with ConVars.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: str
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The string to convert

ARGUMENTS.NAME: typename
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The type to attempt to convert the string to. This can be `vector`, `angle`, `float`, `int`, `bool`, or `string` (case insensitive).

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The result of the conversion, or nil if a bad type is specified.

TableToJSON.DESCRIPTION:
Converts a table to a JSON string. Keep in mind that not every data type can be stored in the JSON format, notably any entity will not be written, as if it wasn't in the table. Same goes for materials and textures, etc.

See [util.JSONToTable](/gmod/util.JSONToTable) for the opposite function.
WARNINGS:
All keys are strings in the JSON format, so all keys of other types will be converted to strings!  
This can lead to loss of data where a number key could be converted into an already existing string key! (for example in a table like this: `{["5"] = "ok", [5] = "BBB"}`)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Table to convert.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: prettyPrint
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Format and indent the JSON.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: A JSON formatted string containing the serialized data

TableToKeyValues.DESCRIPTION:
Converts the given table into a Valve keyValue formatted string.

Use [util.KeyValuesToTable](/gmod/util.KeyValuesToTable) to perform the opposite transformation.

[util.TableToJSON](/gmod/util.TableToJSON) can be used as an alternative.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: table
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The table to convert.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: rootKey
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The root key name for the output KV table.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: The output.

Timer.DESCRIPTION: Creates a timer object. The returned timer will be already started with given duration.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: duration
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How long you want the timer to be. `Elapsed()` will return true only after this much time has passed.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A timer object. It has the following methods:
* `Reset()` - Resets and stops the timer.
* `Start( duration = 0 )` - (Re)starts the timer with given duration
* `Started()` - Returns `true` if the timer has been started. It will continue to return true even after the duration has passed.
* `Elapsed()` - Returns `true` if the timer duration has elapsed since its creation or the call to `Start()`
* `GetElaspedTime()` - Returns amount of time since timer started.

TimerCycle.DESCRIPTION: Returns the time since this function has been last called

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Time since this function has been last called in ms

tobool.DESCRIPTION: Converts string or a number to a bool, if possible. Alias of [tobool](/gmod/Global.tobool).
DEPRECATED: You should use Global.tobool instead.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: input
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A string or a number to convert.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: False if the input is equal to the string or boolean "false", if the input is equal to the string or number "0", or if the input is nil. Returns true otherwise.

TraceEntity.DESCRIPTION: Runs a trace using the entity's collisionmodel between two points. This does not take the entity's angles into account and will trace its unrotated collisionmodel.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tracedata
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Trace data. See [Structures/Trace](/gmod/Structures/Trace)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to use

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Trace result. See [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult)

TraceEntityHull.DESCRIPTION: Identical to [util.TraceHull](/gmod/util.TraceHull) but uses an entity's [Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box) for `mins`/`maxs` inputs. (These 2 keys will be ignored in the provided table)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: tracedata
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Trace data. See [Structures/HullTrace](/gmod/Structures/HullTrace)

ARGUMENTS.NAME: ent
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The entity to use mins/maxs of for the hull trace.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Trace result. See [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult)

TraceHull.DESCRIPTION:
Performs an AABB hull (axis-aligned bounding box, aka not rotated) trace with the given trace data.

This trace type cannot hit hitboxes.

See [util.TraceLine](/gmod/util.TraceLine) for a simple line ("ray") trace.
NOTES: This function may not always give desired results clientside due to certain physics mechanisms not existing on the client. Use it serverside for accurate results.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: TraceData
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: The trace data to use. See [Structures/HullTrace](/gmod/Structures/HullTrace)

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION: Trace result. See [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult)

TraceLine.DESCRIPTION:
Performs an infinitely thin, invisible ray trace (or "trace") in a line from a starting point to an ending point and returns a table of information about what, if anything, the trace line hit or intersected.

Traces intersect with the physics meshes of [solid](/gmod/enums/SOLID), [server-side](/gmod/States), [entities](/gmod/Entity) (including the [game world](/gmod/game.GetWorld)) but cannot detect client-side only entities unless [hitclientonly](/gmod/Structures/Trace#hitclientonly) is set to `true`.
  
See [ents.FindAlongRay](/gmod/ents.FindAlongRay) if you wish for the trace to not stop on first intersection.  
See [util.TraceHull](/gmod/util.TraceHull) for a "box" type trace.

Traces do not differentiate between the inside and the outside faces of physics meshes. Because of this, if a trace starts within a solid physics mesh it will hit the inside faces of the physics mesh and may return unexpected values as a result.


You can use `r_visualizetraces` set to `1` (requires `sv_cheats` set to `1`) to visualize traces in real time for debugging purposes.

ARGUMENTS.NAME: traceConfig
ARGUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: A table of data that configures the trace. See [Structures/Trace](/gmod/Structures/Trace) for available options.

RETURNS.DESCRIPTION:
A table of information detailing where and what the trace line intersected, or `nil` if the trace is being done before the [GM:InitPostEntity](/gmod/GM:InitPostEntity) hook.

			For the table's format and available options see the [Structures/TraceResult](/gmod/Structures/TraceResult) page.

util.DESCRIPTION: This is the list of utility functions.

CreateFromTable.DESCRIPTION: Creates a panel from a table, used alongside [vgui.RegisterFile](/gmod/vgui.RegisterFile) and [vgui.RegisterTable](/gmod/vgui.RegisterTable) to efficiently define, register, and instantiate custom panels.

CursorVisible.DESCRIPTION: Returns whenever the cursor is currently active and visible.

GetAll.DESCRIPTION:
Returns all Lua-created panels.

ie. it lags one frame behind panel layout and is completely unhelpful for [PANEL:Paint](/gmod/PANEL:Paint) if your panels are moving around under the mouse a lot every frame.

Classname of the panel to register. This is what you will need to pass to [vgui.Create](/gmod/vgui.Create)'s first argument.

Widgets allow the player to have mouse interaction with entities, such as being able to manipulate the [bones of an NPC](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O3gG0t39-pQ).
